```text
1	# Agent pane discovery
2
3	Find — and jump to — coding-agent sessions (`claude`, `cursor-agent`, `codex`,
4	`opencode`) that are currently running in *any* tmux pane on this host.
5
6	The pain this solves: you start `claude` in pane A on session `chezmoi`, hop
7	into pane B in another window for a quick test, drift over to a `vibe/foo`
8	session for a Codex task, and three windows later you can't remember which
9	pane has the agent you wanted to nudge. CodeIsland (macOS) tells you which
10	**terminal app** is running an agent, but not the specific tmux pane —
11	useless once you have more than one agent inside one terminal.
12
13	Two complementary surfaces ship in this repo, both backed by tmux:
14
15	| Tool | Scope | Best at |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `tv agent-panes` | All four agents (Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor) | "Where am I running stuff?" cross-agent overview, jump-to-pane |
18	| `tv agent-wakeup` | Same live panes, plus pueue wakeup tasks | "Which agent is quota-blocked, when should I send `continue`?" |
19	| `recon` (optional) | Claude-only, with live status (Working / Idle / Waiting) parsed from pane capture | "Which Claude needs my attention?" — recon's live status detection is richer than what we replicate in tv |
20
21	## `tv agent-panes` (primary)
22
23	Open the picker with `prefix + a` inside tmux, or via the popup menu
24	(`prefix + Space → → Agents → Live agent panes (tv)`), or from any shell
25	with `tv agent-panes`.
26
27	Each row is one running agent pane. The status column shows ● (busy) or
28	○ (idle) for Claude (read from `~/.claude/sessions/{pid}.json`); blank for
29	others.
30
31	```
32	[cc] ● chezmoi:1.1     │  discover-coding-agent-sessions          │  chezmoi
33	[cc] ○ chezmoi:2.1     │  fix-nvm-lazy-loader-permission-request  │  chezmoi
34	[cc] ●  vibe/foo:4.1   │  refactor auth module                    │  foo
35	[oc]   vibe/bar:0.0    │  Generate migration script               │  bar
36	```
37
38	### Keybindings (in the picker)
39
40	| Key | Action |
41	|---|---|
42	| `Enter` / `Alt+T` | Switch tmux focus to that session/window/pane |
43	| `Alt+K` | Kill the pane (with `[y/N]` confirm) |
44	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy the pane target (`session:win.pane`) to clipboard |
45	| `Alt+P` | Copy directory path |
46	| `Alt+R` | Copy session ID |
47	| `Alt+S` | Copy matched `.specstory/history/*.md` path |
48	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview: live `tmux capture-pane` snapshot ↔ stored transcript |
49	| `Esc` | Close the picker |
50
51	### How resolution works
52
53	- **Claude** — Claude Code writes a per-process file at
54	  `~/.claude/sessions/{claude_pid}.json` containing `sessionId`, `cwd`,
55	  `status`, and (when set) a friendly `name`. The discovery walker reads
56	  these directly — *zero heuristics* for Claude. It then walks each
57	  `claude_pid`'s parent chain via `ps -o ppid=` until it finds a tmux
58	  `pane_pid`, which gives the pane target.
59	- **Codex / OpenCode / Cursor** — `pgrep -x <bin>` finds running agent
60	  PIDs, parent-chain walked the same way. Session ID is best-effort: the
61	  walker queries each agent's storage (`opencode.db`, `~/.codex/sessions`,
62	  `~/.cursor/chats`) for the most-recent matching session whose `cwd`
63	  equals the pane's `pane_current_path`. If multiple sessions share a
64	  cwd, the most recently updated wins. The pane is still listed even if
65	  no session ID matches — the row is useful for jump-to-pane regardless.
66
67	## `tv agent-wakeup` (quota waits + scheduled continue)
68
69	Open with `prefix + M-a`, via the popup menu
70	(`prefix + Space → → Agents → Quota wakeup (tv)`), or from a shell with
71	`tv agent-wakeup`.
72
73	The channel reuses the live pane resolver from `tv agent-panes`, captures the
74	last part of each pane scrollback, and conservatively marks panes as quota
75	waiting only when it sees explicit limit wording such as `session limit`,
76	`rate limit`, `limit reached`, or `quota`. It parses reset phrases like
77	`resets 1:50am`, `resets in 70m`, or `resets in 5h 20m`, then shows any
78	queued pueue wakeup task for the pane.
79
80	Claude HUD usage lines such as `Context ... | Usage Limit reached` are
81	ignored because `claude-hud` renders from cached/API usage data and is not an
82	authoritative live indicator that the pane is currently blocked.
83
84	`WAIT_MENU` is the Claude `/rate-limit-options` screen where option 1
85	(`Stop and wait for limit to reset`) is already selected. For that state the
86	recommended action is `enter`, not `continue`.
87
88	| Key | Action |
89	|---|---|
90	| `Enter` | Switch tmux focus to that pane |
91	| `Alt+C` | Schedule a smart wakeup at the detected reset time + 2 minutes |
92	| `Alt+T` | Prompt for a custom time/delay (`01:52am`, `70m`, `5h`, etc.) |
93	| `Alt+N` | Smart send now: `Enter` for `WAIT_MENU`, otherwise `continue` + Enter |
94	| `Alt+X` | Cancel queued wakeup tasks for that pane |
95	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview; the default preview is live `tmux capture-pane` output |
96
97	The shell equivalent is:
98
99	```bash
100	agent-wakeup status
101	agent-continue-at --pane %12 --at 01:52am
102	agent-wakeup send-now --pane %44 --auto        # Enter for /rate-limit-options, continue otherwise
103	agent-wakeup send-now --pane %44 --enter-only  # force selecting Stop-and-wait menu item
104	agent-continue-at --current --delay 70m
105	agent-wakeup cancel --pane %12
106	```
107
108	Scheduled wakeups are pueue tasks in group `agent-wakeup` with labels
109	`agent-wakeup:%pane_id`. The scheduled task re-captures the pane right before
110	sending. If the quota marker has disappeared, it aborts instead of blindly
111	typing into a session that may already be doing unrelated work. With `--auto`,
112	the send step re-captures the pane and chooses `Enter` for a rate-limit menu
113	or `continue` for a normal prompt.
114
115	The fully automatic "detect quota, schedule, continue, repeat until non-quota
116	exit" supervisor is deliberately deferred; see
117	[`backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md).
118
119	## Scheduled work beyond quota waits
120
121	For non-quota delayed work, prefer native agent scheduling when it fits:
122
123	- Claude Code has session-scoped `/loop` / cron tasks, Desktop scheduled
124	  tasks, and cloud Routines.
125	- Codex App has Automations, including thread automations that wake up the
126	  same thread on a schedule.
127	- OpenCode is scriptable through `opencode run --continue` / `--session`, and
128	  its GitHub integration supports cron schedules in GitHub Actions.
129
130	Those native surfaces are better for agent-owned scheduled work. The local
131	`agent-wakeup` / pueue path is still useful when the target is a specific tmux
132	pane, a one-shot future continuation, or a cross-agent workflow that should
133	show up in the same dashboard. The broader local wrapper idea is tracked in
134	[`backlog/agent-delayed-run-scheduler.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/agent-delayed-run-scheduler.md).
135
136	## `recon` (Claude-only fast popup, optional)
137
138	[`gavraz/recon`](https://github.com/gavraz/recon) is a Rust TUI dashboard
139	that focuses on Claude Code only but pays attention to live agent status by
140	parsing the Claude TUI status bar via `tmux capture-pane`. Worth keeping
141	around when you're juggling several Claude sessions and want
142	"who's blocked on me?" at a glance.
143
144	### Install
145
146	Installed automatically via the `rust_cargo_tools` ansible role on
147	`chezmoi apply`:
148
149	```bash
150	cargo install --git https://github.com/gavraz/recon --locked
151	```
152
153	Upgrades flow through the standard cargo path:
154
155	```bash
156	just upgrade-cargo   # or scripts/upgrade_tools.sh cargo
157	```
158
159	### Use
160
161	Open it from the popup menu: `prefix + Space → → Agents → Claude
162	dashboard (recon)`. There's no top-level keybind by default — `prefix + g`
163	(recon's upstream default) is taken by the sesh picker on this repo.
164	Promote it to a top-level binding in `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` if
165	you find yourself reaching for it often.
166
167	The `→ Agents` submenu only shows the recon row when `recon` is on `PATH`,
168	so it disappears cleanly on hosts that haven't installed it.
169
170	## Troubleshooting
171
172	### "I don't see my running Claude"
173
174	Stale `~/.claude/sessions/{pid}.json` files are skipped automatically — if
175	the PID isn't a descendant of any tmux pane, the row is omitted. If you
176	expect to see a session that isn't there:
177
178	```bash
179	~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py panes        # raw TSV, see what it finds
180	ls -lt ~/.claude/sessions/                          # what files exist
181	ps -p <pid_from_filename>                           # is the process alive?
182	tmux list-panes -aF '#{pane_id} #{pane_pid} #{pane_current_command}'
183	```
184
185	If the claude PID is alive but `_find_pane_for_pid` doesn't reach a tmux
186	pane (e.g., claude was launched outside tmux), the row is correctly
187	omitted — `tv agent-panes` only shows panes you can `switch-client` to.
188
189	### "Codex/OpenCode/Cursor row has no session ID"
190
191	The cwd-based reverse lookup couldn't find a stored session whose
192	`directory` matches the pane's `pane_current_path`. Common causes: agent
193	was started with `--cd` to a path that doesn't match storage; storage
194	was migrated. The pane still shows up — Enter still jumps to it; you just
195	won't get an automatic "resume this exact session" handle.
196
197	### "I jumped to a pane and tmux says it doesn't exist"
198
199	The picker is a snapshot. If a pane closes between snapshot and switch,
200	the action falls back to a `tmux display-message` warning and stays put.
201	Re-open the picker (`prefix + a`) to refresh.
202
203	### "Recon doesn't appear in the Agents submenu"
204
205	`menu-agents.sh` probes `command -v recon` and only adds the row when the
206	binary is on `PATH`. If you've just installed it, your tmux server may
207	need a fresh shell environment — `tmux source ~/.tmux.conf` is enough; no
208	restart required.
209
210	## Related
211
212	- [tmux keybindings](tmux/keybindings.md) — popup-menu surface
213	  (`prefix + Space`) where `→ Agents` lives, plus the full `prefix + ?`
214	  binding map.
215	- [Agent sessions browser](agent-overlays.md) — sister channel
216	  `tv agent-sessions` that browses **stored** session history (resume an old
217	  session vs. jump to a running one).
218	- [SpecStory internals](specstory-internals.md) — explains the
219	  `<!-- Provider Session UUID -->` reverse-lookup that lets the picker
220	  surface the matching `.specstory/history/*.md` for each row.
221	- Sibling deferred work: per-pane working/idle status glyph in the tmux
222	  window list itself (Option C of
223	  [`backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md)).
224
```

1	# `tv agent-sessions`: richer preview + `.specstory/history/*.md` linkage
2
3	**Status**: P1 in-progress (2026-04; landing this round) — Cursor transcripts deferred
4	**Effort**: M for the first batch; Cursor transcripts each another M
5	**Related**: `dot_config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml`, `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py`, [docs/tools/specstory-internals.md](../docs/tools/specstory-internals.md)
6
7	## Context
8
9	The `tv agent-sessions` channel aggregates OpenCode / Claude Code / Codex / Cursor-CLI / Cursor-IDE sessions into one `tv` picker with fuzzy search, resume-in-terminal, clipboard copy-by-ID/path. Three gaps the user flagged 2026-04-24:
10
11	1. **Preview shows only "first 5 user messages"** — good for finding a session by text, useless for reading it back. Want the full back-and-forth transcript.
12	2. **No link to the corresponding `.specstory/history/*.md`** — user often wants to reference a prior session to another coding agent, currently has to eyeball-match by timestamp + title.
13	3. **`all` mode ordering looks random** — confirmed: each per-agent handler sorts internally by mtime DESC, but the `all` mode concatenates the five blocks without a global merge. So TV sees OpenCode-block → Claude-block → …, each internally sorted, overall not. The emitted TSV column 1 (`when`) has the right data for a global sort — we just weren't doing the merge.
14
15	## Investigation
16
17	**SpecStory reverse-lookup is grep-able.** Every `.specstory/history/*.md` file embeds `<!-- <Provider> Session <uuid> ... -->` on line 5, and the UUID is the same session id the agent uses for its `--resume` flag. Full derivation, caveats, CLI surface in [docs/tools/specstory-internals.md](../docs/tools/specstory-internals.md) — confirmed against DeepWiki (<https://deepwiki.com/specstoryai/getspecstory>) for the architecture and against the actual files in this repo's `.specstory/history/` for the format.
18
19	**Per-agent transcript-render feasibility** (from probing real session stores):
20
21	| Agent | Source | Difficulty | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| Claude Code (`[cc]`) | `~/.claude/projects/<flat>/<sid>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line | Easy | Filter `type ∈ {user, assistant}`; content is `str` or `list[{type:text, text}]`. Existing `first 5` path already walks this. |
24	| Codex (`[cx]`) | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` | Easy | Filter `type == response_item` + `payload.type == message`; nested but regular. |
25	| OpenCode (`[oc]`) | `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (SQLite) | Medium | SQL join on `message` + `part`; existing preview block already has the SQL skeleton, just needs `LIMIT 5` dropped. |
26	| Cursor Agent CLI (`[cu]`) | `~/.cursor/chats/<wsHash>/<chatId>/store.db` (blobs) | **Painful** | Blobs are binary JSON with no role index; current `first 5` code iterates every blob and guesses role. Full transcript would need the same, with higher error rate over longer sessions. |
27	| Cursor IDE composer (`[ci]`) | `globalStorage/state.vscdb` `cursorDiskKV` table (`composerData:<id>` + `bubbleId:<id>:<bid>`) | Medium | Structured, but two-table lookup and a verbose schema. |
28
29	**TV preview supports scrolling** (`pageup` / `pagedown` for half-page), preview panel sized at 60 rows via the channel's `[ui.preview_panel]`. A multi-hundred-turn transcript fits fine — no need for a self-built TUI yet.
30
31	**Pitfall avoided** — [pitfalls/tv-channel-bare-braces-break-substitution.md](../pitfalls/tv-channel-bare-braces-break-substitution.md) warns that any bare `{...}` in the channel TOML's `command` strings silently breaks ALL `{split:\t:N}` placeholders. Mitigation: keep the rendering code in the Python helper; the TOML just shells out to it.
32
33	## Shipping this round (2026-04)
34
35	| # | Change | File(s) |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| A | **Helper: global mtime DESC sort in `all` mode.** Handlers emit into a shared buffer instead of printing directly; main() sorts + prints once. Single-mode behaviour unchanged (each already sorts locally). | `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py` |
38	| B | **Helper: new TSV column 5 = `specstory_path`.** Single scan of `~/.local/share/chezmoi/.specstory/history/*.md` on startup, reads the first ~10 lines per file to extract the `<!-- ... Session <uuid> ... -->` UUID, builds `{sid → path}` cache. Column is empty string when no match. | `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py` |
39	| C | **Helper: `transcript <cc\|cx\|oc> <sid>` subcommand.** Writes markdown to stdout. Prefers the pre-rendered `.specstory/history/*.md` when available (zero-parsing, matches what user sees on disk); falls back to raw-source rendering for live / un-synced sessions. | `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py` |
40	| D | **TOML: 3-stage preview cycle.** Preview 1 (new, default on open) = metadata header + specstory path + full transcript via `glow --style auto -` (falls back to `bat -l md` if glow is missing). Preview 2 = legacy first-5 user messages (unchanged). Preview 3 = raw dump (unchanged). | `dot_config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml` |
41	| E | **TOML: `Alt+S` → copy SpecStory MD path to clipboard.** New `[actions.copy_specstory]` mirroring `[actions.copy_dir]` (pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC52). Quietly no-ops on empty column. | `dot_config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml` |
42	| F | **Docs split.** Moved filename-algorithm + reverse-lookup + markdown-structure deep dive from `docs/tools/specstory.md` (which is user-facing install/config) into new `docs/tools/specstory-internals.md`. Nav entry added to `mkdocs.yml`. | `docs/tools/specstory-internals.md`, `docs/tools/specstory.md`, `mkdocs.yml` |
43
44	## Deferred (tracked here, not in this batch)
45
46	| # | Change | Why deferred |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| G | **Cursor Agent CLI (`[cu]`) full transcript** | Painful — blob decode + role guessing. Current `first 5` implementation already best-effort; full transcript amplifies the fragility. Defer until user actually browses Cursor Agent sessions often. |
49	| H | **Cursor IDE composer (`[ci]`) full transcript** | Two-table join across `composerData` + `bubbleId:*` is straightforward but verbose (~50 lines). Low current demand (user works mostly in Cursor CLI / Claude). |
50	| I | **Custom TUI fallback** | TV's preview scroll + 60-row panel covers the need. Re-open only if we hit a real TV constraint. |
51	| J | **Add `glow` to the `devtools` ansible role** | Currently installed on the user's macOS box via homebrew directly; `bat` fallback in the preview command means glow absence doesn't break anything. Add to ansible when a fleet host complains. |
52	| K | **Tool-use blocks in the transcript** | Current Claude-side renderer inlines a one-line summary (`> *tool_use: <name>*`). Full collapsible rendering (à la SpecStory's `<tool-use>` / `<details>`) would bring the live transcript to parity with SpecStory's output — but the SpecStory-first path already handles this when the session has been synced, so the deferred renderer is only a last-resort. Trade-off: polish vs complexity in the helper. |
53
54	## Options considered
55
56	### Rendering strategy for preview 1
57
58	| Option | Pros | Cons |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| A. Always re-render from raw source | Works for live / un-synced sessions | Duplicates SpecStory's rendering logic; diverges from what the user sees on disk |
61	| B. Always cat the `.specstory/history/*.md` | Zero parsing; pixel-perfect match with disk artefact; supports all providers uniformly (including ones we can't render well, like Cursor Agent) | Only works after SpecStory flushes — live / in-progress sessions have no file yet |
62	| C. **Prefer B, fall back to A** (chosen) | Best of both; "is this the session I want" works for finished sessions, "what's happening right now" works for live ones | Helper has two code paths to maintain |
63
64	### Sort strategy for `all` mode
65
66	| Option | Pros | Cons |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| A. Sort in TV | Helper stays simple | TV's config has no `sort_by` knob; would need string-pipeline ordering tricks. Fragile. |
69	| B. **Helper buffer + single global sort** (chosen) | One-liner refactor; uses the raw mtime floats each handler already computes; deterministic | Handlers no longer "stream" output for the merged case (acceptable — total row count is ~hundreds) |
70	| C. Per-agent sub-channels only, drop `all` | Simplest | Defeats the aggregation value |
71
72	### Reverse-lookup map
73
74	| Option | Pros | Cons |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| A. Replicate SpecStory's slug algorithm, derive filename from (ts, first-user-msg) | No grep; fast | Drifts with SpecStory versions; breaks on historical files with old formats |
77	| B. **Grep `<!-- ... Session <uuid> ... -->` on helper startup** (chosen) | Version-agnostic; works across all providers with one regex | O(num\_md\_files) startup cost — bounded (~300 files × ~10 lines each = negligible) |
78	| C. Shell out to a future SpecStory subcommand | Zero logic on our end | Subcommand doesn't exist; `specstory list` / `sync` / `watch` don't expose path |
79
80	## Open questions
81
82	- **Should the transcript include tool-use blocks?** Claude JSONL has them, SpecStory renders them collapsed. Our Python fallback currently emits a one-line summary (`> *tool_use: Bash*`). Expand later if the fallback path becomes the dominant one.
83	- **Does the `.specstory/history/` lookup dir need to be configurable?** Hard-coded to `~/.local/share/chezmoi/.specstory/history` today. If the user starts using SpecStory in other repos often, promote to `SPECSTORY_HISTORY_DIRS` env var (colon-separated, multi-dir scan).
84
85	## Decision
86
87	`2026-04-24 chose option C (SpecStory-first → raw-source fallback) + option B (helper buffer sort) + option B (grep-based reverse lookup)`. Cursor transcripts deferred pending demand.
88

```text
1	# Native agent-session dashboard TUI
2
3	**Status**: P? design backlog (2026-06)
4	**Effort**: XL
5	**Related**: `dot_config/television/executable_agent-wakeup.py`, `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py`, `dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py`, [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](../docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md), [backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md](agent-quota-auto-loop.md)
6
7	## Context
8
9	`tv agent-panes`, `tv agent-sessions`, and `tv agent-wakeup` are useful v1
10	surfaces, but they are still separate pickers. The user wants to keep
11	iterating toward one "agent control center" where the important state is
12	visible at a glance:
13
14	- which agent panes are live,
15	- which are active / idle / waiting for user / quota-blocked,
16	- reset timers and scheduled `continue` actions,
17	- transcript / SpecStory links,
18	- tmux session/window/pane location,
19	- direct actions like jump, continue, schedule, cancel, copy session name,
20	  kill pane, or open transcript.
21
22	The likely end state may not be a TV channel plus pueue. TV is excellent for
23	picker workflows, but a dashboard with timers, repeated updates, per-row
24	state machines, and richer actions may want a native TUI.
25
26	## Scope Candidates
27
28	### Minimal native TUI
29
30	- One table of live agent panes.
31	- Side preview with `tmux capture-pane`.
32	- Actions: jump to pane, send `continue`, schedule one wakeup, cancel wakeup.
33	- Reuse existing `agent-wakeup` detection and pueue scheduling backend.
34
35	### Full dashboard
36
37	- Live panes plus stored sessions in one UI.
38	- Pane status classifier: active, idle, waiting user, wait quota, scheduled,
39	  finished, failed, unknown.
40	- Countdown timers for quota reset and scheduled wakeups.
41	- Per-agent adapters for Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor storage and status.
42	- Transcript / SpecStory preview with jump-to-file.
43	- Optional auto-repeat quota loop per pane.
44	- tmux actions: jump pane, copy pane target/session name, kill pane/session,
45	  rename, clear workmux status.
46
47	### Supervisor-backed TUI
48
49	- Long-running daemon owns state polling and scheduling.
50	- TUI is only a client, so it can restart without losing timers.
51	- Scheduler may use pueue initially, but could migrate to an internal queue
52	  if per-pane state and repeat policies become first-class.
53
54	## Architecture Options
55
56	| Option | Shape | Pros | Cons |
57	|---|---|---|---|
58	| A. Extend TV channels | Keep adding `tv agent-*` channels and shell helpers | Fast, low dependency, follows current repo patterns | Hard to model timers/state machines; fragmented UX |
59	| B. Python Textual/Rich TUI | Single Python app using existing helper code | Fast to build; good tables/previews/keybindings | Adds a heavier runtime; packaging/versioning needs care |
60	| C. Rust Ratatui TUI | Native binary with tmux/pueue integration | Fast, distributable, robust TUI ergonomics | Larger implementation cost; duplicates Python discovery unless refactored |
61	| D. Go Bubble Tea TUI | Single static-ish binary, good terminal UX | Good deployment story | Another stack in repo; still needs adapters |
62	| E. Daemon + thin TUI | Separate state/scheduler service plus UI client | Best for resilient timers and auto-repeat | Highest complexity; needs lifecycle management |
63
64	## Current Decision
65
66	`2026-06-19`: keep the shipped v1 on TV + pueue for immediate one-off wakeups,
67	but track the native TUI as a separate backlog item. Do not force the
68	auto-continue loop design into the TV channel if the feature naturally wants
69	a richer dashboard.
70
71	## Open Questions
72
73	- Is the primary UI a tmux popup, a standalone terminal app, or both?
74	- Should the scheduler remain pueue-backed for persistence, or should a
75	  daemon own timers directly?
76	- Which implementation stack fits the repo best: Python Textual/Rich, Rust
77	  Ratatui, or Go Bubble Tea?
78	- Should this become a general `agent-session` command, or live under an
79	  existing namespace like `fleet` / `tmux` / `tv`?
80	- What is the first safe autonomous action beyond one-off `continue`?
81
82	## References
83
84	- [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](../docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md)
85	- [docs/tools/pueue.md](../docs/tools/pueue.md)
86	- [backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md](agent-quota-auto-loop.md)
87
```

/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:292:## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:294:The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:300:3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.

40	# Agent sidebar ordering. herdr's default is "spaces" (grouped by space);
41	# "priority" turns the panel into an attention queue (blocked/waiting agents
42	# float to the top) instead of a per-space grouping. With many concurrent agent
43	# panes the queue is what you actually scan, so this is the more useful default
44	# here. Valid values: "spaces" | "priority" ("workspaces" is an alias for

46	agent_panel_sort = "priority"

48	# Expanded Agent sidebar row layout. herdr's own default is

50	# and we append the `$review` metadata token so the review-pending ⭐ (prefix+m /
51	# hmark) is actually VISIBLE in the sidebar.
52	#
53	# Required since herdr 0.7.4: `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field
54	# were replaced by a namespaced token map, and unlike custom_status a token is
55	# rendered ONLY where a row layout names it — set a token with no layout entry
56	# and the flag silently exists in the API but shows up nowhere.
57	#
58	# Keep `$review` in sync with TOKEN in dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh.

61	[ui.sidebar.agents]

65	]

68	shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
69	# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
70	#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
71	#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
72	# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live
73	# cwd — same as a split. herdr issue #912 changed `follow` so tabs behave like
74	# splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root" was treated as a bug and

80	# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
81	# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything

84	[keys]
85	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
86	split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
87	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
88	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
89	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)

91	# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
92	# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
93	# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
94	# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
95	# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
96	# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
97	# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
98	# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
99	switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
100	focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)

102	# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
103	# prefix+w opens the workspace navigator; navigate_workspace_* are the

105	# hjkl muscle memory carries here too. (These fields can't use prefix+/enter/tab/
106	# left/right or unmodified 1-9 — plain j/k are allowed.)
107	navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]

111	# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
112	# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
113	# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /

122	# btop / nvtop monitors as floating command panes (same mechanism as lazygit —
123	# a real PTY that closes when you quit the tool). Quick Actions can't host these:

126	[[keys.command]]

128	type = "pane"

138	# --- Scratch shell as a real floating popup (prefix+`) ---
139	# Was type = "pane", which took over the layout — it read as a zoom of the
140	# current window rather than a scratch space. type = "popup" (herdr >= 0.7.4)
141	# floats ABOVE the tiled layout instead, so nothing reflows and quitting the
142	# shell puts you back exactly where you were.
143	#
144	# The lazygit/btop/nvtop bindings above deliberately STAY type = "pane": you
145	# quit those immediately (`q`) and return, so the temporary split costs nothing
146	# and a modal popup would buy nothing. Popups are session-modal — you cannot
147	# interact with another pane while one is open — which is the trade-off that
148	# decides this per binding rather than globally.
149	[[keys.command]]
150	key = "prefix+`"
151	type = "popup"
152	command = "$SHELL"
153	width = "85%"
154	height = "80%"

157	# --- Run an arbitrary command in a floating popup (prefix+E) ---
158	# The generalisation of prefix+G: instead of a hardcoded tool, fzf-pick or type

160	# the command exits. Helper: ~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh.

164	# back exactly where you were. That is why this one is NOT type = "pane" like the
165	# lazygit/btop/scratch bindings above.
166	#
167	# Deliberately not a herdr-plus Quick Action (prefix+y): Quick Actions run through
168	# `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin (the same reason btop/nvtop are command panes) and
169	# every action is a fixed command string with no free-text field.
170	#
171	# Exit behaviour: closes on success, holds on failure so the error stays readable.
172	# Override with HERDR_RUN_HOLD=always|never. `--sh` runs via `sh -c` (fast, no
173	# aliases) instead of the default `$SHELL -ic` (sources the interactive rc, so
174	# this repo's aliases/functions resolve).
175	[[keys.command]]

1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6
7	- **Install**:
8	  - **Both platforms** — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-{linux,macos}-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr`, managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`. No tarball, so no unarchive step.
9	  - macOS is **deliberately not** Homebrew, and it is the only tool in this repo where that's true. Upstream disables `herdr update` on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs because the package manager owns the binary — which removes the *only* pane-preserving upgrade path and leaves a server restart, i.e. killing every pane process, as the sole option. The formula was dropped in favour of the release binary so macOS gets `--handoff` too. Boxes provisioned before the switch are migrated by a one-time `brew uninstall herdr` in the same role (leaving both installed would put two binaries on `PATH` and risk a client/server `protocol_mismatch` against yourself).
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: `just upgrade-herdr` (→ `herdr update --handoff`) on both platforms — **run it from outside herdr**, see below
12
13	> **`herdr update` refuses to run from inside a herdr pane.** The handoff replaces the server process that owns the pane you are typing in, so it fails closed:
14	>
15	> ```console
16	> $ herdr update --handoff          # from a pane inside herdr
17	> update failed: run `herdr update` outside herdr after detaching from the session
18	> ```
19	>
20	> The flow is **detach (`prefix+q`) → run it in a plain terminal → reattach with bare `herdr`**. Detaching does not kill anything (client close ≠ session loss), and `--handoff` then swaps the server without exiting pane processes — verified 2026-07 upgrading 0.7.1 → 0.7.5 with a Claude Code session running in a pane, which survived uninterrupted. `just upgrade-herdr` encodes this: it *skips with instructions* rather than failing when it detects `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`, so `just upgrade-all` from a herdr pane doesn't die here. Full trace: [`pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md).
21
22	> **Install is version-blind; upgrades are yours to run.** The Linux ansible task gates on `herdr --version` returning non-zero — *"is it installed at all"*, not *"is it current"* — so a fresh box gets whatever is latest that day and `chezmoi apply` never touches it again. This is the repo's [install-vs-upgrade split](../this_repo/upgrades.md) working as designed, but herdr drifts faster than most because its config can outrun the binary (a `[[keys.command]]` using `type = "popup"`, added in 0.7.4, makes an older herdr reject **the entire keys block** — `reload-config` reports `status: "partial"` + `keeping current keys settings`, and only that one diagnostic line tells you).
23
24	> **Every herdr upgrade stales the agent integrations.** `herdr integration status` versions each one (`current (v9)` / `outdated (v7 < v9)`); reinstall with `herdr integration install <agent>`. These files (`~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh`, `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh`, `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh`, `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js`) are written by herdr and are **not** chezmoi-managed, so `chezmoi apply` will not restore or clobber them. `just upgrade-herdr` reports which went stale but deliberately does not auto-install them.
25	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` + managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`). The overlay enforces our managed tables on every `chezmoi apply` while preserving whatever herdr writes back at runtime (see [Config management](#config-management-why-modify_)).
26
27	> **Why a package-managed herdr strands its own server — the reason macOS left Homebrew.** herdr's socket API is protocol-versioned, and a package-manager upgrade cannot restart the server, so after `brew upgrade herdr` every CLI call (and therefore every `tv herdr-*` channel, `hvibe`/`hcode`, and `[[keys.command]]` helper) fails `protocol_mismatch` until the server restarts — which kills all pane processes. `herdr update --handoff`, the live pane-preserving path, is **disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs**, so a brew-installed herdr has no way to avoid that restart. This repo now installs the self-managed release binary on macOS too, which is what closes the gap; the pitfall below is kept because it still describes what happens on any box that has not been migrated (and `just upgrade-herdr` skips with instructions when it detects a package-managed install). Check with `herdr status` (`compatible:` / `restart_needed:`), not `herdr --version`. Full recovery matrix: [`pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md).
28
29	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.

31	---
32
33	## Model differences vs tmux
34
35	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
36
37	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
38
39	### Named sessions
40
41	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
44	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
45
46	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
47
48	## cwd & workspace-naming model
49
50	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
51
52	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
54	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
55	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
56	- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
57
58	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
59
60	| value | meaning |
61	|---|---|
62	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
63	| `home` | `$HOME` |
64	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
65	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
66
67	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
68
69	```toml
70	[[keys.command]]
71	key = "prefix+C"
72	type = "pane"
73	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
74	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
75	```

96	## Keybindings
97
98	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
99
100	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
101
102	| Key | Action | Type |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
105	| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
106	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
107	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
108	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
109	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator ([in-popup keys](#navigator-keys)) | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
110	| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
111	| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
112
113	> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
114	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
115	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
116	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
117	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
118	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
119	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
120	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
121	| `prefix + M` | btop system monitor | command pane |
122	| `prefix + N` | nvtop GPU monitor | command pane |
123	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
124	| `` prefix + u `` | **URL picker** — fzf-pick a URL from the pane and open it (`x open`); tmux-fzf-url analog. `--source recent` = full scrollback | command pane |
125	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
126	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
127	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
128	| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
129	| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
130	| `prefix + P` | copy focused pane's **process info** to the clipboard | command pane |
131	| `prefix + D` | copy focused pane's **coordinate** (session>space>tab>pane) | command pane |
132	| `prefix + V` | copy focused pane's **content** (visible screen) | command pane |
133	| `prefix + S` | copy focused pane's **content** (full scrollback) | command pane |
134	| `prefix + d` | copy the **workspace ("space") root dir** — the right-click "Copy dir" herdr doesn't have ([details](#copy-to-clipboard)) | command pane |
135	| `prefix + ctrl + d` | copy the focused pane's **live cwd** (the `pwd`/`abspath` answer) | command pane |
136	| `` prefix + p `` | **copy a file path** from the pane — two-tier fzf (paths that exist under the pane cwd on top), copies the resolved absolute path (`x copy`) | command pane |
137	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
138	| `prefix + E` | **run any command** in the pane's cwd — fzf-pick from history or type it; the popup closes itself when the command exits ([details](#run-any-command)) | command **popup** |

142	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
