1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54
55	# Absolutize + validate a `-p/--path DIR` argument in THIS shell. Echoes the
56	# canonical (symlink-resolved) path; on a non-directory, echoes nothing and
57	# returns 1 after a message on stderr.
58	#
59	# LOAD-BEARING for every `--cwd` below: herdr resolves a *relative* `--cwd`
60	# against the SERVER's launch directory (wherever `herdr server` was started),
61	# not the caller's cwd — and on a miss it silently falls back to $HOME, so
62	# `hhere -p ../sibling` opens a workspace at `~` with no error anywhere. tmux
63	# resolves `new-session -c` client-side, which is why the sesh originals
64	# (shere/svibe/scode) never needed this.
65	# See pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md.
66	#
67	# `CDPATH=''` + `--` + `>/dev/null` keep a CDPATH hit from silently retargeting
68	# the cd or echoing the resolved dir into the capture.
69	# $1=dir  $2=caller name (for the error message)
70	function _herdr_abs_dir() {
71	    local abs
72	    abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
73	    if [ -z "$abs" ]; then
74	        echo "${2:-herdr}: --path is not a directory: $1" >&2
75	        return 1
76	    fi
77	    printf '%s\n' "$abs"
78	}
79
80	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
81	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
82	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
83	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
84	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
85	#
86	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
87	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
88	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
89	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
90	function _herdr_session_target() {
91	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
92	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
93	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
94	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
95	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
96	            | head -1)
97	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
98	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
99	            return 1
100	        fi
101	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
102	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
103	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
104	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
105	            return 1
106	        fi
107	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
108	        return 0
109	    fi
110	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
111	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
112	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
113	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
114	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
115	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
116	            | head -1)
117	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
118	    else
119	        printf 'default\t\n'
120	    fi
121	}
122
123	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
124	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
125	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
126	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
127	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
128	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
129	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
130	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
131	    local session="${1:-default}"
132	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
133	        herdr
134	    else
135	        herdr session attach "$session"
136	    fi
137	}
138
139	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
140	#
141	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
142	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
143	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
144	#
145	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
146	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
147	#
148	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
149	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
150	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
151	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
152	#
153	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
154	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
155	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
156	#
157	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
158	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
159	# has no even-out-splits command.
160	#
161	# Usage:
162	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
163	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
164	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
165	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
166	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
167	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
168	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
169	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
170	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
171	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
172	function herdr-vibe() {
173	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
174
175	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
176	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
177	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
178	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
179	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
180	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
181	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
182
183	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
184	        case "$1" in
185	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
186	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
187	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
188	            --session)       session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
189	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
190	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
191	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
192	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
193	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
194	            -h|--help)
195	                cat <<'EOF'
196	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
197
198	Usage:
199	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
200	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
201	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
202	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
203
204	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
205	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
206	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
207	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
208	  tab "edit"   — nvim
209	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
210	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
211
212	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session so
213	the new workspace is visible; run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses it.
214	--no-attach builds in the background either way.
215	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: the current session
216	when inside herdr, else the default session). Start a session first with
217	`herdr --session NAME`.
218
219	Two modes for choosing agents:
220	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
221	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
222
223	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
224	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
225	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
226
227	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
228	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
229	  kill            — let the pane close
230	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
231
232	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
233	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
234	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
235
236	Examples:
237	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
238	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
239	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
240	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
241	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
242	EOF
243	                return 0 ;;
244	            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
245	            *)               break ;;
246	        esac
247	    done
248
249	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
250	        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
251	        return 1
252	    fi
253	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
254	        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
255	        return 1
256	    fi
257
258	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
259
260	    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
261	    local -a agents
262	    agents=()
263	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
264	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
265	            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
266	            return 1
267	        fi
268	        local tok
269	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
270	            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
271	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
272	        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
273	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
274	            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
275	            return 1
276	        fi
277	    else
278	        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
279	            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
280	        fi
281	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
282	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
283	        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
284	        # --tab-per-agent for more).
285	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
286	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
287	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
288	            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
289	        fi
290	        local k
291	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
292	    fi
293
294	    case "$on_exit" in
295	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
296	        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
297	    esac
298
299	    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe). `-p DIR` is absolutized first so
300	    # a bad path reports itself instead of masquerading as "not a git repo".
301	    local repo_root
302	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
303	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hvibe) || return 1
304	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
305	    else
306	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
307	    fi
308	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
309	        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
310	        return 1
311	    fi
312
313	    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
314	    local a missing=""
315	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
316	        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
317	    done
318	    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
319	        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
320	        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
321	        return 1
322	    fi
323
324	    local repo label
325	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
326	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")
327
328	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
329	    # A non-empty sess_sock means an explicit --session override — scope it with
330	    # `local -x` so child `herdr` calls see it but the user's shell is untouched.
331	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
332	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
333	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
334	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
335	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
336
337	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
338	    local existing
339	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
340	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
341	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
342	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
343	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
344	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
345	        fi
346	        return 0
347	    fi
348
349	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
350	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
351	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
352	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
353	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
354	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
355	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
356	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
357	        return 1
358	    fi
359
360	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
361	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
362	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
363	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
364	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
365	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
366	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
367	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
368	        done
369	    else
370	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
371	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
372	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
373	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
374	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
375	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
376	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
377	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
378	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
379	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio
380	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
381	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
382	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
383	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
384	                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
385	            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
386	                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
387	                prev="$np"
388	            fi
389	            m=$((m+1))
390	        done
391	    fi
392
393	    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
394	    local git_inner git_label
395	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
396	    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
397	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
398	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"
399
400	    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
401	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
402	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
403	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
404	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
405	    fi
406	}
407
408	# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
409	#
410	# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
411	#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
412	#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
413	# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
414	#
415	# Usage:
416	#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
417	#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
418	#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
419	#   hcode --no-specstory claude
420	#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
421	#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
422	function herdr-code() {
423	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
424
425	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
426	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
427	        case "$1" in
428	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
429	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
430	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
431	            --session)      session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
432	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
433	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
434	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
435	            --agents)
436	                echo "hcode: --agents is hvibe-only (hcode is single-agent)." >&2
437	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2
438	                return 1 ;;
439	            -h|--help)
440	                cat <<'EOF'
441	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
442
443	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
444	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
445
446	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
447	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
448	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
449	Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
450
451	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session;
452	run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses. --no-attach builds in the background.
453	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
454	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
455
456	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
457	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
458	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
459
460	--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart
461
462	Examples:
463	  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
464	  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
465	  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
466	  hcode --on-exit kill claude
467	EOF
468	                return 0 ;;
469	            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
470	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
471	        esac
472	    done
473
474	    case "$on_exit" in
475	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
476	        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
477	    esac
478
479	    local repo_root
480	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
481	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hcode) || return 1
482	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
483	    else
484	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
485	    fi
486	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
487	        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
488	        return 1
489	    fi
490
491	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
492	        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
493	        return 1
494	    fi
495
496	    local repo label
497	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
498	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")
499
500	    # Resolve target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
501	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
502	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
503	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
504	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
505	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
506
507	    local existing
508	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
509	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
510	        echo "hcode: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
511	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
512	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
513	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
514	        fi
515	        return 0
516	    fi
517
518	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
519	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
520	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
521	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
522	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
523	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
524	        echo "hcode: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
525	        return 1
526	    fi
527
528	    # editor tab: nvim in the initial pane, agent split off to the right at ~25%.
529	    # --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane being split (nvim/left), so 0.75
530	    # leaves nvim at 75% and the new agent pane at 25%.
531	    herdr tab rename "$t0" editor >/dev/null 2>&1
532	    herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")" >/dev/null 2>&1
533	    local ap
534	    ap=$(herdr pane split "$p0" --direction right --ratio 0.75 --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
535	        | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
536	    [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane run "$ap" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
537
538	    # monitor tab.
539	    local mon
540	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=btop
541	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=htop
542	    else                                       mon=top
543	    fi
544	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" monitor "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$mon" "$on_exit" "$mon")"
545
546	    # Focus editor tab, nvim pane (left neighbor of the agent pane).
547	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
548	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
549	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
550	        [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane focus --direction left --pane "$ap" >/dev/null 2>&1
551	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
552	    fi
553	}
554
555	# ── hhere: plain "open a workspace here + attach" ────────────────────────────
556	#
557	# herdr analog of `shere` (sesh-here). The lightweight counterpart to
558	# hvibe/hcode: create a herdr workspace at $PWD (or -p DIR), focus it, and
559	# attach a client when run from outside herdr. NO git requirement and NO agent
560	# layout — just a shell in the workspace root pane. This fills the gap where
561	# every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent pack; with
562	# tmux `tmux new-session` lands you in $PWD directly, but herdr adds a Workspace
563	# layer, so without this you'd launch herdr, create a space (opens at $HOME),
564	# then cd manually.
565	#
566	# Smart argument handling (mirrors shere):
567	#   hhere                          # plain shell at $PWD
568	#   hhere npm run dev              # bare args → run as the root-pane command
569	#   hhere -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
570	#   hhere -p ~/proj                # explicit path, plain shell
571	#   hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev    # explicit path + command
572	#
573	# `-p DIR` is absolutized in THIS shell before it reaches herdr — the server
574	# resolves a relative `--cwd` against its own launch directory and falls back to
575	# $HOME on a miss (silently). A non-existent DIR is a hard error.
576	#
577	# The command (if any) runs raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping. That agent
578	# treatment stays with hcode/hvibe; hhere is deliberately lightweight.
579	#
580	# Idempotent per label (bare basename of the dir, matching herdr's own native
581	# auto-label convention). Caveat: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to the root
582	# pane's LIVE cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see docs/tools/herdr.md § cwd
583	# & workspace-naming), so the reuse is best-effort — if the label has drifted, a
584	# re-run creates a fresh workspace (arguably correct: you're elsewhere now).
585	#
586	# Usage:
587	#   hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
588	function herdr-here() {
589	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hhere: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
590
591	    local cmd="" target="" no_attach=0 session_arg=""
592	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
593	        case "$1" in
594	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
595	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
596	            --session)    session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
597	            --no-attach)  no_attach=1; shift ;;
598	            -h|--help)
599	                cat <<'EOF'
600	hhere — open a plain herdr workspace here + attach (herdr analog of shere)
601
602	Usage: hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
603
604	Creates a herdr workspace at DIR (default $PWD), focuses it, and — when run
605	from OUTSIDE herdr — attaches a client so it is visible. No git repo required
606	and no agent layout: just a shell in the workspace root pane. For agent
607	layouts use hcode (single-agent) or hvibe (multi-agent).
608
609	Smart argument handling:
610	  hhere                        # plain shell at $PWD
611	  hhere npm run dev            # bare args → run as the root-pane command
612	  hhere -c "npm run dev"       # explicit --command flag
613	  hhere -p ~/proj              # explicit path, plain shell
614	  hhere -p ../sibling          # relative paths resolve against YOUR shell
615	  hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev  # explicit path + command
616
617	--path DIR is resolved (and symlink-canonicalized) here, in your shell, before
618	it reaches herdr — a DIR that does not exist is a hard error, not a silent
619	workspace at $HOME.
620
621	Idempotent: re-running in the same dir focuses the existing workspace.
622	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
623	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
624	--no-attach builds in the background.
625	EOF
626	                return 0 ;;
627	            -*)           echo "hhere: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
628	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
629	        esac
630	    done
631	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
632	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
633
634	    # ABSOLUTIZE — load-bearing, do NOT pass `$target` through verbatim; herdr
635	    # resolves a relative `--cwd` server-side and falls back to $HOME on a miss.
636	    # See _herdr_abs_dir above.
637	    target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hhere) || return 1
638
639	    local label
640	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
641
642	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
643	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
644	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
645	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
646	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
647	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
648
649	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
650	    local existing
651	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
652	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
653	        echo "hhere: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
654	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
655	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
656	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
657	        fi
658	        return 0
659	    fi
660
661	    local ws_json ws p0
662	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$target" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
663	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
664	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
665	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ]; then
666	        echo "hhere: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
667	        return 1
668	    fi
669
670	    # Optional command in the root pane (raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping).
671	    [ -n "$cmd" ] && herdr pane run "$p0" "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1
672
673	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
674	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
675	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
676	    fi
677	}
678
679	# ── hroot: like hhere but at the git-root ────────────────────────────────────
680	#
681	# herdr analog of `sroot` (sesh-root). Same as hhere except the target resolves
682	# to the current git top-level (falls back to $PWD outside a repo). Thin wrapper
683	# over herdr-here so there is one code path; -p is not accepted (the root IS the
684	# path), everything else (-c / bare command / --session / --no-attach) passes
685	# through.
686	#
687	# Usage:
688	#   hroot                          # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
689	#   hroot npm run dev              # + run a command
690	#   hroot -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
691	function herdr-root() {
692	    case "$1" in
693	        -h|--help)
694	            cat <<'EOF'
695	hroot — open a plain herdr workspace at the git-root + attach (analog of sroot)
696
697	Usage: hroot [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
698
699	Like hhere, but the workspace opens at the current git top-level (falls back to
700	$PWD outside a repo). All flags except --path pass through to hhere.
701
702	  hroot                # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
703	  hroot npm run dev    # + run a command
704	EOF
705	            return 0 ;;
706	        -p|--path)
707	            echo "hroot: --path is not accepted (root is derived from git). Use hhere -p DIR." >&2
708	            return 1 ;;
709	    esac
710	    local root
711	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
712	    herdr-here -p "$root" "$@"
713	}
714
715	# ── Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ───────────────────────────────────
716	# hmark/hunmark toggle a per-pane "I still need to review this" flag via herdr's
717	# `review` metadata token — ORTHOGONAL to agent state, so peeking into a done pane
718	# (which flips it to idle) does NOT clear the flag. The mark logic lives in
719	# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh (dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh);
720	# these are thin CLI wrappers defaulting the pane to the ambient HERDR_PANE_ID.
721	# The prefix+m keybind and the `tv herdr-review` inbox share that same script.
722	_herdr_review_script="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh"
723
724	# hmark [PANE] — flag a pane for later review (default: current pane).
725	function herdr-mark() {
726	    case "${1:-}" in
727	        -h|--help)
728	            cat <<'EOF'
729	hmark — flag a herdr pane as "review-pending" (⭐), analog of tmux bookmark
730
731	Usage: hmark [PANE_ID]
732
733	With no PANE_ID, flags the CURRENT pane (ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID). The flag is a
734	herdr metadata token (`review`), orthogonal to agent state — it survives the pane
735	going idle when you peek in. Clear with `hunmark`, toggle with prefix+m, list
736	flagged panes with `tv herdr-review` (prefix+i inside herdr).
737	EOF
738	            return 0 ;;
739	    esac
740	    local pane="${1:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}"
741	    [ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "hmark: no pane id (not inside herdr?). Pass one: hmark w1:p1" >&2; return 1; }
742	    "$_herdr_review_script" set "$pane"
743	}
744
745	# hunmark [PANE] — clear the review flag (default: current pane).
746	function herdr-unmark() {
747	    case "${1:-}" in
748	        -h|--help)
749	            cat <<'EOF'
750	hunmark — clear a herdr pane's "review-pending" (⭐) flag
751
752	Usage: hunmark [PANE_ID]
753
754	With no PANE_ID, clears the CURRENT pane (ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID).
755	EOF
756	            return 0 ;;
757	    esac
758	    local pane="${1:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}"
759	    [ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "hunmark: no pane id (not inside herdr?). Pass one: hunmark w1:p1" >&2; return 1; }
760	    "$_herdr_review_script" clear "$pane"
761	}
762
763	# ── Aliases ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
764	alias hvibe='herdr-vibe'
765	alias hcode='herdr-code'
766	alias hhere='herdr-here'
767	alias hroot='herdr-root'
768	alias hmark='herdr-mark'
769	alias hunmark='herdr-unmark'
770

```text
1	# herdr CLI dies with `protocol_mismatch` after `brew upgrade herdr` — and Homebrew installs cannot live-handoff
2
3	## Symptoms
4
5	Right after `brew upgrade herdr` on macOS, **every** `herdr` CLI call fails while the
6	UI you are sitting in keeps working perfectly:
7
8	```console
9	$ herdr workspace list
10	{"id":"cli:workspace:list","error":{"code":"protocol_mismatch",
11	 "message":"client protocol 17 is newer than server protocol 16; restart the Herdr server
12	 before using this command. Stop the old server to use the new version.\nStopping exits pane
13	 processes.\nRun `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=/Users/you/.config/herdr/herdr.sock herdr server stop`,
14	 then restart Herdr with the same socket override."}}
15	```
16
17	Note the exit code is **0** — the error is in the JSON body, not the process status, so
18	naive `cmd || fallback` wrappers do not notice.
19
20	```console
21	$ herdr status
22	client:
23	  version: 0.7.5
24	  protocol: 17
25	server:
26	  status: running
27	  version: 0.7.2
28	  protocol: 16
29	  compatible: no
30	update:
31	  restart_needed: yes
32	```
33
34	Downstream, in this repo, that means the following silently stop working (usually as an
35	**empty picker** rather than an error, because the tv channels pipe through `jq` and
36	swallow stderr with `2>/dev/null`):
37
38	- `prefix + T` → `tv herdr-sesh`, `prefix + a` → `tv herdr-agent-panes`, `prefix + i` → `tv herdr-review`
39	- `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`)
40	- every `[[keys.command]]` helper that calls the CLI: `review-mark.sh`, `pane-copy.sh`,
41	  `path-pick.sh`, `url-pick.sh`, `new-tab-at-space-root.sh`
42
43	The herdr TUI itself is unaffected — the running server and its attached client are both
44	still the old binary, talking the old protocol to each other.
45
46	## Root cause
47
48	herdr's client↔server socket API is versioned by an integer `protocol`. A brew upgrade
49	swaps `/usr/local/bin/herdr` (→ `../Cellar/herdr/<new>/bin/herdr`) but **cannot restart the
50	running server** — so the new CLI (protocol 17) refuses to talk to the old server
51	(protocol 16). herdr fails closed here on purpose rather than risk a mismatched wire format.
52
53	The trap is the recovery path, not the diagnosis:
54
55	> **`herdr update --handoff` — the live, pane-preserving upgrade — is disabled on Homebrew,
56	> mise, and Nix installs.** Upstream: *"`herdr update --handoff` only applies to installs
57	> managed by Herdr's own updater. Homebrew, mise, and Nix installs are updated through their
58	> package managers, so `herdr update` is disabled there and cannot perform live handoff."*
59	> ([session-state docs](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/session-state.mdx))
60
61	So on a **Homebrew-installed herdr** there is **no** way to pick up a new herdr version
62	without stopping the server, and stopping the server **kills every pane process** — shells,
63	dev servers, tests, and every running coding agent.
64
65	Self-managed hosts are the opposite case: the GitHub-release binary in `~/.local/bin/herdr`
66	does have `herdr update --handoff`.
67
68	> **Resolved for this repo (2026-07): macOS no longer uses the formula.** Because the
69	> capability gap above is a property of the *install channel*, not the platform, the
70	> `devtools` role now installs the `herdr-macos-{x86_64,aarch64}` release binary into
71	> `~/.local/bin/herdr` on macOS as well, with a one-time `brew uninstall herdr` to migrate
72	> boxes provisioned earlier. Leaving both in place would put two herdr binaries on `PATH`
73	> and let you `protocol_mismatch` against yourself. `just upgrade-herdr` then drives
74	> `herdr update --handoff` on both platforms and *skips with instructions* if it still finds
75	> a package-managed install.
76	>
77	> This page stays because it remains accurate for any unmigrated box, for a herdr installed
78	> by mise/Nix, and for anyone who reinstalls the formula by hand. The recovery options below
79	> are what you have when the handoff is unavailable — see also
80	> [`herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane`](herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md)
81	> for the separate trap that the handoff refuses to run from inside a pane.
82
83	## Fix / workaround
84
85	There is no way to un-stage the upgrade short of `brew install herdr@<old>` (no such
86	formula exists). Pick one:
87
88	**A. Stay on the old server until a natural restart point.** The mismatch is CLI-only. Keep
89	using the TUI (`prefix+g` navigator, splits, tabs all still work — they are server-internal),
90	just avoid the CLI-backed helpers above. Restart at the end of the day.
91
92	**B. Restart deliberately, leaning on herdr's own restore.** Before stopping, know what
93	survives:
94
95	| Layer | Survives `herdr server stop`? |
96	|---|---|
97	| Workspace / tab / pane **topology** + labels | Yes — snapshot in `~/.config/herdr/session.json` |
98	| Pane **screen history** | Yes, if `[session]` history saving is on |
99	| AI-agent **conversations** | Yes, for agents with `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks + `resume_agents_on_restore = true` |
100	| **Running processes** (shells, servers, tests, `just`, builds) | **No — all killed** |
101
102	```bash
103	HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$HOME/.config/herdr/herdr.sock" herdr server stop
104	herdr    # reattach; topology + agent sessions restore
105	```
106
107	**C. Prevent it up front** — pin herdr out of blanket brew upgrades if a long-running
108	session matters more than being current:
109
110	```bash
111	brew pin herdr        # `just upgrade-brew` / `brew upgrade` then skips it
112	brew unpin herdr      # when you're ready to take the restart
113	```
114
115	## Why this is easy to misdiagnose
116
117	- The UI keeps working flawlessly, so nothing *feels* broken — only the side-channel
118	  helpers stop responding, and they mostly fail as empty pickers.
119	- `herdr --version` reports **0.7.5** (the new client binary) even though the server you are
120	  actually sitting inside is still **0.7.2**. Always cross-check with `herdr status`, which
121	  prints client and server separately plus `compatible:` / `restart_needed:`.
122	- The CLI exits **0** on `protocol_mismatch`; only the JSON body carries the failure.
123
124	## See also
125
126	- [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../docs/tools/herdr.md) — install / upgrade / config-overlay model
127	- Upstream session-state + live-handoff doc: <https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/blob/master/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/session-state.mdx>
128
```
</details></tool-use>

16

7	# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
8	# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
9	# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
10	# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
11	#
12	# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
13	#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
14	#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
15	#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
16	#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
17	#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)
18

20	name = "herdr-agent-panes"
21	description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
22	requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

26	display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
27	output = "{split:\t:0}"
28

31	pane='{split:\t:0}'

33	printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
34	printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
35	printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
36	herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
37	  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
38	'''
39
40	[ui]

42

59	'''
60	mode = "fork"

62	[actions.close_pane]

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy distilled facts about a herdr pane to the system clipboard. Five targets:
6	#
7	#   process  the foreground processes running in the pane (cmdline + pid + cwd)
8	#   coord    the pane's coordinate in herdr's Session > Workspace > Tab > Pane
9	#            hierarchy, in a paste-ready form (the ids the herdr CLI accepts, plus
10	#            the socket path that selects a non-default session — there is NO
11	#            --session flag on the pane/tab/workspace subcommands)
12	#   content  the pane's terminal content — visible screen (--source visible) or
13	#            the full retained scrollback (--source recent, the default)
14	#   dir      the WORKSPACE ("space") root directory — what the sidebar row you
15	#            would right-click represents: the cwd of the space's OLDEST tab.
16	#            Derived by space-root.sh (herdr has no workspace-level cwd field);
17	#            read the caveat there about the sidebar label drifting from it.
18	#   cwd      the pane's LIVE working directory — the `abspath`/`pwd` answer,
19	#            which drifts away from `dir` the moment you cd.
20	#
21	# The pane defaults to the CURRENT focused pane (`herdr pane current`); pass a
22	# pane id to target another. herdr's keybind context passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID
23	# and herdr-plus Quick Actions pass $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID — both are wired to call
24	# this, and both fall through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
25	#
26	# Clipboard sink is the repo's own `x copy` (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x), which
27	# auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52. We resolve it by absolute
28	# path fallback because a herdr command-pane / quick-action pane may run us via
29	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
30	#
31	# Usage:
32	#   pane-copy.sh process [PANE_ID]
33	#   pane-copy.sh coord   [PANE_ID]
34	#   pane-copy.sh content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
35	#   pane-copy.sh dir     [PANE_ID|WORKSPACE_ID]
36	#   pane-copy.sh cwd     [PANE_ID]
37	#
38	# Consumers: the prefix+P/L/V/B keybinds (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and
39	# the copy-pane-* quick actions (dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/
40	# cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
41	set -eu
42
43	usage() {
44	    printf 'usage: %s process|coord|content|dir|cwd [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2
45	    exit 64
46	}
47
48	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
49	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
50
51	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
52	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	    X_BIN=x
54	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
55	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
56	else
57	    echo "pane-copy: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
58	    exit 1
59	fi
60
61	action="${1:-}"
62	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
63	shift
64
65	pane=""
66	source="recent"
67	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
68	    case "$1" in
69	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
70	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
71	        -*) usage ;;
72	        *)
73	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
74	                pane="$1"
75	                shift
76	            else
77	                usage
78	            fi
79	            ;;
80	    esac
81	done
82
83	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
84	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
85	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
86	fi
87	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
88
89	copy() { printf '%s' "$1" | "$X_BIN" copy; }
90
91	case "$action" in
92	    process)
93	        info=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
94	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read process info for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
95	        text=$(printf '%s' "$info" | jq -r '
96	            .result.process_info as $p
97	            | "pane \($p.pane_id)  (shell pid \($p.shell_pid))",
98	              ( $p.foreground_processes[]?
99	                | "  \(.cmdline)  [pid \(.pid), cwd \(.cwd)]" )
100	        ')
101	        [ -n "$text" ] || text="pane $pane  (no foreground processes)"
102	        copy "$text"
103	        echo "copied process info for $pane"
104	        ;;
105	    coord)
106	        pj=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
107	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
108	        ws=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // empty')
109	        tb=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.tab_id // empty')
110	        pn=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
111
112	        ws_label=$(herdr workspace get "$ws" 2>/dev/null \
113	            | jq -r '.result.workspace.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
114	        tb_label=$(herdr tab get "$tb" 2>/dev/null \
115	            | jq -r '.result.tab.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
116
117	        sock="${HERDR_SOCKET_PATH:-}"
118	        session=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null \
119	            | jq -r --arg s "$sock" \
120	                'first(.sessions[]? | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name) // empty' \
121	                2>/dev/null || true)
122	        [ -n "$session" ] || session="default"
123
124	        text=$(printf 'session=%s\nworkspace=%s%s\ntab=%s%s\npane=%s\n' \
125	            "$session" \
126	            "$ws" "${ws_label:+ ($ws_label)}" \
127	            "$tb" "${tb_label:+ ($tb_label)}" \
128	            "$pn")
129	        [ -n "$sock" ] && text=$(printf '%s\nsocket=%s' "$text" "$sock")
130	        text=$(printf '%s\n# herdr pane get %s' "$text" "$pn")
131
132	        copy "$text"
133	        echo "copied coordinate for $pane"
134	        ;;
135	    content)
136	        case "$source" in
137	            visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
138	            *) echo "pane-copy: --source must be visible|recent|recent-unwrapped" >&2; exit 64 ;;
139	        esac
140	        body=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
141	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read content of $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
142	        copy "$body"
143	        echo "copied $source content for $pane"
144	        ;;
145	    dir)
146	        # WORKSPACE ("space") root dir — the sidebar row's directory, NOT the
147	        # pane's live cwd. Derivation is shared with prefix+C's new-tab helper
148	        # and the herdr-sesh tv channel; it lives in space-root.sh, which also
149	        # accepts a bare workspace id. Resolved beside this script rather than
150	        # via PATH (a command-pane may run us without the interactive PATH).
151	        here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
152	        root=$("$here/space-root.sh" "$pane") || exit 1
153	        copy "$root"
154	        echo "copied space dir: $root"
155	        ;;
156	    cwd)
157	        # The pane's LIVE cwd — same answer `abspath` would give inside it.
158	        # foreground_cwd tracks the running process; cwd is the shell's start dir.
159	        dir=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
160	            | jq -r '.result.pane | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
161	        [ -n "$dir" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not resolve cwd for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
162	        copy "$dir"
163	        echo "copied pane cwd: $dir"
164	        ;;
165	    *) usage ;;
166	esac
167
```

2	# ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` (joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads a herdr
6	# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
7	# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
8	# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), then opens each choice via
9	# the repo's cross-platform `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open).
10	#
11	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
12	# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. The
13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs
16	# us via `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
20	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (passed by the keybind), else the current
21	# focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope);
22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
23	#
24	# Consumers: the prefix+u keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
25	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a URL from the pane".
26	set -eu
27

13	# fractions (1/2); validating against the pane's live cwd drops nearly all of it.

20	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
21	#
22	# Usage:
23	#   path-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]
24	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, else the current focused pane. --source
25	# defaults to visible; --source recent scans the full scrollback. --cwd is the
26	# directory relative paths are resolved against for the existence check; it

39	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.

45	    echo "path-pick: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
46	    exit 1
47	fi
48
49	pane=""
50	source="visible"
51	cwd=""

55	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;

33	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md:32:> **為什麼套件管理器裝的 herdr 會擱淺自己的 server —— 這就是 macOS 離開 Homebrew 的原因。** herdr 的 socket API 有 protocol 版本號，而套件管理器的升級沒辦法重啟 server —— 所以 `brew upgrade herdr` 之後，每一個 CLI 呼叫（連帶所有 `tv herdr-*` channel、`hvibe`/`hcode`、以及各個 `[[keys.command]]` helper）都會 `protocol_mismatch` 失敗，直到 server 重啟為止，而重啟會殺掉所有 pane 內的行程。`herdr update --handoff`——那個能保住 pane 的 live 路徑——在 **Homebrew/mise/Nix 安裝上是停用的**，所以 brew 裝的 herdr 沒辦法迴避這次重啟。本 repo 現在在 macOS 上也改裝自管的 release binary，正是為了補掉這個缺口；下面那篇 pitfall 仍然保留，因為它描述的是任何**尚未遷移**的機器上會發生的事（而且 `just upgrade-herdr` 偵測到套件管理器安裝時會跳過並印出指示）。要用 `herdr status`（看 `compatible:` / `restart_needed:`）判斷，不要看 `herdr --version`。完整的復原對照表：[`pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md)。

51	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md:184:- **純開 pair（`hhere` / `hroot`）** 補上了「其他每個 herdr 入口都強制要 git repo + 完整 agent layout」的缺口。tmux 的 `tmux new-session` 會直接把你丟進 `$PWD`；herdr 多了一層 Workspace，所以少了這對指令，你得先啟動 herdr、建一個 space（會依 `new_cwd` 開在 `$HOME`）、再手動 `cd`。`hhere` 一步到位：`herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → 在外部就 attach。不需要 git；選用的指令以**原始**方式執行（不做 specstory/on-exit 包裝——那留給 `hcode`/`hvibe`）。flag 見 `hhere -h` / `hroot -h`。**Label 注意事項**：tab 1 裡 `cd` 之後，herdr 會把 workspace 重新命名為 root pane 的*當前* cwd basename（見上方 **cwd & workspace-naming model** 一節），所以冪等聚焦是盡力而為——label 漂移後重跑會開一個新的 workspace。**`-p DIR` 會先在你的 shell 絕對化**（透過 `_herdr_abs_dir`，與 `hcode`/`hvibe` 共用）再交給 herdr，所以 `hhere -p ../sibling` 這類相對路徑可以正常運作，打錯的 DIR 也會直接報錯，而不是靜默開在 `$HOME`——原因見上方 cwd 模型一節的 `--cwd` 那條。
52	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md:187:- **`--session NAME`** 鎖定某個正在跑的 herdr session（見 [具名 session](#named-sessions)）。預設值：在 herdr 內部時用**當前** session（透過繼承的 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`），否則用 **default** session。這個覆寫用 `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 限縮在函式範圍，所以永遠不會外洩到你的 shell。指定一個沒在跑的 `--session` 會報錯，並提示用 `herdr --session NAME` 先啟動（hvibe 不會自己 spawn server）。

157	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:27:> **Why a package-managed herdr strands its own server — the reason macOS left Homebrew.** herdr's socket API is protocol-versioned, and a package-manager upgrade cannot restart the server, so after `brew upgrade herdr` every CLI call (and therefore every `tv herdr-*` channel, `hvibe`/`hcode`, and `[[keys.command]]` helper) fails `protocol_mismatch` until the server restarts — which kills all pane processes. `herdr update --handoff`, the live pane-preserving path, is **disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs**, so a brew-installed herdr has no way to avoid that restart. This repo now installs the self-managed release binary on macOS too, which is what closes the gap; the pitfall below is kept because it still describes what happens on any box that has not been migrated (and `just upgrade-herdr` skips with instructions when it detects a package-managed install). Check with `herdr status` (`compatible:` / `restart_needed:`), not `herdr --version`. Full recovery matrix: [`pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md).
158	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:46:**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
159	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:56:- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).

This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. 169	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:169:Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. ```text
33	## Model differences vs tmux
34
35	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
36
37	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
38
39	### Named sessions
40
41	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
44	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
45
46	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
47
48	## cwd & workspace-naming model
49
50	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
51
52	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
54	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
55	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
56	- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
57
58	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
59
60	| value | meaning |
61	|---|---|
62	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
63	| `home` | `$HOME` |
64	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
65	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
66
67	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
68
69	```toml
70	[[keys.command]]
71	key = "prefix+C"
72	type = "pane"
73	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
74	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
75	```
76
77	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
78
79	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
82	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
83	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
84	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
85	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux). Panel ordered as an **attention queue**, not grouped by space: `ui.agent_panel_sort = "priority"` (herdr's default is `"spaces"`) |
86	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
87	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
88	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
89	| URL picker (`prefix+u`, tmux-fzf-url) | **Custom command pane + helper** | `prefix+u` → `url-pick.sh` (fzf → `x open`); `--source recent` scans scrollback |
90	| File-path picker (`prefix+p`; extrakto `prefix+Tab` on tmux) | **Custom command pane + helper** | `prefix+p` → `path-pick.sh` — two-tier (exists-under-cwd first) → `x copy` |
91	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
92	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
93	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | Partial — `report-metadata --token` (per-pane metadata tokens, orthogonal to agent state) | **Review-pending flag** (`hmark`/`prefix+m` + `tv herdr-review` inbox); decorative status-bar glyphs still a gap (no format-string interpolation) |
94	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
95

```text
257	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
258
259	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
260
261	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
262	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
263
264	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
265
266	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
267
268	```bash
269	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
270	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
271	```
272
273	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
274
275	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
276	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
277	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
278
279	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
280
281	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
282	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
283
284	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
285
286	```bash
287	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
288	```
289
290	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
291
292	## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
293
294	The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
295
296	Three ways to resolve it, in order of preference here:
297
298	1. **Double-prefix passthrough (recommended, zero config).** tmux keeps its default `bind -T prefix C-b send-prefix` (confirmed present in this repo — not overridden), so **`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b`** forwards a literal `Ctrl+b` to the inner herdr; its prefix bindings then work normally (`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b c` = inner new tab). No herdr or tmux change needed — classic tmux-in-tmux muscle memory.
299	2. **Rebind the inner herdr prefix.** Set `keys.prefix` (e.g. `"ctrl+a"` / `"ctrl+space"`) so the inner herdr uses a non-colliding prefix — one keystroke instead of the double-tap. Cost: it changes herdr's prefix even when run standalone (no longer matching tmux's `Ctrl+b`).
300	3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
301
302	Notes: this repo's tmux uses many root-table `bind -n C-*` bindings that **shadow** inner-app `Ctrl` keys, so herdr's prefix-free *direct* terminal shortcuts aren't reliable under tmux — reach herdr actions through its prefix (via 1 or 2). herdr's own `allow_nested` (config, default `false`) governs herdr-inside-**herdr** only (detected via `HERDR_ENV`), not herdr-inside-tmux.
303

360	## Copy pane + space facts to the clipboard {#copy-to-clipboard}
361
362	Six one-keypress "grab this onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). It distills a herdr CLI call into human-readable text and pipes it to the repo's own [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md) (auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52; `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH). The pane defaults to the **current focused pane** (`herdr pane current`); the keybinds pass `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, the Quick Actions pass `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, and either falls through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
363
364	| Op | Key | Quick Action | What lands on the clipboard |
365	|---|---|---|---|
366	| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | foreground processes — `cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd` (from `herdr pane process-info`) |
367	| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
368	| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
369	| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |
370	| `dir` | `prefix+d` | *Copy space: dir* | the **workspace ("space") root directory** — see below |
371	| `cwd` | `prefix+ctrl+d` | *Copy pane: cwd* | the focused pane's **live** working directory (what `pwd` / [`abspath`](../shells/aliases.md) returns) |
372
373	The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
374
375	Both surfaces share the same helper: the `[[keys.command]]` binds in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and the `copy-*.toml` **Quick Actions** under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (fuzzy-launched via `prefix+y`). `P/D/V/S` are uppercase (`prefix+shift+<letter>`) chosen to dodge herdr's reserved `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane) and this repo's `shift+B` (new_worktree) / `shift+R` (reload); lowercase `d` was the only free mnemonic letter left for the dir ops, with `ctrl+d` keeping the pair adjacent. Confirm no collision with `herdr server reload-config` (empty `diagnostics`).
376
377	### `dir` vs `cwd`, and why the right-click menu can't do this {#space-dir}
378
379	`dir` is the answer to *"what directory is this space about?"* — the thing you'd want from a right-click **Copy dir** on a sidebar workspace row. Three ways to reach it:
380
381	| Surface | How | Scope |
382	|---|---|---|
383	| `prefix+d` | keybind | the **focused** workspace |
384	| `prefix+y` → *Copy space: dir* | herdr-plus Quick Action | the **focused** workspace |
385	| `prefix+T` → **`Alt+Y`** | [`herdr-sesh`](#television-integration) tv channel | **any** workspace in the list — strictly more than right-click could give |
386
387	**herdr's context menus cannot be extended.** They are a fixed enum compiled into the binary — the whole inventory is one packed string blob (`Rename` · `Close` · `New worktree` · `Open worktree...` · `Close group` · `Expand` · `Delete worktree checkout...` for spaces; `New tab` · `Rename pane` · `Split right` · `Split down` · `Close pane` · `Swap with focused pane` · `Clear pane name` for panes). Verified on 0.7.5 from three directions: `config.toml` has no menu table (only `[[keys.command]]` and `ui.right_click_passthrough_modifier`, which governs whether right-click reaches the *inner app*); the plugin manifest's `[[actions]]` carries `contexts = ["workspace"]` that **looks** like menu placement but is inert; and `herdr api schema --json` contains no occurrence of "menu" at all, so nothing can inject one at runtime either.
388
389	> **Upstream status (re-check on herdr upgrades).** Requested four times — [#1511](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1511) (user-defined menu entries), [#1671](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1671), [#1776](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1776), [#1830](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1830) — **all closed `NOT_PLANNED`**, three of them auto-closed by `kangal-bot` for being feature requests on a bug-only tracker. #1776 is where a maintainer-facing report states plainly that `contexts` *"currently only surfaces in the `plugin action list` API response."* The redirected discussions ([#1609](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1609), [#1672](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1672), [#1722](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1722)) are all still open and unanswered.
390
391	**How the space dir is derived — and its one caveat.** herdr exposes **no workspace-level cwd anywhere**: `herdr workspace get` and `herdr api snapshot` both return the same `label` / `number` / `tab_count` / `pane_count` object. So it is computed, by [`~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_space-root.sh) — the SSOT shared by `pane-copy.sh dir`, the `prefix+C` new-tab helper, and the tv channel's preview + `Alt+Y`:
392
393	- **Space root = the cwd of the workspace's *oldest surviving* tab.** `.number` on a tab is a monotonic **creation counter**, not the display index — a space can hold tabs numbered `10/13/14/15` shown as `1/2/3/4` — so `sort_by(.number)[0]` means "oldest", which is the right notion of "the tab this space started as".
394	- **Caveat: the sidebar label is pinned at creation and never re-derived**, so once you `cd` inside that oldest tab the label and the derived dir drift apart, and nothing in the API can recover the original path. Observed live: a space labelled `2026-05-14-grafana-provisioning-with-docker-otel-lgtm` whose oldest tab sits in `…/grafana/dashboards/Jingle.AI`. `dir` reports the latter — the true current directory, not the stale name.
395
396	`cwd` exists because the two genuinely diverge in normal use: a space rooted at `2026-07-24-unify-ashare-sdk` was observed with panes sitting in three unrelated `Documents/Program/*` trees. `dir` is the project; `cwd` is where *this pane* actually is.
