398	## Open a URL from the pane (`prefix+u`)
399
400	The herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` ([`joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`](https://github.com/joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url)). `prefix+u` opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the focused pane; pick one (or several — fzf multi-select) and each opens in the browser. Lowercase `u` is deliberately paired with uppercase `U` (`tv tools`), matching the tmux muscle memory.
401
402	One helper drives it: `~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh). It reads the pane (`herdr pane read`), runs the **same extraction/rewrite passes as tmux-fzf-url**, and opens each choice with the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md) (wslview / open / xdg-open). It mirrors `pane-copy.sh` exactly: pane defaults to `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` (the keybind var) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, and `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH.
403
404	| Aspect | Behavior |
405	|---|---|
406	| Scope | **Visible screen by default** (matches tmux-fzf-url). `url-pick.sh <pane> --source recent` scans the full retained scrollback |
407	| Patterns | `http(s)` / `ftp` / `file`, bare `www.` → `http://`, `IPv4[:port]` → `http://`, `git@…` SSH remotes → `https://…`, quoted `"owner/repo"` → `github.com/owner/repo`, `import "pkg"` → `npmjs.com/package/pkg` |
408	| Open | `x open <url>` per selection; multi-select opens all |
409	| No URLs | prints `no URLs found` and pauses ~1.5 s (a command pane closes the instant the script exits — tmux uses the status line instead) |
410
411	Bound via a `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) — no tv channel needed (fzf is the faithful port). Copy-mode URL opening (tmux's `tmux-open` `o`) has no herdr equivalent; use `prefix+u` for the picker.
412
413	## Copy a file path from the pane (`prefix+p`)
414
415	The copy-path sibling of the URL picker. `prefix+p` opens an fzf popup of the file paths in the focused pane; pick one (or several) and the path is copied to the clipboard. Lowercase `p` ("copy **p**ath") sits under the uppercase copy family (`prefix+P/D/V/S`), the same `u`/`U` convention. On tmux the analog is the **extrakto** plugin (`prefix + Tab`) — see [tmux keybindings](tmux/keybindings.md).
416
417	Helper: `~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh), a direct sibling of `url-pick.sh`/`pane-copy.sh` (same pane + `x`-resolution + `herdr pane read` plumbing), copying via [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md).
418
419	**The noise problem, and how it's handled.** Unlike URLs (which self-identify with `scheme://`), file paths have no marker, so a regex alone matches dates (`2024/01/02`), rates (`10k/s`) and fractions (`1/2`). Two defenses:
420
421	| Defense | Behavior |
422	|---|---|
423	| Extraction | extrakto's path heuristics — slash-bearing tokens (`/…`, `~/…`, `./`, `a/b/c`) + bare `file.ext`; trailing `",):` stripped; rate/fraction tokens excluded outright |
424	| Existence check (the noise-killer) | Each candidate is resolved against the pane cwd (`$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`, else `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd`, else process-info cwd) and `test -e`'d |
425	| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |
426
427	`path:line:col` suffixes (grep `-n` / stack traces / compiler output) are stripped before the existence test, so `pkg.py:42:5` validates as `pkg.py`. Scope is the visible screen by default (`--source recent` for scrollback); multi-select copies newline-joined; an empty result prints `no file paths found` and pauses ~1.5 s.

83	## Fix / workaround
84
85	There is no way to un-stage the upgrade short of `brew install herdr@<old>` (no such
86	formula exists). Pick one:
87
88	**A. Stay on the old server until a natural restart point.** The mismatch is CLI-only. Keep
89	using the TUI (`prefix+g` navigator, splits, tabs all still work — they are server-internal),
90	just avoid the CLI-backed helpers above. Restart at the end of the day.
91
92	**B. Restart deliberately, leaning on herdr's own restore.** Before stopping, know what
93	survives:
94
95	| Layer | Survives `herdr server stop`? |
96	|---|---|
97	| Workspace / tab / pane **topology** + labels | Yes — snapshot in `~/.config/herdr/session.json` |
98	| Pane **screen history** | Yes, if `[session]` history saving is on |
99	| AI-agent **conversations** | Yes, for agents with `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks + `resume_agents_on_restore = true` |
100	| **Running processes** (shells, servers, tests, `just`, builds) | **No — all killed** |
101
102	```bash
103	HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$HOME/.config/herdr/herdr.sock" herdr server stop
104	herdr    # reattach; topology + agent sessions restore
105	```
```

3	Find — and jump to — coding-agent sessions (`claude`, `cursor-agent`, `codex`,

6	The pain this solves: you start `claude` in pane A on session `chezmoi`, hop

8	session for a Codex task, and three windows later you can't remember which

17	| `tv agent-panes` | All four agents (Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor) | "Where am I running stuff?" cross-agent overview, jump-to-pane |
18	| `tv agent-wakeup` | Same live panes, plus pueue wakeup tasks | "Which agent is quota-blocked, when should I send `continue`?" |
19	| `recon` (optional) | Claude-only, with live status (Working / Idle / Waiting) parsed from pane capture | "Which Claude needs my attention?" — recon's live status detection is richer than what we replicate in tv |

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` (joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads a herdr
6	# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
7	# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
8	# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), then opens each choice via
9	# the repo's cross-platform `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open).
10	#
11	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
12	# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. The
13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs
16	# us via `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
20	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (passed by the keybind), else the current
21	# focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope);
22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
23	#
24	# Consumers: the prefix+u keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
25	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a URL from the pane".
26	set -eu
27
28	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
29
30	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
31	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
32
33	# Resolve the opener (`x open`) even without the interactive PATH.
34	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
35	    X_BIN=x
36	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
37	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
38	else
39	    echo "url-pick: opener 'x' not found" >&2
40	    exit 1
41	fi
42
43	pane=""
44	source="visible"
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
49	        -h|--help) usage ;;
50	        -*) usage ;;
51	        *)
52	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
53	                pane="$1"
54	                shift
55	            else
56	                usage
57	            fi
58	            ;;
59	    esac
60	done
61
62	case "$source" in
63	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
64	    *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
65	esac
66
67	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
68	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
70	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
71	fi
72	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
73
74	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
75	    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
76
77	# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, POSIX-ized
78	# (plain vars instead of bash arrays; trailing `|| true` so a no-match grep,
79	# which exits 1, does not trip `set -e`).
80	urls=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]' || true)
81	wwws=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
82	ips=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
83	gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
84	gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
85	npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)
86
87	items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
88
89	if [ -z "$items" ]; then
90	    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
91	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
92	    exit 0
93	fi
94
95	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
96	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
97	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
98
99	printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
100	    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
101	done
102

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy-a-file-path picker — the copy-path sibling of url-pick.sh (which OPENS
6	# URLs). Reads the focused pane, extracts path-like tokens (borrowing extrakto's
7	# path heuristics), and presents a TWO-TIER fzf list: paths that EXIST relative to
8	# the pane cwd on top (copied as their resolved ABSOLUTE path), unverified
9	# candidates (as-seen) below a separator. The choice is copied via `x copy`.
10	#
11	# The existence check is the noise-killer extrakto lacks: file paths have no
12	# scheme:// marker, so regex alone matches dates (2024/01/02), rates (10k/s) and
13	# fractions (1/2); validating against the pane's live cwd drops nearly all of it.
14	#
15	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
16	# script exits), bound to prefix+p in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. Mirrors
17	# the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the keybind var) with a
18	# `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read` for the text, `x copy` for the
19	# clipboard, and an absolute-path `x` fallback because a command pane runs us via
20	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
21	#
22	# Usage:
23	#   path-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]
24	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, else the current focused pane. --source
25	# defaults to visible; --source recent scans the full scrollback. --cwd is the
26	# directory relative paths are resolved against for the existence check; it
27	# defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd →
28	# process-info cwd → $PWD.
29	#
30	# Consumers: the prefix+p keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
31	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Copy a file path from the pane".
32	set -eu
33
34	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
35
36	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
37	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
38
39	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
40	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41	    X_BIN=x
42	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
43	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
44	else
45	    echo "path-pick: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
46	    exit 1
47	fi
48
49	pane=""
50	source="visible"
51	cwd=""
52	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
53	    case "$1" in
54	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
55	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
56	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
57	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
58	        -h|--help) usage ;;
59	        -*) usage ;;
60	        *)
61	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
62	                pane="$1"
63	                shift
64	            else
65	                usage
66	            fi
67	            ;;
68	    esac
69	done
70
71	case "$source" in
72	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
73	    *) echo "path-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
74	esac
75
76	# Resolve pane (keybind passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID; fall back to current).
77	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
78	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
79	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
80	fi
81	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "path-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
82
83	# Resolve cwd for existence checks: --cwd → pane.foreground_cwd → process cwd → $PWD.
84	if [ -z "$cwd" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
85	    cwd=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
86	    [ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
87	        | jq -r '.result.process_info.foreground_processes[0].cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
88	fi
89	[ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd="$PWD"
90
91	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
92	    || { echo "path-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
93
94	# Path candidates (extrakto path heuristics, POSIX-ized): slash-bearing tokens
95	# (abs /…, home ~/…, rel ./ ../ a/b/c) + bare filename.ext. rstrip trailing
96	# ",):; then drop rate/fraction noise (extrakto's exclude: 10k/s, 1/2). dedupe.
97	cands=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" \
98	    | grep -oE '(~|\.\.?)?/?[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+)+|[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8}' \
99	    | sed -E 's/[",):;]+$//' \
100	    | grep -vE '^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$|[kKmMgG]/s$' \
101	    | grep -v '^$' | awk '!seen[$0]++' || true)
102
103	if [ -z "$cands" ]; then
104	    printf 'path-pick: no file paths found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
105	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
106	    exit 0
107	fi
108
109	# Two tiers: exists-under-cwd (resolved absolute) vs the rest (as-seen).
110	exist=""
111	maybe=""
112	OLDIFS=$IFS
113	IFS='
114	'
115	for c in $cands; do
116	    base=$(printf '%s' "$c" | sed -E 's/:[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$//')   # strip :line[:col] for the test
117	    case "$base" in
118	        /*)   abs="$base" ;;
119	        \~/*) abs="$HOME/${base#\~/}" ;;
120	        *)    abs="$cwd/$base" ;;
121	    esac
122	    if [ -e "$abs" ]; then
123	        rp=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$abs")" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s/%s' "$(pwd -P)" "$(basename -- "$abs")") \
124	            || rp="$abs"
125	        exist="$exist$rp
126	"
127	    else
128	        maybe="$maybe$c
129	"
130	    fi
131	done
132	IFS=$OLDIFS
133
134	exist=$(printf '%s' "$exist" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
135	maybe=$(printf '%s' "$maybe" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
136
137	SEP='────────  unverified (not found under cwd)  ────────'
138	list=$(
139	    [ -n "$exist" ] && printf '%s\n' "$exist"
140	    [ -n "$maybe" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$SEP"; printf '%s\n' "$maybe"; }
141	)
142
143	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
144	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$list" | fzf --multi --no-sort --height=100% --border \
145	    --prompt='path> ' --header="Enter=copy · Tab=multi · cwd=$cwd") || exit 0
146
147	# Drop the separator if it slipped into the selection; copy the rest.
148	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | grep -vFx "$SEP" | grep -v '^$' || true)
149	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
150
151	printf '%s' "$chosen" | "$X_BIN" copy
152	echo "copied $(printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | grep -c .) path(s)"
153
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant
2	#
3	# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists
4	# panes from the running herdr server and lets you jump to the one running an
5	# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).
6	#
7	# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
8	# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
9	# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
10	# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
11	#
12	# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
13	#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
14	#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
15	#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
16	#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
17	#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)
18
19	[metadata]
20	name = "herdr-agent-panes"
21	description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
22	requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]
23
24	[source]
25	command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.agent_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
26	display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
27	output = "{split:\t:0}"
28
29	[preview]
30	command = '''
31	pane='{split:\t:0}'
32	printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  [%s]\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
33	printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
34	printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
35	printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
36	herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
37	  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
38	'''
39
40	[ui]
41	input_header = "Live herdr Agent Panes"
42
43	[ui.preview_panel]
44	size = 60
45
46	[keybindings]
47	enter = "actions:focus"
48	alt-t = "actions:focus"
49	alt-k = "actions:close_pane"
50	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
51	alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"
52
53	[actions.focus]
54	description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab"
55	command = '''
56	ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
57	[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
58	[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
59	'''
60	mode = "fork"
61
62	[actions.close_pane]
63	description = "Close the pane (confirm prompt)"
64	command = '''
65	p='{split:\t:0}'
66	[ -z "$p" ] && exit 0
67	printf 'Close pane %s? [y/N] ' "$p"
68	read -r ans
69	case "$ans" in
70	  y|Y|yes|YES) herdr pane close "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "closed $p" || echo "failed (already gone?)" ;;
71	  *) echo "aborted" ;;
72	esac
73	echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _
74	'''
75	mode = "execute"
76
77	[actions.copy_id]
78	description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
79	command = '''
80	d='{split:\t:0}'
81	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
82	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
83	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
84	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
85	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
86	fi
87	'''
88	mode = "fork"
89
90	[actions.copy_dir]
91	description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
92	command = '''
93	d='{split:\t:4}'
94	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
95	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
96	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
97	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
98	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
99	fi
100	'''
101	mode = "fork"

98	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
99	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
100	fi

2	#
3	# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
4	# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches

6	# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
7	# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
8	#
9	# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
10	#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
11	#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
12	#
13	# Actions: Enter = open/focus · Ctrl+D = close workspace · Alt+Y = copy its dir
14	#
15	# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.
16
17	[metadata]
18	name = "herdr-sesh"
19	description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
20	requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]

23	command = [
24	  '''herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]? | "ws\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.label)  (\(.pane_count)p, \(.tab_count)t)"' ''',
25	  '''zoxide query -l 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{print "dir",$0,$0}' ''',
26	]
27	display = "{split:\t:2}"
28	output = "{split:\t:1}"
29
30	[preview]
31	command = '''
32	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
33	case "$kind" in
34	  ws)
35	    printf '\033[1mworkspace %s\033[0m\n' "$ref"
36	    # herdr has NO workspace-level cwd field, so the dir is derived (lowest tab's
37	    # pane cwd). Shown here so Alt+Y tells you what it is about to copy, and so
38	    # Enter tells you which project you are focusing.
39	    dir=$(~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh "$ref" 2>/dev/null || true)
40	    [ -n "$dir" ] && printf 'dir: %s\n' "$dir"
41	    printf '\n'
42	    herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq . 2>/dev/null \
43	      || herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null
44	    ;;
45	  dir)
46	    printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
47	    if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then eza -la --git --color=always "$ref" 2>/dev/null
48	    else ls -la "$ref" 2>/dev/null; fi
49	    ;;
50	esac
51	'''
52
53	[ui]
54	input_header = "herdr Workspaces / Dirs"
55
56	[keybindings]

58	ctrl-d = ["actions:close_ws", "reload_source"]
59	alt-y = "actions:copy_dir"
60
61	[actions.open]
62	description = "Focus the workspace, or open a new workspace at the directory"
63	command = '''

65	[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0

72	# `type = "pane"` command pane, which only vanishes when its command exits. With

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_space-root.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Print the WORKSPACE ("space") root directory for a herdr workspace, given
6	# either a workspace id (`wP`) or any pane id inside it (`wP:p29`).
7	#
8	# Why this script exists: **herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd.** `herdr
9	# workspace get` returns label / number / tab_count / pane_count and nothing
10	# else (verified on 0.7.5), so "the directory this space is about" has to be
11	# derived. It is the SSOT for that derivation — three consumers would otherwise
12	# each carry their own copy and silently drift:
13	#
14	#   new-tab-at-space-root.sh   prefix+C  (new tab at the space dir)
15	#   pane-copy.sh dir           prefix+d  / the "Copy space dir" Quick Action
16	#   herdr-sesh tv channel      prefix+T, Alt+Y (copy any workspace's dir)
17	#
18	# "Space root" = the cwd of the workspace's OLDEST surviving tab. Note `.number`
19	# is a monotonic creation counter, NOT the display index (a workspace can hold
20	# tabs numbered 10/13/14/15 displayed as 1/2/3/4), so sort_by(.number)[0] is the
21	# oldest tab, which is the right notion of "the tab this space started as". We
22	# prefer the LIVE cwd (`foreground_cwd`) over the shell's startup cwd.
23	#
24	# CAVEAT — this is a best-effort answer, not an authoritative one. herdr's
25	# sidebar LABEL is pinned when the workspace is created and is never re-derived,
26	# so once you `cd` inside the oldest tab the two drift apart and nothing in the
27	# API can recover the original path. Observed live: a space labelled
28	# `2026-05-14-grafana-provisioning-with-docker-otel-lgtm` whose oldest tab sits
29	# in `…/grafana/dashboards/Jingle.AI`. There is no better source — `workspace
30	# get` and `herdr api snapshot` return the same cwd-less workspace object.
31	#
32	# A pane id is resolved through `herdr pane get` rather than by string-splitting
33	# on the ":" — the id format is hierarchical in practice (`wP` / `wP:t7` /
34	# `wP:pA`) but that is an observation, not a documented guarantee.
35	#
36	# Usage:
37	#   space-root.sh <workspace_id|pane_id>
38	#   space-root.sh                        # defaults to the current pane's space
39	set -eu
40
41	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "space-root: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
42	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "space-root: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
43
44	target="${1:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}"
45
46	# No id anywhere (ran outside herdr's keybind context) → ask for the focused pane.
47	if [ -z "$target" ]; then
48	    target=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
49	fi
50	[ -n "$target" ] || { echo "space-root: no workspace or pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)" >&2; exit 64; }
51
52	case "$target" in
53	    *:*)
54	        wid=$(herdr pane get "$target" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // ""')
55	        [ -n "$wid" ] || { echo "space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $target" >&2; exit 1; }
56	        ;;
57	    *)
58	        wid="$target"
59	        ;;
60	esac
61
62	# Root tab = the workspace's OLDEST tab (lowest creation counter, not display index).
63	root_tab=$(herdr tab list --workspace "$wid" 2>/dev/null \
64	    | jq -r '.result.tabs | sort_by(.number) | .[0].tab_id // ""')
65	[ -n "$root_tab" ] || { echo "space-root: no tabs in workspace $wid" >&2; exit 1; }
66
67	# `herdr tab get` returns tab metadata only (no pane cwd), so read the root tab's
68	# pane cwd from the full pane list. foreground_cwd = where the tab actually is
69	# now; .cwd = the shell's startup dir, used only when there is no live reading.
70	root=$(herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg t "$root_tab" \
71	    '.result.panes | map(select(.tab_id==$t)) | .[0] // {} | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
72	[ -n "$root" ] || { echo "space-root: could not resolve root dir for $root_tab" >&2; exit 1; }
73
74	printf '%s\n' "$root"
75
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy distilled facts about a herdr pane to the system clipboard. Five targets:
6	#
7	#   process  the foreground processes running in the pane (cmdline + pid + cwd)
8	#   coord    the pane's coordinate in herdr's Session > Workspace > Tab > Pane
9	#            hierarchy, in a paste-ready form (the ids the herdr CLI accepts, plus
10	#            the socket path that selects a non-default session — there is NO
11	#            --session flag on the pane/tab/workspace subcommands)
12	#   content  the pane's terminal content — visible screen (--source visible) or
13	#            the full retained scrollback (--source recent, the default)
14	#   dir      the WORKSPACE ("space") root directory — what the sidebar row you
15	#            would right-click represents: the cwd of the space's OLDEST tab.
16	#            Derived by space-root.sh (herdr has no workspace-level cwd field);
17	#            read the caveat there about the sidebar label drifting from it.
18	#   cwd      the pane's LIVE working directory — the `abspath`/`pwd` answer,
19	#            which drifts away from `dir` the moment you cd.
20	#
21	# The pane defaults to the CURRENT focused pane (`herdr pane current`); pass a
22	# pane id to target another. herdr's keybind context passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID
23	# and herdr-plus Quick Actions pass $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID — both are wired to call
24	# this, and both fall through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
25	#
26	# Clipboard sink is the repo's own `x copy` (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x), which
27	# auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52. We resolve it by absolute
28	# path fallback because a herdr command-pane / quick-action pane may run us via
29	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
30	#
31	# Usage:
32	#   pane-copy.sh process [PANE_ID]
33	#   pane-copy.sh coord   [PANE_ID]
34	#   pane-copy.sh content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
35	#   pane-copy.sh dir     [PANE_ID|WORKSPACE_ID]
36	#   pane-copy.sh cwd     [PANE_ID]
37	#
38	# Consumers: the prefix+P/L/V/B keybinds (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and
39	# the copy-pane-* quick actions (dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/
40	# cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
41	set -eu
42
43	usage() {
44	    printf 'usage: %s process|coord|content|dir|cwd [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2
45	    exit 64
46	}
47
48	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
49	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
50
51	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
52	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	    X_BIN=x
54	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
55	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
56	else
57	    echo "pane-copy: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
58	    exit 1
59	fi
60
61	action="${1:-}"
62	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
63	shift
64
65	pane=""
66	source="recent"
67	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
68	    case "$1" in
69	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
70	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
71	        -*) usage ;;
72	        *)
73	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
74	                pane="$1"
75	                shift
76	            else
77	                usage
78	            fi
79	            ;;
80	    esac
81	done
82
83	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
84	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
85	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
86	fi
87	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
88
89	copy() { printf '%s' "$1" | "$X_BIN" copy; }
90
91	case "$action" in
92	    process)
93	        info=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
94	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read process info for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
95	        text=$(printf '%s' "$info" | jq -r '
96	            .result.process_info as $p
97	            | "pane \($p.pane_id)  (shell pid \($p.shell_pid))",
98	              ( $p.foreground_processes[]?
99	                | "  \(.cmdline)  [pid \(.pid), cwd \(.cwd)]" )
100	        ')
101	        [ -n "$text" ] || text="pane $pane  (no foreground processes)"
102	        copy "$text"
103	        echo "copied process info for $pane"
104	        ;;
105	    coord)
106	        pj=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null) \
107	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
108	        ws=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // empty')
109	        tb=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.tab_id // empty')
110	        pn=$(printf '%s' "$pj" | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
111
112	        ws_label=$(herdr workspace get "$ws" 2>/dev/null \
113	            | jq -r '.result.workspace.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
114	        tb_label=$(herdr tab get "$tb" 2>/dev/null \
115	            | jq -r '.result.tab.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
116
117	        sock="${HERDR_SOCKET_PATH:-}"
118	        session=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null \
119	            | jq -r --arg s "$sock" \
120	                'first(.sessions[]? | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name) // empty' \
121	                2>/dev/null || true)

123
124	        text=$(printf 'session=%s\nworkspace=%s%s\ntab=%s%s\npane=%s\n' \
125	            "$session" \
126	            "$ws" "${ws_label:+ ($ws_label)}" \
127	            "$tb" "${tb_label:+ ($tb_label)}" \
128	            "$pn")

130	        text=$(printf '%s\n# herdr pane get %s' "$text" "$pn")
131
132	        copy "$text"

134	        ;;
135	    content)
136	        case "$source" in
137	            visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
138	            *) echo "pane-copy: --source must be visible|recent|recent-unwrapped" >&2; exit 64 ;;
139	        esac
140	        body=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
141	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read content of $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
142	        copy "$body"
143	        echo "copied $source content for $pane"
144	        ;;
145	    dir)
146	        # WORKSPACE ("space") root dir — the sidebar row's directory, NOT the
147	        # pane's live cwd. Derivation is shared with prefix+C's new-tab helper

151	        here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)

159	        dir=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
160	            | jq -r '.result.pane | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
161	        [ -n "$dir" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not resolve cwd for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
162	        copy "$dir"
163	        echo "copied pane cwd: $dir"
164	        ;;
165	    *) usage ;;
166	esac

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
6	# herdr's per-pane metadata TOKENS (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source review
7	# --token review=…`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
8	# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
9	# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
10	# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
11	#
12	# Why a metadata token and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
13	# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. A pane can
14	# carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking
15	# into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
16	# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
17	#
18	# herdr >= 0.7.4 ONLY. herdr 0.7.4 removed `--custom-status` / the flat
19	# `custom_status` field in favour of this namespaced token map (up to 32 tokens
20	# per pane, names matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$). The removal is NOT listed as a
21	# breaking change upstream — on an older herdr this script dies with
22	# `unknown --custom-status`. See pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md.
23	#
24	# Unlike `custom_status`, a token is NOT rendered by the sidebar automatically —
25	# it only shows where a row layout references it. `$review` is wired into
26	# `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml; drop the
27	# token name here and you must drop it there too.
28	#
29	# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
30	# surfaces `tokens`, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) lets the
31	# `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No sidecar file.
32	#
33	# Usage:
34	#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
35	#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
36	#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
37	#
38	# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
39	# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
40	# focus_clear action. Keep TOKEN in sync with the `.tokens.<name>` lookups in
41	# that channel (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml) and with the
42	# `$review` token in the sidebar row layout.
43	set -eu
44
45	SOURCE_ID='review'
46	TOKEN='review'                 # metadata token name; the tv channel keys off its PRESENCE
47	DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'
48
49	usage() {
50	    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
51	    exit 64
52	}
53
54	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
55
56	action="${1:-}"
57	pane="${2:-}"
58	status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"
59
60	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
61	[ -n "$pane" ] || usage
62
63	_set() {
64	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --token "$TOKEN=$status" >/dev/null
65	    echo "review flag set on $pane"
66	}
67
68	_clear() {
69	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --clear-token "$TOKEN" >/dev/null
70	    echo "review flag cleared on $pane"
71	}
72
73	case "$action" in
74	    set)   _set ;;
75	    clear) _clear ;;
76	    toggle)
77	        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
78	        # Presence of the token IS the flag — a cleared token is absent from the
79	        # map, so no substring match is needed (unlike the pre-0.7.4 single
80	        # `custom_status` string that every source shared).
81	        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
82	            | jq -r --arg t "$TOKEN" '.result.pane.tokens[$t] // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
83	        case "$current" in
84	            '') _set ;;
85	            *)  _clear ;;
86	        esac ;;
87	    *) usage ;;
88	esac
89
```
</details></tool-use>

2-     2	title: Socket API
3-     3	description: Control a running Herdr server from scripts, tools, and coding agents.
4-     4	---
5-     5
6:     6	Herdr exposes a local socket API for scripts and agents that need to inspect or control a running session.
7-     7
8:     8	Most automation should start with the CLI wrappers. Use the raw socket API only when you need direct request/response control or long-lived event subscriptions.
9-     9
10-    10	## Choose an integration layer
11-    11
12-    12	| Layer | Use it for |
13-    13	| --- | --- |
14-    14	| Agent skill | Teaching a coding agent how to use Herdr from inside a pane. |
15:    15	| CLI wrappers | Shell scripts, simple orchestration, and human debugging. |
16:    16	| Raw socket API | Custom tools, protocol clients, and event subscribers. |
17-    17
18-    18	The layers share the same control surface.
19-    19
20-    20	## Schema
21-    21

23-    23	binary:
24-    24

26-    26	herdr api schema
--
29-    29	```
30-    30

32-    32	Schema document for tools, and `--output PATH` writes that document to a file.
33:    33	The schema covers raw requests, success responses, error responses, emitted
34-    34	events, and subscription events.

43:    43	- list, inspect, read, prompt, wait on, rename, focus, start, and attach agents through CLI helpers
44-    44	- report custom agent state from hooks and plugins

46-    46	- install and uninstall built-in integrations
47-    47	- stop the server and reload config

It pins the resolved pane occupant so a replacement cannot satisfy the wait. `agent.prompt` accepts an optional `wait` object with `until` and `timeout_ms`; this submits the prompt and starts the wait in one request, avoiding a race between separate calls.

1-     1	---
2:     2	title: Persistence and remote access
3:     3	description: Detach from Herdr, reattach later, use named sessions, and connect over SSH.
4-     4	---
5-     5
6-     6	Herdr keeps panes running in a background server. Your terminal client can detach and reconnect later.
7-     7
8:     8	For the local, SSH, and `herdr --remote` workflows, see [How to work with Herdr](/docs/how-to-work/).
9-     9
10-    10	## Detach and reattach
11-    11
12:    12	Detach the client with `ctrl+b q`; panes and agents keep running. Reattach by running `herdr` again. Stop the session and its panes with `herdr server stop`.
13-    13
14:    14	When Herdr starts again after a full server stop, it restores the saved session shape. For what survives detach, server restart, screen history replay, native agent session restore, and live handoff, see [Session state and restore](/docs/session-state/).
15-    15
16:    16	## Named sessions
17-    17
18:    18	Use named sessions when you want independent Herdr servers.
19-    19
20-    20	```bash
21:    21	herdr session list
22:    22	herdr session attach work
23:    23	herdr session attach side-project
24:    24	herdr session stop work
25:    25	herdr session delete side-project
26-    26	```
27-    27
28:    28	A named session has its own panes, tabs, workspaces, sockets, and runtime state. It still shares the same global config file.
29-    29
30-    30	Use `--json` for scripts:
31-    31
32-    32	```bash
33:    33	herdr session list --json
34:    34	herdr session stop work --json
35:    35	herdr session delete side-project --json
36-    36	```
37-    37
38:    38	## Remote attach over SSH
39-    39
40:    40	There are two remote modes; [How to work with Herdr](/docs/how-to-work/) compares them. SSH to the server and run `herdr` there for the tmux-style path. Or attach through SSH from your local machine:
41-    41
42-    42	```bash
43:    43	herdr --remote workbox
44:    44	herdr --remote ssh://you@server:2222
45-    45	```
46-    46
47:    47	In this mode your local Herdr is a thin client. It connects over SSH, starts or attaches to the remote Herdr server, and streams the UI back to your local terminal. Because the client runs locally, Herdr can bridge local desktop features such as image clipboard paste into the remote session by copying the image to a remote temp file and pasting that path.
48-    48
49:    49	By default, `herdr --remote` uses your local Herdr keybindings for that attach. This keeps local muscle memory even when the remote server has different config. The local keybindings are a snapshot from attach time; detach and reattach after editing local keybindings. Use `--remote-keybindings server` when you want the remote server config instead. Local custom command keybindings are not sent, because those commands would run on the remote host.
50-    50
51:    51	For repeat targets, use your SSH config:
52-    52
53-    53	```text
54-    54	Host workbox
55-    55	  HostName server.example.com
56-    56	  User you
--
58-    58	```
59-    59
60-    60	Then attach with:
61-    61
62-    62	```bash
63:    63	herdr --remote workbox
64-    64	```
65-    65
66:    66	Remote attach supports Linux and macOS hosts on x86_64 and aarch64. Herdr checks the remote platform, prefers a matching `herdr` already on the remote `PATH`, then checks common direct, Homebrew, mise, and Nix profile install paths. If no matching binary exists, interactive runs prompt to install one to `~/.local/bin/herdr`; non-interactive runs fail instead of modifying the host. If `~/.local/bin` is not on the remote `PATH`, Herdr warns after install.
67-    67
68:    68	Native Windows `herdr --remote` is not part of the Windows beta. From Windows, SSH into the server and run `herdr` there.
69-    69
70:    70	By default, `herdr --remote` runs remote setup and the bridge through a temporary SSH config that includes your SSH config first, then adds fallback keepalive settings and a private per-attach control socket for connection reuse. Existing user keepalive settings win. Set `[remote].manage_ssh_config = false` to use plain `ssh` without Herdr's generated config or control socket.
71-    71
72:    72	Remote attach uses your normal OpenSSH authentication. If the target uses a passphrase-protected key in a non-interactive shell, script, CI job, or mobile terminal that cannot show the passphrase prompt, load the key into ssh-agent first:
73-    73
74-    74	```bash
75-    75	ssh-add
76:    76	herdr --remote workbox
77-    77	```
78-    78
79:    79	For any remote authentication failure, verify plain SSH access first with `ssh workbox`, then run `herdr --remote workbox` again.
80-    80
81:    81	By default, remote attach uses the normal restart/stop flow if it needs to replace or restart a running remote server. To opt into experimental live handoff for a supported running remote server, pass `--handoff`:
82-    82
83-    83	```bash

85-    85	```
86-    86
87:    87	If you SSH into the server first and run `herdr` there, Herdr runs entirely on the server. That mode is useful and simple, but it cannot access your local desktop clipboard beyond normal terminal text paste.
88-    88
89:    89	When your local and remote platforms match, Herdr can copy the current local binary for direct installs. For Homebrew, mise, and Nix installs, or when the platforms differ, it downloads the matching release asset for the current client version from `https://herdr.dev/latest.json`.
90-    90
91:    91	For local builds or custom binaries, set `HERDR_REMOTE_BINARY` to a local file path before running remote attach.
92-    92
93-    93	```bash

95-    95	```

106-   106

98:Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
100:> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
124:| `` prefix + u `` | **URL picker** — fzf-pick a URL from the pane and open it (`x open`); tmux-fzf-url analog. `--source recent` = full scrollback | command pane |
127:| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
128:| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
129:| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
133:| `prefix + S` | copy focused pane's **content** (full scrollback) | command pane |
182:- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
199:`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
211:- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`. `Ctrl+D` closes the selected workspace; **`Alt+Y` copies its directory** (works on workspace *and* zoxide-dir rows — see [`dir` vs `cwd`](#space-dir)). The preview shows that derived dir above the raw `workspace get` JSON, so you can see what `Alt+Y` will hand you.
213:- `herdr-review` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml`) — the **review-pending inbox**: lists only panes carrying the ⭐ flag (a non-empty `tokens.review`). Enter focuses the pane's workspace/tab and **keeps** the flag; `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read"). Bound to `prefix+i`. See the **Review-pending flag** section below.
217:> **`mode = "execute"`, not `"fork"`, for the Enter action of a channel bound to a command pane.** A `type = "pane"` binding only vanishes when its command exits, and tv exits after an `execute` action but stays alive after a `fork` one — so a `fork` Enter leaves the picker pane hovering over the workspace you just focused. `herdr-sesh`'s `[actions.open]` is `execute` for exactly this reason; its `ctrl-d` (`close_ws`) keeps `fork` because it pairs with `reload_source` and tv must survive to redraw the list. Same trade-off applies to `herdr-agent-panes` / `herdr-review`, which are still `fork` (their Enter re-focuses without leaving the picker — deliberate for triage, change it if you want one-shot jumps).
251:- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
261:- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
264:## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
266:herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
269:herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
270:herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
273:What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
275:- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
276:- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
277:- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
279:**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
281:- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
282:- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
284:**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
290:If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
292:## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
294:The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
300:3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
306:The tmux setup has a per-window bookmark (`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`, rendered via `#{?@bookmark_status,…}`). herdr has **no `#{@option}` status-bar interpolation**, so that exact mechanism doesn't port — but the *use case* that actually matters here does: **"the agent finished (`done`) but I haven't reviewed it yet."** herdr collapses a `done` pane to `idle` the moment you peek in, losing the only signal that it still needs attention.
311:herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --token review="⭐ REVIEW"   # set (persistent — no --ttl-ms)
312:herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --clear-token review         # clear
315:Verified: a pane can carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `tokens` map and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth. Presence of the token *is* the flag, so the glyph text is free-form.
317:> **herdr ≥ 0.7.4 only, and the token needs a row layout to be visible.** 0.7.4 replaced `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field with this namespaced token map — a silent removal, not listed as a breaking change. Two consequences: on older herdr the helper dies with `unknown --custom-status`, and unlike `custom_status` a token is rendered **only** where a sidebar row layout names it. That is why `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` pins `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` with `"$review"` appended to herdr's default first row — drop that and the flag still works through `prefix+i`, but the ⭐ disappears from the sidebar. See [`pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md).
319:Surfaces (all sharing one script, `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` = `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh` — the analog of tmux's `toggle-bookmark.sh`):
325:| `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i` | the **inbox**: lists only flagged panes. `Enter` focuses & **keeps** the ⭐ (you may still be mid-review); `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read") |
327:Three names must move together: `TOKEN` in `review-mark.sh`, the `.tokens.review` lookups in [`herdr-review.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml), and `"$review"` in the sidebar row layout.
356:> Two portability traps are handled inside the helper and are worth knowing if you edit it: `~/.zsh_history` is extended-history format (`: <ts>:<elapsed>;<cmd>`) **and contains non-UTF8 bytes**, so BSD `sed` aborts with `sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence` unless the parse runs under `LC_ALL=C`; and the newest-first reversal uses POSIX `awk` because `tail -r` is BSD-only while `tac` is GNU-only.
368:| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
369:| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |
373:The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
391:**How the space dir is derived — and its one caveat.** herdr exposes **no workspace-level cwd anywhere**: `herdr workspace get` and `herdr api snapshot` both return the same `label` / `number` / `tab_count` / `pane_count` object. So it is computed, by [`~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_space-root.sh) — the SSOT shared by `pane-copy.sh dir`, the `prefix+C` new-tab helper, and the tv channel's preview + `Alt+Y`:
402:One helper drives it: `~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh). It reads the pane (`herdr pane read`), runs the **same extraction/rewrite passes as tmux-fzf-url**, and opens each choice with the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md) (wslview / open / xdg-open). It mirrors `pane-copy.sh` exactly: pane defaults to `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` (the keybind var) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, and `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH.
406:| Scope | **Visible screen by default** (matches tmux-fzf-url). `url-pick.sh <pane> --source recent` scans the full retained scrollback |
407:| Patterns | `http(s)` / `ftp` / `file`, bare `www.` → `http://`, `IPv4[:port]` → `http://`, `git@…` SSH remotes → `https://…`, quoted `"owner/repo"` → `github.com/owner/repo`, `import "pkg"` → `npmjs.com/package/pkg` |
417:Helper: `~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh), a direct sibling of `url-pick.sh`/`pane-copy.sh` (same pane + `x`-resolution + `herdr pane read` plumbing), copying via [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md).
425:| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |
427:`path:line:col` suffixes (grep `-n` / stack traces / compiler output) are stripped before the existence test, so `pkg.py:42:5` validates as `pkg.py`. Scope is the visible screen by default (`--source recent` for scrollback); multi-select copies newline-joined; an empty result prints `no file paths found` and pauses ~1.5 s.
431:herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --token usage="…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into (the same hook the **Review-pending flag** section above uses, but since herdr 0.7.4 tokens are a namespaced map, so a `usage` token and the `review` token coexist instead of contending for one field). A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
437:- **Decorative status-bar glyphs** (📌/🔖 as free-floating window labels): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation, so tmux-style status-bar bookmarks don't port. *(The specific "mark-unread / review-pending ⭐" use case IS solved — see the **Review-pending flag** section above — via a per-pane metadata token; only the purely decorative status-bar glyph remains a gap.)*

82	# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
83	[keys]
84	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
85	split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
86	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
87	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
88	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)
89
90	# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
91	# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
92	# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
93	# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
94	# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
95	# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
96	# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
97	# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
98	switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
99	focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)
100
101	# --- Workspace navigate-mode: vim j/k (entered via prefix+w) ---
102	# prefix+w opens the workspace navigator; navigate_workspace_* are the
103	# navigate-mode-only movement keys. Add vim j/k alongside the default arrows so
104	# hjkl muscle memory carries here too. (These fields can't use prefix+/enter/tab/
105	# left/right or unmodified 1-9 — plain j/k are allowed.)
106	navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
107	navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]
108
109	# --- Custom command panes (the tmux-popup recreations) ---
110	# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
111	# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
112	# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /
113	# $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD in its environment.
114
115	[[keys.command]]
116	key = "prefix+G"
117	type = "pane"
118	command = "lazygit"
119	description = "lazygit (popup pane)"
120
121	# btop / nvtop monitors as floating command panes (same mechanism as lazygit —
122	# a real PTY that closes when you quit the tool). Quick Actions can't host these:
123	# herdr-plus runs an action via `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin, so an interactive TUI
124	# either exits immediately (btop) or can't receive function keys like F10 (nvtop).
125	[[keys.command]]
126	key = "prefix+M"
127	type = "pane"
128	command = "btop"
129	description = "btop system monitor (popup pane)"
130
131	[[keys.command]]
132	key = "prefix+N"
133	type = "pane"
134	command = "nvtop"
135	description = "nvtop GPU monitor (popup pane)"
136
137	# --- Scratch shell as a real floating popup (prefix+`) ---
138	# Was type = "pane", which took over the layout — it read as a zoom of the
139	# current window rather than a scratch space. type = "popup" (herdr >= 0.7.4)
140	# floats ABOVE the tiled layout instead, so nothing reflows and quitting the
141	# shell puts you back exactly where you were.
142	#
143	# The lazygit/btop/nvtop bindings above deliberately STAY type = "pane": you
144	# quit those immediately (`q`) and return, so the temporary split costs nothing
145	# and a modal popup would buy nothing. Popups are session-modal — you cannot
146	# interact with another pane while one is open — which is the trade-off that
147	# decides this per binding rather than globally.
148	[[keys.command]]
149	key = "prefix+`"
150	type = "popup"
151	command = "$SHELL"
152	width = "85%"
153	height = "80%"
154	description = "scratch shell (popup)"
155
156	# --- Run an arbitrary command in a floating popup (prefix+E) ---
157	# The generalisation of prefix+G: instead of a hardcoded tool, fzf-pick or type
158	# any command, run it in the FOCUSED PANE'S cwd, and the popup closes itself when
159	# the command exits. Helper: ~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh.

163	# back exactly where you were. That is why this one is NOT type = "pane" like the
164	# lazygit/btop/scratch bindings above.
165	#
166	# Deliberately not a herdr-plus Quick Action (prefix+y): Quick Actions run through
167	# `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin (the same reason btop/nvtop are command panes) and
168	# every action is a fixed command string with no free-text field.
169	#
170	# Exit behaviour: closes on success, holds on failure so the error stays readable.
171	# Override with HERDR_RUN_HOLD=always|never. `--sh` runs via `sh -c` (fast, no
172	# aliases) instead of the default `$SHELL -ic` (sources the interactive rc, so
173	# this repo's aliases/functions resolve).

175	key = "prefix+E"
176	type = "popup"
177	command = "~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh"
178	width = "80%"
179	height = "70%"
180	description = "run a command in the pane cwd (popup)"

286	#                  row represents, i.e. what a right-click "Copy dir" would give

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
5	# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
6	# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
7	# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
8	# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
9	# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
10	# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
11	#
12	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
13	# new contents on stdout.
14	#
15	# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
19	#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
22	#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
23	#
24	# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
25	# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
26	# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
27	# round-trips both.
28	#
29	# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
30	# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
31	# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
32	# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
33	#
34	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
35	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
36	# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
37	# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
38	# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
39	set -eu
40
41	tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
42	trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM
43
44	cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
45	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
46	TOML
47
48	live=$(cat)
49
50	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -
54	else
55	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
56	  cat "$tmpl_file"
57	  exit 0
58	fi
59
60	HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63
64	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
65	with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
66	    template_text = fh.read()
67
68
69	def emit_template():
70	    sys.stdout.write(template_text)
71
72
73	# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
74	try:
75	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
76	except ModuleNotFoundError:
77	    try:
78	        import tomli as tomllib
79	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
80	        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
81	        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
82	        emit_template()
83	        sys.exit(0)
84
85	# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
86	# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
87	try:
88	    import tomlkit
89	except ModuleNotFoundError:
90	    print(
91	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
92	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
93	        file=sys.stderr,
94	    )
95	    emit_template()
96	    sys.exit(0)
97
98	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
99
100	live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
101	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
102	live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
103
104	# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
105	for key, value in live.items():
106	    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
107	        continue
108	    doc[key] = value
109
110	sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
111	PYEOF
112
```
