1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54
55	# Absolutize + validate a `-p/--path DIR` argument in THIS shell. Echoes the
56	# canonical (symlink-resolved) path; on a non-directory, echoes nothing and
57	# returns 1 after a message on stderr.
58	#
59	# LOAD-BEARING for every `--cwd` below: herdr resolves a *relative* `--cwd`
60	# against the SERVER's launch directory (wherever `herdr server` was started),
61	# not the caller's cwd — and on a miss it silently falls back to $HOME, so
62	# `hhere -p ../sibling` opens a workspace at `~` with no error anywhere. tmux
63	# resolves `new-session -c` client-side, which is why the sesh originals
64	# (shere/svibe/scode) never needed this.
65	# See pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md.
66	#
67	# `CDPATH=''` + `--` + `>/dev/null` keep a CDPATH hit from silently retargeting
68	# the cd or echoing the resolved dir into the capture.
69	# $1=dir  $2=caller name (for the error message)
70	function _herdr_abs_dir() {
71	    local abs
72	    abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
73	    if [ -z "$abs" ]; then
74	        echo "${2:-herdr}: --path is not a directory: $1" >&2
75	        return 1
76	    fi
77	    printf '%s\n' "$abs"
78	}
79
80	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
81	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
82	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
83	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
84	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
85	#
86	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
87	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
88	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
89	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
90	function _herdr_session_target() {
91	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
92	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
93	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
94	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
95	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
96	            | head -1)
97	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
98	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
99	            return 1
100	        fi
101	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
102	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
103	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
104	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
105	            return 1
106	        fi
107	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
108	        return 0
109	    fi
110	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
111	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
112	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
113	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
114	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
115	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
116	            | head -1)
117	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
118	    else
119	        printf 'default\t\n'
120	    fi
121	}
122
123	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
124	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
125	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
126	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
127	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
128	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
129	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
130	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
131	    local session="${1:-default}"
132	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
133	        herdr
134	    else
135	        herdr session attach "$session"
136	    fi
137	}
138
139	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
140	#
141	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
142	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
143	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
144	#
145	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
146	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
147	#
148	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
149	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
150	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
151	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
152	#
153	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
154	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
155	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
156	#
157	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
158	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
159	# has no even-out-splits command.
160	#
161	# Usage:
162	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
163	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
164	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
165	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
166	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
167	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
168	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
169	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
170	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
171	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
172	function herdr-vibe() {
173	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
174
175	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
176	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
177	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
178	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
179	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
180	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
181	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
182
183	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
184	        case "$1" in
185	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
186	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
187	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
188	            --session)       session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
189	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
190	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
191	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
192	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
193	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
194	            -h|--help)
195	                cat <<'EOF'
196	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
197
198	Usage:
199	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
200	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
201	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
202	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
203
204	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
205	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
206	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
207	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
208	  tab "edit"   — nvim
209	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
210	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
211
212	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session so
213	the new workspace is visible; run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses it.
214	--no-attach builds in the background either way.
215	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: the current session
216	when inside herdr, else the default session). Start a session first with
217	`herdr --session NAME`.
218
219	Two modes for choosing agents:
220	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
221	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
222
223	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
224	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
225	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
226
227	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
228	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
229	  kill            — let the pane close
230	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
231
232	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
233	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
234	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
235
236	Examples:
237	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
238	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
239	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
240	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
241	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
242	EOF
243	                return 0 ;;
244	            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
245	            *)               break ;;
246	        esac
247	    done
248
249	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
250	        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
251	        return 1
252	    fi
253	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
254	        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
255	        return 1
256	    fi
257
258	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
259
260	    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
261	    local -a agents
262	    agents=()
263	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
264	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
265	            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
266	            return 1
267	        fi
268	        local tok
269	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
270	            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
271	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
272	        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
273	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
274	            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
275	            return 1
276	        fi
277	    else
278	        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
279	            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
280	        fi
281	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
282	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
283	        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
284	        # --tab-per-agent for more).
285	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
286	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
287	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
288	            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
289	        fi
290	        local k
291	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
292	    fi
293
294	    case "$on_exit" in
295	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
296	        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
297	    esac
298
299	    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe). `-p DIR` is absolutized first so
300	    # a bad path reports itself instead of masquerading as "not a git repo".
301	    local repo_root
302	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
303	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hvibe) || return 1
304	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
305	    else
306	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
307	    fi
308	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
309	        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
310	        return 1
311	    fi
312
313	    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
314	    local a missing=""
315	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
316	        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
317	    done
318	    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
319	        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
320	        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
321	        return 1
322	    fi
323
324	    local repo label
325	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
326	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")
327
328	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
329	    # A non-empty sess_sock means an explicit --session override — scope it with
330	    # `local -x` so child `herdr` calls see it but the user's shell is untouched.
331	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
332	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
333	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
334	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
335	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
336
337	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
338	    local existing
339	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
340	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
341	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
342	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
343	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
344	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
345	        fi
346	        return 0
347	    fi
348
349	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
350	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
351	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
352	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
353	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
354	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
355	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
356	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
357	        return 1
358	    fi
359
360	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
361	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
362	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
363	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
364	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
365	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
366	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
367	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
368	        done
369	    else
370	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
371	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
372	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
373	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
374	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
375	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
376	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
377	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
378	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
379	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio
380	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
381	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
382	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
383	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
384	                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
385	            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
386	                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
387	                prev="$np"
388	            fi
389	            m=$((m+1))
390	        done
391	    fi
392
393	    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
394	    local git_inner git_label
395	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
396	    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
397	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
398	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"
399
400	    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
401	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
402	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
403	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
404	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
405	    fi
406	}
407
408	# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
409	#
410	# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
411	#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
412	#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
413	# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
414	#
415	# Usage:
416	#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
417	#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
418	#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
419	#   hcode --no-specstory claude
420	#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
421	#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
422	function herdr-code() {
423	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
424
425	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
426	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
427	        case "$1" in
428	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
429	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
430	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
431	            --session)      session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
432	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
433	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
434	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
435	            --agents)
436	                echo "hcode: --agents is hvibe-only (hcode is single-agent)." >&2
437	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2
438	                return 1 ;;
439	            -h|--help)
440	                cat <<'EOF'
441	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
442
443	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
444	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
445
446	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
447	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
448	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
449	Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
450
451	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session;
452	run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses. --no-attach builds in the background.
453	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
454	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
455
456	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
457	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
458	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
459
460	--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart
461
462	Examples:
463	  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
464	  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
465	  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
466	  hcode --on-exit kill claude
467	EOF
468	                return 0 ;;
469	            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
470	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
471	        esac
472	    done
473
474	    case "$on_exit" in
475	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
476	        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
477	    esac
478
479	    local repo_root
480	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
481	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hcode) || return 1
482	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
483	    else
484	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
485	    fi
486	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
487	        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
488	        return 1
489	    fi
490
491	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
492	        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
493	        return 1
494	    fi
495
496	    local repo label
497	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
498	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")
499
500	    # Resolve target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
501	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
502	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
503	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
504	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
505	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
506
507	    local existing
508	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
509	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
510	        echo "hcode: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
511	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
512	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
513	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
514	        fi
515	        return 0
516	    fi
517
518	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
519	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
520	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
521	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
522	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
523	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
524	        echo "hcode: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
525	        return 1
526	    fi
527
528	    # editor tab: nvim in the initial pane, agent split off to the right at ~25%.
529	    # --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane being split (nvim/left), so 0.75
530	    # leaves nvim at 75% and the new agent pane at 25%.
531	    herdr tab rename "$t0" editor >/dev/null 2>&1
532	    herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")" >/dev/null 2>&1
533	    local ap
534	    ap=$(herdr pane split "$p0" --direction right --ratio 0.75 --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
535	        | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
536	    [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane run "$ap" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
537
538	    # monitor tab.
539	    local mon
540	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=btop
541	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=htop
542	    else                                       mon=top
543	    fi
544	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" monitor "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$mon" "$on_exit" "$mon")"
545
546	    # Focus editor tab, nvim pane (left neighbor of the agent pane).
547	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
548	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
549	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
550	        [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane focus --direction left --pane "$ap" >/dev/null 2>&1
551	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
552	    fi
553	}
554
555	# ── hhere: plain "open a workspace here + attach" ────────────────────────────
556	#
557	# herdr analog of `shere` (sesh-here). The lightweight counterpart to
558	# hvibe/hcode: create a herdr workspace at $PWD (or -p DIR), focus it, and
559	# attach a client when run from outside herdr. NO git requirement and NO agent
560	# layout — just a shell in the workspace root pane. This fills the gap where
561	# every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent pack; with
562	# tmux `tmux new-session` lands you in $PWD directly, but herdr adds a Workspace
563	# layer, so without this you'd launch herdr, create a space (opens at $HOME),
564	# then cd manually.
565	#
566	# Smart argument handling (mirrors shere):
567	#   hhere                          # plain shell at $PWD
568	#   hhere npm run dev              # bare args → run as the root-pane command
569	#   hhere -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
570	#   hhere -p ~/proj                # explicit path, plain shell
571	#   hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev    # explicit path + command
572	#
573	# `-p DIR` is absolutized in THIS shell before it reaches herdr — the server
574	# resolves a relative `--cwd` against its own launch directory and falls back to
575	# $HOME on a miss (silently). A non-existent DIR is a hard error.
576	#
577	# The command (if any) runs raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping. That agent
578	# treatment stays with hcode/hvibe; hhere is deliberately lightweight.
579	#
580	# Idempotent per label (bare basename of the dir, matching herdr's own native
581	# auto-label convention). Caveat: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to the root
582	# pane's LIVE cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see docs/tools/herdr.md § cwd
583	# & workspace-naming), so the reuse is best-effort — if the label has drifted, a
584	# re-run creates a fresh workspace (arguably correct: you're elsewhere now).
585	#
586	# Usage:
587	#   hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
588	function herdr-here() {
589	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hhere: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
590
591	    local cmd="" target="" no_attach=0 session_arg=""
592	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
593	        case "$1" in
594	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
595	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
596	            --session)    session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
597	            --no-attach)  no_attach=1; shift ;;
598	            -h|--help)
599	                cat <<'EOF'
600	hhere — open a plain herdr workspace here + attach (herdr analog of shere)
601
602	Usage: hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
603
604	Creates a herdr workspace at DIR (default $PWD), focuses it, and — when run
605	from OUTSIDE herdr — attaches a client so it is visible. No git repo required
606	and no agent layout: just a shell in the workspace root pane. For agent
607	layouts use hcode (single-agent) or hvibe (multi-agent).
608
609	Smart argument handling:
610	  hhere                        # plain shell at $PWD
611	  hhere npm run dev            # bare args → run as the root-pane command
612	  hhere -c "npm run dev"       # explicit --command flag
613	  hhere -p ~/proj              # explicit path, plain shell
614	  hhere -p ../sibling          # relative paths resolve against YOUR shell
615	  hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev  # explicit path + command
616
617	--path DIR is resolved (and symlink-canonicalized) here, in your shell, before
618	it reaches herdr — a DIR that does not exist is a hard error, not a silent
619	workspace at $HOME.
620
621	Idempotent: re-running in the same dir focuses the existing workspace.
622	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
623	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
624	--no-attach builds in the background.
625	EOF
626	                return 0 ;;
627	            -*)           echo "hhere: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
628	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
629	        esac
630	    done
631	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
632	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
633
634	    # ABSOLUTIZE — load-bearing, do NOT pass `$target` through verbatim; herdr
635	    # resolves a relative `--cwd` server-side and falls back to $HOME on a miss.
636	    # See _herdr_abs_dir above.
637	    target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hhere) || return 1
638
639	    local label
640	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
641
642	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
643	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
644	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
645	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
646	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}

648
649	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
650	    local existing
651	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
652	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
653	        echo "hhere: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
654	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
655	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
656	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
657	        fi
658	        return 0
659	    fi
660
661	    local ws_json ws p0
662	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$target" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
663	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
664	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
665	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ]; then
666	        echo "hhere: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
667	        return 1
668	    fi
669
670	    # Optional command in the root pane (raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping).
671	    [ -n "$cmd" ] && herdr pane run "$p0" "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1
672
673	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
674	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
675	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
676	    fi
677	}
678
679	# ── hroot: like hhere but at the git-root ────────────────────────────────────
680	#
681	# herdr analog of `sroot` (sesh-root). Same as hhere except the target resolves
682	# to the current git top-level (falls back to $PWD outside a repo). Thin wrapper
683	# over herdr-here so there is one code path; -p is not accepted (the root IS the
684	# path), everything else (-c / bare command / --session / --no-attach) passes
685	# through.
686	#
687	# Usage:
688	#   hroot                          # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
689	#   hroot npm run dev              # + run a command
690	#   hroot -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
691	function herdr-root() {
692	    case "$1" in
693	        -h|--help)
694	            cat <<'EOF'
695	hroot — open a plain herdr workspace at the git-root + attach (analog of sroot)
696
697	Usage: hroot [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
698
699	Like hhere, but the workspace opens at the current git top-level (falls back to
700	$PWD outside a repo). All flags except --path pass through to hhere.
701
702	  hroot                # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
703	  hroot npm run dev    # + run a command
704	EOF
705	            return 0 ;;
706	        -p|--path)
707	            echo "hroot: --path is not accepted (root is derived from git). Use hhere -p DIR." >&2
708	            return 1 ;;
709	    esac
710	    local root
711	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
712	    herdr-here -p "$root" "$@"
713	}
714
715	# ── Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐) ───────────────────────────────────
716	# hmark/hunmark toggle a per-pane "I still need to review this" flag via herdr's
717	# `review` metadata token — ORTHOGONAL to agent state, so peeking into a done pane
718	# (which flips it to idle) does NOT clear the flag. The mark logic lives in
719	# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh (dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh);
720	# these are thin CLI wrappers defaulting the pane to the ambient HERDR_PANE_ID.
721	# The prefix+m keybind and the `tv herdr-review` inbox share that same script.
722	_herdr_review_script="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh"
723
724	# hmark [PANE] — flag a pane for later review (default: current pane).
725	function herdr-mark() {
726	    case "${1:-}" in
727	        -h|--help)
728	            cat <<'EOF'
729	hmark — flag a herdr pane as "review-pending" (⭐), analog of tmux bookmark
730
731	Usage: hmark [PANE_ID]
732
733	With no PANE_ID, flags the CURRENT pane (ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID). The flag is a
734	herdr metadata token (`review`), orthogonal to agent state — it survives the pane
735	going idle when you peek in. Clear with `hunmark`, toggle with prefix+m, list
736	flagged panes with `tv herdr-review` (prefix+i inside herdr).
737	EOF
738	            return 0 ;;
739	    esac
740	    local pane="${1:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}"
741	    [ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "hmark: no pane id (not inside herdr?). Pass one: hmark w1:p1" >&2; return 1; }
742	    "$_herdr_review_script" set "$pane"
743	}
744
745	# hunmark [PANE] — clear the review flag (default: current pane).
746	function herdr-unmark() {
747	    case "${1:-}" in
748	        -h|--help)
749	            cat <<'EOF'
750	hunmark — clear a herdr pane's "review-pending" (⭐) flag
751
752	Usage: hunmark [PANE_ID]
753
754	With no PANE_ID, clears the CURRENT pane (ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID).
755	EOF
756	            return 0 ;;
757	    esac
758	    local pane="${1:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}"
759	    [ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "hunmark: no pane id (not inside herdr?). Pass one: hunmark w1:p1" >&2; return 1; }
760	    "$_herdr_review_script" clear "$pane"
761	}
762
763	# ── Aliases ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
764	alias hvibe='herdr-vibe'
765	alias hcode='herdr-code'
766	alias hhere='herdr-here'
767	alias hroot='herdr-root'
768	alias hmark='herdr-mark'
769	alias hunmark='herdr-unmark'

2	# ~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Open a NEW TAB rooted at the WORKSPACE ("space") directory, NOT the focused
6	# pane's live cwd.
7	#
8	# Why this exists: on herdr >=0.7.x, `new_cwd = "follow"` makes a new tab inherit
9	# the FOCUSED pane's cwd — herdr issue #912 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912)
10	# changed `follow` so new tabs behave like pane splits, and the older "new tab
11	# opens at the workspace's initial dir" was treated as a bug and removed. There
12	# is NO new_cwd value for "workspace dir", so we compute it and pass it via
13	# `herdr tab create --cwd`. (herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field either —
14	# `herdr workspace get` has no cwd — so it must be derived.)
15	#
16	# "Space dir" = the cwd of the workspace's OLDEST surviving tab. That derivation
17	# is NOT inlined here: it lives in the sibling ~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh,
18	# shared with `pane-copy.sh dir` (prefix+d) and the herdr-sesh tv channel. Change
19	# it there, once — including the caveat about the sidebar label drifting from it.
20	#
21	# Bound to prefix+C (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). prefix+c and the mouse
22	# "+" button keep herdr's native follow-the-focused-pane behavior. Uses the
23	# keybind-context $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (falls back to ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID).
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   new-tab-at-space-root.sh [pane_id]   # pane_id defaults to the current pane
27	set -eu
28
29	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
30	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
31
32	pane="${1:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}"
33	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: no pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)" >&2; exit 64; }
34
35	wid=$(herdr pane get "$pane" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // ""')
36	[ -n "$wid" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
37
38	# Root dir derivation is shared — see space-root.sh. Resolve it beside this
39	# script rather than via PATH: a herdr command-pane may run us without the
40	# interactive PATH.
41	here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
42	root=$("$here/space-root.sh" "$wid") || exit 1
43
44	exec herdr tab create --workspace "$wid" --cwd "$root" --focus

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy-a-file-path picker — the copy-path sibling of url-pick.sh (which OPENS
6	# URLs). Reads the focused pane, extracts path-like tokens (borrowing extrakto's
7	# path heuristics), and presents a TWO-TIER fzf list: paths that EXIST relative to
8	# the pane cwd on top (copied as their resolved ABSOLUTE path), unverified
9	# candidates (as-seen) below a separator. The choice is copied via `x copy`.
10	#
11	# The existence check is the noise-killer extrakto lacks: file paths have no
12	# scheme:// marker, so regex alone matches dates (2024/01/02), rates (10k/s) and
13	# fractions (1/2); validating against the pane's live cwd drops nearly all of it.
14	#
15	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
16	# script exits), bound to prefix+p in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. Mirrors
17	# the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the keybind var) with a
18	# `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read` for the text, `x copy` for the
19	# clipboard, and an absolute-path `x` fallback because a command pane runs us via
20	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
21	#
22	# Usage:
23	#   path-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]
24	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, else the current focused pane. --source
25	# defaults to visible; --source recent scans the full scrollback. --cwd is the
26	# directory relative paths are resolved against for the existence check; it
27	# defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd →
28	# process-info cwd → $PWD.
29	#
30	# Consumers: the prefix+p keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
31	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Copy a file path from the pane".
32	set -eu
33
34	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
35
36	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
37	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
38
39	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
40	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41	    X_BIN=x
42	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
43	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
44	else
45	    echo "path-pick: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
46	    exit 1
47	fi
48
49	pane=""
50	source="visible"
51	cwd=""
52	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
53	    case "$1" in
54	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
55	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
56	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
57	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
58	        -h|--help) usage ;;
59	        -*) usage ;;
60	        *)
61	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
62	                pane="$1"
63	                shift
64	            else
65	                usage
66	            fi
67	            ;;
68	    esac
69	done
70
71	case "$source" in
72	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
73	    *) echo "path-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
74	esac
75
76	# Resolve pane (keybind passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID; fall back to current).
77	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
78	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
79	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
80	fi
81	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "path-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
82
83	# Resolve cwd for existence checks: --cwd → pane.foreground_cwd → process cwd → $PWD.
84	if [ -z "$cwd" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
85	    cwd=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
86	    [ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
87	        | jq -r '.result.process_info.foreground_processes[0].cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
88	fi
89	[ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd="$PWD"
90
91	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
92	    || { echo "path-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
93
94	# Path candidates (extrakto path heuristics, POSIX-ized): slash-bearing tokens
95	# (abs /…, home ~/…, rel ./ ../ a/b/c) + bare filename.ext. rstrip trailing
96	# ",):; then drop rate/fraction noise (extrakto's exclude: 10k/s, 1/2). dedupe.
97	cands=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" \
98	    | grep -oE '(~|\.\.?)?/?[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+)+|[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8}' \
99	    | sed -E 's/[",):;]+$//' \
100	    | grep -vE '^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$|[kKmMgG]/s$' \
101	    | grep -v '^$' | awk '!seen[$0]++' || true)
102
103	if [ -z "$cands" ]; then
104	    printf 'path-pick: no file paths found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
105	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
106	    exit 0
107	fi
108
109	# Two tiers: exists-under-cwd (resolved absolute) vs the rest (as-seen).
110	exist=""
111	maybe=""
112	OLDIFS=$IFS
113	IFS='
114	'
115	for c in $cands; do
116	    base=$(printf '%s' "$c" | sed -E 's/:[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$//')   # strip :line[:col] for the test
117	    case "$base" in
118	        /*)   abs="$base" ;;
119	        \~/*) abs="$HOME/${base#\~/}" ;;
120	        *)    abs="$cwd/$base" ;;
121	    esac
122	    if [ -e "$abs" ]; then
123	        rp=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$abs")" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s/%s' "$(pwd -P)" "$(basename -- "$abs")") \
124	            || rp="$abs"
125	        exist="$exist$rp
126	"
127	    else
128	        maybe="$maybe$c
129	"
130	    fi
131	done
132	IFS=$OLDIFS
133
134	exist=$(printf '%s' "$exist" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
135	maybe=$(printf '%s' "$maybe" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
136
137	SEP='────────  unverified (not found under cwd)  ────────'
138	list=$(
139	    [ -n "$exist" ] && printf '%s\n' "$exist"
140	    [ -n "$maybe" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$SEP"; printf '%s\n' "$maybe"; }
141	)
142
143	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
144	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$list" | fzf --multi --no-sort --height=100% --border \
145	    --prompt='path> ' --header="Enter=copy · Tab=multi · cwd=$cwd") || exit 0
146
147	# Drop the separator if it slipped into the selection; copy the rest.
148	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | grep -vFx "$SEP" | grep -v '^$' || true)
149	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0

151	printf '%s' "$chosen" | "$X_BIN" copy
152	echo "copied $(printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | grep -c .) path(s)"
153

4	#

10	#

12	# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. The
13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs
16	# us via `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
20	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (passed by the keybind), else the current
21	# focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope);
22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
23	#
24	# Consumers: the prefix+u keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
25	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a URL from the pane".
26	set -eu
27
28	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
29
30	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
31	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
32
33	# Resolve the opener (`x open`) even without the interactive PATH.
34	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
35	    X_BIN=x
36	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
37	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
38	else
39	    echo "url-pick: opener 'x' not found" >&2
40	    exit 1
41	fi
42
43	pane=""
44	source="visible"
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
49	        -h|--help) usage ;;
50	        -*) usage ;;
51	        *)
52	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
53	                pane="$1"
54	                shift
55	            else
56	                usage
57	            fi
58	            ;;
59	    esac
60	done
61
62	case "$source" in
63	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
64	    *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
65	esac
66
67	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
68	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
70	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
71	fi
72	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
73
74	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
75	    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
76
77	# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, POSIX-ized
78	# (plain vars instead of bash arrays; trailing `|| true` so a no-match grep,
79	# which exits 1, does not trip `set -e`).
80	urls=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]' || true)
81	wwws=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
82	ips=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)
83	gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
84	gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
85	npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)
86
87	items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
88
89	if [ -z "$items" ]; then
90	    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
91	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
92	    exit 0
93	fi
94
95	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
96	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
97	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
98
99	printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
100	    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
101	done

2	# ~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_run-command.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Run an ARBITRARY command in the focused pane's cwd, inside a floating popup that
6	# closes by itself when the command exits. This is the generalisation of the
7	# hardcoded `prefix+G` (lazygit) binding — the tmux `display-popup -E` experience,
8	# with a command you pick or type instead of one baked into the config.
9	#
10	# Why a popup and not the alternatives:
11	#   - `type = "pane"` (prefix+G/M/N/`) splits the TILED layout for the duration.
12	#   - `prefix+c` + type + `exit` is four steps and churns the tab bar.
13	#   - `type = "popup"` (herdr >= 0.7.4) is session-modal and floats ABOVE the
14	#     layout, so nothing reflows and you land exactly where you were.
15	# It also cannot live as a herdr-plus Quick Action (prefix+y): those run through
16	# `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin — the same reason btop/nvtop are command panes — and
17	# every Quick Action is a fixed command string with no free-text field.
18	#
19	# Bound to prefix+E in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
20	#
21	# Usage:
22	#   run-command.sh [--cwd DIR] [--sh] [--] [QUERY...]
23	# --cwd  directory to run in; defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD (injected by the
24	#        keybind) → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd → $PWD. Preferring the env var
25	#        means this keeps working even when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a
26	#        stale server.
27	# --sh   run via `sh -c` (fast, no aliases) instead of the default `$SHELL -ic`
28	#        (sources the interactive rc, so this repo's aliases/functions resolve).
29	# QUERY  seeds the picker (and, with no fzf, prefills nothing — it is run as-is).
30	#
31	# Exit behaviour is governed by HERDR_RUN_HOLD:
32	#   fail (default)  close on success, wait for a key on non-zero exit
33	#   always          always wait for a key
34	#   never           never wait
35	#
36	# Consumers: the prefix+E keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
37	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Run any command in a popup".
38	set -eu
39
40	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [--cwd DIR] [--sh] [--] [QUERY...]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
41
42	cwd=""
43	use_sh=0
44	query=""
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
49	        --sh) use_sh=1; shift ;;
50	        -h|--help) usage ;;
51	        --) shift; break ;;
52	        -*) usage ;;
53	        *) break ;;
54	    esac
55	done

82
83	# Newest-first, de-duplicated, timestamps stripped.
84	#   - LC_ALL=C is REQUIRED: ~/.zsh_history carries non-UTF8 bytes and BSD sed
85	#     aborts with "sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence" under a UTF-8 locale.
86	#   - The reverse is done in awk because `tail -r` is BSD-only and `tac` GNU-only.
87	#   - Lines ending in a backslash are multi-line history entries; skip them.
88	_history() {
89	    [ -r "$histfile" ] || return 0
90	    LC_ALL=C sed 's/^: [0-9]*:[0-9]*;//' "$histfile" 2>/dev/null \
91	        | grep -v '\\$' \
92	        | awk 'NF' \
93	        | awk '{a[NR]=$0} END{for(i=NR;i>0;i--) if(!seen[a[i]]++) print a[i]}'
94	}
95

97	cmd=""

100	    # Line layout is NOT fixed — fzf omits trailing lines it has nothing for:

102	    #   Enter     with a match     rc 0    query \n ""        \n selection
103	    #   Alt+Enter with a match     rc 0    query \n alt-enter \n selection
104	    #   Enter     with no match    rc 1    query                              (1 line)
105	    #   Alt+Enter with no match    rc 1    query \n alt-enter
106	    #   Esc                        rc 130  —
107	    #

109	    # command from line 3 only on rc 0; every other path falls back to the

114	    # `ls -la /tmp`, Enter takes the history entry. That made the picker feel
115	    # like it could only replay old commands. Alt+ (not Ctrl+) per the repo's
116	    # keybinding convention.

119	        --print-query --expect=alt-enter --no-sort --height=100% --border \
120	        --query="$query" \
121	        --header='enter: run highlighted · alt-enter: run what you typed · esc: cancel' \
122	        --prompt="run [$(basename "$cwd")]> ")

127	        *) exit 0 ;;   # 130 = Esc, or fzf failed — run nothing
128	    esac

130	    if [ "$key" = "alt-enter" ]; then
131	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p')      # literal query, always
132	    elif [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
133	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '3p')      # highlighted selection
134	    else
135	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p')      # no match → the query
136	    fi
137	else
138	    if [ -n "$query" ]; then
139	        cmd="$query"
140	    else
141	        printf 'run [%s]> ' "$(basename "$cwd")"

144	fi

146	[ -n "$cmd" ] || exit 0

148	# --- run it -----------------------------------------------------------------

150
151	set +e
152	if [ "$use_sh" -eq 1 ]; then
153	    sh -c "$cmd"

155	    # -i so the interactive rc is sourced and this repo's aliases/functions exist.
156	    "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -ic "$cmd"

158	rc=$?
159	set -e

161	# --- hold policy ------------------------------------------------------------
162	hold="${HERDR_RUN_HOLD:-fail}"
163	case "$hold" in
164	    never) ;;
165	    always) _wait=1 ;;
166	    *) [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && _wait=1 ;;
167	esac
168	if [ "${_wait:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then

174	exit "$rc"

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: hook-aware deep-merge of a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json.
4	#
5	# Why hook-aware? Claude Code rewrites this file at runtime AND CodeIsland
6	# (https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland, macOS notch HUD) auto-installs its
7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. workmux's `wm setup` ALSO writes Stop /
9	# UserPromptSubmit / Notification hook entries (see docs/tools/workmux.md
10	# → "Claude leak"). A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays
11	# wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would silently
12	# delete every CodeIsland / workmux entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and the
13	# tools would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
14	#
15	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
16	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
17	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
18	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
19	# notify.sh + workmux status updates while CodeIsland / workmux setup /
20	# any other tool freely manage their own parallel entries in the same
21	# event arrays.
22	#
23	# Workmux integration: We declare the workmux Stop / SubagentStop /
24	# UserPromptSubmit / Notification hooks here directly so they're enforced
25	# on every chezmoi apply WITHOUT requiring users to also run `wm setup`.
26	# The `command -v workmux` guard lets the hook no-op silently on machines
27	# where workmux isn't installed yet (fresh box, Linux without ansible run,
28	# etc.). This patches Claude's by-design 🤖-leak: Anthropic's Stop hook
29	# fires on every turn end, but workmux's `working` state never auto-clears
30	# without an explicit `done` set.
31	#
32	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
33	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.
34	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role). On a fresh-box first
35	# apply, jq isn't yet installed; this script falls back to passing the live
36	# file through unchanged. See pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
37	#
38	# Completion feedback is gated on the `agentSounds` prompt (none|notify|peon|
39	# both) — see docs/tools/agent-sounds.md. This file is a TEMPLATE for that
40	# reason; the peon-ping hook entries below were lifted verbatim from a real
41	# `peon-ping-setup` run against a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (its README
42	# documents a different, wrong command shape). We declare them ourselves and
43	# NEVER run `peon-ping-setup` on a managed machine — same rule as workmux's
44	# `wm setup`. The `[ -x … ]` guard makes the hook a silent no-op on a box
45	# where the binary isn't installed yet (fresh box, Linux without ansible),
46	# mirroring the mandatory `command -v workmux` guard.
47	#
48	# claude-hud is deliberately `enabledPlugins: false`. It ships two commands
49	# (`claude-hud:setup` / `claude-hud:configure`) that are install/config-time
50	# only, yet every session paid ~45 tokens to list them to the model. This is
51	# NOT a `skillOverrides` job — verified 2026-07 on CC 2.1.220 that neither
52	# "off" nor "user-invocable-only" gates *plugin* commands (the listing filter
53	# keys on a name that differs from the displayed `claude-hud:setup`); those

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   scripts/generate_completions.sh [--force] [--quiet] [--help]
6	#
7	# Modes:
8	#   default   Skip tools whose completion file is already newer than the binary
9	#             (binary-mtime check — same idiom as 95_bitwarden.zsh / 47_mi_router.sh).
10	#   --force   Regenerate every tool's completion regardless of mtime.
11	#   --quiet   Suppress per-tool progress; still print final summary.
12	#
13	# Output paths (lazy-autoload conventions):
14	#   zsh:  ~/.zfunc/_<tool>                                              (in fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl:68)
15	#   bash: ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>
16	#         (auto-loaded on first TAB by bash-completion v2)
17	#
18	# Tools NOT handled here (covered elsewhere — don't double-up):
19	#   sesh, tv, worktrunk        → shell-startup mtime check (dot_config/zsh/tools/{22_sesh,12_television,37_worktrunk}.zsh)
20	#   bw                         → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh)
21	#   marimo, thefuck, try-cli   → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/shell/{29_marimo,27_thefuck}.sh + dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh)
22	#   mi-router                  → tyro self-gen at startup  (dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh)
23	#   fleet, mlf, pqsum, x       → hand-written eager-load   (dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-49_*_completion.*)
24	#
25	# Invoked from:
26	#   - .chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl   (every chezmoi apply, no --force)
27	#   - `just completions-refresh`                                          (manual, --force)
28	#
29	# Skip from chezmoi apply: export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1
30	# Full design: docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md "How autocomplete works" + Section A.
31
32	set -euo pipefail
33
34	force=0
35	quiet=0
36	for a in "$@"; do
37	  case "$a" in
38	    --force) force=1 ;;
39	    --quiet) quiet=1 ;;
40	    -h | --help)
41	      sed -n '2,30p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'
42	      exit 0
43	      ;;
44	    *)
45	      echo "generate_completions: unknown arg: $a" >&2
46	      exit 2
47	      ;;
48	  esac
49	done
50
51	ZFUNC="${HOME}/.zfunc"
52	BASHDIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions"
53
54	mkdir -p "$ZFUNC" "$BASHDIR"
55
56	n_z_regen=0
57	n_b_regen=0
58	n_z_skip=0
59	n_b_skip=0
60	n_missing=0
61
62	# regen <tool> <zsh-args> <bash-args>
63	# Uses word-splitting on $zargs / $bargs deliberately (the upstream completion
64	# subcommands are 1-3 words, no quoting needed).
65	regen() {
66	  local tool="$1" zargs="$2" bargs="$3"
67	  local bin
68	  if ! bin="$(command -v "$tool" 2>/dev/null)"; then
69	    n_missing=$((n_missing + 1))
70	    return 0
71	  fi
72	  local zfile="${ZFUNC}/_${tool}"
73	  local bfile="${BASHDIR}/${tool}"
74
75	  # zsh
76	  if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$zfile" ] || [ "$bin" -nt "$zfile" ]; then
77	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word-split intentional
78	    if "$tool" $zargs >"$zfile.tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$zfile.tmp" ]; then
79	      mv "$zfile.tmp" "$zfile"
80	      n_z_regen=$((n_z_regen + 1))
81	      [ "$quiet" = 0 ] && printf '  zsh   %-10s → %s\n' "$tool" "$zfile"
82	    else
83	      rm -f "$zfile.tmp"
84	    fi
85	  else
86	    n_z_skip=$((n_z_skip + 1))
87	  fi
88
89	  # bash
90	  if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$bfile" ] || [ "$bin" -nt "$bfile" ]; then
91	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
92	    if "$tool" $bargs >"$bfile.tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$bfile.tmp" ]; then
93	      mv "$bfile.tmp" "$bfile"
94	      n_b_regen=$((n_b_regen + 1))
95	      [ "$quiet" = 0 ] && printf '  bash  %-10s → %s\n' "$tool" "$bfile"
96	    else
97	      rm -f "$bfile.tmp"
98	    fi
99	  else
100	    n_b_skip=$((n_b_skip + 1))
101	  fi
102
103	  # `set -e` + `[ test ] && cmd` at function tail is a bash footgun: when
104	  # `--quiet` makes the test fail, the &&-short-circuit returns 1, the inner
105	  # `if`-`then` body returns 1, regen() returns 1, and set -e aborts.
106	  return 0
107	}
108
109	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
110	# Inventory: tool, zsh-args (after `<tool>`), bash-args (after `<tool>`)
111	# Add a new row when you add a new upstream CLI to the ansible / brew install
112	# set AND it self-generates completion (most modern CLIs do — check `<tool>
113	# completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`).
114	# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
115	regen chezmoi "completion zsh" "completion bash"
116	regen mise "completion zsh" "completion bash"
117	regen uv "generate-shell-completion zsh" "generate-shell-completion bash"
118	regen just "--completions zsh" "--completions bash"
119	regen starship "completions zsh" "completions bash"
120	regen gh "completion -s zsh" "completion -s bash"
121	regen docker "completion zsh" "completion bash"
122	regen rg "--generate complete-zsh" "--generate complete-bash"
123	regen fd "--gen-completions zsh" "--gen-completions bash"
124	regen bat "--completion zsh" "--completion bash"
125	regen delta "--generate-completion zsh" "--generate-completion bash"
126	regen zellij "setup --generate-completion zsh" "setup --generate-completion bash"
127	regen pueue "completions zsh" "completions bash"
128	regen opencode "completion zsh" "completion bash"
129	regen translate "completion zsh" "completion bash"
130
131	if [ "$n_z_regen" -gt 0 ] || [ "$n_b_regen" -gt 0 ] || [ "$quiet" = 0 ]; then
132	  printf 'completions: regenerated %d zsh + %d bash | skipped %d zsh + %d bash | %d not installed\n' \
133	    "$n_z_regen" "$n_b_regen" "$n_z_skip" "$n_b_skip" "$n_missing"
134	fi
135

1	---
2	# Go CLI tools installation via `go install`.
3	# The Go toolchain is installed via mise (gated on installExtraRuntimes; see
4	# dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl). This role no-ops cleanly when Go is absent.
5
6	# =============================================================================
7	# Resolve the mise-managed Go bin dir (no-op the whole role if Go is absent)
8	# =============================================================================
9	# `mise which go` prints the absolute path to the managed go binary
10	# (~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin/go); its dirname is the bin dir we
11	# prepend to PATH so `go install` runs. Empty/failed → Go isn't installed
12	# (installExtraRuntimes=false, or mise missing) and the install task below is
13	# skipped. Mirrors the herdr-plus build idiom in dot_ansible/roles/devtools.
14	- name: Resolve mise Go bin dir
15	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
16	    set -o pipefail
17	    gobin="$(mise which go 2>/dev/null)" || exit 0
18	    [ -n "$gobin" ] && dirname "$gobin"
19	  args:
20	    executable: /bin/bash
21	  environment:
22	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
23	  register: go_bindir
24	  changed_when: false
25	  failed_when: false
26
27	# =============================================================================
28	# Install Go CLI tools (Linux; macOS uses Homebrew)
29	# =============================================================================
30	# GOBIN forces binaries into ~/.local/bin (the blessed dir already on PATH),
31	# not ~/go/bin (GOPATH/bin) or the version-pinned mise toolchain dir. GOPATH is
32	# pinned to ~/.local/share/go (XDG data) so the build-time module cache lands
33	# there instead of recreating ~/go — matches the interactive shell
34	# (dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh) and scripts/upgrade_tools.sh cat_go. The
35	# `creates:` guard makes this install-only + idempotent — version bumps go
36	# through `just upgrade-go` (scripts/upgrade_tools.sh cat_go), never a re-apply.
37	#
38	# macOS is EXCLUDED: those tools (currently just `translate`) install via Homebrew
39	# (dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.tmpl → daviddwlee84/tap), so this go path is
40	# Linux-only — otherwise both mechanisms fight over the binary and ~/.local/bin
41	# shadows brew. cat_go() has the mirror gate. Revisit if a future go tool needs macOS.
42	- name: Install Go CLI tools via go install (Linux; macOS uses Homebrew)
43	  when:
44	    - (go_bindir.stdout | default('') | trim) != ""
45	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] != 'Darwin'
46	  ansible.builtin.command: "go install {{ item.name }}"
47	  args:
48	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
49	  loop: "{{ go_tools }}"
50	  loop_control:
51	    label: "{{ item.name }}"
52	  environment:
53	    GOBIN: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
54	    GOPATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/go"
55	    PATH: "{{ (go_bindir.stdout | trim) }}:{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

200	# and warn — the next apply (after ansible) does the real merge.
201	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
202	  printf '%s\n' "modify_settings.json: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
203	  printf '%s' "$base"
204	  exit 0
205	fi
206
207	# Hook-aware merge:
208	#   1. Compute non-hook portion of overlay (everything except .hooks).
209	#   2. Deep-merge that into base normally: base * overlay_no_hooks.
210	#   3. For each event in overlay.hooks, append entries whose .hooks[0].command
211	#      isn't already represented in the live event array (by exact-string
212	#      command match on .hooks[0].command). Live entries are preserved
213	#      verbatim, and new overlay entries are added at the end.
214	#   4. Prune OUR OWN entries that the current agentSounds tier disables.
215	#
216	# Step 4 is the one deliberate exception to "never subtract". Without it the
217	# additive merge makes `agentSounds` a one-way ratchet: switching notify -> none
218	# would leave the already-installed notify.sh hook wired forever, so `none`
219	# would not actually silence a machine that previously had sound (verified
220	# 2026-07 — this is exactly what happened on the first apply).
221	#
222	# The invariant that matters is preserved: we only ever prune commands WE
223	# declare. $prune is built from our own fingerprints, never from a foreign
224	# command, so CodeIsland / workmux / herdr entries can never be touched no
225	# matter what the tier is. Empty event arrays are dropped so turning everything
226	# off doesn't leave "SessionStart": [] litter behind.
227	{{- $prune := list }}
228	{{- if not $notify }}{{ $prune = append $prune "/.claude/hooks/notify.sh" }}{{ end }}
229	{{- if not $peon }}{{ $prune = append $prune "/.claude/hooks/peon-ping/peon.sh" }}{{ end }}
230	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" --argjson prune {{ $prune | toJson | quote }} '
231	  . as $base
232	  | ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
233	  | ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
234	  | ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
235	  | $merged
236	  | .hooks = (
237	      ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
238	      | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
239	          $live_hooks;
240	          .[$ev.key] = (
241	            (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
242	            | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
243	            | $live_arr + (
244	                $ev.value
245	                | map(select(
246	                    (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
247	                    | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
248	                  ))
249	              )
250	          )
251	        )
252	    )
253	  | .hooks = (
254	      .hooks
255	      | map_values(
256	          map(select(
257	            (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
258	            | ($prune | any(. as $frag | $cmd | contains($frag))) | not
259	          ))
260	        )
261	      | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))
262	    )
263	'

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).
