163	**Dynamic candidates wired up:**
164
165	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
166	- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
167	- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
168	- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
169	- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
170	- `appsrc which <name>` / `appsrc size <name>` — `_appsrc_names` shells out to `appsrc scan --list-names` (installed GUI app names) and adds `_command_names -e` / `compgen -c` (PATH commands), so both a GUI app name and a shell command complete. Same shell-out pattern as `_wake` / `_fleet_hosts_one`.
171
172	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
173
174	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
175	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
176	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
177	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
178	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
179	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
180
181	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
182
183	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
184
185	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
186	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
187	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
188	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
189
190	### What we DO track
191
192	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
193	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
194	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
195	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
196
197	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
198
199	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
200
201	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
202
203	Output paths:
204	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
205	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
206
207	### Manual rerun
208
209	```bash
210	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
211	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
212	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
213	```
214
215	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
216
217	### Opt out
218
219	```bash
220	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
221	```
222
223	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
224
225	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
226
227	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
228
229	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
230
231	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
232	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
233	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
234	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg` / `agent-warmup`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
235
236	## Priority / Override Order
237
238	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
239
240	```
241	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
242	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
243	3. ~/.docker/completions/
244	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
245	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
246	```
247
248	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
249
250	```zsh
251	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
252	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
253	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
254	```
255
256	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
257
258	```zsh
259	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
260	```
261
262	## FAQ
263
264	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
265	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
266
267	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
268	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
269
270	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
271	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
272

458	## Session Management
459
460	> `sesh-*` requires `sesh` + `tmux`; `tsesh` also requires the `try-cli` Ruby gem. `mrun` / `tmrun` / `zjrun` only need tmux or zellij (whichever backend is selected) — no sesh dependency.
461
462	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
463	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
464	| `sesh-sessions` | function | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` (zsh widget: `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh`; bash ble.sh binding: `dot_config/bash/06_sesh.bash.tmpl`) | fzf popup picker for all sesh sessions (also bound to `Alt+S` in both shells) |
465	| `sesh-here` / `shere` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Lightweight: bare shell session at `$PWD` (no nvim, no project layout). Pass args/`-c CMD` to override |
466	| `sesh-root` / `sroot` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Connect sesh to current git root (falls back to `$PWD`); honors sesh.toml wildcards/default |
467	| `sesh-code` / `scode` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Repo-scoped coding-agent layout: nvim 75% \| `specstory run [agent]` 25%, plus btop window. Session named `coding-agent/<repo>` (collision-safe). Refuses outside git repos. Flags: `--on-exit shell\|kill\|restart`, `--no-specstory` |
468	| `sesh-vibe` / `svibe` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Parametric multi-agent layout: `svibe [N] [CLI]` (homogeneous) or `svibe --agents claude,codex,opencode,…` (heterogeneous). N tiled agent panes + lazygit window + nvim window. Session named `vibe/<repo>`. Same `--on-exit` / `--no-specstory` flags as scode. Requires bash 4+ when invoked from bash |
469	| `herdr-vibe` / `hvibe` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` | **herdr** analog of `svibe` (needs the `herdr` server + `jq`). `hvibe [N] [CLI]` or `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode`. Builds workspace `vibe/<repo>`: `agents` tab with N even-width agent panes (`--tab-per-agent` → one tab each) + `git` + `edit` tabs. Reuses svibe's specstory/on-exit/git-root logic. Idempotent per repo. Attaches when run outside herdr (just focuses inside). Same `--on-exit` / `--no-specstory` / `--min-width` flags, plus `--session NAME` (target a running herdr session; default = current/`default`) |
470	| `herdr-code` / `hcode` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` | **herdr** analog of `scode` (needs `herdr` + `jq`). Builds workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`: `editor` tab (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + `monitor` tab (btop). Refuses outside git repos. Attaches when run outside herdr. Flags: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `-a/--agent`, `--session NAME` |
471	| `herdr-here` / `hhere` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` | **herdr** analog of `shere` (needs `herdr` + `jq`). Lightweight: creates a plain workspace at `$PWD` (or `-p DIR`), focuses + attaches it — **no** git repo and **no** agent layout, just a shell. Bare args / `-c CMD` run in the root pane. Idempotent per dir-basename. `-p DIR` is absolutized in-shell (relative paths OK; a non-directory is a hard error — herdr resolves a relative `--cwd` server-side and would silently open `$HOME`). Flags: `-p/--path`, `-c/--command`, `--no-attach`, `--session NAME` |
472	| `herdr-root` / `hroot` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` | **herdr** analog of `sroot`. Like `hhere` but the workspace opens at the current git root (falls back to `$PWD`). Thin wrapper over `hhere`; all flags except `--path` pass through |
473	| `herdr-mark` / `hmark` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` | Flag a herdr pane as **review-pending** (⭐) — defaults to the current pane (`$HERDR_PANE_ID`), or pass `hmark w1:p1`. Uses a herdr metadata token (`review`), orthogonal to agent state, so peeking into a done pane (→ idle) does **not** clear it. Also on `prefix+m` (toggle); list flagged panes via `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i`. Logic in `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` |
474	| `herdr-unmark` / `hunmark` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` | Clear a pane's review-pending (⭐) flag (default: current pane) |
475	| `try-sesh` / `tsesh` | function / alias | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | Open a `try` ephemeral workspace and immediately connect via sesh |
476	| `mrun` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh` | Fire-and-forget: detached tmux/zellij session running CMD at `$PWD`, returns immediately. `mrun [-b tmux\|zellij] [-n NAME] [-d DIR] [-f] [--on-exit shell\|kill\|restart] [-k] [--] CMD [ARGS...]`. Default `--on-exit shell` keeps the session alive after CMD exits (drops to login shell, re-run via history-Up); `-k` restores fire-and-forget kill semantics. Backend default tmux (override via `$MRUN_BACKEND`). Soft-warns on TUI commands. Prints attach hint to stderr |
477	| `tmrun` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh` | `mrun -b tmux`. Detached tmux session running CMD; attach with `tmux attach -t NAME` |
478	| `zjrun` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh` | `mrun -b zellij`. Generates ephemeral KDL under `$TMPDIR/mrun-layout-*` (with `default_tab_template` so the standard tab-bar / status-bar plugins are restored), spawns detached zellij session; attach with `zellij attach NAME` |
479	| `agent-wakeup` | function | `dot_config/shell/62_agent_wakeup.sh` | Wrapper for `~/.config/television/agent-wakeup.py`: list quota-blocked agent panes, schedule/cancel pueue-backed wakeups, or send `continue` now |
480	| `agent-continue-at` | function | `dot_config/shell/62_agent_wakeup.sh` | Shortcut for `agent-wakeup schedule`; examples: `agent-continue-at --pane %12 --at 01:52am`, `agent-continue-at --current --delay 70m` |
481	| `tmux-kill-clean` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Clear tmux-resurrect's `last` auto-restore pointer, then `tmux kill-server` so an intentional full quit does not resurrect stale sessions |
482	| `tmux-forget-last` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Clear only tmux-resurrect's `last` auto-restore pointer; historical snapshots stay available for manual restore |

486	## Worktree Management
487
488	> Requires `worktrunk` (`wt`) and/or `workmux` (`wm`). `wtcd` also requires `jq` + `fzf`.
489	>
490	> Worktrunk's own aliases (`wt sw`, `wt ls`, `wt rm`, `wt cc`, `wt oc`) are defined in `dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml`, not in zsh — they work from any shell and from the interactive picker.
491	>
492	> Workmux (`wm`) is a separate tool that coexists with worktrunk; it's the source of the 🤖/💬/✅ icons in the tmux window list. See [docs/tools/workmux.md](../tools/workmux.md) for the wt-vs-wm split.
493
494	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
495	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
496	| `wt` | function | `dot_config/shell/37_worktrunk.sh` | Wrapper around the `wt` binary that captures `cd`/`exec` directives so `wt switch` actually changes the parent shell's `$PWD` (eval'd from `wt config shell init zsh`) |
497	| `wtcd` | function | `dot_config/shell/37_worktrunk.sh` | fzf-tmux picker over `wt list --format=json` paths; `cd`s into the chosen worktree WITHOUT switching tmux/sesh session — useful for peeking at sibling worktrees |
498	| `wm` | alias | `dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh` | Short alias for `workmux` (defined only on macOS — Linux ansible install creates a `wm` symlink in `~/.local/bin`). See [docs/tools/workmux.md](../tools/workmux.md) |
499	| `wmsb` | alias | `dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh` | `workmux sidebar` — toggle the always-visible agent status panel; also enables 10s pane-silence interrupted-agent detection |
500	| `wmclear` | function | `dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh` | Manual reset for stuck `@workmux_status` markers. `wmclear` clears current window; `wmclear N` clears window N; `wmclear --all` nukes every marker in current session. Workaround for the upstream sticky `working` (🤖) state |
501	| `tmux_status_set` | function | `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` | Generic per-window tmux badge: `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 [target]` writes `@my_build_status`. POSIX, sourced by both zsh + bash. See [workmux.md → Reusing the per-window status mechanism](../tools/workmux.md#reusing-the-per-window-status-mechanism-without-workmux) |
502	| `tmux_status_get` | function | `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` | Read back a `@<name>_status` marker (empty + nonzero exit if unset) |
503	| `tmux_status_clear` | function | `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` | Unset a marker on current or `target` window |
504	| `tmux_status_clear_all` | function | `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` | Walk every window in every session, unset `@<name>_status` |

569	### Proxy helpers
570
571	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs). Detection order: env → **macOS System Proxy** (when HTTPEnable and a loopback port is listening — what Clash Verge / CFW "System Proxy" writes) → Clash Verge / mihomo / CFW config files whose declared port is actually open → probe ports `7897/7890/7891/17890/1087/8118/8080`. Preferring System Proxy avoids a stale `~/.config/clash` winning over a live Verge instance on `7897`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block. Copilot Node clients need `HTTPS_PROXY` / `--proxy-env` separately — see [docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](../tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md).
572
573	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
574	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
575	| `withproxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a single command with proxy env vars exported to the child only (e.g. `withproxy curl ...`) |
576	| `try_direct_then_proxy` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Run a command direct; on failure, retry via `withproxy`. Used as the default for reader functions. |
577	| `proxy-on` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Export `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` in the current shell |
578	| `proxy-off` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Unset all proxy env vars in the current shell |
579	| `proxy-status` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Report state: **active** (exported), **available** (detected), or **unavailable** |
580	| `proxy-test` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Test detected proxy egress with `curl https://www.google.com/generate_204` (HTTP, not ICMP ping) |
581	| `proxy-refresh` | function | `dot_config/shell/50_networking.sh` | Clear cached detection, re-probe, print status (use after toggling your proxy) |

583	### Docker registry egress (`docker-net`)
584
585	> `docker pull` runs in the **daemon**, so neither your shell's proxy env nor `~/.docker/config.json`'s `proxies.default` affects it — that block only reaches containers at `docker run` / `docker build` time. `docker-net` covers the daemon layer: it resolves the local proxy through the same `__net_detect_proxy` as `proxy-status`, writes `daemon.json`'s `proxies` key (Engine ≥ 23), and provides a per-pull fallback ladder for images no mirror carries. Full guide: [docs/tools/docker-net.md](../tools/docker-net.md). macOS: every verb works except `on`/`off`, which refuse because Docker Desktop / OrbStack run the daemon in a VM (proxy is a UI setting). Mirror strategy and the four install variants: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md).
586
587	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
588	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
589	| `docker-net status` | function | `dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh` | One screen: install shape, daemon proxy, mirrors in effect, detected local proxy, TUN interception, stale-config warnings |
590	| `docker-net doctor` | function | `dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh` | Nine-section diagnosis. `--deep` also probes ghcr/gcr/quay/registry.k8s.io from the **daemon's** side (nothing is downloaded) |
591	| `docker-net on` | function | `dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh` | Write `daemon.json` `proxies` from the detected proxy and restart the daemon (confirms first — a restart kills running containers) |
592	| `docker-net off` | function | `dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh` | Remove that block and restart |
593	| `docker-net mirrors` | function | `dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh` | Mirror health only — classifies DNS-gone / 403 / 502 / TLS-reset / timeout |
594	| `docker-net pull` | function | `dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh` | Pull via a fallback ladder: plain pull → explicit mirror prefix + retag → `skopeo copy` through the shell's proxy (no daemon restart) |

681	## macOS apps
682
683	> Graceful GUI app control via `osascript` + Apple Events. Prefer over `killall` for apps with state (OrbStack, Docker Desktop, Slack, etc.) — `quit` sends ⌘Q-equivalent, letting the app tear down cleanly. App NAME is the AppleScript name (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not bundle ID; passed via `osascript argv` so spaces/quotes are safe.
684
685	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
686	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
687	| `appquit <AppName>` | function | `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS), `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) | **Cross-platform.** macOS: Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q). Linux: `pkill -TERM -f <pattern>` resolved from `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` overrides or auto-derived from `.desktop` scan; Electron + Firefox honour SIGTERM as graceful quit. |
688	| `applaunch <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch in background (no focus steal). Linux: `gtk-launch <desktop-id>` via `setsid -f`. App-defined startup behaviour applies. |
689	| `appactivate <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** macOS: launch + bring to front. Linux: D-Bus call to GNOME `window-calls` extension if installed (best fidelity), otherwise falls back to `applaunch` (single-instance apps re-focus). |
690	| `apprestart <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** `appquit` + poll until process gone (≤15s) + `applaunch`. On Linux, launches the app even if it wasn't running (mirrors macOS silent-quit semantics). |
691	| `apprunning <AppName>` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Silent predicate; exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Linux backend: `pgrep -f <pattern>`. |
692	| `applist [--pids\|--all]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform.** Default: names of running apps the helper recognises. `--pids` adds `<pid>\t<name>` (used by `tv {mac,linux}-apps`). macOS lists foreground GUI apps via System Events; Linux enumerates registered overrides + auto-derived from `.desktop` scan filtered to running processes. Linux `--all` shows non-running entries too. |
693	| `appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, divergent fidelity.** macOS: best-effort "Not Responding" via timed-out Apple Event. Linux: only meaningful for apps registered with `--mpris=NAME` (Spotify, mpv, VLC); for Electron/Firefox/most apps it degrades to `apprunning` with a stderr note — no public Linux API analog to macOS Apple Events. |
694	| `linux_app_register NAME [OPTS]` | function | `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` | **Linux-only.** Register an app for the Linux `app-*` helpers — `--desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Typical call site: `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (sourced at shell startup, never auto-stubbed). Override file matters for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak where auto-derivation can't resolve the runtime binary path — see `pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md`. `linux_app_register --list` prints the current registry. |

698	## Media / AV

713	## System audio & playback
714
715	> Control **system volume / mute / playback / now-playing** from the shell. Cross-platform `sys*` verbs with the same names on both OSes (macOS `osascript`; Linux `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` + `playerctl`). Two tiers: `sysvol`/`sysmute` are **built-in** (always work, no extra tools); `sysplay`/`sysnow` need the **extended** tools from `installMediaControl=true`, degrading gracefully with an install hint otherwise. Remote one-key mute: `fleet exec --login --group all -- sysmute on`. Full story + caveats: [docs/tools/media-control.md](../tools/media-control.md).
716
717	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
718	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
719	| `sysvol [N\|+N\|-N]` | function | `dot_config/shell/57_macos_audio.sh.tmpl` (macOS), `dot_config/shell/57_linux_audio.sh.tmpl` (Linux) | **Cross-platform, built-in.** No arg prints current output volume (0–100); `N` sets absolute; `+N`/`-N` adjusts relative. macOS via `osascript`; Linux via first of `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` (override `SYSAUDIO_BACKEND`). |
720	| `sysmute [on\|off\|toggle]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, built-in.** Mute system output; default `toggle`. The remote one-key-mute primitive. |
721	| `sysplay [next\|previous]` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, extended.** No arg toggles play/pause; `next`/`previous` skip. macOS: `nowplaying-cli` (any app) or per-app AppleScript fallback (Music/Spotify). Linux: `playerctl` (MPRIS). Prints install hint if the extended tool is absent. |
722	| `sysnow` | function | same as above | **Cross-platform, extended.** Print the currently playing track (`Artist - Title`). ⚠ macOS 15.4+ locked the MediaRemote API, so this covers Music/Spotify only (not web audio); Linux reads any MPRIS player via `playerctl`. |

On zsh it force-reinitializes `zsh-vi-mode` after re-sourcing so vim mode survives the reload — OMZ's unconditional `bindkey -e` + zsh-vi-mode's once-only init guard otherwise silently drop you back to emacs keys ([pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/zsh-vim-mode-lost-after-source-rc.md)) |

750	| `abspath [-r] [-t] [PATH...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh` | Print absolute path(s): no args → logical cwd (like `pwd`); `PATH...` → one absolute path per line. Logical by default (normalizes `.`/`..`, keeps symlinks, existence not required); `-r`/`--resolve` → physical path (follows symlinks, must exist); `-t`/`--tilde` → abbreviate a `$HOME`-rooted result to `~`. stdout stays pipe-clean, so `abspath FILE \| x copy` grabs a path to the clipboard (fills the `realpath FILE \| x copy` hint in `x`'s help). Requires python3 |
751	| `cref [-a\|-c] [-L] [-n] [--] FILE[:LINE[-LINE]]` | function | `dot_config/shell/59_cref.sh` | Copy a Cursor/Claude-Code-style file mention (`@path`, `@path:12`, `@path:12-40`) to the clipboard — the shell twin of Neovim's `<leader>y` [copy-reference](../neovim/copy-reference.md) maps. Path flavor: default = **git-root-relative** (falls back to cwd/`~`/absolute the way nvim's `:~:.` does); `-a`/`--absolute` = machine-absolute; `-c`/`--cwd` = relative to `$PWD`. Line info comes from `FILE:LINE[-LINE]`, trailing positionals (`cref FILE 12 40`), or — with no FILE arg — the first stdin line in grep/ripgrep `FILE:LINE:…` format (`rg -n foo \| cref`); a trailing `:col[:text]` is dropped and `:12-12` collapses to `:12`. Copies via the `x` CLI (OSC 52, SSH-safe); `-n`/`--no-copy` prints only, `-L`/`--no-line` forces a bare `@path`. stdout stays pipe-clean; `Copied @…` toast on stderr. Requires python3 |

762	| `cpcmd [N]` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh` | Print + copy the **Nth-latest command's input line** (default N=1). Reads zsh history so works outside tmux too |

GUI/keyboard twins: right-click pane → "Copy pane path", `prefix + M-p` menu, and `prefix + C-p`. |

Reuses the AI Capture agent fallback (claude / opencode / codex / cursor-agent); 10-min cached in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/`. `-d` includes the visible area of each session's active pane (20-100 lines, self-capture skipped); set `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` in `~/.shellrc.adhoc` to make `-d` implicit (override with `--shallow`). `--sort closability` orders keep → check → safe (default: alphabetical); `--only {safe,check,keep}` filters to one tier. `-r` bypasses cache; `-i` opens fzf picker that switches client on Enter (also reachable via tmux `prefix + Space → Sessions → AI session summary`); `--dry-run` prints the prompt without calling the LLM. **On hosts with multiple tmux binaries** (apt + appimage, brew + system) export `TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/path/to/tmux` so tsum talks to the right server. |

811	## Copilot agent gateway
812
813	> Back Claude Code and Codex with models served by a **GitHub Copilot** subscription via the maintained [copilot-api fork](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api), installed once at a pinned version. Claude Code prefers Claude when entitled and otherwise gets a Sol/Terra/Luna role profile; Codex prefers native Responses OpenAI models. Full guide + **ToS/rate-limit risks** + settings-layer design: [docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](../tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md). One-time `copilot-proxy auth` is required. Reversible launchers keep committed project settings and chezmoi-managed user settings untouched.

817	| `copilot-proxy [start\|stop\|restart\|status\|doctor [--live]\|logs [N]\|whoami\|auth]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | Manage the pinned proxy (`@jeffreycao/copilot-api@2.1.0`). `doctor` distinguishes stale model cache, geo/policy filtering and network failure, validates main + Claude roles, and separately checks the remote ChatGPT `codex_apps` route. `--live` costs one inference quota unit; the Apps GET does not. |
818	| `claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [args...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | One-off Claude Code session on the proxy, **zero file writes**: auto-starts the proxy and injects the complete role-aware `ANTHROPIC_*` env per-process. An active `copilot-here` local pin outranks this env. Auto-wraps in `specstory run claude`; passthrough args preserve the configured `claude_cmd`. Revert = run plain `claude` next time. |
819	| `claude-copilot-once [--no-specstory] [args...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | One-shot session via the **`copilot-here` pin** (`settings.local.json`, which outranks shell env), auto-reverted: checks the proxy is up (notifies, **never** auto-starts) → `copilot-here on` → runs `claude-copilot` → `copilot-here off` on exit (even on Ctrl-C). Leaves an existing pin untouched. Reminds how to `copilot-proxy stop`. Needs `jq` |
820	| `codex-copilot [--no-specstory] [args...]` / `codex-copilot-once` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | Zero-persistence Codex launcher on the local Responses gateway. Auto-starts proxy/shim; explicit `-m` wins, otherwise live ranking is OpenAI/Codex → Claude → Gemini. Defaults to SpecStory and preserves project/user `codex_cmd`; neither name edits Codex config. |
821	| `copilot-run <cmd...>` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | Generic building block: auto-start the proxy, then run *any* command with the proxy env injected (e.g. `copilot-run specstory run claude`, `copilot-run claude --resume`) |
822	| `copilot-here [on\|off\|status]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | Sticky per-project toggle via the **gitignored** `./.claude/settings.local.json` (overrides the committed project settings, so `plansDirectory` stays untouched). `on` jq-merges the proxy env block + ensures git ignores the file (`.git/info/exclude`); `off` removes exactly those keys (keeps other content, deletes the file when empty); `status` shows pin + model and warns when the proxy is down. Needs `jq` |
823	| `copilot-model [<id>\|-l\|-c\|--auto]` | function | `dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh` | Switch the main model and derive a full Claude Code profile. `--auto` requires live `/v1/models`: Claude first, else Sol > Terra > GPT-5.5 > GPT-5.4 > GPT-5.3 Codex > Luna > mini > Gemini. OpenAI roles map Main/Fable/Opus=Sol, Sonnet=Terra, Haiku/background=Luna; `[1m]` comes from context metadata. Local pins store all roles; global state remains one main-id line. `-c` shows the complete profile. |
824	| `copilot-raycast [status\|generate [--dry-run] [--all]\|diff\|probe [MODEL]\|doctor\|edit]` | function | `dot_config/shell/45_copilot_raycast.sh` | Generate Raycast's AI **Custom Providers** file (`~/.config/raycast/ai/providers.yaml`) from the live proxy catalogue, so every Copilot model shows up in Quick AI / AI Chat / AI Commands. Each model id is filtered by a **zero-quota probe** — `POST /chat/completions` with `{"messages":[]}` is rejected before inference, and the error separates usable models (`messages must be non-empty`) from ones `/v1/models` only *claims* to serve (`model_not_supported`, `unsupported_api_for_model`); no field in the static metadata predicts this. `base_url` follows `_copilot_pinned_base` (the throttle shim when it is on), the sweep POSTs to `:4141` direct. Writes are backed up to `~/.local/state/copilot-raycast/backups/`, `yq`-validated and atomically moved — a malformed file makes Raycast **silently** drop *every* custom provider. Other providers in the file are preserved verbatim (needs `yq`). `status`/`doctor` read `raycastAI_modelRouterModelInfo` from Raycast's prefs to show what it actually loaded. Needs `jq` + `curl`; `yq` for validation/preservation. Env: `COPILOT_RAYCAST_{CONFIG,ID,LABEL,SUFFIX,TEMP,JOBS,PROBE_BASE,KEEP}` |

Idempotent per dir-basename. `-p DIR` is absolutized in-shell (relative paths OK; a non-directory is a hard error — herdr resolves a relative `--cwd` server-side and would silently open `$HOME`). 2	# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x (bash hand-rolled subcommand parser).

8	_x() {
9	    local context state state_descr line
10	    typeset -A opt_args
11
12	    _arguments -C \
13	        '1: :->subcommand' \
14	        '*::arg:->args'
15
16	    case "$state" in
17	        subcommand)
18	            local -a subs=(
19	                'copy:Copy stdin or FILE to system clipboard'
20	                'copy-file:Copy file objects to the desktop clipboard'

36	                        '--force[copy even if file looks like a private key]' \
37	                        '*:path:_files'
38	                    ;;

40	                    _arguments '*:target:_files'
41	                    ;;
42	            esac
43	            ;;
44	    esac
45	}
46

1	# 24_herdr.sh - herdr workspace layout helpers (shared backend; bash 4+ / zsh).
2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).
22
23	# Skip entirely if herdr isn't installed (it's a trial tool, not on every host).
24	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
25
26	# ── Internal helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
27
28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}
54
55	# Absolutize + validate a `-p/--path DIR` argument in THIS shell. Echoes the
56	# canonical (symlink-resolved) path; on a non-directory, echoes nothing and
57	# returns 1 after a message on stderr.
58	#
59	# LOAD-BEARING for every `--cwd` below: herdr resolves a *relative* `--cwd`
60	# against the SERVER's launch directory (wherever `herdr server` was started),
61	# not the caller's cwd — and on a miss it silently falls back to $HOME, so
62	# `hhere -p ../sibling` opens a workspace at `~` with no error anywhere. tmux
63	# resolves `new-session -c` client-side, which is why the sesh originals
64	# (shere/svibe/scode) never needed this.
65	# See pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md.
66	#
67	# `CDPATH=''` + `--` + `>/dev/null` keep a CDPATH hit from silently retargeting
68	# the cd or echoing the resolved dir into the capture.
69	# $1=dir  $2=caller name (for the error message)
70	function _herdr_abs_dir() {
71	    local abs
72	    abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
73	    if [ -z "$abs" ]; then
74	        echo "${2:-herdr}: --path is not a directory: $1" >&2
75	        return 1
76	    fi
77	    printf '%s\n' "$abs"
78	}
79
80	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
81	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
82	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
83	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
84	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
85	#
86	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
87	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
88	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
89	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
90	function _herdr_session_target() {
91	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
92	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
93	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
94	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
95	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
96	            | head -1)
97	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
98	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
99	            return 1
100	        fi
101	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
102	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
103	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
104	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
105	            return 1
106	        fi
107	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
108	        return 0
109	    fi
110	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
111	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
112	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
113	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
114	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
115	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
116	            | head -1)
117	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
118	    else
119	        printf 'default\t\n'
120	    fi
121	}
122
123	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
124	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
125	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
126	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
127	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
128	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
129	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
130	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
131	    local session="${1:-default}"
132	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
133	        herdr
134	    else
135	        herdr session attach "$session"
136	    fi
137	}

139	# ── hvibe: parametric multi-agent pack ──────────────────────────────────────
140	#
141	# A herdr "vibe" workspace: tab "agents" with N agent panes (side-by-side
142	# splits by default), tab "git" (lazygit), tab "edit" (nvim). Built directly
143	# with herdr CLI calls so pane count stays parametric.
144	#
145	# Workspace label: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (idempotent — re-running focuses it).
146	# Refuses outside a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo).
147	#
148	# Each agent pane is specstory-wrapped (known providers) and on-exit-wrapped,
149	# exactly like `svibe` — the wrapping helpers are shared, only the layout calls
150	# differ. herdr auto-detects agent state per pane, so all N agents surface
151	# individually in the sidebar even when they share the "agents" tab.
152	#
153	# Two modes for choosing agents (same as svibe):
154	#   Homogeneous (positional):  hvibe 3 codex        → 3 panes all codex
155	#   Heterogeneous (--agents):  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode
156	#
157	# --tab-per-agent puts each agent in its OWN tab (own rolled-up state dot in the
158	# sidebar) instead of side-by-side splits — better for many agents, since herdr
159	# has no even-out-splits command.
160	#
161	# Usage:
162	#   hvibe                                       # auto N × claude (specstory)
163	#   hvibe 2                                     # 2× claude
164	#   hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× specstory run codex
165	#   hvibe 2 opencode                            # 2× opencode (raw)
166	#   hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
167	#   hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
168	#   hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude, no md auto-save
169	#   hvibe --on-exit restart 2 codex             # auto-respawn loop
170	#   hvibe -p ~/repo 2 claude                    # explicit path
171	#   hvibe --no-attach 2 claude                  # create in background
172	function herdr-vibe() {
173	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hvibe: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
174
175	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
176	    local n_agents=0 n_agents_set=0 agent_cli="claude" agents_csv="" tab_per_agent=0
177	    local min_width="${HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
178	    # Stagger between pane launches so agents that share a global resource at
179	    # cold start (opencode's single SQLite DB + WAL pragma) don't race. Set 0
180	    # to launch all at once. Same rationale as svibe's SVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER.
181	    local launch_stagger="${HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER:-0.25}"
182
183	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
184	        case "$1" in
185	            -p|--path)       target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
186	            --on-exit)       on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
187	            --agents)        agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
188	            --session)       session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
189	            --min-width)     min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
190	            --tab-per-agent) tab_per_agent=1; shift ;;
191	            --no-specstory)  specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
192	            --specstory)     specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
193	            --no-attach)     no_attach=1; shift ;;
194	            -h|--help)
195	                cat <<'EOF'
196	hvibe — herdr multi-agent pack (herdr analog of svibe)
197
198	Usage:
199	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
200	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
201	  hvibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
202	        [--min-width COLS] [--tab-per-agent] [--session NAME] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
203
204	Builds a new herdr workspace `vibe/<repo>`:
205	  tab "agents" — N agent panes (side-by-side splits; each auto-detected in
206	                 the sidebar). --tab-per-agent → one tab per agent instead.
207	  tab "git"    — lazygit (falls back to `git status`)
208	  tab "edit"   — nvim
209	Idempotent: re-running in the same repo focuses the existing workspace.
210	Requires:  a git repo (pass -p DIR, or cd into one).
211
212	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session so
213	the new workspace is visible; run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses it.
214	--no-attach builds in the background either way.
215	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: the current session
216	when inside herdr, else the default session). Start a session first with
217	`herdr --session NAME`.
218
219	Two modes for choosing agents:
220	  Homogeneous:    hvibe 3 codex → 3 panes all codex
221	  Heterogeneous:  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode  (list length = panes)
222
223	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
224	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
225	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
226
227	--on-exit MODE (per pane, on Ctrl+C / clean exit):
228	  shell (default) — drop to a shell with a re-run hint
229	  kill            — let the pane close
230	  restart         — auto-respawn in a loop
231
232	--min-width COLS (default $HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80) auto-picks N when omitted:
233	  N = clamp(term_width / min-width, 1, 6)
234	$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER (seconds, default 0.25) delays each pane launch.
235
236	Examples:
237	  hvibe                                       # auto N × claude
238	  hvibe 3 codex                               # 3× codex
239	  hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode        # 3 panes, mixed
240	  hvibe --tab-per-agent --agents claude,codex # one tab each
241	  hvibe --no-specstory 2 claude               # raw claude
242	EOF
243	                return 0 ;;
244	            -*)              echo "hvibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
245	            *)               break ;;
246	        esac
247	    done
248
249	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
250	        echo "hvibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
251	        return 1
252	    fi
253	    if ! [[ "$launch_stagger" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
254	        echo "hvibe: HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER must be a non-negative number (got: $launch_stagger)" >&2
255	        return 1
256	    fi
257
258	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
259
260	    # Build the agents array (same two paths as svibe; mixing is rejected).
261	    local -a agents
262	    agents=()
263	    if [ -n "$agents_csv" ]; then
264	        if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
265	            echo "hvibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
266	            return 1
267	        fi
268	        local tok
269	        while IFS= read -r tok; do
270	            tok="${tok## }"; tok="${tok%% }"
271	            [ -n "$tok" ] && agents+=( "$tok" )
272	        done < <(printf '%s\n' "$agents_csv" | tr ',' '\n')
273	        if [ "${#agents[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
274	            echo "hvibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
275	            return 1
276	        fi
277	    else
278	        if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
279	            n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
280	        fi
281	        [ $# -gt 0 ] && agent_cli="$1"
282	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width. Clamp [1,6] (lower than svibe's 12:
283	        # herdr right-splits nest, so many panes get cramped — use
284	        # --tab-per-agent for more).
285	        if [ "$n_agents_set" -eq 0 ]; then
286	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
287	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
288	            (( n_agents > 6 )) && n_agents=6
289	        fi
290	        local k
291	        for (( k = 0; k < n_agents; k++ )); do agents+=( "$agent_cli" ); done
292	    fi
293
294	    case "$on_exit" in
295	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
296	        *) echo "hvibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
297	    esac
298
299	    # Resolve git root (required, like svibe). `-p DIR` is absolutized first so
300	    # a bad path reports itself instead of masquerading as "not a git repo".
301	    local repo_root
302	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
303	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hvibe) || return 1
304	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
305	    else
306	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
307	    fi
308	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
309	        echo "hvibe: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or cd into a repo." >&2
310	        return 1
311	    fi
312
313	    # Fail-fast: every agent CLI must exist in PATH.
314	    local a missing=""
315	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
316	        command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $a"
317	    done
318	    if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
319	        echo "hvibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH:$missing" >&2
320	        echo "       Available: claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini (install as needed)." >&2
321	        return 1
322	    fi
323
324	    local repo label
325	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
326	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/$repo")
327
328	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
329	    # A non-empty sess_sock means an explicit --session override — scope it with
330	    # `local -x` so child `herdr` calls see it but the user's shell is untouched.
331	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
332	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
333	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
334	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
335	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
336
337	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
338	    local existing
339	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
340	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
341	        echo "hvibe: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
342	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
343	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
344	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
345	        fi
346	        return 0
347	    fi
348
349	    # Create the workspace; capture the initial pane/tab (become the first agent).
350	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
351	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
352	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
353	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
354	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
355	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
356	        echo "hvibe: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
357	        return 1
358	    fi
359
360	    local first_agent="${agents[@]:0:1}"
361	    if [ "$tab_per_agent" -eq 1 ]; then
362	        # One tab per agent. Initial tab hosts the first agent (labeled by it).
363	        herdr tab rename "$t0" "$first_agent" >/dev/null 2>&1
364	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
365	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
366	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
367	            _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" "$a" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")"
368	        done
369	    else
370	        # Side-by-side splits in one "agents" tab. Thread `prev` so each new pane
371	        # splits off the previous one → predictable left-to-right columns.
372	        herdr tab rename "$t0" agents >/dev/null 2>&1
373	        herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$first_agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
374	        # Even columns: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so set each
375	        # split's ratio explicitly. --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane
376	        # being split (the left one); the new pane gets the rest. Splitting the
377	        # rightmost pane on step m (of N-1) with ratio 1/(N-m+1) leaves every
378	        # finalized column at 1/N width.
379	        local n_total="${#agents[@]}" prev="$p0" np m=1 ratio
380	        for a in "${agents[@]:1}"; do
381	            [ "$launch_stagger" != "0" ] && sleep "$launch_stagger"
382	            ratio=$(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.4f\", 1/($n_total-$m+1)}")
383	            np=$(herdr pane split "$prev" --direction right --ratio "$ratio" --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
384	                | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
385	            if [ -n "$np" ]; then
386	                herdr pane run "$np" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$a" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
387	                prev="$np"
388	            fi
389	            m=$((m+1))
390	        done
391	    fi
392
393	    # git + edit tabs (same on-exit treatment as the agents).
394	    local git_inner git_label
395	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then git_inner="lazygit"; else git_inner="git status"; fi
396	    git_label="${git_inner%% *}"
397	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" git  "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$git_inner" "$on_exit" "$git_label")"
398	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" edit "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")"
399
400	    # Focus the workspace + agents tab unless --no-attach.
401	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
402	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
403	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
404	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
405	    fi
406	}
407
408	# ── hcode: repo-scoped single-agent layout ──────────────────────────────────
409	#
410	# herdr analog of `scode`. Workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
411	#   tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
412	#   tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top fallback)
413	# Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
414	#
415	# Usage:
416	#   hcode                     # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
417	#   hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
418	#   hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
419	#   hcode --no-specstory claude
420	#   hcode --on-exit kill claude
421	#   hcode -p ~/work/foo
422	function herdr-code() {
423	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hcode: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
424
425	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto" session_arg=""
426	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
427	        case "$1" in
428	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
429	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
430	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
431	            --session)      session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
432	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
433	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
434	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
435	            --agents)
436	                echo "hcode: --agents is hvibe-only (hcode is single-agent)." >&2
437	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: hvibe --agents '$2'" >&2
438	                return 1 ;;
439	            -h|--help)
440	                cat <<'EOF'
441	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
442
443	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
444	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
445
446	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
447	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
448	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)
449	Idempotent per repo; refuses outside a git repo.
450
451	Attach behavior: run from OUTSIDE herdr → attaches a client to the session;
452	run from INSIDE herdr → just focuses. --no-attach builds in the background.
453	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
454	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
455
456	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
457	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
458	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
459
460	--on-exit MODE (per pane): shell (default) | kill | restart
461
462	Examples:
463	  hcode                     # default agent (specstory → claude)
464	  hcode codex               # right pane: specstory run codex
465	  hcode opencode            # right pane: opencode (raw)
466	  hcode --on-exit kill claude
467	EOF
468	                return 0 ;;
469	            -*)             echo "hcode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
470	            *)              [ -z "$agent" ] && agent="$1"; shift ;;
471	        esac
472	    done
473
474	    case "$on_exit" in
475	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
476	        *) echo "hcode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
477	    esac
478
479	    local repo_root
480	    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
481	        target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hcode) || return 1
482	        repo_root=$(cd -- "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 && _sesh_git_root)
483	    else
484	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
485	    fi
486	    if [ -z "$repo_root" ]; then
487	        echo "hcode: not inside a git repo. Pass -p DIR, or use hvibe in any dir." >&2
488	        return 1
489	    fi
490
491	    if [ -n "$agent" ] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
492	        echo "hcode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
493	        return 1
494	    fi
495
496	    local repo label
497	    repo=$(basename "$repo_root")
498	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/$repo")
499
500	    # Resolve target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
501	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
502	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
503	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
504	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
505	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
506
507	    local existing
508	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
509	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
510	        echo "hcode: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
511	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
512	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
513	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
514	        fi
515	        return 0
516	    fi
517
518	    local ws_json ws p0 t0
519	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$repo_root" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
520	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
521	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
522	    t0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.tab_id // empty')
523	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ] || [ -z "$t0" ]; then
524	        echo "hcode: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
525	        return 1
526	    fi
527
528	    # editor tab: nvim in the initial pane, agent split off to the right at ~25%.
529	    # --ratio is the fraction KEPT by the pane being split (nvim/left), so 0.75
530	    # leaves nvim at 75% and the new agent pane at 25%.
531	    herdr tab rename "$t0" editor >/dev/null 2>&1
532	    herdr pane run "$p0" "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")" >/dev/null 2>&1
533	    local ap
534	    ap=$(herdr pane split "$p0" --direction right --ratio 0.75 --cwd "$repo_root" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
535	        | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty')
536	    [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane run "$ap" "$(_herdr_agent_cmd "$agent" "$specstory_mode" "$on_exit")" >/dev/null 2>&1
537
538	    # monitor tab.
539	    local mon
540	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=btop
541	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then mon=htop
542	    else                                       mon=top
543	    fi
544	    _herdr_tool_tab "$ws" "$repo_root" monitor "$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$mon" "$on_exit" "$mon")"
545
546	    # Focus editor tab, nvim pane (left neighbor of the agent pane).
547	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
548	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
549	        herdr tab focus "$t0" >/dev/null 2>&1
550	        [ -n "$ap" ] && herdr pane focus --direction left --pane "$ap" >/dev/null 2>&1
551	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
552	    fi
553	}

555	# ── hhere: plain "open a workspace here + attach" ────────────────────────────
556	#
557	# herdr analog of `shere` (sesh-here). The lightweight counterpart to
558	# hvibe/hcode: create a herdr workspace at $PWD (or -p DIR), focus it, and
559	# attach a client when run from outside herdr. NO git requirement and NO agent
560	# layout — just a shell in the workspace root pane. This fills the gap where
561	# every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent pack; with
562	# tmux `tmux new-session` lands you in $PWD directly, but herdr adds a Workspace
563	# layer, so without this you'd launch herdr, create a space (opens at $HOME),
564	# then cd manually.
565	#
566	# Smart argument handling (mirrors shere):
567	#   hhere                          # plain shell at $PWD
568	#   hhere npm run dev              # bare args → run as the root-pane command
569	#   hhere -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
570	#   hhere -p ~/proj                # explicit path, plain shell
571	#   hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev    # explicit path + command
572	#
573	# `-p DIR` is absolutized in THIS shell before it reaches herdr — the server
574	# resolves a relative `--cwd` against its own launch directory and falls back to
575	# $HOME on a miss (silently). A non-existent DIR is a hard error.
576	#
577	# The command (if any) runs raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping. That agent
578	# treatment stays with hcode/hvibe; hhere is deliberately lightweight.
579	#
580	# Idempotent per label (bare basename of the dir, matching herdr's own native
581	# auto-label convention). Caveat: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to the root
582	# pane's LIVE cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see docs/tools/herdr.md § cwd
583	# & workspace-naming), so the reuse is best-effort — if the label has drifted, a
584	# re-run creates a fresh workspace (arguably correct: you're elsewhere now).
585	#
586	# Usage:
587	#   hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
588	function herdr-here() {
589	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hhere: jq is required." >&2; return 1; }
590
591	    local cmd="" target="" no_attach=0 session_arg=""
592	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
593	        case "$1" in
594	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
595	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
596	            --session)    session_arg="$2"; shift 2 ;;
597	            --no-attach)  no_attach=1; shift ;;
598	            -h|--help)
599	                cat <<'EOF'
600	hhere — open a plain herdr workspace here + attach (herdr analog of shere)
601
602	Usage: hhere [--path DIR] [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
603
604	Creates a herdr workspace at DIR (default $PWD), focuses it, and — when run
605	from OUTSIDE herdr — attaches a client so it is visible. No git repo required
606	and no agent layout: just a shell in the workspace root pane. For agent
607	layouts use hcode (single-agent) or hvibe (multi-agent).
608
609	Smart argument handling:
610	  hhere                        # plain shell at $PWD
611	  hhere npm run dev            # bare args → run as the root-pane command
612	  hhere -c "npm run dev"       # explicit --command flag
613	  hhere -p ~/proj              # explicit path, plain shell
614	  hhere -p ../sibling          # relative paths resolve against YOUR shell
615	  hhere -p ~/proj npm run dev  # explicit path + command
616
617	--path DIR is resolved (and symlink-canonicalized) here, in your shell, before
618	it reaches herdr — a DIR that does not exist is a hard error, not a silent
619	workspace at $HOME.
620
621	Idempotent: re-running in the same dir focuses the existing workspace.
622	--session NAME targets a running herdr session (default: current session when
623	inside herdr, else the default session; start one with `herdr --session NAME`).
624	--no-attach builds in the background.
625	EOF
626	                return 0 ;;
627	            -*)           echo "hhere: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
628	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
629	        esac
630	    done
631	    [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$cmd" ] && cmd="$*"
632	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
633
634	    # ABSOLUTIZE — load-bearing, do NOT pass `$target` through verbatim; herdr
635	    # resolves a relative `--cwd` server-side and falls back to $HOME on a miss.
636	    # See _herdr_abs_dir above.
637	    target=$(_herdr_abs_dir "$target" hhere) || return 1
638
639	    local label
640	    label=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
641
642	    # Resolve the target herdr session (optional --session; else ambient/default).
643	    local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
644	    sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
645	    sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}
646	    sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
647	    [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
648
649	    # Idempotent: focus an existing workspace instead of duplicating.
650	    local existing
651	    existing=$(_herdr_ws_by_label "$label")
652	    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
653	        echo "hhere: workspace '$label' already exists ($existing) — focusing." >&2
654	        if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
655	            herdr workspace focus "$existing" >/dev/null 2>&1
656	            _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
657	        fi
658	        return 0
659	    fi
660
661	    local ws_json ws p0
662	    ws_json=$(herdr workspace create --cwd "$target" --label "$label" --no-focus 2>/dev/null)
663	    ws=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id // empty')
664	    p0=$(printf '%s' "$ws_json" | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
665	    if [ -z "$ws" ] || [ -z "$p0" ]; then
666	        echo "hhere: failed to create workspace (is the herdr server running?)." >&2
667	        return 1
668	    fi
669
670	    # Optional command in the root pane (raw — no specstory/on-exit wrapping).
671	    [ -n "$cmd" ] && herdr pane run "$p0" "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1
672
673	    if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then
674	        herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
675	        _herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"
676	    fi
677	}
678
679	# ── hroot: like hhere but at the git-root ────────────────────────────────────
680	#
681	# herdr analog of `sroot` (sesh-root). Same as hhere except the target resolves
682	# to the current git top-level (falls back to $PWD outside a repo). Thin wrapper
683	# over herdr-here so there is one code path; -p is not accepted (the root IS the
684	# path), everything else (-c / bare command / --session / --no-attach) passes
685	# through.
686	#
687	# Usage:
688	#   hroot                          # plain shell at git-root (else $PWD)
689	#   hroot npm run dev              # + run a command
690	#   hroot -c "npm run dev"         # explicit --command flag
691	function herdr-root() {
692	    case "$1" in
693	        -h|--help)
694	            cat <<'EOF'
695	hroot — open a plain herdr workspace at the git-root + attach (analog of sroot)
696
697	Usage: hroot [--command CMD] [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [CMD...]
698
699	Like hhere, but the workspace opens at the current git top-level (falls back to
700	$PWD outside a repo). All flags except --path pass through to hhere.
701

1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_space-root.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Print the WORKSPACE ("space") root directory for a herdr workspace, given
6	# either a workspace id (`wP`) or any pane id inside it (`wP:p29`).
7	#
8	# Why this script exists: **herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd.** `herdr
9	# workspace get` returns label / number / tab_count / pane_count and nothing
10	# else (verified on 0.7.5), so "the directory this space is about" has to be
11	# derived. It is the SSOT for that derivation — three consumers would otherwise
12	# each carry their own copy and silently drift:
13	#
14	#   new-tab-at-space-root.sh   prefix+C  (new tab at the space dir)
15	#   pane-copy.sh dir           prefix+d  / the "Copy space dir" Quick Action
16	#   herdr-sesh tv channel      prefix+T, Alt+Y (copy any workspace's dir)
17	#
18	# "Space root" = the cwd of the workspace's OLDEST surviving tab. Note `.number`
19	# is a monotonic creation counter, NOT the display index (a workspace can hold
20	# tabs numbered 10/13/14/15 displayed as 1/2/3/4), so sort_by(.number)[0] is the
21	# oldest tab, which is the right notion of "the tab this space started as". We
22	# prefer the LIVE cwd (`foreground_cwd`) over the shell's startup cwd.
23	#
24	# CAVEAT — this is a best-effort answer, not an authoritative one. herdr's
25	# sidebar LABEL is pinned when the workspace is created and is never re-derived,
26	# so once you `cd` inside the oldest tab the two drift apart and nothing in the
27	# API can recover the original path. Observed live: a space labelled
28	# `2026-05-14-grafana-provisioning-with-docker-otel-lgtm` whose oldest tab sits
29	# in `…/grafana/dashboards/Jingle.AI`. There is no better source — `workspace
30	# get` and `herdr api snapshot` return the same cwd-less workspace object.
31	#
32	# A pane id is resolved through `herdr pane get` rather than by string-splitting
33	# on the ":" — the id format is hierarchical in practice (`wP` / `wP:t7` /
34	# `wP:pA`) but that is an observation, not a documented guarantee.
35	#
36	# Usage:
37	#   space-root.sh <workspace_id|pane_id>
38	#   space-root.sh                        # defaults to the current pane's space
39	set -eu
40
41	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "space-root: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
42	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "space-root: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
43
44	target="${1:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}"
45
46	# No id anywhere (ran outside herdr's keybind context) → ask for the focused pane.
47	if [ -z "$target" ]; then
48	    target=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
49	fi
50	[ -n "$target" ] || { echo "space-root: no workspace or pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)" >&2; exit 64; }
51
52	case "$target" in
53	    *:*)
54	        wid=$(herdr pane get "$target" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // ""')
55	        [ -n "$wid" ] || { echo "space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $target" >&2; exit 1; }
56	        ;;
57	    *)
58	        wid="$target"
59	        ;;
60	esac
61
62	# Root tab = the workspace's OLDEST tab (lowest creation counter, not display index).
63	root_tab=$(herdr tab list --workspace "$wid" 2>/dev/null \
64	    | jq -r '.result.tabs | sort_by(.number) | .[0].tab_id // ""')
65	[ -n "$root_tab" ] || { echo "space-root: no tabs in workspace $wid" >&2; exit 1; }
66
67	# `herdr tab get` returns tab metadata only (no pane cwd), so read the root tab's
68	# pane cwd from the full pane list. foreground_cwd = where the tab actually is
69	# now; .cwd = the shell's startup dir, used only when there is no live reading.
70	root=$(herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg t "$root_tab" \
71	    '.result.panes | map(select(.tab_id==$t)) | .[0] // {} | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
72	[ -n "$root" ] || { echo "space-root: could not resolve root dir for $root_tab" >&2; exit 1; }
73
74	printf '%s\n' "$root"
75
```

4	#
5	# Run an ARBITRARY command in the focused pane's cwd, inside a floating popup that
6	# closes by itself when the command exits. This is the generalisation of the
7	# hardcoded `prefix+G` (lazygit) binding — the tmux `display-popup -E` experience,
8	# with a command you pick or type instead of one baked into the config.
9	#
10	# Why a popup and not the alternatives:
11	#   - `type = "pane"` (prefix+G/M/N/`) splits the TILED layout for the duration.
12	#   - `prefix+c` + type + `exit` is four steps and churns the tab bar.
13	#   - `type = "popup"` (herdr >= 0.7.4) is session-modal and floats ABOVE the
14	#     layout, so nothing reflows and you land exactly where you were.
15	# It also cannot live as a herdr-plus Quick Action (prefix+y): those run through
16	# `sh -c` with no PTY/stdin — the same reason btop/nvtop are command panes — and
17	# every Quick Action is a fixed command string with no free-text field.
18	#
19	# Bound to prefix+E in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
20	#
21	# Usage:
22	#   run-command.sh [--cwd DIR] [--sh] [--] [QUERY...]
23	# --cwd  directory to run in; defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD (injected by the
24	#        keybind) → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd → $PWD. Preferring the env var
25	#        means this keeps working even when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a
26	#        stale server.
27	# --sh   run via `sh -c` (fast, no aliases) instead of the default `$SHELL -ic`
28	#        (sources the interactive rc, so this repo's aliases/functions resolve).
29	# QUERY  seeds the picker (and, with no fzf, prefills nothing — it is run as-is).
30	#
31	# Exit behaviour is governed by HERDR_RUN_HOLD:
32	#   fail (default)  close on success, wait for a key on non-zero exit
33	#   always          always wait for a key
34	#   never           never wait
35	#
36	# Consumers: the prefix+E keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
37	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Run any command in a popup".
38	set -eu
39
40	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [--cwd DIR] [--sh] [--] [QUERY...]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
41
42	cwd=""
43	use_sh=0
44	query=""
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
49	        --sh) use_sh=1; shift ;;
50	        -h|--help) usage ;;
51	        --) shift; break ;;
52	        -*) usage ;;
53	        *) break ;;

59	fi
