```text
67	    pane="${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-}"
68	    if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	        pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
70	    fi
71	    if [ -n "$pane" ]; then
72	        cwd=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
73	            | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // .result.pane.cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
74	    fi
75	fi
76	[ -n "$cwd" ] && [ -d "$cwd" ] || cwd="$PWD"
77
78	# --- history source ---------------------------------------------------------
79	# $HISTFILE is a zsh interactive var and is NOT exported into the `sh -c` context
80	# a keybind command runs in, so default it explicitly.
81	histfile="${HISTFILE:-$HOME/.zsh_history}"
82
83	# Newest-first, de-duplicated, timestamps stripped.
84	#   - LC_ALL=C is REQUIRED: ~/.zsh_history carries non-UTF8 bytes and BSD sed
85	#     aborts with "sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence" under a UTF-8 locale.
86	#   - The reverse is done in awk because `tail -r` is BSD-only and `tac` GNU-only.
87	#   - Lines ending in a backslash are multi-line history entries; skip them.
88	_history() {
89	    [ -r "$histfile" ] || return 0
90	    LC_ALL=C sed 's/^: [0-9]*:[0-9]*;//' "$histfile" 2>/dev/null \
91	        | grep -v '\\$' \
92	        | awk 'NF' \
93	        | awk '{a[NR]=$0} END{for(i=NR;i>0;i--) if(!seen[a[i]]++) print a[i]}'
94	}
95
96	# --- pick the command -------------------------------------------------------
97	cmd=""
98	if command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
99	    # --print-query + --expect together make the outcomes distinguishable.
100	    # Line layout is NOT fixed — fzf omits trailing lines it has nothing for:
101	    #
102	    #   Enter     with a match     rc 0    query \n ""        \n selection
103	    #   Alt+Enter with a match     rc 0    query \n alt-enter \n selection
104	    #   Enter     with no match    rc 1    query                              (1 line)
105	    #   Alt+Enter with no match    rc 1    query \n alt-enter
106	    #   Esc                        rc 130  —
107	    #
108	    # So the key is read from line 2 (empty/absent ⇒ plain Enter) and the
109	    # command from line 3 only on rc 0; every other path falls back to the
110	    # query on line 1. Verified against fzf directly with -1/-0.
111	    #
112	    # Alt+Enter exists because plain Enter cannot express "run exactly what I
113	    # typed" while fzf still has a match: if you type `ls -la` and history holds
114	    # `ls -la /tmp`, Enter takes the history entry. That made the picker feel
115	    # like it could only replay old commands. Alt+ (not Ctrl+) per the repo's
116	    # keybinding convention.
117	    set +e
118	    out=$(_history | fzf \
119	        --print-query --expect=alt-enter --no-sort --height=100% --border \
120	        --query="$query" \
121	        --header='enter: run highlighted · alt-enter: run what you typed · esc: cancel' \
122	        --prompt="run [$(basename "$cwd")]> ")
123	    rc=$?
124	    set -e
125	    case "$rc" in
126	        0 | 1) ;;
127	        *) exit 0 ;;   # 130 = Esc, or fzf failed — run nothing
128	    esac
129	    key=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '2p')
130	    if [ "$key" = "alt-enter" ]; then
131	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p')      # literal query, always
132	    elif [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
133	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '3p')      # highlighted selection
134	    else
135	        cmd=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n '1p')      # no match → the query
136	    fi
137	else
138	    if [ -n "$query" ]; then
139	        cmd="$query"
140	    else
141	        printf 'run [%s]> ' "$(basename "$cwd")"
142	        IFS= read -r cmd || exit 0
143	    fi
144	fi
145
146	[ -n "$cmd" ] || exit 0
147
148	# --- run it -----------------------------------------------------------------
149	cd "$cwd" || { echo "run-command: cannot cd to $cwd" >&2; exit 1; }
150
151	set +e
152	if [ "$use_sh" -eq 1 ]; then
153	    sh -c "$cmd"
154	else
155	    # -i so the interactive rc is sourced and this repo's aliases/functions exist.
156	    "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -ic "$cmd"
157	fi
158	rc=$?
159	set -e
160
161	# --- hold policy ------------------------------------------------------------
162	hold="${HERDR_RUN_HOLD:-fail}"
163	case "$hold" in
164	    never) ;;
165	    always) _wait=1 ;;
166	    *) [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && _wait=1 ;;
167	esac
168	if [ "${_wait:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
169	    [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && printf '\n[exit %s] ' "$rc" || printf '\n[exit 0] '
170	    printf 'press Enter to close…'
171	    IFS= read -r _ || true
172	fi
173
174	exit "$rc"
175
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
3:[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
9:  - macOS is **deliberately not** Homebrew, and it is the only tool in this repo where that's true. Upstream disables `herdr update` on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs because the package manager owns the binary — which removes the *only* pane-preserving upgrade path and leaves a server restart, i.e. killing every pane process, as the sole option. The formula was dropped in favour of the release binary so macOS gets `--handoff` too. Boxes provisioned before the switch are migrated by a one-time `brew uninstall herdr` in the same role (leaving both installed would put two binaries on `PATH` and risk a client/server `protocol_mismatch` against yourself).
13:> **`herdr update` refuses to run from inside a herdr pane.** The handoff replaces the server process that owns the pane you are typing in, so it fails closed:
16:> $ herdr update --handoff          # from a pane inside herdr
17:> update failed: run `herdr update` outside herdr after detaching from the session
20:> The flow is **detach (`prefix+q`) → run it in a plain terminal → reattach with bare `herdr`**. Detaching does not kill anything (client close ≠ session loss), and `--handoff` then swaps the server without exiting pane processes — verified 2026-07 upgrading 0.7.1 → 0.7.5 with a Claude Code session running in a pane, which survived uninterrupted. `just upgrade-herdr` encodes this: it *skips with instructions* rather than failing when it detects `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`, so `just upgrade-all` from a herdr pane doesn't die here. Full trace: [`pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md).
...
```

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
5	# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
6	# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
7	# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
8	# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
9	# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
10	# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
11	#
12	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
13	# new contents on stdout.
14	#
15	# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
19	#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
22	#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
23	#
24	# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
25	# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
26	# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
27	# round-trips both.
28	#
29	# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
30	# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
31	# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
32	# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
33	#
34	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
35	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
36	# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
37	# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
38	# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
39	set -eu
40
41	tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
42	trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM
43
44	cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
45	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
46	TOML
47
48	live=$(cat)
49
50	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -
54	else
55	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
56	  cat "$tmpl_file"
57	  exit 0
58	fi
59
60	HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63
64	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
65	with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
66	    template_text = fh.read()
67
68
69	def emit_template():
70	    sys.stdout.write(template_text)
71
72
73	# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
74	try:
75	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
76	except ModuleNotFoundError:
77	    try:
78	        import tomli as tomllib
79	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
80	        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
81	        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
82	        emit_template()
83	        sys.exit(0)
84
85	# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
86	# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
87	try:
88	    import tomlkit
89	except ModuleNotFoundError:
90	    print(
91	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
92	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
93	        file=sys.stderr,
94	    )
95	    emit_template()
96	    sys.exit(0)
97
98	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
99
100	live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
101	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
102	live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
103
104	# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
105	for key, value in live.items():
106	    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
107	        continue
108	    doc[key] = value
109
110	sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
111	PYEOF
112
```

```text
13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs
16	# us via `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
20	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (passed by the keybind), else the current
21	# focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope);
22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
23	#
24	# Consumers: the prefix+u keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
25	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a URL from the pane".
26	set -eu
27
28	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
29
30	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
31	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
32
33	# Resolve the opener (`x open`) even without the interactive PATH.
34	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
35	    X_BIN=x
36	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
37	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
38	else
39	    echo "url-pick: opener 'x' not found" >&2
40	    exit 1
41	fi
42
43	pane=""
44	source="visible"
45	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
46	    case "$1" in
47	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
48	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
49	        -h|--help) usage ;;
50	        -*) usage ;;
51	        *)
52	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
53	                pane="$1"
54	                shift
55	            else
56	                usage
57	            fi
58	            ;;
59	    esac
60	done
61
62	case "$source" in
63	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
64	    *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
65	esac
66
67	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
68	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
70	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
71	fi
72	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
73
74	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
75	    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }

77	# Extraction — same passes/rewrites as tmux-fzf-url's fzf-url.sh, POSIX-ized

83	gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
84	gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
85	npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)
86
87	items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
88

90	    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
91	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
92	    exit 0

96	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
97	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
98
99	printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
100	    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
101	done
```

The herdr integration already contains the key multi-session discovery primitive: `herdr session list --json`, mapping a named or ambient socket to `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`. That matters because a robust grep cannot assume the current/default server; it must enumerate running sessions and issue each pane query against the correct socket, while treating stopped or disappearing sessions as expected race conditions.

```text
9:  - macOS is **deliberately not** Homebrew, and it is the only tool in this repo where that's true. Upstream disables `herdr update` on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs because the package manager owns the binary — which removes the *only* pane-preserving upgrade path and leaves a server restart, i.e. killing every pane process, as the sole option. The formula was dropped in favour of the release binary so macOS gets `--handoff` too. Boxes provisioned before the switch are migrated by a one-time `brew uninstall herdr` in the same role (leaving both installed would put two binaries on `PATH` and risk a client/server `protocol_mismatch` against yourself).
10:- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
13:> **`herdr update` refuses to run from inside a herdr pane.** The handoff replaces the server process that owns the pane you are typing in, so it fails closed:
20:> The flow is **detach (`prefix+q`) → run it in a plain terminal → reattach with bare `herdr`**. Detaching does not kill anything (client close ≠ session loss), and `--handoff` then swaps the server without exiting pane processes — verified 2026-07 upgrading 0.7.1 → 0.7.5 with a Claude Code session running in a pane, which survived uninterrupted. `just upgrade-herdr` encodes this: it *skips with instructions* rather than failing when it detects `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`, so `just upgrade-all` from a herdr pane doesn't die here. Full trace: [`pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md).
27:> **Why a package-managed herdr strands its own server — the reason macOS left Homebrew.** herdr's socket API is protocol-versioned, and a package-manager upgrade cannot restart the server, so after `brew upgrade herdr` every CLI call (and therefore every `tv herdr-*` channel, `hvibe`/`hcode`, and `[[keys.command]]` helper) fails `protocol_mismatch` until the server restarts — which kills all pane processes. `herdr update --handoff`, the live pane-preserving path, is **disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs**, so a brew-installed herdr has no way to avoid that restart. This repo now installs the self-managed release binary on macOS too, which is what closes the gap; the pitfall below is kept because it still describes what happens on any box that has not been migrated (and `just upgrade-herdr` skips with instructions when it detects a package-managed install). Check with `herdr status` (`compatible:` / `restart_needed:`), not `herdr --version`. Full recovery matrix: [`pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md).
35:herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
37:The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
41:- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42:- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43:- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
46:**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
50:herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
56:- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
89:| URL picker (`prefix+u`, tmux-fzf-url) | **Custom command pane + helper** | `prefix+u` → `url-pick.sh` (fzf → `x open`); `--source recent` scans scrollback |
94:| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
98:Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
100:> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
124:| `` prefix + u `` | **URL picker** — fzf-pick a URL from the pane and open it (`x open`); tmux-fzf-url analog. `--source recent` = full scrollback | command pane |
133:| `prefix + S` | copy focused pane's **content** (full scrollback) | command pane |
142:> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
165:> **For a spaces-only overview, reach for `prefix + T`** (`tv herdr-sesh`) instead. It is a flat workspace list by construction — a permanent collapse-all view — and it can additionally *create* a space from a zoxide frecency dir, which the native navigator cannot. `prefix + w` is the other space-level option (native sidebar navigate mode) but has no fuzzy search.
169:Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
182:- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
240:These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
251:- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
255:To change herdr's managed config, edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` and `chezmoi apply` — it now reaches every host. Validate with `herdr server reload-config` (reports keybind collisions in its `diagnostics`; an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means the config — including array key bindings — parsed clean).
261:- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
262:- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
264:## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
266:herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
269:herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
270:herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
273:What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
275:- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
276:- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
277:- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
279:**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
282:- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
284:**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
290:If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
292:## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
294:The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
300:3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
315:Verified: a pane can carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `tokens` map and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth. Presence of the token *is* the flag, so the glyph text is free-form.
351:| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`. Preferring the env var means it still works when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a stale server |
367:| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
368:| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
369:| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |
373:The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
375:Both surfaces share the same helper: the `[[keys.command]]` binds in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and the `copy-*.toml` **Quick Actions** under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (fuzzy-launched via `prefix+y`). `P/D/V/S` are uppercase (`prefix+shift+<letter>`) chosen to dodge herdr's reserved `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane) and this repo's `shift+B` (new_worktree) / `shift+R` (reload); lowercase `d` was the only free mnemonic letter left for the dir ops, with `ctrl+d` keeping the pair adjacent. Confirm no collision with `herdr server reload-config` (empty `diagnostics`).
387:**herdr's context menus cannot be extended.** They are a fixed enum compiled into the binary — the whole inventory is one packed string blob (`Rename` · `Close` · `New worktree` · `Open worktree...` · `Close group` · `Expand` · `Delete worktree checkout...` for spaces; `New tab` · `Rename pane` · `Split right` · `Split down` · `Close pane` · `Swap with focused pane` · `Clear pane name` for panes). Verified on 0.7.5 from three directions: `config.toml` has no menu table (only `[[keys.command]]` and `ui.right_click_passthrough_modifier`, which governs whether right-click reaches the *inner app*); the plugin manifest's `[[actions]]` carries `contexts = ["workspace"]` that **looks** like menu placement but is inert; and `herdr api schema --json` contains no occurrence of "menu" at all, so nothing can inject one at runtime either.
402:One helper drives it: `~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh). It reads the pane (`herdr pane read`), runs the **same extraction/rewrite passes as tmux-fzf-url**, and opens each choice with the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md) (wslview / open / xdg-open). It mirrors `pane-copy.sh` exactly: pane defaults to `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` (the keybind var) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, and `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH.
406:| Scope | **Visible screen by default** (matches tmux-fzf-url). `url-pick.sh <pane> --source recent` scans the full retained scrollback |
407:| Patterns | `http(s)` / `ftp` / `file`, bare `www.` → `http://`, `IPv4[:port]` → `http://`, `git@…` SSH remotes → `https://…`, quoted `"owner/repo"` → `github.com/owner/repo`, `import "pkg"` → `npmjs.com/package/pkg` |
417:Helper: `~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh), a direct sibling of `url-pick.sh`/`pane-copy.sh` (same pane + `x`-resolution + `herdr pane read` plumbing), copying via [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md).
425:| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |
427:`path:line:col` suffixes (grep `-n` / stack traces / compiler output) are stripped before the existence test, so `pkg.py:42:5` validates as `pkg.py`. Scope is the visible screen by default (`--source recent` for scrollback); multi-select copies newline-joined; an empty result prints `no file paths found` and pauses ~1.5 s.
```

```text
1	# Session/workspace switcher cable channel for herdr (tv) — sesh analog
2	#
3	# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
4	# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches
5	# herdr WORKSPACES (the project-level unit) and opens new ones from zoxide
6	# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
7	# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
8	#
9	# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
10	#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
11	#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
12	#
13	# Actions: Enter = open/focus · Ctrl+D = close workspace · Alt+Y = copy its dir
14	#
15	# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.
16
17	[metadata]
18	name = "herdr-sesh"
19	description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
20	requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]
21
22	[source]
23	command = [
24	  '''herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]? | "ws\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.label)  (\(.pane_count)p, \(.tab_count)t)"' ''',
25	  '''zoxide query -l 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{print "dir",$0,$0}' ''',
26	]
27	display = "{split:\t:2}"
28	output = "{split:\t:1}"
29
30	[preview]
31	command = '''
32	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
33	case "$kind" in
34	  ws)
35	    printf '\033[1mworkspace %s\033[0m\n' "$ref"
36	    # herdr has NO workspace-level cwd field, so the dir is derived (lowest tab's
37	    # pane cwd). Shown here so Alt+Y tells you what it is about to copy, and so
38	    # Enter tells you which project you are focusing.
39	    dir=$(~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh "$ref" 2>/dev/null || true)
40	    [ -n "$dir" ] && printf 'dir: %s\n' "$dir"
41	    printf '\n'
42	    herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq . 2>/dev/null \
43	      || herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null
44	    ;;
45	  dir)
46	    printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
47	    if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then eza -la --git --color=always "$ref" 2>/dev/null
48	    else ls -la "$ref" 2>/dev/null; fi
49	    ;;
50	esac
51	'''
52
53	[ui]
54	input_header = "herdr Workspaces / Dirs"
55
56	[keybindings]
57	enter = "actions:open"
58	ctrl-d = ["actions:close_ws", "reload_source"]
59	alt-y = "actions:copy_dir"
60
61	[actions.open]
62	description = "Focus the workspace, or open a new workspace at the directory"
63	command = '''
64	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
65	[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0
66	case "$kind" in
67	  ws)  herdr workspace focus "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
68	  dir) herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
69	esac
70	'''
71	# `execute` (not `fork`) so tv EXITS after the action — the binding is a herdr
72	# `type = "pane"` command pane, which only vanishes when its command exits. With
73	# `fork` tv stays alive and the picker pane lingers over the workspace you just
74	# focused. `close_ws` below deliberately keeps `fork`: it pairs with
75	# `reload_source`, so tv must stay open to redraw the list.
76	mode = "execute"
77
78	[actions.close_ws]
79	description = "Close the selected herdr workspace"
80	command = '''
81	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
82	[ "$kind" = "ws" ] && [ -n "$ref" ] && herdr workspace close "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1
83	'''
84	mode = "fork"
85
86	# Alt+Y — copy the selected row's DIRECTORY to the clipboard.
87	#
88	# This is the repo's stand-in for a right-click "Copy dir" on a sidebar workspace
89	# row: herdr's context menus are a fixed enum compiled into the binary (no config
90	# table, no plugin manifest field, no "menu" anywhere in `herdr api schema`), so
91	# there is nothing to extend. Upstream requests #1511/#1671/#1776/#1830 were all
92	# closed NOT_PLANNED; discussions #1609/#1672/#1722 are still open. See
93	# docs/tools/herdr.md.
94	#
95	# It is strictly MORE capable than the right-click would be: it works on ANY
96	# workspace in the list, not just the one you happen to have focused, and it
97	# covers the zoxide `dir` rows too.
98	#
99	# Alt+ per the repo convention (tmux's prefix is Ctrl+b, so ctrl-* chords may not
100	# reach tv). `execute` so tv exits after copying — this channel runs inside a
101	# herdr `type = "pane"` command pane, which only closes when its command exits.
102	[actions.copy_dir]
103	description = "Copy the workspace's root dir (or the directory row's path) to the clipboard"
104	command = '''
105	kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
106	[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0
107	case "$kind" in
108	  ws)
109	    # Reuse pane-copy.sh: it accepts a bare workspace id and already resolves
110	    # `x` by absolute-path fallback for the no-interactive-PATH case.
111	    ~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh dir "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1
112	    ;;
113	  dir)
114	    if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then xbin=x; else xbin="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"; fi
115	    printf '%s' "$ref" | "$xbin" copy >/dev/null 2>&1
116	    ;;
117	esac
118	'''
```

```text
20:> The flow is **detach (`prefix+q`) → run it in a plain terminal → reattach with bare `herdr`**. Detaching does not kill anything (client close ≠ session loss), and `--handoff` then swaps the server without exiting pane processes — verified 2026-07 upgrading 0.7.1 → 0.7.5 with a Claude Code session running in a pane, which survived uninterrupted. `just upgrade-herdr` encodes this: it *skips with instructions* rather than failing when it detects `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`, so `just upgrade-all` from a herdr pane doesn't die here. Full trace: [`pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md).
27:> **Why a package-managed herdr strands its own server — the reason macOS left Homebrew.** herdr's socket API is protocol-versioned, and a package-manager upgrade cannot restart the server, so after `brew upgrade herdr` every CLI call (and therefore every `tv herdr-*` channel, `hvibe`/`hcode`, and `[[keys.command]]` helper) fails `protocol_mismatch` until the server restarts — which kills all pane processes. `herdr update --handoff`, the live pane-preserving path, is **disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs**, so a brew-installed herdr has no way to avoid that restart. This repo now installs the self-managed release binary on macOS too, which is what closes the gap; the pitfall below is kept because it still describes what happens on any box that has not been migrated (and `just upgrade-herdr` skips with instructions when it detects a package-managed install). Check with `herdr status` (`compatible:` / `restart_needed:`), not `herdr --version`. Full recovery matrix: [`pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md).
35:herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
37:The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
39:### Named sessions
41:- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42:- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43:- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
44:- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
46:**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
50:herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
52:- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53:- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
56:- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
83:| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
94:| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
100:> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
109:| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator ([in-popup keys](#navigator-keys)) | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
131:| `prefix + D` | copy focused pane's **coordinate** (session>space>tab>pane) | command pane |
161:3. **The navigator's expand set is separate from the sidebar's** `collapsed_space_keys` — the latter is what `~/.config/herdr/session.json` persists, driven by the sidebar's right-click `Expand` / `Close group` menu. Collapsing a space in one does not affect the other.
169:Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
179:- **The plain-open pair (`hhere` / `hroot`)** fills the gap where every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent layout. With tmux, `tmux new-session` lands you in `$PWD` directly; herdr adds a Workspace layer, so without these you'd launch herdr, create a space (which opens at `$HOME` per `new_cwd`), then `cd` by hand. `hhere` does the one-shot: `herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → attach if outside. No git requirement; the optional command runs **raw** (no specstory/on-exit wrapping — that stays with `hcode`/`hvibe`). `hhere -h` / `hroot -h` for flags. **Label caveat**: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to its root pane's *live* cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see the **cwd & workspace-naming model** section above), so the idempotent-focus is best-effort — a drifted label makes a re-run open a fresh workspace. **`-p DIR` is absolutized in your shell** (via `_herdr_abs_dir`, shared with `hcode`/`hvibe`) before it reaches herdr, so relative paths like `hhere -p ../sibling` work and a typo'd DIR is a hard error instead of a silent workspace at `$HOME` — see the `--cwd` bullet in the cwd model section for why that guard exists.
180:- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
181:- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
182:- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
185:- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
201:Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
211:- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`. `Ctrl+D` closes the selected workspace; **`Alt+Y` copies its directory** (works on workspace *and* zoxide-dir rows — see [`dir` vs `cwd`](#space-dir)). The preview shows that derived dir above the raw `workspace get` JSON, so you can see what `Alt+Y` will hand you.
235:| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json.tmpl` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
240:These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
251:- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
261:- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
262:- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
264:## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
266:herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
269:herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
270:herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
273:What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
275:- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
276:- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
277:- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
279:**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
281:- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
282:- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
284:**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
290:If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
292:## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
294:The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
300:3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
315:Verified: a pane can carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `tokens` map and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth. Presence of the token *is* the flag, so the glyph text is free-form.
339:| **`type = "popup"`** | session-modal float **above** the layout — nothing reflows, and you land exactly where you were |
343:`prefix + `` ` `` (scratch shell) is a popup too, for the same reason — as a command pane it took over the layout and read as a *zoom* of the current window rather than a scratch space. `prefix+G` / `prefix+M` / `prefix+N` (lazygit / btop / nvtop) deliberately stay `type = "pane"`: you quit those immediately with `q`, so the temporary split costs nothing, and popups are **session-modal** — you cannot touch another pane while one is open. That modality is why this is decided per binding rather than globally.
351:| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`. Preferring the env var means it still works when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a stale server |
367:| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
368:| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
373:The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
387:**herdr's context menus cannot be extended.** They are a fixed enum compiled into the binary — the whole inventory is one packed string blob (`Rename` · `Close` · `New worktree` · `Open worktree...` · `Close group` · `Expand` · `Delete worktree checkout...` for spaces; `New tab` · `Rename pane` · `Split right` · `Split down` · `Close pane` · `Swap with focused pane` · `Clear pane name` for panes). Verified on 0.7.5 from three directions: `config.toml` has no menu table (only `[[keys.command]]` and `ui.right_click_passthrough_modifier`, which governs whether right-click reaches the *inner app*); the plugin manifest's `[[actions]]` carries `contexts = ["workspace"]` that **looks** like menu placement but is inert; and `herdr api schema --json` contains no occurrence of "menu" at all, so nothing can inject one at runtime either.
402:One helper drives it: `~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh). It reads the pane (`herdr pane read`), runs the **same extraction/rewrite passes as tmux-fzf-url**, and opens each choice with the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md) (wslview / open / xdg-open). It mirrors `pane-copy.sh` exactly: pane defaults to `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` (the keybind var) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, and `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH.
407:| Patterns | `http(s)` / `ftp` / `file`, bare `www.` → `http://`, `IPv4[:port]` → `http://`, `git@…` SSH remotes → `https://…`, quoted `"owner/repo"` → `github.com/owner/repo`, `import "pkg"` → `npmjs.com/package/pkg` |
417:Helper: `~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh), a direct sibling of `url-pick.sh`/`pane-copy.sh` (same pane + `x`-resolution + `herdr pane read` plumbing), copying via [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md).
424:| Existence check (the noise-killer) | Each candidate is resolved against the pane cwd (`$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`, else `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd`, else process-info cwd) and `test -e`'d |
425:| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |
```

1	# Shell Script Testing
2
3	How this repo tests shell code, the landscape of shell-testing tools, and when to reach for each.
4
5	---
6
7	## TL;DR for this repo
8
9	| Tool | Role | Scope |
10	|------|------|-------|
11	| [**bats-core**](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core) | Behaviour / unit tests | `tests/unit/`, `tests/smoke/` |
12	| [**shellcheck**](https://www.shellcheck.net/) | Static analysis (bugs, bad quoting) | Pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` + `scripts/lib/*.sh` (severity=warning) + `dot_config/{shell,bash}/` (severity=error); `just lint-shell` for broad warning sweep |
13	| [**shfmt**](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) | Formatter (consistency check) | Pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` (not `scripts/lib/` — see [Shell logging](shell-logging.md#maintaining-it)) |
14
15	Run everything with `just check-all`. Run just the fast unit suite with `just bats`. See [the repo tests/ tree](#how-this-repo-structures-tests) below.
16
17	**What's intentionally _not_ in scope:** ansible-role tests, bootstrap / `run_once` tests, chezmoi-template expansion tests, Python script tests, GitHub Actions CI. Coverage is deliberately narrow — this is a personal dotfiles repo, not a library.
18
19	---
20
21	## The three shell-testing frameworks
22
23	Most people pick between Bats, ZUnit, and ShellSpec. Short version of when each makes sense:
24
25	### Bats (Bash Automated Testing System) — what this repo uses
26
27	A Bash testing framework. Tests go in `*.bats` files; each test is a `@test "name" { ... }` block. Provides `run`, `$status`, `$output`, `setup`, `teardown`, plus TAP / JUnit output for CI.
28
29	Pick Bats when:
30
31	- You mainly write Bash.
32	- You're testing CLI scripts or zsh scripts via **black-box** behaviour (run the command, check exit code + stdout/stderr).
33	- You want the most popular / best-documented shell testing ecosystem.
34
35	Not ideal when:
36
37	- You're testing zsh-specific functions (plugins, autoload, `${(P)var}`, parameter expansion flags) at the function level — Bats has no zsh affinity.
38	- You need mocking, coverage, or BDD grammar.
39
40	Companion libraries (optional, **not vendored here** to keep ceremony low):
41
42	- [`bats-assert`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-assert) — `assert_equal`, `assert_output --partial`, etc.
43	- [`bats-file`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-file) — file-system assertions.
44	- [`bats-support`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-support) — shared helpers for the above.
45
46	### ZUnit — zsh-native
47
48	A [ZSH testing framework](https://github.com/zunit-zsh/zunit). Testcase syntax is similar to Bats but written in zsh, so zsh-specific constructs work naturally in both the tests and the code under test.
49
50	Pick ZUnit when:
51
52	- You're writing a zsh plugin, autoload function, or zsh-heavy library.
53	- You want the test harness to _be_ zsh rather than drive zsh from bash.
54
55	Trade-off: smaller ecosystem than Bats, needs [Revolver](https://github.com/molovo/revolver) as a dependency. Not installed by this repo.
56
57	### ShellSpec — full-featured, cross-shell
58
59	[ShellSpec](https://github.com/shellspec/shellspec) is a BDD framework that runs on dash, bash, ksh, zsh, and POSIX shells. Supports mocking, parameterised tests, parallel execution, coverage.
60
61	Pick ShellSpec when:
62
63	- You're shipping a shell library that must work across multiple shells.
64	- You want RSpec-style `Describe` / `It` / `When` / `The output should …` syntax.
65	- You need mocking or coverage reports.
66
67	Trade-off: heavier to learn than Bats; overkill for simple CLI behaviour checks.
68
69	### How to decide
70
71	| Situation | Pick |
72	|-----------|------|
73	| Bash CLI script, short & simple tests | **Bats** |
74	| zsh plugin / autoload-heavy code you want tested at the function level | ZUnit |
75	| Cross-shell library, or need mocking / coverage / BDD | ShellSpec |
76	| zsh CLI script tested via its external behaviour | **Bats** (drive zsh from bash, assert on output) |
77
78	This repo falls in the last row — most "zsh" code here is really "zsh script invoked as a CLI," so Bats is the simplest fit even though the code under test is zsh.
79
80	---
81
82	## How this repo structures tests
83
84	```
85	tests/
86	├── test_helper.bash          # shared helpers, sourced by every .bats file
87	├── unit/
88	│   ├── zsh_proxy.bats        # proxy helpers in 50_networking.zsh
89	│   ├── ghget.bats            # GitHub tree-URL parsing in 41_github.zsh
90	│   └── lan_scan.bats         # pure helpers in lan-scan.sh
91	└── smoke/
92	    └── docker_install.bats   # runs inside Docker after full install
93	```
94
95	### `tests/test_helper.bash`
96
97	Small helper library (<40 lines). Provides:
98
99	- `$REPO_ROOT` — absolute path to the chezmoi source.
100	- `setup_path_stub` — creates a temp dir and prepends it to `PATH`. Exposes the path via `$BATS_STUB_DIR` (not stdout), so the export survives — **do not wrap it in `$(...)`**. Command substitution runs the helper in a subshell and the `export PATH` is lost.
101	- `cleanup_path_stubs` — removes any stub dirs registered during the test.
102	- Default `teardown()` that calls `cleanup_path_stubs`. If a test file defines its own `teardown()`, call `cleanup_path_stubs` at the end to preserve cleanup.
103
104	### `tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats`
105
106	Exercises the proxy helpers in `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh`:
107
108	- `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` takes precedence over probing.
109	- Active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:`) takes precedence over generic loopback probing.
110	- Port probe order: `7890 → 7891 → 1087 → 8118 → 8080`.
111	- `_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE=none` when nothing responds.
112	- `__zsh_net_all_proxy_url` returns `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` when set; falls back to the HTTP cache otherwise.
113	- `proxy-on` exports all six env vars (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`).
114	- Split HTTP / SOCKS wiring regression guard (commit `fa4c063`).
115	- `proxy-off` clears all six plus `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy`, and drops cached detection state.
116	- `proxy-status` exit codes: `1` when unavailable, `0` when available.
117
118	Key technique: each test runs `zsh -f -c '...'` (no startup files) so the in-file cache (`$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE`) can't leak between tests, and `nc` is stubbed via a temp dir on `PATH` — no real network traffic.
119
120	### `tests/unit/ghget.bats`
121
122	Pins URL parsing for `ghget` in `dot_config/zsh/tools/41_github.zsh`:
123
124	- Rejects missing / non-GitHub / `/blob/` (file, not tree) URLs with exit 1.
125	- For valid URLs, checks that `owner`, `repo`, `branch`, and the subdir path all reach the `curl` + `tar` invocations intact. Query strings and trailing slashes are stripped.
126	- Refuses to overwrite an existing destination directory before touching the network.
127
128	Key technique: `curl` and `tar` are stubbed with bash scripts that log their args to `$CAPTURE_LOG`. The `tar` stub also fabricates the expected extracted directory (reading `-C` target and the last positional) so the post-extract `mv` in `ghget` succeeds — no real network, no real tarball.
129
130	### `tests/unit/lan_scan.bats`
131
132	Pins pure helpers in `dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh`:
133
134	- `is_usable_ip` — accepts normal host IPs; rejects link-local (`169.254/16`), multicast (`224–239/4`), broadcast, network address, and `.0` / `.255` in the host octet.
135	- `vendor_for_mac` — normalises colon / dash / no-sep MAC formats, looks up the 6-hex prefix in an nmap-style OUI database.
136
137	Key technique: the script dispatches at load time (line 325+), so bare `source` runs the `all` subcommand and tries to probe the network. Work around by sourcing with `clean` as the first positional arg against an isolated `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` — `clean` is harmless under an isolated cache dir, and the function definitions remain in scope afterwards.
138
139	### `tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`
140
141	Runs inside the Dockerfile-built test image after `chezmoi apply` + ansible have completed. Asserts post-install state:
142
143	- `chezmoi apply` is idempotent (re-apply produces empty `chezmoi diff`).
144	- `zsh -n` passes on `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zshenv`, and every `~/.config/zsh/**/*.zsh`.
145	- `nvim --headless "+lua print('ok')" +qa` exits 0.
146	- Core CLI tools on `PATH`: `nvim rg fd fzf zsh just bats`.
147	- oh-my-zsh plugins present (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-completions`).
148	- Unit tests pass under the container's zsh (catches "works on my Mac" regressions).
149
150	Invoked by `just docker-test` → `docker compose run --build --rm test` → `bats /tmp/dotfiles-source/tests/smoke`.
151

153
154	## Running tests
155
156	```bash
157	# Fast feedback loop (no Docker, no network, sub-second)
158	just bats
159
160	# Smoke tests inside a clean Ubuntu container (slow — builds image)
161	just docker-test
162
163	# Everything: ansible syntax + pre-commit + bats + docker-test
164	just check-all
165	```
166
167	---
168
169	## Patterns worth reusing
170
171	### Testing zsh code from bats
172
173	Bats is bash-based, so drive zsh as a subprocess. Use `zsh -f -c 'source FILE; <call>'` to skip startup files (isolates the code under test) and capture output via `run` or `$(...)`:
174
175	```bash
176	@test "my zsh function does X" {
177	  result="$(zsh -f -c "
178	    source '$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/zsh/tools/my_file.zsh'
179	    my_function arg1 arg2
180	  ")"
181	  [ "$result" = "expected" ]
182	}
183	```
184
185	### Stubbing external commands
186
187	Prepend a temp dir to `PATH` containing a fake binary:
188
189	```bash
190	@test "probe order regression" {
191	  setup_path_stub   # populates $BATS_STUB_DIR, updates $PATH
192
193	  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/nc" <<'EOF'
194	#!/usr/bin/env bash
195	port=""
196	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do port="$1"; shift; done
197	[ "$port" = "$EXPECT_PORT" ] && exit 0 || exit 1
198	EOF
199	  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/nc"
200
201	  EXPECT_PORT=1087 zsh -f -c "source '$REPO_ROOT/.../file.zsh'; my_probe"
202	}
203	```
204
205	Bats runs every `@test` block in its own subshell, so `PATH` modifications don't leak across tests. `cleanup_path_stubs` (default `teardown`) removes the temp dirs.
206
207	### Asserting zsh variables from bash
208
209	Inside `zsh -f -c '...'`, use zsh indirect expansion (`${(P)v}`) to print a variable named in another variable:
210
211	```bash
212	for v in http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy; do
213	  printf '%s=%s\n' "$v" "${(P)v}"
214	done
215	```
216
217	Then bats asserts on the `$output`:
218
219	```bash
220	[[ "$output" == *"http_proxy=http://test:1234"* ]]
221	```
222
223	---
224
225	## shellcheck + shfmt
226
227	[shellcheck](https://www.shellcheck.net/) is a static analyser for shell scripts. [shfmt](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) is a formatter / format-check. Both run via pre-commit in this repo. For generic pre-commit mechanics (cache location, `uv`-managed bootstrap Python, debugging broken hook envs), see [`docs/tools/pre-commit.md`](../tools/pre-commit.md).
228
229	Pre-commit hook sources (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`):
230
231	- [`shellcheck-py`](https://github.com/shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py) — ships a Python-installable wheel of shellcheck, so pre-commit environments don't need a system-wide `shellcheck` binary.
232	- [`pre-commit-shfmt`](https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt) — pre-commit wrapper around `shfmt` with no Go toolchain required.
233
234	### Other config-file syntax checks
235
236	In addition to shell tooling, `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs these [pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks](https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks) validators:
237
238	- `check-yaml` — ansible playbooks, role definitions, docker-compose, pre-commit itself.
239	- `check-toml` — TV cable channel configs, starship, yazi, alacritty, etc. `.tmpl` files are excluded because chezmoi's `{{ ... }}` go-template tokens aren't valid TOML until rendered.
240	- `check-json` — VS Code settings, claude config, lazyvim lockfile, etc.
241	- `check-merge-conflict`, `check-added-large-files`, `detect-private-key`, `end-of-file-fixer`, `trailing-whitespace`.
242
243	Ansible **playbook syntax** is checked via `just ansible-syntax-check` / `just lint`, not pre-commit — running a full playbook parse on every commit is too slow for the pre-commit hot path. Run `just lint` manually before pushing ansible-touching changes.
244
245	Hook scope (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`): two tiers.
246
247	1. **`^scripts/[^/]+\.sh$`** at `--severity=warning` — the original strict scope; always green.
248	2. **`^dot_config/(shell/[^/]+\.sh|bash/[^/]+\.bash)$`** at `--severity=error` — added 2026-05. Catches actual bugs (e.g. SC2142 alias-with-positional-param) while we gradually clean up the ~40 preexisting warnings the broader scope surfaces. Drop to `--severity=warning` once `just lint-shell` is clean — tracked in [`backlog/shellcheck-broaden-shared-scope.md`](../../backlog/shellcheck-broaden-shared-scope.md).
249
250	Always excluded:
251
252	- `dot_config/zsh/**/*.zsh` — zsh-specific syntax (`(( ... ))` math, `${(P)v}` expansion flags, `print -u2`, `emulate -L zsh`, `zmodload`) trips shellcheck's bash parser and produces too many false positives.
253	- `*.sh.tmpl` / `*.bash.tmpl` — chezmoi go-template tokens (`{{ if eq .profile "macos" }}`) look like unbalanced braces to shellcheck.
254	- `scripts/adhoc/*.sh` — experimental / throwaway scripts by convention.
255
256	If a zsh file needs static analysis later, the best options are:
257
258	- Run shellcheck with `# shellcheck shell=bash` and manually silence known-false positives — tedious.
259	- Switch to a zsh-aware linter (there isn't a widely adopted one).
260	- Or just write a Bats test that covers the behaviour you care about.
261
262	Quick commands:
263
264	```bash
265	# Run both shellcheck hook entries (scripts/ + shared) on all files
266	pre-commit run shellcheck --all-files
267
268	# Run only the broader (shared shell modules) scope at severity=error
269	pre-commit run shellcheck-shared --all-files
270
271	# Broad warning sweep across scripts/ + dot_config/{shell,bash}/ —
272	# exits non-zero on findings; useful for gradual cleanup. Uses uvx
273	# shellcheck-py when system shellcheck isn't on PATH.
274	just lint-shell
275
276	# Run only shfmt
277	pre-commit run shfmt --all-files
278
279	# shfmt is in -w mode (writes in place via the hook) — to format manually:
280	shfmt -i 2 -ci -bn -w scripts/*.sh
281	```
282
283	---
284
285	## Adding a new test
286
287	1. Decide unit vs smoke:
288	   - Pure logic with stub-able inputs → `tests/unit/`.
289	   - Assertions about post-install system state → `tests/smoke/`.
290	2. Create `tests/unit/<thing>.bats` (or smoke/). Start with:
291	   ```bash
292	   #!/usr/bin/env bats
293	   load "../test_helper.bash"
294
295	   @test "brief description" {
296	     run some-command
297	     [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
298	   }
299	   ```
300	3. Run `just bats` (or `just docker-test`) to verify.
301	4. If the test needs a stub, use `setup_path_stub` + `$BATS_STUB_DIR`.
302
303	Rule of thumb for deciding whether a test is worth adding: **would a silent regression here cost me more than ten minutes to diagnose?** If no, skip the test. Personal dotfiles don't need 80% coverage.
304
305	---
306
307	## Testing TUIs and interactive programs
308
309	The frameworks above are for **shell** code driven as a CLI. They don't fit **full-screen TUIs** — Bats can black-box a line-oriented command (run it, check exit code + stdout), but it can't render the terminal screen grid, follow cursor moves, or drive an alternate-screen app reliably.
310
311	This repo has exactly **one** genuine full-screen TUI: **`mlf`** (`scripts/mlf/tui.py`, a Python [Textual](https://textual.textualize.io/) app). Everything else billed as "interactive" is a line CLI, a `questionary` / `getpass` prompt wizard (`dotcfg`, the router CLIs), a `y/N` loop (`pqsum --clean`), or delegates its picker to Television (`fleet hosts`, `yth` → `tv …`).
312
313	**Decision (2026-07) — chosen direction, not yet built:**
314
315	| Target | Tool | Why |
316	|---|---|---|
317	| The `mlf` Textual app (ours) | Textual [`Pilot`](https://textual.textualize.io/guide/testing/) + [`pytest-textual-snapshot`](https://github.com/Textualize/pytest-textual-snapshot) | First-party, headless / in-process (no PTY, no daemon), deterministic; `async with app.run_test() as pilot` + `snap_compare()` SVG regression |
318	| Arbitrary third-party TUI binaries | [`pexpect`](https://pexpect.readthedocs.io/) + [`pyte`](https://github.com/selectel/pyte) | Boring-stable PTY driver + screen-grid renderer; every newer "terminal Playwright" wraps this same stack |
319
320	Rejected: [`shell-use`](https://github.com/microsoft/shell-use) (Microsoft's "Playwright for the terminal") — genuinely capable (keyboard/mouse, per-cell color, snapshot expect, SVG), but pre-1.0 beta with a self-declared unstable CLI/install and a background daemon, which conflicts with this repo's low-churn mandate. Prior art already in-repo: `agent-warmup` drives the interactive `claude` TUI via a detached tmux `send-keys` session.
321
322	Status: **greenfield** — there's no repo-wide `pytest` / dev-deps group or test CI job yet (the only pytest suite lives in the `agent-history-hygiene` skill), so this is deferred. Full evaluation, options table, and implementation sketch: [`backlog/tui-testing-harness.md`](../../backlog/tui-testing-harness.md).
323
324	---
325

329	- [ZUnit repo](https://github.com/zunit-zsh/zunit) (needs [Revolver](https://github.com/molovo/revolver))
330	- [ShellSpec docs](https://shellspec.info/) · [ShellSpec repo](https://github.com/shellspec/shellspec)
331	- [shellcheck wiki](https://www.shellcheck.net/wiki/) · pre-commit hook: [shellcheck-py](https://github.com/shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py)
332	- [shfmt flags](https://github.com/mvdan/sh/blob/master/cmd/shfmt/shfmt.1.scd) · pre-commit hook: [pre-commit-shfmt](https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt)
333	- Install location in this repo: `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (bats-core is cross-platform; no companion libraries installed by default).

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
2	# Unit tests for `ghget` in dot_config/shell/41_github.sh.
3	#
4	# ghget parses GitHub tree URLs and downloads a subdirectory. The parsing path
5	# is pure string manipulation in zsh — high silent-regression risk (wrong
6	# owner/repo/branch slice → downloads the wrong thing, or a confusing failure
7	# half-way through). Tests stub `curl` and `tar` via PATH so no network runs.
8
9	load "../test_helper.bash"
10
11	GH_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/shell/41_github.sh"
12
13	# Stub curl + tar that just echo the args they were called with into a log
14	# file, so tests can assert on what URL curl was asked to fetch / what tar
15	# was asked to extract.
16	_install_curl_tar_stubs() {
17	  setup_path_stub
18	  : "${CAPTURE_LOG:=$BATS_STUB_DIR/capture.log}"
19	  export CAPTURE_LOG
20
21	  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/curl" <<'EOF'
22	#!/usr/bin/env bash
23	echo "curl $*" >> "$CAPTURE_LOG"
24	# Emit minimal bytes so the pipe to tar has something — tar stub ignores input.
25	printf 'fakearchive'
26	EOF
27	  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/tar" <<'EOF'
28	#!/usr/bin/env bash
29	echo "tar $*" >> "$CAPTURE_LOG"
30	# Drain stdin so curl doesn't get EPIPE.
31	cat > /dev/null
32	# Create the expected extracted directory so ghget's post-check passes.
33	# Args contain `--strip-components=N` and an archive path like
34	# `<repo>-<branch>/<subdir>`. The last positional arg (after --strip and -C)
35	# ends with the subdir we need to create under -C target.
36	#
37	# We extract:
38	#   -C <tmpdir>  → tmpdir is the flag-value right after -C
39	#   last positional → "<archive_root>/<subdir_path>" — we want the *leaf* of
40	#   subdir_path as the dir under tmpdir (because --strip-components drops
41	#   archive_root and any intermediate path components).
42	tmpdir=""
43	archive_entry=""
44	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
45	  case "$1" in
46	    -C) tmpdir="$2"; shift 2 ;;
47	    -*) shift ;;
48	    *)  archive_entry="$1"; shift ;;
49	  esac
50	done
51	leaf="${archive_entry##*/}"
52	mkdir -p "$tmpdir/$leaf"
53	: > "$tmpdir/$leaf/marker"
54	EOF
55	  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/curl" "$BATS_STUB_DIR/tar"
56	}
57
58	# Run ghget under a temp $PWD so downloads land in an isolated dir that
59	# teardown will wipe.
60	_in_tmp_pwd() {
61	  _BATS_TMPPWD="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-ghget.XXXXXX")"
62	  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$_BATS_TMPPWD")
63	  cd "$_BATS_TMPPWD"
64	}
65

70	}
```

```text
8	# drops real hosts from LAN scans; a mis-normalised MAC prefix silently

12	# "all" command and tries to probe the network. Work around by sourcing with
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
2	# Unit tests for dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh.
3	#
4	# Strategy mirrors zsh_proxy.bats: every test sources the file fresh inside an
5	# explicit `zsh -f -c` / `bash --norc -c`, so no cache or global leaks between
6	# tests, and `docker` / `curl` are stubbed via $BATS_STUB_DIR so nothing touches
7	# a daemon or the network.
8	#
9	# Several tests deliberately run in BOTH shells. This file is sourced by zsh and
10	# bash alike, and the two disagree about word splitting: zsh does not split
11	# unquoted parameter expansions, so a `set -- $raw` parser that works in bash
12	# silently collapses to one field in zsh. Testing one shell would not catch it.
13

15
16	DNET_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/shell/51_docker_net.sh"
17
18	# Run a snippet with 51_docker_net.sh sourced, in the named shell.
19	_dnet_run() {
20	  local shell="$1" snippet="$2"
21	  case "$shell" in
22	    zsh) zsh -f -c "source '$DNET_FILE'; $snippet" ;;
23	    bash) bash --norc -c "source '$DNET_FILE'; $snippet" ;;
24	  esac
25	}
26
27	# A `docker` stub whose `info --format` prints one canned pipe-delimited record.
28	_make_docker_info_stub() {

31	#!/usr/bin/env bash
32	if [ "\$1" = "info" ]; then printf '%s' '$record'; exit 0; fi
33	exit 0
34	STUB
35	  chmod +x "$dir/docker"
36	}
```
