403	@test "on: refuses a VM-backed daemon under ZSH too, not just bash" {
404	  # Regression guard for `local path`: zsh ties the `path` array to `PATH`, so a
405	  # `local path` inside a function BLANKS PATH — every external command then
406	  # fails and `_dnet_have docker` returns false, which made `_dnet_shape` report
407	  # `none` and this very guard stop firing. bash treats `path` as an ordinary
408	  # variable, so the bash-only version of this test passed throughout.

417	@test "no zsh-special name is used as a local anywhere in the file" {
418	  # path/fpath/cdpath/manpath are tied to their scalar twins; status/argv/
419	  # options/signals are reserved. Declaring any of them `local` has effects far
420	  # away from the declaration.
421	  # Parse the DECLARED NAMES only — `local action="${1:-status}"` mentions
422	  # `status` in its default value and must not trip this.
423	  names="$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*local[[:space:]]+[^;#]*' "$DNET_FILE" \
424	             | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*local[[:space:]]+//' \
425	             | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -E 's/=.*//' | grep -v '^-' | grep -v '^$')"
426	  bad="$(printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -xE 'path|fpath|cdpath|manpath|status|argv|options|signals|psvar|mailpath' || true)"
427	  [ -z "$bad" ]
428	}

13	#            the full retained scrollback (--source recent, the default)

17	#            read the caveat there about the sidebar label drifting from it.

19	#            which drifts away from `dir` the moment you cd.

21	# The pane defaults to the CURRENT focused pane (`herdr pane current`); pass a
22	# pane id to target another. herdr's keybind context passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID
23	# and herdr-plus Quick Actions pass $HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID — both are wired to call
24	# this, and both fall through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
25	#
26	# Clipboard sink is the repo's own `x copy` (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x), which
27	# auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52. We resolve it by absolute
28	# path fallback because a herdr command-pane / quick-action pane may run us via
29	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
30	#
31	# Usage:
32	#   pane-copy.sh process [PANE_ID]
33	#   pane-copy.sh coord   [PANE_ID]
34	#   pane-copy.sh content [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
35	#   pane-copy.sh dir     [PANE_ID|WORKSPACE_ID]
36	#   pane-copy.sh cwd     [PANE_ID]

38	# Consumers: the prefix+P/L/V/B keybinds (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and
39	# the copy-pane-* quick actions (dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/
40	# cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
41	set -eu
42
43	usage() {
44	    printf 'usage: %s process|coord|content|dir|cwd [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]\n' "$0" >&2
45	    exit 64
46	}
47
48	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
49	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "pane-copy: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
50
51	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
52	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	    X_BIN=x
54	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
55	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
56	else
57	    echo "pane-copy: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
58	    exit 1
59	fi
60
61	action="${1:-}"
62	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
63	shift
64
65	pane=""
66	source="recent"
67	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
68	    case "$1" in
69	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
70	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
71	        -*) usage ;;
72	        *)
73	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then

90
91	case "$action" in

116

123

125	            "$session" \
126	            "$ws" "${ws_label:+ ($ws_label)}" \
127	            "$tb" "${tb_label:+ ($tb_label)}" \
128	            "$pn")
129	        [ -n "$sock" ] && text=$(printf '%s\nsocket=%s' "$text" "$sock")
130	        text=$(printf '%s\n# herdr pane get %s' "$text" "$pn")
131
132	        copy "$text"

134	        ;;
135	    content)
136	        case "$source" in
137	            visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
138	            *) echo "pane-copy: --source must be visible|recent|recent-unwrapped" >&2; exit 64 ;;
139	        esac
140	        body=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
141	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read content of $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
142	        copy "$body"
143	        echo "copied $source content for $pane"
144	        ;;
145	    dir)
146	        # WORKSPACE ("space") root dir — the sidebar row's directory, NOT the
147	        # pane's live cwd. Derivation is shared with prefix+C's new-tab helper
148	        # and the herdr-sesh tv channel; it lives in space-root.sh, which also

151	        here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)

159	        dir=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \

162	        copy "$dir"
163	        echo "copied pane cwd: $dir"

13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs

22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.

53	                pane="$1"

55	            else
56	                usage
57	            fi
58	            ;;
59	    esac
60	done
61
62	case "$source" in
63	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
64	    *) echo "url-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
65	esac
66
67	# Default to the current focused pane when no id was passed (or an empty env var).
68	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
69	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "url-pick: jq required to resolve current pane" >&2; exit 1; }
70	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
71	fi
72	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "url-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
73
74	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
75	    || { echo "url-pick: failed to read pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }

78	# (plain vars instead of bash arrays; trailing `|| true` so a no-match grep,

80	urls=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]' || true)
81	wwws=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(https?://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's#^#http://#' || true)

83	gits=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's#:#/#g' | sed 's#^\(ssh///\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$#https://\2#' || true)
84	gh=$(printf   '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[.A-Za-z0-9_-]+)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#^#https://github.com/#' || true)
85	npm=$(printf  '%s\n' "$content" | grep -oE "import[[:space:]]+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's#^#https://npmjs.com/package/#' || true)
86
87	items=$(printf '%s\n' "$urls" "$wwws" "$gh" "$npm" "$ips" "$gits" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
88
89	if [ -z "$items" ]; then
90	    printf 'url-pick: no URLs found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
91	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
92	    exit 0
93	fi
94
95	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
96	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$items" | fzf --multi --prompt='url> ' --height=100% --border --no-sort) || exit 0
97	[ -n "$chosen" ] || exit 0
98
99	printf '%s\n' "$chosen" | while IFS= read -r url; do
100	    [ -n "$url" ] && "$X_BIN" open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
101	done
102

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# sesh-preview — multi-section preview for sesh fzf picker
3	#
4	# Sesh passes one argument that is either:
5	#   - an absolute path (zoxide / find sources)
6	#   - a session name like "icon  name  /path" (sesh's --icons output)
7	#
8	# We extract the path (last token), then render in this priority:
9	#   1. Header: dir name + git branch (if any) + last-modified
10	#   2. README.md (first 25 lines, syntax-highlighted via bat if available)
11	#   3. Recent git log (5 commits, oneline) — only if a git repo
12	#   4. Directory listing (eza tree if available, else ls)
13	#
14	# Designed to be safely called from sesh's preview_command. Stays under
15	# ~50 lines of output so fzf preview pane doesn't scroll on first paint.
16
17	set -u
18
19	raw="${1:-}"
20	[[ -z "$raw" ]] && exit 0
21
22	# Extract the path: last whitespace-separated token. Works for both
23	# bare paths and sesh's "icon  name  /path" format.
24	path="${raw##* }"
25	# Strip trailing slash for consistency
26	path="${path%/}"
27
28	# Sesh sometimes hands us the session name only (no path). Resolve via sesh.
29	if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then
30	    # Try interpreting whole arg as session name → ask sesh for its path
31	    resolved="$(sesh list -t -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg n "$raw" \
32	        '.[] | select(.Name==$n) | .Path' 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
33	    [[ -n "$resolved" && -d "$resolved" ]] && path="$resolved"
34	fi
35
36	[[ ! -d "$path" ]] && { echo "(not a directory: $path)"; exit 0; }
37
38	# Color helpers — use tput if terminal supports it
39	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
40	    bold=$(tput bold 2>/dev/null || true)
41	    dim=$(tput dim 2>/dev/null || true)
42	    reset=$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null || true)
43	    cyan=$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null || true)
44	    yellow=$(tput setaf 3 2>/dev/null || true)
45	else
46	    bold="" dim="" reset="" cyan="" yellow=""
47	fi
48
49	# ── 1. Header ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50	name="$(basename "$path")"
51	parent_short="$(dirname "$path" | sed "s|^$HOME|~|")"
52	echo "${bold}${cyan}${name}${reset} ${dim}— ${parent_short}/${reset}"
53
54	if git_branch=$(git -C "$path" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null); then
55	    git_status_count=$(git -C "$path" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
56	    git_ahead_behind=$(git -C "$path" rev-list --left-right --count "@{upstream}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null \
57	        | awk '{ if ($1>0||$2>0) printf "↓%s ↑%s", $1, $2 }')
58	    echo "${dim}git:${reset} ${yellow}${git_branch}${reset} ${dim}(${git_status_count} dirty${git_ahead_behind:+, $git_ahead_behind})${reset}"
59	fi
60
61	# Last modified (mtime of dir)
62	if mtime=$(stat -f "%Sm" -t "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" "$path" 2>/dev/null); then
63	    echo "${dim}mtime: ${mtime}${reset}"
64	fi
65
66	echo
67
68	# ── 2. README ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69	readme=""
70	for f in README.md README.rst README.txt readme.md README; do
71	    if [[ -f "$path/$f" ]]; then readme="$path/$f"; break; fi
72	done
73
74	if [[ -n "$readme" ]]; then
75	    echo "${bold}── README ──${reset}"
76	    if command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
77	        bat --color=always --style=plain --line-range=:25 --paging=never "$readme"
78	    else
79	        head -25 "$readme"
80	    fi
81	    echo
82	fi
83
84	# ── 3. Recent commits ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
85	if [[ -n "${git_branch:-}" ]]; then
86	    echo "${bold}── Recent commits ──${reset}"
87	    git -C "$path" log --oneline --color=always -5 2>/dev/null
88	    echo
89	fi
90
91	# ── 4. Directory tree ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
92	echo "${bold}── Files ──${reset}"
93	if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then
94	    eza --tree --level=2 --git-ignore --color=always --icons \
95	        --ignore-glob='node_modules|.git|__pycache__|.venv|target|dist|build' \
96	        "$path" 2>/dev/null | head -30
97	else
98	    ls -la "$path" | head -25
99	fi
100
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#   "yt-dlp>=2025.1",
6	#   "tyro>=0.9",
7	#   "rich>=13.9",
8	#   "platformdirs>=4",
9	# ]
10	# ///
11	"""yth — search your own YouTube watch history from the terminal.
12
13	Bare `yth` (no args) launches the `tv yth` fuzzy picker over your history.
14	Subcommands below bypass it for scripted / one-shot use.
15
16	Subcommands:
17	  import-takeout <file>          Backfill history from a Google Takeout
18	                                 watch-history.json (primary, cookie-free).
19	  sync                           Incremental sync of recent history via
20	                                 yt-dlp :ythistory (needs login cookies).
21	  enrich [--limit N | --all]     Fill missing description/duration/upload_date
22	                                 for videos (yt-dlp; cookie-free for public).
23	  fetch-subs <id>… | --recent N  Download + index subtitle text (auto+manual).
24	             | --all
25	  search <query> [--subs]        FTS5 search over title/channel/description
26	         [--json] [--limit N]    (add --subs to also match caption text).
27	  list [--tsv] [--limit N]       All history, newest first (--tsv feeds tv).
28	  show <id> [--json]             Detail for one video (DB-only, no network).
29	  open <id> | copy <id>          Open in browser / copy URL to clipboard.
30	  play <id>                      mpv if configured+installed, else browser.
31
32	Data lives in a local sqlite DB (platformdirs user_data_dir/yth/history.db).
33	Cookie source + subtitle langs are configured in user_config_dir/yth/config.toml.
34
35	Mirrors the structure of `mlf` (see dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf) and pairs
36	with the `tv yth` channel (dot_config/television/cable/yth.toml).
37	"""
38	from __future__ import annotations
39
40	import os
41	import shutil
42	import subprocess
43	import sys
44	from pathlib import Path
45
46	USAGE = """\
47	Usage: yth [<subcommand>] [args...]
48
49	Bare `yth` opens the `tv yth` fuzzy picker. Subcommands bypass it.
50
51	  import-takeout <file>              Import a Google Takeout watch-history.json.
52	  sync                               Incremental :ythistory sync (needs cookies).
53	  enrich [--limit N | --all]         Fetch per-video metadata (public: no cookies).
54	  fetch-subs <id>... | --recent N    Download + index subtitle text.
55	             | --all
56	  search <query> [--subs] [--json]   FTS5 search (title/channel/description;
57	         [--limit N] [--raw]         --subs also matches captions).
58	  list [--tsv] [--limit N]           List history, newest first (--tsv for tv).
59	  show <id> [--json]                 One-video detail (DB-only).
60	  open <id> | copy <id> | play <id>  Open / copy URL / play.
61
62	Examples:
63	  yth import-takeout ~/Downloads/watch-history.json
64	  yth search "rust async" --subs
65	  yth enrich --limit 200
66	  yth fetch-subs --recent 50
67	  yth show dQw4w9WgXcQ
68	"""
69
70
71	def _source_path() -> Path:
72	    """Locate the chezmoi source dir so we can import scripts.yth.*.
73
74	    Identical strategy to executable_mlf:_source_path / executable_fleet.
75	    Trust `chezmoi source-path`; fall back to ~/.local/share/chezmoi.
76	    """
77	    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
78	    if chezmoi:
79	        try:
80	            out = subprocess.run(
81	                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
82	                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
83	            )
84	            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
85	                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
86	        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
87	            pass
88	    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
89	    if (fallback / "scripts" / "yth" / "__init__.py").is_file():
90	        return fallback
91	    print(
92	        "yth: cannot locate chezmoi source dir.\n"
93	        "  Tried: `chezmoi source-path` and ~/.local/share/chezmoi.\n"
94	        "  Install chezmoi or ensure the source dir exists.",
95	        file=sys.stderr,
96	    )
97	    sys.exit(2)
98
99
100	def _dispatch_tv(args: list[str]) -> int:
101	    """Exec `tv yth` (the picker). Replaces this process so Ctrl+C reaches tv."""
102	    tv = shutil.which("tv")
103	    if not tv:
104	        print(
105	            "yth: `tv` (television) not in PATH — run a subcommand instead,\n"
106	            "  e.g. `yth search <query>` or `yth list`.  `yth -h` for help.",
107	            file=sys.stderr,
108	        )
109	        return 2
110	    os.execvp(tv, [tv, "yth", *args])
111
112
113	def _leaf(module: str, prog: str, args: list[str]) -> int:
114	    """Rewrite argv and hand off to a leaf module's tyro-based main()."""
115	    sys.argv = [prog, *args]
116	    mod = __import__(f"scripts.yth.{module}", fromlist=["main"])
117	    return mod.main()
118
119
120	def _dispatch_open(args: list[str]) -> int:
121	    if not args or not args[0].strip():
122	        print("yth open: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
123	        return 2
124	    from scripts.yth import open_id
125
126	    return open_id(args[0])
127
128
129	def _dispatch_copy(args: list[str]) -> int:
130	    if not args or not args[0].strip():
131	        print("yth copy: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
132	        return 2
133	    from scripts.yth import copy_id
134
135	    return copy_id(args[0])
136
137
138	def _dispatch_play(args: list[str]) -> int:
139	    if not args or not args[0].strip():
140	        print("yth play: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
141	        return 2
142	    from scripts.yth import play_id
143
144	    return play_id(args[0])
145
146
147	def main() -> int:
148	    # Help paths print USAGE and exit BEFORE any heavy import, so
149	    # `yth -h | grep ...` stays fast + scriptable and never loads yt_dlp.
150	    if len(sys.argv) >= 2 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
151	        print(USAGE)
152	        return 0
153
154	    src = _source_path()
155	    if str(src) not in sys.path:
156	        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
157
158	    # Bare `yth` → tv picker.
159	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
160	        return _dispatch_tv([])
161
162	    sub = sys.argv[1]
163	    rest = sys.argv[2:]
164
165	    # Leaf modules own their own tyro parsing. Subcommand `-` → module `_`.
166	    leaves = {
167	        "import-takeout": ("import_takeout", "yth import-takeout"),
168	        "sync": ("sync", "yth sync"),
169	        "enrich": ("enrich", "yth enrich"),
170	        "fetch-subs": ("fetch_subs", "yth fetch-subs"),
171	        "search": ("search", "yth search"),
172	        "list": ("list", "yth list"),
173	        "show": ("show", "yth show"),
174	    }
175	    if sub in leaves:
176	        module, prog = leaves[sub]
177	        return _leaf(module, prog, rest)
178
179	    shims = {"open": _dispatch_open, "copy": _dispatch_copy, "play": _dispatch_play}
180	    if sub in shims:
181	        return shims[sub](rest)
182	    if sub == "tv":
183	        return _dispatch_tv(rest)
184
185	    print(f"yth: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
186	    return 2
187
188
189	if __name__ == "__main__":
190	    sys.exit(main())
191

Fuzzy matching therefore sees only the displayed pane ID, status, and cwd basename—not pane contents.\n- Preview: `herdr pane read \"$pane\" --source visible --lines 80`; this is the visible buffer only, not full retained scrollback.\n- Actions: Enter/Alt+T focus workspace then tab in `fork` mode; Alt+K confirms and closes the pane by pane ID in `execute` mode; Ctrl+Y copies pane ID; Alt+P copies the TSV cwd. There is no focus-by-pane-ID action because the repo records `pane focus` as directional only.\n\n2. `tv herdr-review`\n- Enumeration: also runs `herdr pane list`, but filters to panes with non-empty `.tokens.review`; TSV is `pane_id`, `workspace_id`, `tab_id`, review-token text, and cwd.\n- Preview: the same visible-only `herdr pane read ... --source visible --lines 80`.\n- Actions: Enter/Alt+T focus workspace + tab and retain the token; Alt+C focuses and calls `review-mark.sh clear <pane_id>`, then reloads; Ctrl+Y copies pane ID; Alt+P copies cwd. Focus actions are `fork`, so the picker intentionally remains for triage.\n- The review flag is stored in herdr itself via `pane report-metadata --source review --token review=...`; clearing uses `--clear-token review`. It is not a sidecar-file inbox.\n\n3. `tv herdr-sesh`\n- Enumeration: two sources only—`herdr workspace list` from the current socket/session and `zoxide query -l`. Rows are `ws <workspace_id> <label/counts>` or `dir <path> <path>`.\n- Important mismatch: it does not enumerate named herdr sessions, servers, sockets, panes, or tabs, and it never runs `herdr session list` or `herdr session attach`. Its name/description says “session/workspace,” but implementation is workspace + directory only.\n- Workspace preview: derives a root dir through `space-root.sh`, then renders raw `herdr workspace get` JSON. Directory preview uses `eza -la --git`, falling back to `ls -la`.\n- Enter focuses an existing workspace or creates one at a zoxide path; Ctrl+D closes only `ws` rows and reloads; Alt+Y copies a workspace’s derived root or a directory row’s path. Enter and copy use `execute` so the temporary command pane exits; close uses `fork` so Television can reload.\n- Workspace root derivation is best-effort: choose the lowest `.number` tab, find its first pane in `herdr pane list`, then use `foreground_cwd // cwd`. No workspace-level cwd exists.\n\nCapture, scrollback, and search findings:\n- `capture-pane`: zero references in the active herdr config/helpers/channels. Herdr’s equivalent used here is `herdr pane read`.\n- `rg`: zero command references in the active herdr implementation.\n- No Television channel performs pane-content search. Television fuzzy-searches each channel’s source/display TSV; pane text is preview-only and is not appended to candidate rows.\n- Full retained scrollback is available outside these three channel previews through `pane-copy.sh content --source recent`, bound to prefix+S and the herdr-plus “Copy pane: content (scrollback)” action.\n- `url-pick.sh` and `path-pick.sh` can read `--source recent`, but their configured prefix+u/p invocations default to visible content. Their `grep` calls extract URLs or path-shaped tokens; they are not global/channel content search. `run-command.sh` has one unrelated `grep` for shell-history cleanup.\n\nIdentifier/session model:\n- Pane channels carry concrete `w…:p…`, `w…`, and `w…:t…` pane/workspace/tab IDs in TSV and act with those IDs.\n- None of the three channels carries a server ID, named-session field, or socket path. Because herdr command panes inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, all source/preview/action CLI calls implicitly target that one current session/socket.\n- Named-session resolution exists only in the shell helpers: `_herdr_session_target` maps a session name to `socket_path` using `herdr session list --json` and scopes `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` for `hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`. `pane-copy.sh coord` is the only inspected helper that resolves the current socket back to a session name and copies session/workspace/tab/pane/socket coordinates.\n\nCompletion and tests:\n- No hand-written zsh/bash herdr completion file exists, and `scripts/generate_completions.sh` has no herdr regeneration row. `24_herdr.sh` only declares functions and aliases.\n- The only herdr references under `tests/` are two Claude-overlay tests proving a runtime-installed `herdr-agent-state.sh` SessionStart hook survives additive merge and tier pruning. 16007	chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets

16044	## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)
16045
16046	Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.
16047
16048	- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
16049	- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
16050	- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
16051	- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
16052	- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
16053	- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
16054	- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
16055	- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
16056	- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
16057	- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
16058	- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
16059	- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
16060	- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
16061	- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
16062	- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
16063	- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
16064	- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

16145	可以，但**目前不是 herdr 原生的 `grep` 子命令**；可組合：
16146
16147	1. `herdr pane list` 列出 pane
16148	2. `herdr pane read` 讀取各 pane
16149	3. 交給 `rg` 搜尋並輸出 pane ID
16150
16151	```zsh
16152	needle='要搜尋的文字或 regex'
16153
16154	herdr pane list |
16155	  jq -r '.result.panes[]? | [.workspace_id, .tab_id, .pane_id] | @tsv' |
16156	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r workspace tab pane; do
16157	    if matches="$(
16158	      herdr pane read "$pane" \
16159	        --source recent \
16160	        --format text 2>/dev/null |
16161	        rg -n --color=never -- "$needle"
16162	    )"; then
16163	      printf '\nworkspace=%s tab=%s pane=%s\n%s\n' \
16164	        "$workspace" "$tab" "$pane" "$matches"
16165	    fi
16166	  done
16167	```
16168
16169	輸出大致會是：
16170
16171	```text
16172	workspace=w1 tab=w1:t2 pane=w1:p4
16173	183:Found the expected deployment result
16174	```

16176	### `--source` 的差異
16177
16178	- `--source visible`：只找目前螢幕可見內容
16179	- `--source recent`：搜尋 herdr 保留的完整 scrollback，較適合定位歷史輸出
16180	- 固定字串搜尋可把 `rg` 改成 `rg -nF`
16181	- 不分大小寫則加 `-i`
16182
16183	repo 現有的 scrollback-copy 也是使用 `pane read --source recent`：
16184	`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:135`
16185
16186	### Session／remote server 限制
16187
16188	上述命令只搜尋**目前 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 指向的 session**。herdr 的 pane/workspace/tab 子命令沒有 `--session` 參數；要搜尋其他 named session，需要：
16189
16190	```zsh
16191	HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$socket_path" <上面的搜尋>
16192	```
16193
16194	`socket_path` 可由：
16195
16196	```zsh
16197	herdr session list --json
16198	```
16199
16200	取得。這個 routing 模型記錄在 `docs/tools/herdr.md:35` 及 `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh:80`。
16201
16202	如果 server 在其他機器：
16203
16204	- 搜尋命令需要在能存取該 server socket 的遠端環境執行，例如 SSH 到 server 後執行。
16205	- `herdr --remote HOST` 是互動式 thin-client attach，並不是 `herdr pane list/read` 的遠端前綴。

16213	- `tv herdr-review`：同樣只有 preview 顯示 visible content
16214	- `tv herdr-sesh`：只列 workspace 與 zoxide directory，不讀 pane content

16290	# chezmoi-dotfiles

16292	This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
16293	deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
16294	custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
16295	— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
16296	selected at init.

16298	## Orientation (read this first)
16299
16300	- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
16301	  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
16302	- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
16303	  managed source file for that target.
16304	- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
16305	  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
16306	  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
16307	- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds

16311	## chezmoi essentials
16312
16313	```bash
16314	chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
16315	chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
16316	chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
16317	chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
16318	chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
16319	chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
16320	chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
16321	chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
16322	chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
16323	```
16324
16325	- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
16326	  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
16327	- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
16328	  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
16329	  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
16330	- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
16331	- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
16332	  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
16333	  `just upgrade-*`.

16335	## What's enabled on THIS machine
16336
16337	(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
16338	- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
16339	- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.

16353	## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)
16354
16355	Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.
16356
16357	- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
16358	- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
16359	- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
16360	- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
16361	- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
16362	- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
16363	- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
16364	- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
16365	- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
16366	- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
16367	- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
16368	- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
16369	- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
16370	- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
16371	- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
16372	- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
16373	- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.
16374
16375	**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

135	- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
136	- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
137	- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
138	- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
139	- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.
140
141	**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).
142

146	that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

151	tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue

153	```

4829	3	# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
4830	4	# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches
4831	5	# herdr WORKSPACES (the project-level unit) and opens new ones from zoxide
4832	6	# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
4833	7	# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
4834	8	#
4835	9	# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
4836	10	#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
4837	11	#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
4838	12	#
4839	13	# Actions: Enter = open/focus · Ctrl+D = close workspace · Alt+Y = copy its dir
4840	14	#
4841	15	# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.
4842	16
4843	17	[metadata]
4844	18	name = "herdr-sesh"
4845	19	description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
4846	20	requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]

4848	22	[source]

5900	26	Design calls / caveats:
5901	27	- `type="pane"` opens a **tiling split**, not a floating popup (herdr issue [#785](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/785) — centered float for `[[keys.command]]` is *not planned*; only plugins get `--placement overlay`). The launcher pane is short-lived (hvibe creates + focuses a new workspace, then the launcher pane closes), so the transient split is tolerable — verify it doesn't leave a stray pane behind.
5902	28	- `hvibe` resolves the git root from `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`; if that pane isn't in a repo, hvibe errors (by design). Consider a `type="pane"` so the error is visible before the pane closes.
5903	29	- Pick keys that don't collide — `prefix+shift+*` is reserved by herdr built-ins; `prefix+alt+*` is free (same rule as the tmux side). Run `herdr server reload-config` and check `diagnostics` for collisions.
5904	30	- Aliases don't expand in non-interactive shells — bind the **function name** `herdr-vibe` (or `hvibe` only if the command runs through an interactive `$SHELL -lc`). Safer: `command = "zsh -lic 'hvibe -p \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD\"'"` or call `herdr-vibe` directly.

 `./docs/tools/herdr.md`

```text
35	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
36
37	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
38
39	### Named sessions
40
41	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
44	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
45
46	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
47
48	## cwd & workspace-naming model
49
50	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
51
52	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
54	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
55	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
56	- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
57
58	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
59
60	| value | meaning |
61	|---|---|
62	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
63	| `home` | `$HOME` |
64	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
65	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
66
67	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
68
69	```toml
70	[[keys.command]]
71	key = "prefix+C"
72	type = "pane"
73	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
74	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
75	```

96	## Keybindings
97
98	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
99
100	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
101
102	| Key | Action | Type |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |

190
191	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).

197	```

199	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. 243
244	herdr can rewrite `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` at runtime — finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime.

That is the real reason a host could feel "out of sync" while `chezmoi diff` showed clean (the diff was clean *because* `create_` never re-touches the file). Note this is independent of hosts: `chezmoi diff` of the source against each host's live file can be byte-identical yet a repo edit still won't land until you refresh.

251	- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.

257	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
258
259	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
260
261	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
262	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
263
264	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
265
266	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
267
268	```bash
269	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
270	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
271	```
272
273	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
274
275	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
276	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
277	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
278
279	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
280
281	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
282	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
283
284	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
285
286	```bash
287	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
288	```
```

305
306	The tmux setup has a per-window bookmark (`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`, rendered via `#{?@bookmark_status,…}`). herdr has **no `#{@option}` status-bar interpolation**, so that exact mechanism doesn't port — but the *use case* that actually matters here does: **"the agent finished (`done`) but I haven't reviewed it yet."** herdr collapses a `done` pane to `idle` the moment you peek in, losing the only signal that it still needs attention.
307
308	The fix uses herdr's **per-pane metadata tokens**, which are orthogonal to native agent detection:
309
310	```bash
311	herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --token review="⭐ REVIEW"   # set (persistent — no --ttl-ms)
312	herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --clear-token review         # clear
313	```
314
315	Verified: a pane can carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `tokens` map and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth. Presence of the token *is* the flag, so the glyph text is free-form.
316
317	> **herdr ≥ 0.7.4 only, and the token needs a row layout to be visible.** 0.7.4 replaced `--custom-status` / the flat `custom_status` field with this namespaced token map — a silent removal, not listed as a breaking change. Two consequences: on older herdr the helper dies with `unknown --custom-status`, and unlike `custom_status` a token is rendered **only** where a sidebar row layout names it. That is why `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` pins `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` with `"$review"` appended to herdr's default first row — drop that and the flag still works through `prefix+i`, but the ⭐ disappears from the sidebar. See [`pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md).
318
319	Surfaces (all sharing one script, `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` = `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh` — the analog of tmux's `toggle-bookmark.sh`):
320
321	| Surface | Action |
322	|---|---|
323	| `hmark` / `hunmark` (aliases in `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`) | set / clear on the current pane (ambient `$HERDR_PANE_ID`), or pass a pane id |
324	| `prefix+m` | toggle the flag on the focused pane (uses `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`) |
325	| `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i` | the **inbox**: lists only flagged panes. `Enter` focuses & **keeps** the ⭐ (you may still be mid-review); `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read") |
326
327	Three names must move together: `TOKEN` in `review-mark.sh`, the `.tokens.review` lookups in [`herdr-review.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml), and `"$review"` in the sidebar row layout.
328
329	## Run any command in a popup (`prefix + E`) {#run-any-command}
330
331	`prefix + G` proves the shape — a transient pane that runs something and vanishes when it exits — but its command is hardcoded. `prefix + E` is the generalisation: **fzf-pick a command from shell history (or just type a new one), it runs in the focused pane's cwd, and the popup closes itself on exit.** Helper: `~/.config/herdr/run-command.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_run-command.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_run-command.sh).
332
333	**Why `type = "popup"` and not the alternatives** — this is the only binding here that is not a command *pane*:
334
335	| Approach | Problem |
336	|---|---|
337	| `type = "pane"` (`prefix+G/M/N`) | splits the **tiled layout** for the duration; everything reflows |
338	| `prefix + c` → type → `exit` | four steps, and churns the tab bar |
339	| **`type = "popup"`** | session-modal float **above** the layout — nothing reflows, and you land exactly where you were |
340
341	`type = "popup"` requires **herdr ≥ 0.7.4** (added in #1125, with `width`/`height` in cells or percentages). It is the true `tmux display-popup -E` analog.
342
343	`prefix + `` ` `` (scratch shell) is a popup too, for the same reason — as a command pane it took over the layout and read as a *zoom* of the current window rather than a scratch space. `prefix+G` / `prefix+M` / `prefix+N` (lazygit / btop / nvtop) deliberately stay `type = "pane"`: you quit those immediately with `q`, so the temporary split costs nothing, and popups are **session-modal** — you cannot touch another pane while one is open. That modality is why this is decided per binding rather than globally.
344
345	**It cannot be a herdr-plus Quick Action** (`prefix + y`), which is the intuitive place to look. Two blockers: Quick Actions run through `sh -c` with **no PTY/stdin** — the same reason `btop`/`nvtop` are command panes rather than Quick Actions — and every action is a fixed `command = "…"` string with no free-text field.
346
347	Behaviour:
348
349	| | |
350	|---|---|
351	| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`. Preferring the env var means it still works when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a stale server |
352	| **picker** | fzf over `$HISTFILE` (default `~/.zsh_history`), newest-first and de-duplicated. **Enter** runs the highlighted history entry; **`Alt+Enter` runs exactly what you typed**, even when history still matches it; typing something with no match at all and pressing Enter also runs it as a new command; `Esc` runs nothing. Falls back to a plain `read` prompt when fzf is absent |
353	| **shell** | `$SHELL -ic` by default, so this repo's aliases and functions resolve (`gst`, `cas`, `x`, …). `--sh` switches to `sh -c` — fast, but aliases do not exist |
354	| **on exit** | closes on success; on failure prints `[exit N]` and waits for Enter so the error stays readable. `HERDR_RUN_HOLD=always\|never` overrides |
355
356	> Two portability traps are handled inside the helper and are worth knowing if you edit it: `~/.zsh_history` is extended-history format (`: <ts>:<elapsed>;<cmd>`) **and contains non-UTF8 bytes**, so BSD `sed` aborts with `sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence` unless the parse runs under `LC_ALL=C`; and the newest-first reversal uses POSIX `awk` because `tail -r` is BSD-only while `tac` is GNU-only.
357
358	> **Why `Alt+Enter` had to exist.** Plain Enter cannot express *"run exactly what I typed"* while fzf still has a match — type `ls -la` with `ls -la /tmp` in history and Enter takes the history entry, which makes the picker feel like it can only replay old commands. `--expect=alt-enter` adds the escape hatch. Note that fzf's line layout is **not fixed**: with `--print-query --expect`, a no-match Enter prints only the query (one line), while an accepted match prints query / key / selection. The helper therefore reads the key from line 2 (empty or absent ⇒ plain Enter) and only trusts line 3 on exit code 0.
359
360	## Copy pane + space facts to the clipboard {#copy-to-clipboard}
361
362	Six one-keypress "grab this onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). It distills a herdr CLI call into human-readable text and pipes it to the repo's own [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md) (auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52; `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH). The pane defaults to the **current focused pane** (`herdr pane current`); the keybinds pass `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, the Quick Actions pass `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, and either falls through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
363
364	| Op | Key | Quick Action | What lands on the clipboard |
365	|---|---|---|---|
366	| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | foreground processes — `cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd` (from `herdr pane process-info`) |
367	| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
368	| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
369	| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |
370	| `dir` | `prefix+d` | *Copy space: dir* | the **workspace ("space") root directory** — see below |
371	| `cwd` | `prefix+ctrl+d` | *Copy pane: cwd* | the focused pane's **live** working directory (what `pwd` / [`abspath`](../shells/aliases.md) returns) |
372
373	The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
374
375	Both surfaces share the same helper: the `[[keys.command]]` binds in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and the `copy-*.toml` **Quick Actions** under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (fuzzy-launched via `prefix+y`). `P/D/V/S` are uppercase (`prefix+shift+<letter>`) chosen to dodge herdr's reserved `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane) and this repo's `shift+B` (new_worktree) / `shift+R` (reload); lowercase `d` was the only free mnemonic letter left for the dir ops, with `ctrl+d` keeping the pair adjacent. Confirm no collision with `herdr server reload-config` (empty `diagnostics`).
376
377	### `dir` vs `cwd`, and why the right-click menu can't do this {#space-dir}
378
379	`dir` is the answer to *"what directory is this space about?"* — the thing you'd want from a right-click **Copy dir** on a sidebar workspace row. Three ways to reach it:
380
381	| Surface | How | Scope |
382	|---|---|---|
383	| `prefix+d` | keybind | the **focused** workspace |
384	| `prefix+y` → *Copy space: dir* | herdr-plus Quick Action | the **focused** workspace |
385	| `prefix+T` → **`Alt+Y`** | [`herdr-sesh`](#television-integration) tv channel | **any** workspace in the list — strictly more than right-click could give |
386
387	**herdr's context menus cannot be extended.** They are a fixed enum compiled into the binary — the whole inventory is one packed string blob (`Rename` · `Close` · `New worktree` · `Open worktree...` · `Close group` · `Expand` · `Delete worktree checkout...` for spaces; `New tab` · `Rename pane` · `Split right` · `Split down` · `Close pane` · `Swap with focused pane` · `Clear pane name` for panes). Verified on 0.7.5 from three directions: `config.toml` has no menu table (only `[[keys.command]]` and `ui.right_click_passthrough_modifier`, which governs whether right-click reaches the *inner app*); the plugin manifest's `[[actions]]` carries `contexts = ["workspace"]` that **looks** like menu placement but is inert; and `herdr api schema --json` contains no occurrence of "menu" at all, so nothing can inject one at runtime either.
388
389	> **Upstream status (re-check on herdr upgrades).** Requested four times — [#1511](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1511) (user-defined menu entries), [#1671](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1671), [#1776](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1776), [#1830](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1830) — **all closed `NOT_PLANNED`**, three of them auto-closed by `kangal-bot` for being feature requests on a bug-only tracker. #1776 is where a maintainer-facing report states plainly that `contexts` *"currently only surfaces in the `plugin action list` API response."* The redirected discussions ([#1609](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1609), [#1672](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1672), [#1722](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1722)) are all still open and unanswered.
390
391	**How the space dir is derived — and its one caveat.** herdr exposes **no workspace-level cwd anywhere**: `herdr workspace get` and `herdr api snapshot` both return the same `label` / `number` / `tab_count` / `pane_count` object. So it is computed, by [`~/.config/herdr/space-root.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_space-root.sh) — the SSOT shared by `pane-copy.sh dir`, the `prefix+C` new-tab helper, and the tv channel's preview + `Alt+Y`:
392
393	- **Space root = the cwd of the workspace's *oldest surviving* tab.** `.number` on a tab is a monotonic **creation counter**, not the display index — a space can hold tabs numbered `10/13/14/15` shown as `1/2/3/4` — so `sort_by(.number)[0]` means "oldest", which is the right notion of "the tab this space started as".
394	- **Caveat: the sidebar label is pinned at creation and never re-derived**, so once you `cd` inside that oldest tab the label and the derived dir drift apart, and nothing in the API can recover the original path. Observed live: a space labelled `2026-05-14-grafana-provisioning-with-docker-otel-lgtm` whose oldest tab sits in `…/grafana/dashboards/Jingle.AI`. `dir` reports the latter — the true current directory, not the stale name.
395
396	`cwd` exists because the two genuinely diverge in normal use: a space rooted at `2026-07-24-unify-ashare-sdk` was observed with panes sitting in three unrelated `Documents/Program/*` trees. `dir` is the project; `cwd` is where *this pane* actually is.
397
398	## Open a URL from the pane (`prefix+u`)
399
400	The herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` ([`joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`](https://github.com/joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url)). `prefix+u` opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the focused pane; pick one (or several — fzf multi-select) and each opens in the browser. Lowercase `u` is deliberately paired with uppercase `U` (`tv tools`), matching the tmux muscle memory.
401
402	One helper drives it: `~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh). It reads the pane (`herdr pane read`), runs the **same extraction/rewrite passes as tmux-fzf-url**, and opens each choice with the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md) (wslview / open / xdg-open). It mirrors `pane-copy.sh` exactly: pane defaults to `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` (the keybind var) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, and `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH.
403
404	| Aspect | Behavior |
405	|---|---|
406	| Scope | **Visible screen by default** (matches tmux-fzf-url). `url-pick.sh <pane> --source recent` scans the full retained scrollback |
407	| Patterns | `http(s)` / `ftp` / `file`, bare `www.` → `http://`, `IPv4[:port]` → `http://`, `git@…` SSH remotes → `https://…`, quoted `"owner/repo"` → `github.com/owner/repo`, `import "pkg"` → `npmjs.com/package/pkg` |
408	| Open | `x open <url>` per selection; multi-select opens all |
409	| No URLs | prints `no URLs found` and pauses ~1.5 s (a command pane closes the instant the script exits — tmux uses the status line instead) |
410
411	Bound via a `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) — no tv channel needed (fzf is the faithful port). Copy-mode URL opening (tmux's `tmux-open` `o`) has no herdr equivalent; use `prefix+u` for the picker.
412
413	## Copy a file path from the pane (`prefix+p`)
414
415	The copy-path sibling of the URL picker. `prefix+p` opens an fzf popup of the file paths in the focused pane; pick one (or several) and the path is copied to the clipboard. Lowercase `p` ("copy **p**ath") sits under the uppercase copy family (`prefix+P/D/V/S`), the same `u`/`U` convention. On tmux the analog is the **extrakto** plugin (`prefix + Tab`) — see [tmux keybindings](tmux/keybindings.md).
416
417	Helper: `~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh), a direct sibling of `url-pick.sh`/`pane-copy.sh` (same pane + `x`-resolution + `herdr pane read` plumbing), copying via [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md).
418
419	**The noise problem, and how it's handled.** Unlike URLs (which self-identify with `scheme://`), file paths have no marker, so a regex alone matches dates (`2024/01/02`), rates (`10k/s`) and fractions (`1/2`). Two defenses:
420
421	| Defense | Behavior |
422	|---|---|
423	| Extraction | extrakto's path heuristics — slash-bearing tokens (`/…`, `~/…`, `./`, `a/b/c`) + bare `file.ext`; trailing `",):` stripped; rate/fraction tokens excluded outright |
424	| Existence check (the noise-killer) | Each candidate is resolved against the pane cwd (`$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`, else `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd`, else process-info cwd) and `test -e`'d |
425	| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |
426
427	`path:line:col` suffixes (grep `-n` / stack traces / compiler output) are stripped before the existence test, so `pkg.py:42:5` validates as `pkg.py`. Scope is the visible screen by default (`--source recent` for scrollback); multi-select copies newline-joined; an empty result prints `no file paths found` and pauses ~1.5 s.
428
429	## AI usage / quota status
430
431	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --token usage="…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into (the same hook the **Review-pending flag** section above uses, but since herdr 0.7.4 tokens are a namespaced map, so a `usage` token and the `review` token coexist instead of contending for one field). A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
432
433	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)

1002:46	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
1014:58	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
1018:62	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
1023:67	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
1041:85	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux). Panel ordered as an **attention queue**, not grouped by space: `ui.agent_panel_sort = "priority"` (herdr's default is `"spaces"`) |
1056:100	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.

It is a flat workspace list by construction — a permanent collapse-all view — and it can additionally *create* a space from a zoxide frecency dir, which the native navigator cannot. `prefix + w` is the other space-level option (native sidebar navigate mode) but has no fuzzy search.
1135:179	- **The plain-open pair (`hhere` / `hroot`)** fills the gap where every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent layout. With tmux, `tmux new-session` lands you in `$PWD` directly; herdr adds a Workspace layer, so without these you'd launch herdr, create a space (which opens at `$HOME` per `new_cwd`), then `cd` by hand. `hhere` does the one-shot: `herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → attach if outside. No git requirement; the optional command runs **raw** (no specstory/on-exit wrapping — that stays with `hcode`/`hvibe`). `hhere -h` / `hroot -h` for flags. **Label caveat**: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to its root pane's *live* cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see the **cwd & workspace-naming model** section above), so the idempotent-focus is best-effort — a drifted label makes a re-run open a fresh workspace. **`-p DIR` is absolutized in your shell** (via `_herdr_abs_dir`, shared with `hcode`/`hvibe`) before it reaches herdr, so relative paths like `hhere -p ../sibling` work and a typo'd DIR is a hard error instead of a silent workspace at `$HOME` — see the `--cwd` bullet in the cwd model section for why that guard exists.
1138:182	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
1161:205	> **Quick Actions are for one-off, non-interactive commands** (the shipped examples all `open <url>`). herdr-plus runs a chosen action via `sh -c` with no PTY and no interactive stdin, so an interactive TUI misbehaves — btop exits immediately, nvtop can't receive F10. For a TUI you want the lazygit-style *floating command pane* (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) instead — that's why **btop** (`prefix+M`) and **nvtop** (`prefix+N`) are keybinds, not Quick Actions.
1173:217	> **`mode = "execute"`, not `"fork"`, for the Enter action of a channel bound to a command pane.** A `type = "pane"` binding only vanishes when its command exits, and tv exits after an `execute` action but stays alive after a `fork` one — so a `fork` Enter leaves the picker pane hovering over the workspace you just focused. `herdr-sesh`'s `[actions.open]` is `execute` for exactly this reason; its `ctrl-d` (`close_ws`) keeps `fork` because it pairs with `reload_source` and tv must survive to redraw the list. Same trade-off applies to `herdr-agent-panes` / `herdr-review`, which are still `fork` (their Enter re-focuses without leaving the picker — deliberate for triage, change it if you want one-shot jumps).

1	# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant
2	#
3	# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists
4	# panes from the running herdr server and lets you jump to the one running an
5	# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).
6	#
7	# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
8	# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
9	# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
10	# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
11	#
12	# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
13	#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
14	#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
15	#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
16	#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
17	#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)
18
19	[metadata]
20	name = "herdr-agent-panes"
21	description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
22	requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]
23
24	[source]
25	command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.agent_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
26	display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
27	output = "{split:\t:0}"
28
29	[preview]
30	command = '''
31	pane='{split:\t:0}'
32	printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  [%s]\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
33	printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
34	printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
35	printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
36	herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
37	  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
38	'''
39
40	[ui]
41	input_header = "Live herdr Agent Panes"
42
43	[ui.preview_panel]
44	size = 60
45
46	[keybindings]
47	enter = "actions:focus"
48	alt-t = "actions:focus"
49	alt-k = "actions:close_pane"
50	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
51	alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"
52
53	[actions.focus]
54	description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab"
55	command = '''
56	ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
57	[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
58	[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
59	'''
60	mode = "fork"
61
62	[actions.close_pane]
63	description = "Close the pane (confirm prompt)"
64	command = '''
65	p='{split:\t:0}'
66	[ -z "$p" ] && exit 0
67	printf 'Close pane %s? [y/N] ' "$p"
68	read -r ans
69	case "$ans" in
70	  y|Y|yes|YES) herdr pane close "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "closed $p" || echo "failed (already gone?)" ;;
71	  *) echo "aborted" ;;
72	esac
73	echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _
74	'''
75	mode = "execute"
76
77	[actions.copy_id]
78	description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
79	command = '''
80	d='{split:\t:0}'
81	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
82	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
83	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
84	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
85	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
86	fi
87	'''
88	mode = "fork"
89
90	[actions.copy_dir]
91	description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
92	command = '''
93	d='{split:\t:4}'
94	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
95	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
96	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
97	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
98	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
99	fi
100	'''
101	mode = "fork"
102

10	"""fleet — umbrella CLI for the dotfiles fleet.

12	Top-level layout (2026-05-13):
13
14	  fleet chezmoi <action>         Chezmoi-specific deploy ops (apply / status /
15	                                 diff / tail / kill / compact). Backed by
16	                                 scripts/fleet/apply.py.
17	  fleet tmux [...]               Cross-host tmux session summary
18	  fleet info [...]               Cross-host system status snapshot
19	  fleet pueue [...]              Cross-host pueue queue summary
20	  fleet exec [OPTS] -- CMD [...]  Cross-host ad-hoc command runner
21	  fleet hosts [NAME|--list*]     Interactive picker (via `tv fleet-hosts`)
22	                                 for SSH'ing into a fleet-configured host.
23	                                 Backed by scripts/fleet/hosts.py.
24	  fleet edit                     $EDITOR ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
25	                                 (fleet-meta — used by every subcommand)
26
27	The `fleet chezmoi <action>` namespace was introduced to free the top
28	level for generic primitives. `apply` / `status` / `diff` / etc. are NO
29	LONGER top-level subcommands — they only exist under `chezmoi`. The
30	`just fleet-*` recipes still call scripts/fleet/apply.py directly with
31	its underlying flags (`--readiness`, `--status`, `--kill-orphans`,
32	`--compact`, etc.) and continue to work unchanged.
33
34	Discovers the chezmoi source dir at runtime via `chezmoi source-path` (falls
35	back to ~/.local/share/chezmoi), so the binary works from any cwd.
36
37	Deployed by chezmoi as ~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet. See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md.
38	"""

47	USAGE = """\
48	Usage: fleet <subcommand> [args...]
49
50	Chezmoi-specific deploy ops (under `chezmoi` namespace):
51	  chezmoi apply [--hosts ...] [--dry-run] [--force] [...]

54	  chezmoi status --quick  Skip remote `git fetch` (faster).
55	  chezmoi status --live   Process-liveness probe (use during/after apply).
