61	  chezmoi kill [--hosts ...]
62	                          pkill chezmoi/ansible across the fleet.
63	  chezmoi compact [--run-id ID]
64	                          Post-mortem summary.
65
66	Generic primitives (top-level — work regardless of deploy tool):
67	  edit                    Open ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml in $EDITOR.
68	  tmux [--hosts ...] [--json] [--deep]
69	                          Cross-host tmux session summary.
70	  info [--hosts ...] [--ff] [--full] [--modules a,b,c] [--json]

74	                          merged JSON to `pqsum` for cleanability + recovery

78	                          Cross-host argv-list command runner. Argv after
79	                          `--` is safe by default (no shell expansion). Use
80	                          --shell bash|zsh for pipes/globs; --login for full
81	                          rc-loaded env; --ai for succeeded/differed/failed
82	                          classification across hosts.

86	                          the picker and SSHes directly. `--list*` modes are
87	                          script-friendly inventory dumps; `--describe` /
88	                          `--probe` back the TV cable's preview + Alt+T.

90	Examples:
91	  fleet chezmoi status               # readiness across all hosts
92	  fleet chezmoi apply --hosts ts_nas # apply to one host
93	  fleet chezmoi diff hanru_mac       # dry-run diff against one host

96	  fleet pueue --ai                   # AI summary of every host's queue
97	  fleet pueue --ai --report --out /tmp/q.md
98	                                     # markdown report across the fleet
99	  fleet exec -- pueue --version      # audit version drift
100	  fleet exec --ai -- df -h /         # AI summary of disk usage
101	  fleet exec --shell bash -- 'cat *.log | wc -l'
102	                                     # opt-in shell expansion (pipes/globs)
103	  fleet hosts                        # TV picker → Enter to SSH
104	  fleet hosts lab-box                # SSH straight into one host
105	  fleet hosts --list-tsv             # name<TAB>target<TAB>kind (cable source)
106
107	See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md for full mental model.
108	"""

111	def _source_path() -> Path:
112	    """Locate the chezmoi source dir. Required to find scripts/fleet_*."""
113	    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
114	    if chezmoi:
115	        try:
116	            out = subprocess.run(
117	                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
118	                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
119	            )
120	            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
121	                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
122	        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
123	            pass
124	    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
125	    if (fallback / "scripts" / "fleet" / "apply.py").is_file():
126	        return fallback
127	    print(
128	        "fleet: cannot locate chezmoi source dir.\n"
129	        "  Tried: `chezmoi source-path` and ~/.local/share/chezmoi.\n"
130	        "  Install chezmoi or ensure the source dir exists.",
131	        file=sys.stderr,
132	    )
133	    sys.exit(2)

136	def _dispatch_apply(forwarded: list[str]) -> int:
137	    """Forward to scripts.fleet.apply.main() with argv swap."""
138	    sys.argv = ["fleet apply", *forwarded]

143	def _dispatch_status(args: list[str]) -> int:
144	    """`fleet status` overload:
145	       default        → --readiness
146	       --quick        → --readiness --readiness-no-fetch
147	       --live         → --status
148	       --live --watch → --status --watch N (default 10)
149	    """
150	    live = "--live" in args
151	    quick = "--quick" in args
152	    rest = [a for a in args if a not in ("--live", "--quick")]
153	    if live:
154	        flags = ["--status"]
155	        # Default watch interval when --live is passed without a numeric --watch
156	        if "--watch" not in rest:
157	            pass  # one-shot probe
158	    else:
159	        flags = ["--readiness"]
160	        if quick:
161	            flags.append("--readiness-no-fetch")
162	    return _dispatch_apply(flags + rest)

206	def _dispatch_edit(_args: list[str]) -> int:
207	    """Open ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml in $EDITOR; seed it on first run."""

214	    editor = os.environ.get("EDITOR", "nvim")
215	    return subprocess.call([editor, str(cfg)])

248	_CHEZMOI_ACTIONS = """\
249	Subcommands under `fleet chezmoi`:
250	  apply [...]      Run chezmoi update --init across the fleet
251	  status           Pre-flight readiness probe
252	  status --quick   Skip remote git fetch
253	  status --live    Process-liveness probe

255	  tail HOST[:RUN]  Live-tail remote fleet-apply log

261	def _dispatch_chezmoi(forwarded: list[str]) -> int:
262	    """Route `fleet chezmoi <action> [args...]` to the chezmoi-backend helpers.
263
264	    The top-level `apply`/`status`/`diff`/`tail`/`kill`/`compact` subcommands
265	    were removed on 2026-05-13 to free the top level for generic primitives
266	    (`tmux` / `info` / `pueue` / `exec`). All chezmoi-specific deploy ops
267	    live under this namespace now.
268	    """
269	    if not forwarded or forwarded[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
270	        print(_CHEZMOI_ACTIONS)
271	        return 0
272	    action = forwarded[0]
273	    rest = forwarded[1:]
274	    nested = {
275	        "apply": _dispatch_apply,
276	        "status": _dispatch_status,
277	        "diff": _dispatch_diff,
278	        "tail": _dispatch_tail,
279	        "kill": _dispatch_kill,
280	        "compact": _dispatch_compact,
281	    }
282	    fn = nested.get(action)
283	    if fn is None:
284	        print(f"fleet chezmoi: unknown action '{action}'\n\n{_CHEZMOI_ACTIONS}", file=sys.stderr)
285	        return 2
286	    return fn(rest)
287
288
289	def main() -> int:
290	    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
291	        print(USAGE)
292	        return 0
293
294	    sub = sys.argv[1]
295	    rest = sys.argv[2:]
296
297	    src = _source_path()
298	    if str(src) not in sys.path:
299	        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
300
301	    dispatch = {
302	        # Chezmoi-specific deploy ops under `fleet chezmoi <action>`.
303	        # The bare top-level names (apply/status/diff/tail/kill/compact) were
304	        # removed on 2026-05-13 — `fleet apply` now errors with "unknown
305	        # subcommand" by design so the namespace stays clean.
306	        "chezmoi": _dispatch_chezmoi,
307	        # Fleet-meta (inventory editor; no SSH).
308	        "edit": _dispatch_edit,
309	        # Generic cross-host primitives (deploy-tool-agnostic).
310	        "tmux": _dispatch_tmux,
311	        "info": _dispatch_info,
312	        "pueue": _dispatch_pueue,
313	        "exec": _dispatch_exec,
314	        "hosts": _dispatch_hosts,
315	    }
316	    fn = dispatch.get(sub)
317	    if fn is None:
318	        print(f"fleet: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
319	        return 2
320	    return fn(rest)

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# herdr analog of tmux's `prefix + u` (joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url). Reads a herdr
6	# pane's text, extracts every URL-like token (same rewrite rules as tmux-fzf-url:
7	# http(s)/ftp/file, bare www., IPv4[:port], git@ SSH remotes, quoted owner/repo,
8	# npm imports), fuzzy-picks with fzf (multi-select), then opens each choice via
9	# the repo's cross-platform `x open` (wslview / open / xdg-open).
10	#
11	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
12	# script exits), bound to prefix+u in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. The
13	# SAME building blocks as the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the
14	# keybind-context pane) with a `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read`
15	# for the text, and an absolute-path opener fallback because a command pane runs
16	# us via `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
17	#
18	# Usage:
19	#   url-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent]
20	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (passed by the keybind), else the current
21	# focused pane. --source defaults to visible (tmux-fzf-url's on-screen scope);
22	# --source recent scans the full retained scrollback.
23	#
24	# Consumers: the prefix+u keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
25	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Open a URL from the pane".
26	set -eu
27

2	# ~/.config/herdr/path-pick.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Copy-a-file-path picker — the copy-path sibling of url-pick.sh (which OPENS
6	# URLs). Reads the focused pane, extracts path-like tokens (borrowing extrakto's
7	# path heuristics), and presents a TWO-TIER fzf list: paths that EXIST relative to
8	# the pane cwd on top (copied as their resolved ABSOLUTE path), unverified
9	# candidates (as-seen) below a separator. The choice is copied via `x copy`.
10	#
11	# The existence check is the noise-killer extrakto lacks: file paths have no
12	# scheme:// marker, so regex alone matches dates (2024/01/02), rates (10k/s) and
13	# fractions (1/2); validating against the pane's live cwd drops nearly all of it.
14	#
15	# Runs inside a herdr `[[keys.command]] type="pane"` (a PTY that closes when this
16	# script exits), bound to prefix+p in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml. Mirrors
17	# the sibling pane-copy.sh: $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (the keybind var) with a
18	# `herdr pane current` fallback, `herdr pane read` for the text, `x copy` for the
19	# clipboard, and an absolute-path `x` fallback because a command pane runs us via
20	# `sh -c` without the interactive-shell PATH.
21	#
22	# Usage:
23	#   path-pick.sh [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]
24	# PANE defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID, else the current focused pane. --source
25	# defaults to visible; --source recent scans the full scrollback. --cwd is the
26	# directory relative paths are resolved against for the existence check; it
27	# defaults to $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD → `herdr pane get` foreground_cwd →
28	# process-info cwd → $PWD.
29	#
30	# Consumers: the prefix+p keybind (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). See
31	# docs/tools/herdr.md § "Copy a file path from the pane".
32	set -eu
33
34	usage() { printf 'usage: %s [PANE_ID] [--source visible|recent] [--cwd DIR]\n' "$0" >&2; exit 64; }
35
36	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
37	command -v fzf   >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "path-pick: fzf is required"  >&2; exit 1; }
38
39	# Resolve the clipboard CLI (`x copy`) even without the interactive PATH.
40	if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then
41	    X_BIN=x
42	elif [ -x "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x" ]; then
43	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"
44	else
45	    echo "path-pick: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
46	    exit 1
47	fi
48
49	pane=""
50	source="visible"
51	cwd=""
52	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
53	    case "$1" in
54	        --source) source="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
55	        --source=*) source="${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
56	        --cwd) cwd="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
57	        --cwd=*) cwd="${1#--cwd=}"; shift ;;
58	        -h|--help) usage ;;
59	        -*) usage ;;
60	        *)
61	            if [ -z "$pane" ]; then
62	                pane="$1"
63	                shift
64	            else
65	                usage
66	            fi
67	            ;;
68	    esac
69	done
70
71	case "$source" in
72	    visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
73	    *) echo "path-pick: --source must be visible|recent" >&2; exit 64 ;;
74	esac
75
76	# Resolve pane (keybind passes $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID; fall back to current).
77	if [ -z "$pane" ]; then

79	    pane=$(herdr pane current 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
80	fi
81	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "path-pick: could not determine a pane id" >&2; exit 1; }
82

84	if [ -z "$cwd" ] && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
85	    cwd=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.pane.foreground_cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
86	    [ -n "$cwd" ] || cwd=$(herdr pane process-info --pane "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
87	        | jq -r '.result.process_info.foreground_processes[0].cwd // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)

90
91	content=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \

94	# Path candidates (extrakto path heuristics, POSIX-ized): slash-bearing tokens
95	# (abs /…, home ~/…, rel ./ ../ a/b/c) + bare filename.ext. rstrip trailing
96	# ",):; then drop rate/fraction noise (extrakto's exclude: 10k/s, 1/2). dedupe.
97	cands=$(printf '%s\n' "$content" \
98	    | grep -oE '(~|\.\.?)?/?[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._+~-]+)+|[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8}' \

103	if [ -z "$cands" ]; then
104	    printf 'path-pick: no file paths found in pane %s (%s)\n' "$pane" "$source" >&2
105	    sleep 1.5   # command pane closes on exit — pause so the message is visible
106	    exit 0
107	fi
108
109	# Two tiers: exists-under-cwd (resolved absolute) vs the rest (as-seen).
110	exist=""
111	maybe=""
112	OLDIFS=$IFS
113	IFS='
114	'
115	for c in $cands; do
116	    base=$(printf '%s' "$c" | sed -E 's/:[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$//')   # strip :line[:col] for the test
117	    case "$base" in
118	        /*)   abs="$base" ;;
119	        \~/*) abs="$HOME/${base#\~/}" ;;
120	        *)    abs="$cwd/$base" ;;
121	    esac
122	    if [ -e "$abs" ]; then
123	        rp=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$(dirname -- "$abs")" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s/%s' "$(pwd -P)" "$(basename -- "$abs")") \
124	            || rp="$abs"
125	        exist="$exist$rp
126	"
127	    else
128	        maybe="$maybe$c
129	"
130	    fi
131	done
132	IFS=$OLDIFS
133
134	exist=$(printf '%s' "$exist" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
135	maybe=$(printf '%s' "$maybe" | grep -v '^$' | sort -u || true)
136
137	SEP='────────  unverified (not found under cwd)  ────────'
138	list=$(
139	    [ -n "$exist" ] && printf '%s\n' "$exist"
140	    [ -n "$maybe" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$SEP"; printf '%s\n' "$maybe"; }
141	)
142
143	# fzf multi-select; Esc / no-match (exit 130 / 1) → clean no-op.
144	chosen=$(printf '%s\n' "$list" | fzf --multi --no-sort --height=100% --border \
145	    --prompt='path> ' --header="Enter=copy · Tab=multi · cwd=$cwd") || exit 0

1	# herdr: fix hvibe/hcode attach + add `--session`, document sessions & `--remote`
2
3	## Context
4
5	While using herdr the user hit a cluster of small gaps:
6
7	1. **`hvibe`/`hcode` don't attach when run from *outside* herdr.** They end with `herdr workspace focus`, which only moves an *already-attached* client's focus. From a plain terminal the workspace is created but nothing appears — you must then type `herdr` to attach. (Inside herdr, `workspace focus` already switches the live client, so that path is fine.)
8	2. **No way to target a specific herdr session.** A herdr server hosts multiple named **sessions** (`default`, `test`, …), each with its own socket. `hvibe`/`hcode` always hit whatever socket the CLI defaults to. There's no `--session` flag.
9	3. **Docs gaps.** `docs/tools/herdr.md` is thorough on Workspace→Tab→Pane but never documents (a) that a server hosts **multiple named sessions** (the extra top tree level the user discovered), nor (b) **`herdr --remote`** at all. No `herdr.zh-TW.md` exists.
10
11	Empirically verified during planning (we are currently running *inside* herdr's `default` session):
12	- `herdr` CLI subcommands honor the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — setting it to another session's `socket_path` routes `workspace create/list` to that session (probe workspace landed in `test`, invisible to `default`). There is **no** `--session`/`--socket` flag on the subcommands; the env var is the only lever.
13	- Ambient env inside a herdr pane: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (= current session's socket). So "am I inside herdr" = `[ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ]`, and inside herdr the CLI already targets the current session for free.
14	- `herdr session list --json` → `.sessions[] | {name, running, socket_path, default}` — authoritative name→socket resolver (the text table's `herdr.socket` is wrong; JSON says `herdr.sock`).
15	- `herdr --remote <target>` **auto-installs** a matching server binary on the remote over SSH; the user's `Connection closed by … port 22` was transient (key-auth SSH to `local_ubuntu` works now; the client log shows `--remote` bridging clipboard fine the day before).
16
17	Outcome: `hvibe`/`hcode` behave correctly from any context and accept `--session`; docs cover named sessions + remote; a zh-TW page and the missing zh-TW alias rows are added.
18
19	## Design decisions (resolved)
20
21	- **Attach from outside** mirrors `svibe`'s `_sesh_attach_or_switch` ($TMUX branch) but adapted: the repo-named object in herdr is the *workspace*, so we attach the whole **session** and rely on the prior `workspace focus` for landing spot. Attach runs as a **child process (no `exec`)**, exactly like svibe.
22	- **`--session` targeting** uses `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=…` (function-scoped export, auto-restored on return — supported in bash 4+ and zsh, matching the file's existing `local -a`/`[[ ]]`/process-subst baseline). Never a bare `export` (would leak the override into the user's shell).
23	- **`--session` when the target isn't running → error with a hint** (`herdr --session NAME` to start it first), rather than trying to spawn a headless server (chicken/egg with workspace creation). Small, predictable.
24	- Default session name is `default`; attach via bare `herdr` for default, `herdr session attach <name>` for named.
25
26	## Changes
27
28	### 1. `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (primary)
29
30	Add two small shared helpers near the existing `_herdr_*` helpers:
31
32	```sh
33	# Resolve the target session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session value.
34	# Echoes "<name>\t<socket_override_or_empty>". socket is non-empty ONLY when the
35	# caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit --session). Errors (return 1)
36	# if an explicit --session isn't a running session.
37	function _herdr_session_target() { … herdr session list --json | jq … ; }
38
39	# From OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client so the just-focused workspace is visible.
40	# Inside herdr (HERDR_ENV set) the focus calls already switched the live client.
41	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
42	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
43	    local session="${1:-default}"
44	    if [ "$session" = default ]; then herdr; else herdr session attach "$session"; fi
45	}
46	```
47
48	In **both** `herdr-vibe` and `herdr-code`:
49	- Parse a new `--session NAME` flag (add to the `while`/`case`, the `-h` help text, and reject empty).
50	- After arg parsing, resolve the session:
51	  ```sh
52	  local sess_line sess_name sess_sock
53	  sess_line=$(_herdr_session_target "$session_arg") || return 1
54	  sess_name=${sess_line%%$'\t'*}; sess_sock=${sess_line#*$'\t'}
55	  [ -n "$sess_sock" ] && local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$sess_sock"
56	  ```
57	  (When inside herdr with no `--session`, `sess_sock` is empty → ambient socket is used untouched; `sess_name` is derived for the — unused — attach path.)
58	- **Idempotent fast path** (`existing` found): keep `herdr workspace focus "$existing"` but append `_herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"` (still gated on `--no-attach`).
59	- **End-of-build attach block** (`if [ "$no_attach" -ne 1 ]; then …`): keep the existing `workspace focus`/`tab focus`/`pane focus` lines, add `_herdr_attach_if_outside "$sess_name"` as the last line inside the block.
60	- Update each `-h` help block: document `--session NAME` and the new "attaches when run outside herdr" behavior.
61
62	No change to the reused `_sesh_*` helpers or the layout logic.
63
64	### 2. `docs/tools/herdr.md`
65
66	- **"Model differences vs tmux"**: state that a herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions** (`default` + named, each its own socket under `sessions/<name>/herdr.sock`); full depth is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** (one level deeper than tmux). Add a short **"Named sessions"** subsection: `herdr --session NAME`, `herdr session list|attach|stop|delete`, and that CLI subcommands target a session via **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** (no `--session` flag on subcommands).
67	- **New "Remote (`herdr --remote`)"** section: thin-client model (SSHes to target, **auto-installs** the server binary, bridges clipboard/image-paste, keeps local keybindings); usage `herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]`; prereqs (SSH access + install perms + a supported host); the `[remote].manage_ssh_config` knob; troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed` = transient SSH close → verify plain SSH reachability + check `herdr-client.log`/`herdr.log`.
68	- **`hvibe`/`hcode` section**: document new `--session` flag + auto-attach-from-outside.
69	- Fix the custom-command env note to distinguish **ambient** pane env (`HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`/`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`) from the `[[keys.command]]`-only `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars.
70
71	### 3. `docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md` (new)
72
73	Full zh-TW translation. Reuse the fixed boilerplate: `# Herdr —— …` H1 + the verbatim `!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"` block (copy from `docs/tools/worktrunk.zh-TW.md:1-11`); `中文 (English)` on first use; leave CLI flags/filenames untranslated. Mirror the English section set. No `mkdocs.yml` nav edit needed — the `i18n` plugin (`docs_structure: suffix`) auto-pairs it.
74
75	### 4. `docs/shells/aliases.md` + `docs/shells/aliases.zh-TW.md`
76
77	- `aliases.md:469-470`: add `--session` to the `hvibe`/`hcode` row descriptions.
78	- `aliases.zh-TW.md`: **backfill the two missing `herdr-vibe`/`herdr-code` rows** (existing gap — the zh-TW table skips from `svibe` at :461 to `try-sesh` at :462), including `--session`.
79
80	### 5. Light touch-ups (review only, likely no change)
81
82	- `backlog/hvibe-herdr-surfacing.md`: add a one-line "Update (2026-07): hvibe/hcode now auto-attach from outside herdr + take `--session`" note (that backlog's axis — surfacing in the herdr UI via keybinding/tv/Projects — remains open).
83	- `TODO.md:124-125`, `README.md:258`, `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:1013-1014`: no change (install facts / capability summary unchanged).
84
85	## Verification
86
87	1. **Shell syntax**: `bash -n` **and** `zsh -n` on `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`.
88	2. **Functional (against the live server; we're inside herdr `default`)**:
89	   - `source ~/.config/shell/22_sesh.sh; source dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` (or `chezmoi apply` first), then `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h` show `--session`.
90	   - `hvibe --no-attach --session test -p <some repo>` → confirm the `vibe/<repo>` workspace lands in the **test** session via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=<test sock> herdr workspace list`, and is **absent** from `default`; then `herdr workspace close` it to clean up.

 `./pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`

```text
1	# `hhere -p ../sibling` ignores the path and opens the workspace at `~`
2
3	## Symptoms
4
5	From a repo, point `hhere` at a sibling directory with a **relative** path:
6
7	```console
8	Pueue-Raycast-Extension on  main
9	❯ hhere -p ../Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension
10	```
11
12	The command **succeeds** — exit 0, nothing on stderr, no herdr error JSON — and a
13	workspace is created. But the new space's shell is sitting in `$HOME`, not in
14	`../Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension`. Confirm with:
15
16	```console
17	$ herdr pane list --workspace w1E | jq -r '.result.panes[].cwd'
18	/Users/david
19	```
20
21	Two details that make this hard to spot:
22
23	- **Absolute paths work fine.** `hhere -p ~/Documents/Program/Foo` (the shell
24	  expands `~` before `hhere` ever sees it) lands correctly, so the flag looks
25	  like it works — only the relative form is broken.
26	- **The workspace label is still right.** The label comes from `basename` in the
27	  shell function, so the space is *named* `Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension` while
28	  its pane is in `~`. herdr only auto-relabels to the live cwd basename after a
29	  `cd` in tab 1, so nothing renames the space to `~` to give the game away.
30
31	The same applied to `hcode -p ../foo` / `hvibe -p ../foo`, but there the miss
32	surfaced as the misleading error `not inside a git repo` instead.
33
34	## Root cause
35
36	**`herdr workspace create --cwd` is resolved by the herdr *server*, not by the
37	calling shell.** The server's own working directory is whatever directory
38	`herdr server` happened to be launched from — for a server started from this
39	repo, `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi`:
40
41	```console
42	$ lsof -a -p "$(pgrep -f 'herdr server')" -d cwd | tail -1
43	herdr  1576 david  cwd  DIR  1,5  2528  24013827  /Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi
44	```
45
46	So the relative path is joined to *that*, not to your `$PWD`. Proof — from
47	`/tmp/hh-test/alpha`, both of these ignore `$PWD` completely:
48
49	```console
50	$ cd /tmp/hh-test/alpha
51	$ herdr workspace create --cwd ./docs --label T --no-focus | jq -r '.result.root_pane.cwd'
52	/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs      # ← server cwd + ./docs
53
54	$ herdr workspace create --cwd ../bravo --label T2 --no-focus | jq -r '.result.root_pane.cwd'
55	/Users/david                                # ← miss → SILENT fallback to $HOME
56	```
57
58	The second line is the whole bug: when the server-side join misses, herdr does
59	**not** error — it falls back to `$HOME` and returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}`.
60
61	**tmux does not behave this way**, which is why the sesh originals
62	(`shere` / `scode` / `svibe`) never needed a guard and the herdr ports looked
63	like faithful analogs. tmux resolves `new-session -c` **client-side**:
64
65	```console
66	$ cd /tmp/tmux-rel/alpha
67	$ tmux new-session -d -s T -c ../bravo
68	$ tmux display-message -p -t T '#{pane_current_path}'
69	/private/tmp/tmux-rel/bravo                 # ← correct, despite the tmux server
70	                                            #   also living in .../chezmoi
71	```
72
73	## Fix
74
75	Absolutize `-p/--path` **in the calling shell**, before it reaches herdr —
76	`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh` → `_herdr_abs_dir`, used by `hhere`, `hcode`,
77	and `hvibe`:
78
79	```bash
80	function _herdr_abs_dir() {
81	    local abs
82	    abs=$(CDPATH=''; cd -- "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
83	    if [ -z "$abs" ]; then
84	        echo "${2:-herdr}: --path is not a directory: $1" >&2
85	        return 1
86	    fi
87	    printf '%s\n' "$abs"
88	}
89	```
90
91	- `CDPATH=''` — without it, a `CDPATH` hit can retarget the `cd` to a *different*
92	  directory of the same name **and** echo the resolved path into the capture,
93	  giving a two-line `$target`. (Same idiom already used in
94	  `dot_config/herdr/executable_path-pick.sh`.) Path arguments should not honour
95	  `CDPATH`; `-p bravo` now means `./bravo`, always.
96	- `--` — a target beginning with `-` is a path, not a `cd` flag.
97	- `>/dev/null` — belt-and-braces against the same echo.
98	- `pwd -P` — canonicalize symlinks, matching what `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
99	  returns for the `hcode`/`hvibe` paths.
100	- **Returning 1 on a non-directory is the point.** Previously a typo'd `-p` was
101	  indistinguishable from success; now `hhere -p ../typo` says
102	  `hhere: --path is not a directory: ../typo` instead of silently opening `~`,
103	  and `hcode -p ../typo` no longer misreports it as `not inside a git repo`.
104
105	`hroot` needs nothing — it derives its path from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
106	(absolute) and passes it through `hhere`.
107
108	## Generalisable rule
109
110	**Any path handed to a daemon over a socket must be absolutized by the client.**
111	The server has its own cwd and no idea where you are. This applies to every
112	`--cwd` in `24_herdr.sh` and to future herdr CLI surfaces
113	(`tab create --cwd`, `pane split --cwd`) — those are currently safe only because
114	they are fed `$repo_root` from `git rev-parse`, which is already absolute. If a
115	new call site ever gets a user-supplied path, route it through `_herdr_abs_dir`.
116
117	The `--cwd` consumers that are *not* affected, and why:
118
119	| Call site | Path source | Safe because |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| `24_herdr.sh` `hvibe`/`hcode` `workspace create` / `pane split` / `_herdr_tool_tab` | `_sesh_git_root` | `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` is absolute |
122	| `dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh` | `herdr pane get` → `foreground_cwd` | herdr reports absolute paths |
123	| `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml` → `actions.open` | zoxide | `zoxide query -l` emits absolute paths |
124
125	## Related
126
127	- [`docs/tools/herdr.md`](../docs/tools/herdr.md) § cwd & workspace-naming model
128	- `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` — the tmux originals, unaffected (client-side `-c`)
129
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	#
3	# ping-monitor — record ping over time and flag latency spikes.
4	#
5	# Normal Wi-Fi gaming shows a low, steady baseline with occasional huge
6	# spikes. Pinging your own gateway isolates whether those spikes are local
7	# (Wi-Fi / router) vs. upstream: if the GATEWAY already spikes, the problem
8	# is the local wireless medium, not the ISP / game server. See
9	# docs/playbooks/wifi-latency-spikes.md.
10	#
11	# Usage:
12	#   ping-monitor [TARGET] [SPIKE_MS] [INTERVAL_S]
13	#   ping-monitor -g | --gateway [SPIKE_MS] [INTERVAL_S]
14	#
15	# Examples:
16	#   ping-monitor                 # ping default gateway, spike >100ms
17	#   ping-monitor -g 10           # gateway, flag anything >10ms (local test)
18	#   ping-monitor 8.8.8.8 150 0.5 # upstream, >150ms spike, every 0.5s
19	#
20	# Ctrl-C prints a summary (min/avg/max, p50/p95/p99, spike count, loss).
21	# A full log is written to ~/ping-monitor-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.log.
22
23	set -u
24
25	is_macos() { [[ "$(uname -s)" == Darwin ]]; }
26
27	default_gateway() {
28	    if is_macos; then
29	        route -n get default 2>/dev/null | awk '/gateway:/{print $2; exit}'
30	    else
31	        ip route show default 2>/dev/null | awk '/default/{print $3; exit}'
32	    fi
33	}
34
35	# One ICMP echo, ~$1s timeout, to $2. Prints the RTT in ms, or nothing on loss.
36	ping_once() {
37	    local timeout_s="$1" host="$2" out
38	    if is_macos; then
39	        out="$(ping -c1 -t"$timeout_s" "$host" 2>/dev/null)"
40	    else
41	        out="$(ping -c1 -W"$timeout_s" "$host" 2>/dev/null)"
42	    fi
43	    printf '%s' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*time=\([0-9.]*\) *ms.*/\1/p'
44	}
45
46	# ---- args ----
47	TARGET=""
48	case "${1:-}" in
49	    -g | --gateway)
50	        TARGET="$(default_gateway)"
51	        shift
52	        [[ -z "$TARGET" ]] && { echo "ping-monitor: could not find default gateway" >&2; exit 1; }
53	        ;;
54	    -h | --help)
55	        sed -n '3,28p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
56	        exit 0
57	        ;;
58	    "" ) ;;
59	    * ) TARGET="$1"; shift ;;
60	esac
61
62	if [[ -z "$TARGET" ]]; then
63	    TARGET="$(default_gateway)"
64	    [[ -z "$TARGET" ]] && { echo "ping-monitor: no target and no default gateway; pass a host" >&2; exit 1; }
65	    echo "No target given; using default gateway: $TARGET"
66	fi
67
68	THRESHOLD="${1:-100}"
69	INTERVAL="${2:-1}"
70	TIMEOUT=2
71
72	LOG="$HOME/ping-monitor-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
73
74	count=0 loss=0 spikes=0 sum=0 min="" max=0
75	times_file="$(mktemp)"
76
77	RED=$'\033[31m'; YEL=$'\033[33m'; DIM=$'\033[2m'; RST=$'\033[0m'
78
79	cleanup() {
80	    echo ""
81	    echo "================ summary ================"
82	    echo "target          : $TARGET"
83	    echo "spike threshold : ${THRESHOLD} ms"
84	    local total=$(( count + loss ))
85	    echo "packets         : $total  (ok $count / timeout $loss)"
86	    if (( total > 0 )); then
87	        echo "loss            : $(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.1f\", $loss*100/$total}")%"
88	    fi
89	    if (( count > 0 )); then
90	        echo "min/avg/max     : ${min} / $(awk "BEGIN{printf \"%.1f\", $sum/$count}") / ${max} ms"
91	        sort -n "$times_file" > "${times_file}.s"
92	        local p50 p95 p99
93	        p50=$(awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{print a[int(NR*0.50)?int(NR*0.50):1]}' "${times_file}.s")
94	        p95=$(awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{print a[int(NR*0.95)?int(NR*0.95):1]}' "${times_file}.s")
95	        p99=$(awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{print a[int(NR*0.99)?int(NR*0.99):1]}' "${times_file}.s")
96	        echo "p50/p95/p99     : ${p50} / ${p95} / ${p99} ms"
97	        rm -f "${times_file}.s"
98	    fi
99	    echo "spikes          : ${spikes}  (>${THRESHOLD}ms)"
100	    echo "log             : $LOG"
101	    echo "========================================"
102	    rm -f "$times_file"
103	    exit 0
104	}
105	trap cleanup INT TERM
106
107	echo "Monitoring $TARGET  (spike >${THRESHOLD}ms, every ${INTERVAL}s)  log-> $LOG"
108	echo "Ctrl-C to stop and see the summary"
109	echo "----------------------------------------------"
110
111	while true; do
112	    ts="$(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
113	    t="$(ping_once "$TIMEOUT" "$TARGET")"
114	    if [[ -z "$t" ]]; then
115	        loss=$((loss + 1))
116	        line="$ts  TIMEOUT / loss"
117	        echo "${RED}${line}${RST}"; echo "$line" >> "$LOG"
118	    else
119	        count=$((count + 1))
120	        echo "$t" >> "$times_file"
121	        sum=$(awk "BEGIN{print $sum + $t}")
122	        [[ -z "$min" ]] && min="$t"
123	        (( $(awk "BEGIN{print ($t < $min)}") )) && min="$t"
124	        (( $(awk "BEGIN{print ($t > $max)}") )) && max="$t"
125	        if (( $(awk "BEGIN{print ($t >= $THRESHOLD)}") )); then
126	            spikes=$((spikes + 1))
127	            line="$ts  ${t} ms  <<< SPIKE"
128	            echo "${RED}${line}${RST}"; echo "$line" >> "$LOG"
129	        elif (( $(awk "BEGIN{print ($t >= $THRESHOLD*0.5)}") )); then
130	            line="$ts  ${t} ms"
131	            echo "${YEL}${line}${RST}"; echo "$line" >> "$LOG"
132	        else
133	            line="$ts  ${t} ms"
134	            echo "${DIM}${line}${RST}"; echo "$line" >> "$LOG"
135	        fi
136	    fi
137	    sleep "$INTERVAL"
138	done
139
```

176	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.

180
181	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
182
183	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
184
185	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
186	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
187	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
188	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
189
190	### What we DO track
191
192	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
193	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
194	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
195	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
196
197	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
198
199	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
200
201	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
202
203	Output paths:
204	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
205	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
206
207	### Manual rerun
208
209	```bash
210	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
211	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
212	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
213	```
214
215	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
216
217	### Opt out
218
219	```bash
220	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
221	```
222
223	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
224
225	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
226
227	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
228
229	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
230
231	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
232	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
233	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
234	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg` / `agent-warmup`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
235
236	## Priority / Override Order
237
238	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
239
240	```
241	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
242	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
243	3. ~/.docker/completions/
244	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
245	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
246	```
247
248	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
249
250	```zsh
251	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
252	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
253	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
254	```
255
256	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
257
258	```zsh
259	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
260	```
261
262	## FAQ
263
264	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
265	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
266
267	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
268	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
269
270	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
271	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.

49	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
50
51	The `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism spans **6 surfaces that must move together** — devtools install, `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`, `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`, `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl` hooks, `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (+ its `modify_package.json`), and `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`'s producers API. Exact contents: [workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md) § Status icon mechanics; why it leaks: [workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
52
53	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (writes parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears). The workmux hook entries are **unconditional** — the `agentSounds` prompt gates only the notify.sh / peon-ping entries in the same file. `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux) stay distinct tools.
54
55	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
56
57	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply`; see [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template and disambiguation table.
58
59	**Fallback rules**, so this still binds when the skill can't be loaded:
60
61	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
62	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
63	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
64	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it recurs across machines, silently corrupts state, or has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.

66	## Chezmoi templating conventions
67
68	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
69
70	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
71
72	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
73
74	## Hard repo invariants
75
76	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
77
78	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
79
80	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
81
82	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
83
84	**Hard rules**:
85
86	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
87	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
88	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
89
90	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
91
92	### Three-tier user-local override layer
93
94	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
95
96	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
97
98	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
99
100	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
101
102	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
103
104	**Hard rules**:
105
106	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
107	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
108	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
109	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
110	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
111
112	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
113
114	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
115
116	**Hard rules**:
117
118	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
119	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
120	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
121	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
122	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
123	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
124
125	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
126
127	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
128
129	**Hard rules**:
130
131	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
132	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
133	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
134	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
135	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
136
137	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
138
139	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
140
141	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
142
143	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
144
145	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
146	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
147	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
148	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
149	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
150	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
151	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
152	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
153
154	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
155
156	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
157	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
158
159	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
160
161	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
162
163	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
164
165	**Hard rules**:
166
167	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
168	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
169	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
170	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
171
172	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
173
174	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
175
176	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
177
178	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
179	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
180	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
181	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
182	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
183
184	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
185
186	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
187
188	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# sesh-preview — multi-section preview for sesh fzf picker
3	#
4	# Sesh passes one argument that is either:
5	#   - an absolute path (zoxide / find sources)
6	#   - a session name like "icon  name  /path" (sesh's --icons output)
7	#
8	# We extract the path (last token), then render in this priority:
9	#   1. Header: dir name + git branch (if any) + last-modified
10	#   2. README.md (first 25 lines, syntax-highlighted via bat if available)
11	#   3. Recent git log (5 commits, oneline) — only if a git repo
12	#   4. Directory listing (eza tree if available, else ls)
13	#
14	# Designed to be safely called from sesh's preview_command. Stays under
15	# ~50 lines of output so fzf preview pane doesn't scroll on first paint.
16
17	set -u
18
19	raw="${1:-}"
20	[[ -z "$raw" ]] && exit 0
21
22	# Extract the path: last whitespace-separated token. Works for both
23	# bare paths and sesh's "icon  name  /path" format.
24	path="${raw##* }"
25	# Strip trailing slash for consistency
26	path="${path%/}"
27
28	# Sesh sometimes hands us the session name only (no path). Resolve via sesh.
29	if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then
30	    # Try interpreting whole arg as session name → ask sesh for its path
31	    resolved="$(sesh list -t -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg n "$raw" \
32	        '.[] | select(.Name==$n) | .Path' 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
33	    [[ -n "$resolved" && -d "$resolved" ]] && path="$resolved"
34	fi
35
36	[[ ! -d "$path" ]] && { echo "(not a directory: $path)"; exit 0; }
37
38	# Color helpers — use tput if terminal supports it
39	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
40	    bold=$(tput bold 2>/dev/null || true)
41	    dim=$(tput dim 2>/dev/null || true)
42	    reset=$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null || true)
43	    cyan=$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null || true)
44	    yellow=$(tput setaf 3 2>/dev/null || true)
45	else
46	    bold="" dim="" reset="" cyan="" yellow=""
47	fi
48
49	# ── 1. Header ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50	name="$(basename "$path")"
51	parent_short="$(dirname "$path" | sed "s|^$HOME|~|")"
52	echo "${bold}${cyan}${name}${reset} ${dim}— ${parent_short}/${reset}"
53
54	if git_branch=$(git -C "$path" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null); then
55	    git_status_count=$(git -C "$path" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
56	    git_ahead_behind=$(git -C "$path" rev-list --left-right --count "@{upstream}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null \
57	        | awk '{ if ($1>0||$2>0) printf "↓%s ↑%s", $1, $2 }')
58	    echo "${dim}git:${reset} ${yellow}${git_branch}${reset} ${dim}(${git_status_count} dirty${git_ahead_behind:+, $git_ahead_behind})${reset}"
59	fi
60
61	# Last modified (mtime of dir)
62	if mtime=$(stat -f "%Sm" -t "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" "$path" 2>/dev/null); then
63	    echo "${dim}mtime: ${mtime}${reset}"
64	fi
65
66	echo
67
68	# ── 2. README ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69	readme=""
70	for f in README.md README.rst README.txt readme.md README; do
71	    if [[ -f "$path/$f" ]]; then readme="$path/$f"; break; fi
72	done
73
74	if [[ -n "$readme" ]]; then
75	    echo "${bold}── README ──${reset}"
76	    if command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
77	        bat --color=always --style=plain --line-range=:25 --paging=never "$readme"
78	    else
79	        head -25 "$readme"
80	    fi
81	    echo
82	fi
83
84	# ── 3. Recent commits ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
85	if [[ -n "${git_branch:-}" ]]; then
86	    echo "${bold}── Recent commits ──${reset}"
87	    git -C "$path" log --oneline --color=always -5 2>/dev/null
88	    echo
89	fi
90
91	# ── 4. Directory tree ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
92	echo "${bold}── Files ──${reset}"
93	if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then
94	    eza --tree --level=2 --git-ignore --color=always --icons \
95	        --ignore-glob='node_modules|.git|__pycache__|.venv|target|dist|build' \
96	        "$path" 2>/dev/null | head -30
97	else
98	    ls -la "$path" | head -25
99	fi
100
```

189	    if not ts:

191	    m = _ISO_PAT.match(ts)
192	    if not m:
193	        return None
194	    head, tz = m.group(1), m.group(2)
195	    if not tz:
196	        normalised = head
197	    elif tz == "Z":
198	        normalised = head + "+00:00"
199	    elif re.match(r"^[+-]\d{4}$", tz):
200	        normalised = head + f"{tz[:3]}:{tz[3:]}"
201	    else:
202	        normalised = head + tz
203	    try:

205	    except ValueError:

111
112	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Most live in the POSIX `dot_config/shell/` layer (sourced by both zsh and bash); zsh-only ones live in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
113
114	| Tool | Where | How | Cached? |
115	|------|-------|-----|---------|
116	| `fzf` | `dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh` | `eval "$(fzf --zsh)"` (zsh) / `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` (bash) | — |
117	| `zoxide` | `dot_config/shell/20_zoxide.sh` | `eval "$(zoxide init <shell>)"` | — |
118	| `direnv` | `dot_config/shell/30_direnv.sh` | `eval "$(direnv hook <shell>)"` | — |
119	| `marimo` | `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh` | `_MARIMO_COMPLETE=<shell>_source marimo` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/marimo_completion.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `marimo-update-completion` |

122
123	> **Cached entries** auto-invalidate when the tool's binary mtime is newer than the cache file (`[ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]`) — catches `mise install <NEW>`, `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`. Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. The pattern mirrors `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` (the canonical example).
124
125	### D. No completion support
126
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).

1	# 48_pqsum_completion.zsh - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
2	# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum (argparse, positional mode +
3	# many flags). Dynamic group completion via `pueue status --json | jq`.
4
5	(( $+commands[pqsum] )) || return 0
6
7	_pqsum() {
8	    local context state state_descr line
9	    typeset -A opt_args
10
11	    _arguments -C \
12	        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
13	        '(-g --group)'{-g,--group}'=[restrict to one pueue group]:group:->group' \
14	        '--report[emit markdown report (ai mode only)]' \
15	        '--out=[write report to PATH]:path:_files' \
16	        '--clean[execute cleanup commands on safe-to-clean groups]' \
17	        '--yes[skip y/N prompts (with --clean)]' \
18	        '--multi-host[tell LLM the input describes multiple hosts]' \
19	        '--stdin-json[read pre-merged host snapshots from stdin]' \
20	        '--raw-stdin[read raw `pueue status --json` from stdin]' \
21	        '--host=[override host name when --raw-stdin is set]:hostname:_hosts' \
22	        '--deep[include extra recovery context (last ~20 log lines per failed task)]' \
23	        '(-r --refresh)'{-r,--refresh}'[bypass prompt-hash cache]' \
24	        '--no-cache[do not read or write the cache]' \
25	        '--dry-run[print AI prompt; no AI call]' \
26	        '1:mode:(text ai json)'
27
28	    case "$state" in
29	        group)
30	            local -a groups
31	            if (( $+commands[pueue] )) && (( $+commands[jq] )); then
32	                groups=( ${(f)"$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)"} )
33	                (( ${#groups} )) && _describe 'pueue group' groups
34	            fi
35	            ;;
36	    esac
37	}
38
39	compdef _pqsum pqsum
40

130
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).

172	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
173
174	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
175	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
176	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
177	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
178	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
179	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
180
181	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
182
183	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
184
185	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
186	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
187	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
188	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
189
190	### What we DO track
191
192	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
193	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
194	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
195	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
196
197	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
198
199	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
200
201	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
202
203	Output paths:
204	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
205	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
206
207	### Manual rerun
208
209	```bash
210	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
211	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
212	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
213	```
214
215	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
216
217	### Opt out
218
219	```bash
220	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
221	```
222
223	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
224
225	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
226
227	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
228
229	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
230
231	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
232	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
233	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
234	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg` / `agent-warmup`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-54_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
235
236	## Priority / Override Order
237
238	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
239
240	```
241	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
242	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
243	3. ~/.docker/completions/
244	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
245	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
246	```
247
248	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
249
250	```zsh
251	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
252	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
253	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
254	```
```

116	## Why two scopes?
117
118	| Use case | Where to install |
119	|---|---|
120	| Skill you want available in every project, on every machine | Global (edit `$managed` in the merger script) |
121	| Skill that only makes sense inside this specific repo | Project (`npx skills add ... -y` from repo root, commit `skills-lock.json`) |
122	| Skill you're prototyping locally before deciding | Project, then promote to global once stable |
123
124	`project-knowledge-harness` is in **both** scopes today because (a) the harness
125	itself targets *any* project so it belongs globally, and (b) we want to use it
126	on the chezmoi repo immediately, which the global install covers but
127	project-scope makes the lock-file dependency explicit for anyone reading
128	`skills-lock.json` here.
129
130	## First-party templated skill (`chezmoi-dotfiles`)
131
132	Everything above is about **npx-pulled** skills (static clones from external
133	repos, in chezmoi-ignored `.agents/skills/**`). There is exactly one **first-party,
134	chezmoi-managed, *templated*** skill that breaks that mould:
135
136	| | npx skills | `chezmoi-dotfiles` |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| Source | external git repo, cloned by `npx skills` | `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl` in this repo |
139	| Owner | `npx skills` CLI (`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`) | chezmoi (a normal managed target) |
140	| Per-host content | identical everywhere | **rendered from `.chezmoi.toml`** — only lists tools this host selected |
141	| Updates | `npx skills` / `just upgrade-skills` | **re-renders on every `chezmoi apply`** |
142
143	**Why it exists:** so an agent opened in *any* directory can operate these dotfiles
144	and discover the repo's custom tooling (in-house CLIs, `tv` channels, keymaps, `just`
145	recipes) — most of which live under `docs/**`, which is **not** deployed to `$HOME`
146	and is only reachable via `chezmoi source-path`. The skill is deliberately **lean
147	and self-discovering** (it points at `docs/`, `tv list-channels`, `just --list`,
148	`ls $(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/`) so it rarely needs editing.
149
150	**Deployment:**
151
152	- Real file → `~/.agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md` (the universal,
153	  cross-agent dir). Symlink `~/.claude/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles →
154	  ../../.agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles` (source: `dot_claude/skills/symlink_chezmoi-dotfiles`)
155	  so Claude Code discovers it — same per-agent-symlink shape `npx skills` uses.
156	- Re-included past the broad npx ignore in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` using **single-`*`**
157	  globs (`.agents/skills/*` + `.agents/skills/*/**`, not a bare `**`). This is
158	  load-bearing: a recursive `**` (or a bare `.agents/skills` dir line) excludes the
159	  *parent* directory, after which chezmoi — like gitignore — silently ignores the
160	  `!` re-include. Verify with `chezmoi managed | grep chezmoi-dotfiles`.
161	- It is **not** in any npx lock file (chezmoi-owned), so it never collides with an
162	  npx skill — provided the name stays namespaced (hence `chezmoi-dotfiles`, not a
163	  bare `dotfiles`, which could clash in the flat skill namespace).
164
165	**Keeping it in sync:** see the `CLAUDE.md` cross-file maintenance row. Short
166	version: freshness is automatic; only edit the `.tmpl` when a section must be gated
167	on a **new prompt key** or a stable new CLI is worth naming.
168

1250:294	The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
1256:300	3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
