1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
6	# herdr's per-pane metadata TOKENS (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source review
7	# --token review=…`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
8	# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
9	# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
10	# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
11	#
12	# Why a metadata token and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
13	# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. A pane can
14	# carry `tokens.review = "⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking
15	# into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
16	# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
17	#
18	# herdr >= 0.7.4 ONLY. herdr 0.7.4 removed `--custom-status` / the flat
19	# `custom_status` field in favour of this namespaced token map (up to 32 tokens
20	# per pane, names matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$). The removal is NOT listed as a
21	# breaking change upstream — on an older herdr this script dies with
22	# `unknown --custom-status`. See pitfalls/herdr-0.7.4-drops-custom-status.md.
23	#
24	# Unlike `custom_status`, a token is NOT rendered by the sidebar automatically —
25	# it only shows where a row layout references it. `$review` is wired into
26	# `[ui.sidebar.agents] rows` in .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml; drop the
27	# token name here and you must drop it there too.
28	#
29	# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
30	# surfaces `tokens`, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) lets the
31	# `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No sidecar file.
32	#
33	# Usage:
34	#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
35	#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
36	#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
37	#
38	# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
39	# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
40	# focus_clear action. Keep TOKEN in sync with the `.tokens.<name>` lookups in
41	# that channel (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml) and with the
42	# `$review` token in the sidebar row layout.
43	set -eu
44
45	SOURCE_ID='review'
46	TOKEN='review'                 # metadata token name; the tv channel keys off its PRESENCE
47	DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'
48
49	usage() {
50	    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
51	    exit 64
52	}
53
54	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
55
56	action="${1:-}"
57	pane="${2:-}"
58	status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"
59
60	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
61	[ -n "$pane" ] || usage
62
63	_set() {
64	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --token "$TOKEN=$status" >/dev/null
65	    echo "review flag set on $pane"
66	}
67
68	_clear() {
69	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --clear-token "$TOKEN" >/dev/null
70	    echo "review flag cleared on $pane"
71	}
72
73	case "$action" in
74	    set)   _set ;;
75	    clear) _clear ;;
76	    toggle)
77	        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
78	        # Presence of the token IS the flag — a cleared token is absent from the
79	        # map, so no substring match is needed (unlike the pre-0.7.4 single
80	        # `custom_status` string that every source shared).
81	        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
82	            | jq -r --arg t "$TOKEN" '.result.pane.tokens[$t] // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
83	        case "$current" in
84	            '') _set ;;
85	            *)  _clear ;;
86	        esac ;;
87	    *) usage ;;
88	esac
89

3	# many flags). Dynamic group completion via `pueue status --json | jq`.

6
7	_pqsum() {
8	    local context state state_descr line
9	    typeset -A opt_args
10
11	    _arguments -C \
12	        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
13	        '(-g --group)'{-g,--group}'=[restrict to one pueue group]:group:->group' \
14	        '--report[emit markdown report (ai mode only)]' \
15	        '--out=[write report to PATH]:path:_files' \
16	        '--clean[execute cleanup commands on safe-to-clean groups]' \
17	        '--yes[skip y/N prompts (with --clean)]' \
18	        '--multi-host[tell LLM the input describes multiple hosts]' \
19	        '--stdin-json[read pre-merged host snapshots from stdin]' \
20	        '--raw-stdin[read raw `pueue status --json` from stdin]' \
21	        '--host=[override host name when --raw-stdin is set]:hostname:_hosts' \
22	        '--deep[include extra recovery context (last ~20 log lines per failed task)]' \
23	        '(-r --refresh)'{-r,--refresh}'[bypass prompt-hash cache]' \
24	        '--no-cache[do not read or write the cache]' \
25	        '--dry-run[print AI prompt; no AI call]' \
26	        '1:mode:(text ai json)'
27
28	    case "$state" in
29	        group)
30	            local -a groups
31	            if (( $+commands[pueue] )) && (( $+commands[jq] )); then
32	                groups=( ${(f)"$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)"} )
33	                (( ${#groups} )) && _describe 'pueue group' groups
34	            fi
35	            ;;
36	    esac
37	}
38
39	compdef _pqsum pqsum

```text
139	## Cache
140
141	`scan` caches to `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/appsrc/<hostname>.json`, keyed
142	**per item by mtime** — a re-scan only recomputes apps whose bundle changed. The
143	forward-inventory calls (cheap) always re-run. Flags: `-r/--refresh` (recompute
144	all), `--no-cache` (don't read or write). Ballpark on a laptop: full GUI+CLI
145	scan ~15 s cold, ~5 s warm (~2 200 items); `which` is instant.
146
147	## Integration
148
149	- **`appsrc tui`** — interactive Textual dashboard over the full inventory. A
150	  background worker scans (fast, no sizes); `/` filters by name/source, `s` sizes
151	  the currently-visible rows and sorts biggest-first (bounding `du` cost to what's
152	  on screen), `o`/`n` sort by source/name, `Enter` opens the size breakdown,
153	  `t`/`m` show the selected tool's `tldr`/`man` page (suspends into the pager),
154	  `y`/`r` copy path / reveal, `R` rescan, `q` quits. Needs a real terminal.
155	- **`tv appsrc`** — fuzzy-pick the full GUI+CLI inventory; type a source label
156	  (`cask`, `manual`, `app-store`, `apt`…) to narrow. `Enter` = detail, `Alt+S` =
157	  size, `Alt+T`/`Alt+M` = tldr/man, `Alt+C` = copy path, `Alt+O` = reveal,
158	  `Alt+J` = JSON.
159	- **`tv appsrc-size`** — the same picker pre-sorted by footprint (biggest first,
160	  human sizes shown) for hunting space hogs; preview/`Enter` = the size report.
161	- **Completions** shell out to `appsrc scan --list-names` for GUI app names + PATH
162	  commands, so `appsrc which/size <Tab>` completes either.
163
164	`appsrc` is the *runtime* companion to
165	[`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`](../this_repo/tool-managers.md), which records
166	how **this repo** installs tools by design; `appsrc` inspects whatever is
167	actually on the machine.
168
169	## Maintaining it
170
171	Four things bite if you don't know them:
172
173	- **Everything lives in the one launcher.** Detection, sizing and the inline
174	  `AppsrcTUI` are all in `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_appsrc` — there is
175	  deliberately **no** `scripts/appsrc/` package; the TUI calls the same module
176	  functions the CLI does. `textual` is declared in the PEP 723 header only and
177	  imported lazily inside `do_tui`, so the plain CLI never pays for it.
178	- **Mirror the mnemonics.** The TUI's `BINDINGS` letters
179	  (`s`ize / `o`source / `n`ame / `t`ldr / `m`an / `y`copy / `r`eveal) and the
180	  `tv appsrc` / `tv appsrc-size` channels' `Alt+<letter>` actions are
181	  intentionally the same letters so muscle memory carries between the fast
182	  picker and the sortable dashboard. Change one → change both, same commit.
183	- **`scan --tsv` column order is a wire format.** It is
184	  `name·source·path·kind·package[·size]`, and both `.toml` channels index into it
185	  with `{split:\t:N}`. Reordering or inserting a column silently shifts every
186	  picker field — fix the channels in the same commit.
187	- **TUI subprocess work must be asyncio-native.** Never call blocking
188	  `subprocess` inside a `@work(thread=True)` worker; it intermittently deadlocks
189	  into an empty table with no crash (a Textual pilot test still passes — only a
190	  real terminal hangs). Use `create_subprocess_exec`. See
191	  [`pitfalls/appsrc-tui-subprocess-thread-hang.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/appsrc-tui-subprocess-thread-hang.md).
192	  Relatedly, the filter `Input` stays `can_focus=False` until `/` opens it —
193	  otherwise it swallows the single-letter keybindings.
```

```text
110	at `~/.config/yth/config.toml`, cache at `~/.cache/yth/`. Set `$YTH_DB` to override the DB
111	path (used by tests). Schema: `videos` (+ `videos_fts`), `watch_events` (one row per watch;
112	stats via the `video_stats` view), `subtitles` (+ `subtitles_fts`), `meta`. FTS is
113	external-content with triggers, so `enrich`/`fetch-subs` UPDATEs re-index automatically.
114
115	## Cross-file invariants
116
117	Touching `yth` means keeping these in sync (see the `CLAUDE.md` cross-file table row):
118
119	1. `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` — launcher (PEP723 deps + dict-dispatch). Shared helpers
120	   live in `scripts/yth/__init__.py`; leaf subcommands in `scripts/yth/*.py`.
121	2. `dot_config/television/cable/yth.toml` — the `o/b/y/p/s/j` mnemonics mirror any future
122	   `yth tui`; new actions use `Alt+`.
123	3. `dot_config/zsh/tools/53_yth_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/53_yth_completion.bash` —
124	   keep the two in sync (Strategy B).
125	4. `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` — the `yt-dlp` entry (dual with the
126	   launcher PEP723 block).
127	5. Docs: this page (+ `yth.zh-TW.md`), `docs/shells/aliases.md`, `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md`
128	   §F, `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` A–Z + uv inventory, `mkdocs.yml` nav,
129	   `dot_agents/skills/chezmoi-dotfiles/SKILL.md.tmpl`.
130
131	## Troubleshooting
132
133	- **`Sign in to confirm you're not a bot`** on `enrich`/`fetch-subs`/`sync` — YouTube
134	  bot-check, common from datacenter IPs. It's treated as transient (not stamped), so it
135	  retries next run. Configure cookies (`--cookies` for enrich/fetch-subs) or run from a
136	  residential IP.
137	- **`no captions`** — the video genuinely has no subtitles in the configured `langs`. Add
138	  langs (`--langs en,en-orig,zh-Hant`) or accept it (the video is stamped so it won't retry;
139	  `--force` to retry).
140	- **`yth sync: no cookie source configured`** — expected until you set `cookiefile` or
141	  `from_browser`. Prefer `yth import-takeout` for full history (no cookies needed).
142	- **Empty `tv yth`** — no history imported yet. Run `yth import-takeout` or `yth sync`.
143

```text
35	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
36
37	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
38
39	### Named sessions
40
41	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
44	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
45
46	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
47
48	## cwd & workspace-naming model
49
50	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
51
52	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
54	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
55	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
56	- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
57
58	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
59
60	| value | meaning |
61	|---|---|
62	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
63	| `home` | `$HOME` |
64	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
65	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
66
67	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
68
69	```toml
70	[[keys.command]]
71	key = "prefix+C"
72	type = "pane"
73	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
74	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
75	```
76
77	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
78
79	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
82	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
83	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
84	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
85	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux). Panel ordered as an **attention queue**, not grouped by space: `ui.agent_panel_sort = "priority"` (herdr's default is `"spaces"`) |
86	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
87	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
88	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
89	| URL picker (`prefix+u`, tmux-fzf-url) | **Custom command pane + helper** | `prefix+u` → `url-pick.sh` (fzf → `x open`); `--source recent` scans scrollback |
90	| File-path picker (`prefix+p`; extrakto `prefix+Tab` on tmux) | **Custom command pane + helper** | `prefix+p` → `path-pick.sh` — two-tier (exists-under-cwd first) → `x copy` |
91	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
92	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
93	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | Partial — `report-metadata --token` (per-pane metadata tokens, orthogonal to agent state) | **Review-pending flag** (`hmark`/`prefix+m` + `tv herdr-review` inbox); decorative status-bar glyphs still a gap (no format-string interpolation) |
94	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
95
96	## Keybindings
97
98	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
99

356	> Two portability traps are handled inside the helper and are worth knowing if you edit it: `~/.zsh_history` is extended-history format (`: <ts>:<elapsed>;<cmd>`) **and contains non-UTF8 bytes**, so BSD `sed` aborts with `sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence` unless the parse runs under `LC_ALL=C`; and the newest-first reversal uses POSIX `awk` because `tail -r` is BSD-only while `tac` is GNU-only.

358	> **Why `Alt+Enter` had to exist.** Plain Enter cannot express *"run exactly what I typed"* while fzf still has a match — type `ls -la` with `ls -la /tmp` in history and Enter takes the history entry, which makes the picker feel like it can only replay old commands. `--expect=alt-enter` adds the escape hatch. Note that fzf's line layout is **not fixed**: with `--print-query --expect`, a no-match Enter prints only the query (one line), while an accepted match prints query / key / selection. The helper therefore reads the key from line 2 (empty or absent ⇒ plain Enter) and only trusts line 3 on exit code 0.

362	Six one-keypress "grab this onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). 377	### `dir` vs `cwd`, and why the right-click menu can't do this {#space-dir}
378
379	`dir` is the answer to *"what directory is this space about?"* — the thing you'd want from a right-click **Copy dir** on a sidebar workspace row. Three ways to reach it:
380
381	| Surface | How | Scope |
382	|---|---|---|
383	| `prefix+d` | keybind | the **focused** workspace |
384	| `prefix+y` → *Copy space: dir* | herdr-plus Quick Action | the **focused** workspace |

387	**herdr's context menus cannot be extended.** They are a fixed enum compiled into the binary — the whole inventory is one packed string blob (`Rename` · `Close` · `New worktree` · `Open worktree...` · `Close group` · `Expand` · `Delete worktree checkout...` for spaces; `New tab` · `Rename pane` · `Split right` · `Split down` · `Close pane` · `Swap with focused pane` · `Clear pane name` for panes). 389	> **Upstream status (re-check on herdr upgrades).** Requested four times — [#1511](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1511) (user-defined menu entries), [#1671](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1671), [#1776](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1776), [#1830](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/1830) — **all closed `NOT_PLANNED`**, three of them auto-closed by `kangal-bot` for being feature requests on a bug-only tracker. #1776 is where a maintainer-facing report states plainly that `contexts` *"currently only surfaces in the `plugin action list` API response."* The redirected discussions ([#1609](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1609), [#1672](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1672), [#1722](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/1722)) are all still open and unanswered.

421	| Defense | Behavior |
422	|---|---|
423	| Extraction | extrakto's path heuristics — slash-bearing tokens (`/…`, `~/…`, `./`, `a/b/c`) + bare `file.ext`; trailing `",):` stripped; rate/fraction tokens excluded outright |
424	| Existence check (the noise-killer) | Each candidate is resolved against the pane cwd (`$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`, else `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd`, else process-info cwd) and `test -e`'d |
425	| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |

427	`path:line:col` suffixes (grep `-n` / stack traces / compiler output) are stripped before the existence test, so `pkg.py:42:5` validates as `pkg.py`. Scope is the visible screen by default (`--source recent` for scrollback); multi-select copies newline-joined; an empty result prints `no file paths found` and pauses ~1.5 s.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	#
3	# crash-blackbox — flight recorder for machines that hard-power-off with no logs.
4	#
5	# When a box loses power outright (PSU trip, VRM fault, AGESA reset) the kernel
6	# never gets to run, so journald's write buffer dies with it and the last ~30s
7	# of evidence is simply gone. This samples the sensors every second and fsyncs
8	# each row, so the CSV survives the cut and `report` can show you the seconds
9	# leading up to it.
10	#
11	# Usage:
12	#   crash-blackbox run [--interval S]   # the sampling loop (what the service runs)
13	#   crash-blackbox install              # install + enable the systemd service (sudo)
14	#   crash-blackbox uninstall            # stop + remove it (sudo)
15	#   crash-blackbox status               # service state + current readings
16	#   crash-blackbox report [--seconds N] # what the sensors said before each power cut
17	#
18	# The payoff is `report`: it splits the log on boot markers, cross-checks each
19	# segment against `journalctl --list-boots`, and for every boot that ended
20	# without a clean shutdown it prints the final N samples. A pump dropping to
21	# 0 RPM, a thermal runaway, or a GPU power spike shows up there. *Nothing*
22	# showing up is itself the finding — it points at the power path, not the load.
23	#
24	# Diagnostic ladder this belongs to: docs/playbooks/random-hard-poweroff.md
25
26	import argparse
27	import csv
28	import glob
29	import os
30	import shutil
31	import subprocess
32	import sys
33	import time
34	from datetime import datetime
35
36	STATE_DIR = os.path.join(
37	    os.environ.get("XDG_STATE_HOME", os.path.expanduser("~/.local/state")),
38	    "crash-blackbox",
39	)
40	CSV_PATH = os.path.join(STATE_DIR, "blackbox.csv")
41	SERVICE_NAME = "crash-blackbox.service"
42	SYSTEM_UNIT = f"/etc/systemd/system/{SERVICE_NAME}"
43	USER_UNIT = os.path.join(
44	    os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", os.path.expanduser("~/.config")),
45	    "systemd", "user", SERVICE_NAME,
46	)
47	# ~350 bytes/row at 1 Hz is ~29 MB/day. Rotating at 64 MB keeps roughly two days
48	# per file and caps total disk use at 128 MB (current + .1). Reading only ever
49	# needs the tail, so there is no reason to hoard more; `report` reads .1 as well
50	# so a cut landing just after a rotation still has its run-up.
51	ROTATE_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
52	BOOT_MARKER = "=== BOOT ==="
53
54	# Chips that carry signal for a power-loss investigation; skipping the rest keeps
55	# the row width sane. Matched as prefixes — Super-I/O chips are named per model
56	# (nct6799 / nct6796 / it8686 / …) and pinning exact numbers silently loses the fan
57	# channels on the next board.
58	CHIP_PREFIXES = ("k10temp", "coretemp", "nvme", "amdgpu", "nct6", "it87", "it86")
59
60
61	def chip_wanted(name):
62	    return name.startswith(CHIP_PREFIXES)
63
64
65	def die(msg):
66	    print(f"crash-blackbox: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
67	    sys.exit(1)
68
69
70	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

21	# source (dead PPA, GFW-blocked host, expired Release file) makes
22	# `apt-get update` exit non-zero, and with `update_cache: true` inlined in the
23	# install task the whole play used to die right here with the unhelpful
24	# "Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries: ''". Base packages all live in
25	# the main Ubuntu/Debian archives, so installing against a stale cache is
26	# almost always fine. See pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md.
27	- name: Update apt cache (Debian/Ubuntu, best-effort)
28	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
29	  become: true
30	  tags: [sudo]
31	  ansible.builtin.apt:
32	    update_cache: true
33	    cache_valid_time: 3600
34	  register: base_apt_cache
35	  ignore_errors: true
36
37	# The apt module swallows the underlying fetch errors (empty msg above), so
38	# re-run `apt-get update` via CLI purely to surface WHICH source is broken.
39	- name: Diagnose broken apt sources (cache update failed)
40	  when:
41	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
42	    - base_apt_cache is failed

44	  tags: [sudo]
45	  ansible.builtin.command: apt-get update
46	  register: base_apt_diag
47	  changed_when: false
48	  failed_when: false
49
50	# `Err:` lines (which repo) land on stdout, `E:`/`W:` summaries on stderr.
51	# msg is a list so each broken source renders on its own output line.
52	- name: Report broken apt sources
53	  when:
54	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
55	    - base_apt_cache is failed
56	  tags: [sudo]
57	  vars:
58	    base_apt_broken_lines: >-
59	      {{ base_apt_diag.stdout_lines | default([]) | select('match', '^(Err|Ign):.*') | list
60	         + base_apt_diag.stderr_lines | default([]) }}
61	  ansible.builtin.debug:
62	    msg: "{{ ['apt cache update FAILED — continuing with the existing (possibly stale) package lists.',
63	              'Broken source(s) reported by `apt-get update`:']
64	             + base_apt_broken_lines
65	             + ['Fix or remove the offending file under /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ and re-run: chezmoi apply'] }}"

16176	### `--source` 的差異
16177
16178	- `--source visible`：只找目前螢幕可見內容
16179	- `--source recent`：搜尋 herdr 保留的完整 scrollback，較適合定位歷史輸出
16180	- 固定字串搜尋可把 `rg` 改成 `rg -nF`
16181	- 不分大小寫則加 `-i`
16182
16183	repo 現有的 scrollback-copy 也是使用 `pane read --source recent`：
16184	`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:135`
16185
16186	### Session／remote server 限制
16187
16188	上述命令只搜尋**目前 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` 指向的 session**。herdr 的 pane/workspace/tab 子命令沒有 `--session` 參數；要搜尋其他 named session，需要：
16189
16190	```zsh
16191	HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$socket_path" <上面的搜尋>
16192	```
16193
16194	`socket_path` 可由：
16195
16196	```zsh
16197	herdr session list --json
16198	```
16199
16200	取得。這個 routing 模型記錄在 `docs/tools/herdr.md:35` 及 `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh:80`。
16201
16202	如果 server 在其他機器：
16203
16204	- 搜尋命令需要在能存取該 server socket 的遠端環境執行，例如 SSH 到 server 後執行。
16205	- `herdr --remote HOST` 是互動式 thin-client attach，並不是 `herdr pane list/read` 的遠端前綴。
16206
16207	### 現有 `tv herdr-*` 不會搜尋 pane 內容
16208
16209	目前：
16210
16211	- `tv herdr-agent-panes`：只 fuzzy-search pane ID、workspace、tab、agent status、cwd；preview 才讀取 `visible` 內容
16212	  `dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml:24`
16213	- `tv herdr-review`：同樣只有 preview 顯示 visible content
16214	- `tv herdr-sesh`：只列 workspace 與 zoxide directory，不讀 pane content
16215
16216	因此，在 `tv herdr-agent-panes` 直接輸入 terminal 裡的文字，**不會命中該 pane**。

1	# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant
2	#
3	# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists
4	# panes from the running herdr server and lets you jump to the one running an
5	# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).
6	#
7	# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
8	# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
9	# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
10	# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
11	#
12	# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
13	#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
14	#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
15	#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
16	#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
17	#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)
18
19	[metadata]
20	name = "herdr-agent-panes"
21	description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
22	requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]
23
24	[source]
25	command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.agent_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
26	display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
27	output = "{split:\t:0}"
28
29	[preview]
30	command = '''
31	pane='{split:\t:0}'
32	printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  [%s]\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
33	printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
34	printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
35	printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
36	herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
37	  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
38	'''
39
40	[ui]
41	input_header = "Live herdr Agent Panes"
42
43	[ui.preview_panel]
44	size = 60
45
46	[keybindings]
47	enter = "actions:focus"
48	alt-t = "actions:focus"
49	alt-k = "actions:close_pane"
50	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
```
</details></tool-use>

5	# the flag is set by hmark / prefix+m (see dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh)
6	# and stored as the pane's `review` metadata TOKEN, orthogonal to agent state.
7	# Bound to `prefix+i` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
8	#
9	# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB but KEEPS the ⭐ (you may still be
10	# mid-review). Alt+C = focus AND clear the flag ("mark read"). herdr has no
11	# "focus pane by id" (pane focus is directional only), so we focus at tab
12	# granularity — enough with one agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
13	#
14	# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) via jq,
15	# filtered to panes that HAVE a non-empty `tokens.review` — presence is the flag,
16	# so the glyph text is free-form. Keep the token name in sync with TOKEN in
17	# review-mark.sh. herdr >= 0.7.4 (0.7.4 replaced the flat `custom_status` field
18	# with this token map; on older herdr the filter silently matches nothing):
19	#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
20	#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
21	#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
22	#   3. tokens.review  (⭐ REVIEW)
23	#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)
24
25	[metadata]
26	name = "herdr-review"
27	description = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐) — jump to sessions you flagged for later"
28	requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]
29
30	[source]
31	command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | select((.tokens.review? // "") != "") | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.tokens.review)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
32	display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:3}  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
33	output = "{split:\t:0}"
34
35	[preview]
36	command = '''
37	pane='{split:\t:0}'
38	printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
39	printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
40	printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
41	printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
42	herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
43	  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
44	'''
45
46	[ui]
47	input_header = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐)"
48
49	[ui.preview_panel]
50	size = 60
```
</details></tool-use>

80	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
81	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
82	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
83	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
84	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
85	#
86	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
87	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
88	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
89	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
90	function _herdr_session_target() {
91	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
92	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
93	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
94	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
95	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
96	            | head -1)
97	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
98	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
99	            return 1
100	        fi
101	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
102	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
103	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
104	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
105	            return 1
106	        fi
107	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
108	        return 0
109	    fi
110	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
111	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
112	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
113	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
114	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
115	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
116	            | head -1)
117	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
118	    else
119	        printf 'default\t\n'
120	    fi
121	}

### Comparable executable patterns

### Why multi-session search favors Python

- Herdr’s hierarchy and socket model are documented at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:35-46`.
- A server can have multiple named sessions, each with its own socket; `session list --json` supplies authoritative `socket_path` values at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:37-44`.
- Pane/workspace/tab commands have no `--session` option; each invocation must receive the selected socket through `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:46`.
- Pane content already uses `herdr pane read --source visible|recent`; full retained scrollback is the established `recent` behavior at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:362-373`.
- `pane list` does not contain workspace/tab labels, so useful coordinates require joining session, workspace, tab, and pane JSON. Doing this once per session in Python avoids repeated `jq`, newline-delimited shell state, and N+1 `get` calls.
- Sessions or panes can disappear between list and read. Python can continue collecting other results, issue precise stderr warnings, and still produce deterministic partial output.
- Remote thin-client attach is not a generic prefix for `pane list/read`; remote execution remains an explicit limitation. The remote model is described at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/herdr.md:264-300`.

### Dependencies

- `ripgrep` and `jq` are baseline packages on macOS at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml:4-18` and Debian/Ubuntu at `:67-82`.
- Their tool inventory entries already exist at:

  - `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:1156` (`ripgrep`)
- Therefore, `herdr-grep` should require `herdr` and `rg`, but Python should replace `jq` for internal parsing. No tool-manager change is needed unless a genuinely new external dependency is introduced.

### Output and exit conventions

Recommended surface:

- Default source: `recent`; `--visible` as a convenient alias for `--source visible`.
- Explicit modes: regex by default, `-F/--fixed-strings`, `-i/--ignore-case`, optionally `-S/--smart-case`.
- Session selection: default current/ambient session, `--session NAME`, and mutually exclusive `--all-sessions`.
- Human output: grep-like records containing `session/workspace/tab/pane`, line number, and matched text.
- `--json`: stable JSON records containing session name/socket, workspace ID/label, tab ID/label, pane ID, source, line number, and text.
- Add `--tsv` only if a Television channel will consume it; TSV column order then becomes a wire-format invariant, as demonstrated by `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_appsrc:868-877` and documented at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/appsrc.md:183-186`.

For a grep-shaped command, use conventional `rg` semantics:

- `0`: at least one match and collection completed.
- `1`: no matches and collection completed.

 `./docs/tools/herdr.md`

```text
259	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
260
261	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
262	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
263
264	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
265
266	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
267
268	```bash
269	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
270	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
271	```
272
273	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
274
275	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
276	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
277	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
278
279	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
280
281	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
282	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
283
284	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
285
286	```bash
287	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
288	```
289
290	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
291
292	## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
293
294	The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
295
296	Three ways to resolve it, in order of preference here:
297
298	1. **Double-prefix passthrough (recommended, zero config).** tmux keeps its default `bind -T prefix C-b send-prefix` (confirmed present in this repo — not overridden), so **`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b`** forwards a literal `Ctrl+b` to the inner herdr; its prefix bindings then work normally (`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b c` = inner new tab). No herdr or tmux change needed — classic tmux-in-tmux muscle memory.
299	2. **Rebind the inner herdr prefix.** Set `keys.prefix` (e.g. `"ctrl+a"` / `"ctrl+space"`) so the inner herdr uses a non-colliding prefix — one keystroke instead of the double-tap. Cost: it changes herdr's prefix even when run standalone (no longer matching tmux's `Ctrl+b`).
300	3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
301
302	Notes: this repo's tmux uses many root-table `bind -n C-*` bindings that **shadow** inner-app `Ctrl` keys, so herdr's prefix-free *direct* terminal shortcuts aren't reliable under tmux — reach herdr actions through its prefix (via 1 or 2). herdr's own `allow_nested` (config, default `false`) governs herdr-inside-**herdr** only (detected via `HERDR_ENV`), not herdr-inside-tmux.
```

# Recommended v1 Implementation Plan

## 1. CLI contract

Create `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_herdr-grep` as an executable, pure-stdlib Python CLI using `argparse`, `json`, `os`, `shutil`, and `subprocess`.

### Synopsis

```text
herdr-grep [OPTIONS] PATTERN
herdr-grep --list-sessions
```

Search options:

```text
-F, --fixed-strings
-i, --ignore-case
--source {visible,recent,recent-unwrapped}
--visible
--session NAME
--all-sessions
--json
-h, --help
```

Contract:

- `PATTERN` is one ripgrep regex by default.
- `-F` treats it literally.
- `-i` enables case-insensitive matching and combines with `-F`.
- Default source is `recent`, meaning full retained scrollback.
- `--visible` is a convenience alias for `--source visible`.
- Put `--source` and `--visible` in one mutually exclusive argparse group.
- Put `--session` and `--all-sessions` in another mutually exclusive group.
- A pattern beginning with `-` uses the standard terminator:

  ```text
  herdr-grep -- -leading-dash
  ```

- `--list-sessions` is public, standalone, and prints sorted running session names, one per line. It exists primarily for shell completion and does not require `rg`.
- Reject combining `--list-sessions` with `PATTERN` or search options as usage error 2.
- Do not add v1 context, count, color, multiline, pane-filter, TSV, `--host`, or Television options.
- Do not expose Herdr’s `detection` read source in v1.

### Session selection

Mirror `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh:80-121` exactly:

1. Always discover sessions with:

   ```text
   herdr session list --json
   ```

2. No session flag:
   - If `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is inherited, leave it untouched and scan that ambient socket.
   - Resolve its display name by matching `socket_path`; if no entry matches, use `default`, matching `_herdr_session_target`.
   - Without an ambient socket, leave the environment untouched so Herdr selects its default socket.

3. `--session NAME`:
   - Require an exact session entry.
   - Require `running == true`.
   - Require a non-empty `socket_path`.
   - Copy the parent environment and set `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` only in child Herdr calls.

4. `--all-sessions`:
   - Select only entries with `running == true`.
   - Sort them by session name.
   - Give each session’s Herdr children its own `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`.
   - Stopped entries are silently outside the scan, not failures.
   - An empty running-session set is a complete empty scan: exit 1.

Treat invalid JSON or an invalid top-level session schema as fatal exit 2. Validate each entry’s `name`, `running`, and `socket_path`; duplicate names or malformed entries also make discovery incomplete rather than guessing.

### Pane enumeration and reading

For each target session, sequentially run:

```text
herdr pane list
```

Parse only `.result.panes`. For every valid pane, retain these fields directly:

- `pane_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `tab_id`
- `agent_status`
- `foreground_cwd`
- `cwd`

Never derive workspace or tab identity by splitting `pane_id`.

Sort panes lexically by:

```text
(workspace_id, tab_id, pane_id)
```

Read each pane with:

```text
herdr pane read PANE_ID --source SOURCE --format text
```

This reuses the retained-scrollback behavior established at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:135-143`.

Use argv arrays throughout, `shell=False`, captured stdout/stderr, UTF-8 decoding with replacement for invalid terminal bytes, and a copied child environment. An empty successful pane read is simply a no-match input.

## 2. Ripgrep adapter

Resolve `herdr` and `rg` once with `shutil.which`. Missing dependencies produce exit 2 with a clear `herdr-grep:` diagnostic.

Build one canonical matcher argv:

```text
rg --no-config --json --text [--fixed-strings] [--ignore-case] -- PATTERN
```

Reasons:

- `--json` provides an unambiguous internal protocol.
- `--no-config` prevents `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` from silently changing v1 semantics.
- `--text` ensures pane text is searched even if captured content contains NUL-like bytes.
- `--` safely protects patterns beginning with `-`.

Before any pane enumeration, run this matcher once with empty stdin:

- Exit 0 or 1 means the pattern is valid.
- Exit 2 or malformed output means fatal exit 2.
- This prevents repeating an invalid-regex error once per pane.

For each pane:

- Exit 0: parse the JSON-lines stream.
- Exit 1: no matches in that pane.
- Any other exit, malformed JSON line, or malformed match event: record a pane-level failure and continue.
- Parse all events for a pane before accepting its records, so malformed output does not produce a half-trusted pane result.

Ripgrep emits one `match` event per matching line. Preserve every occurrence from that event’s `submatches` array.

## 3. Output contract

### Human output

Emit one line per matching line:

```text
SESSION/PANE_ID:LINE_NUMBER:LINE
```

Example:

```text
default/w3:p7:42:connection refused while opening socket
```

Rules:

- Matching lines containing several occurrences are printed once, matching normal grep behavior.
- The session and pane prefix is repeated on every output line.
- Remove only the captured line terminator; preserve the rest of the line.
- No headings, summaries, colors, or “no matches” message.
- Rich pane metadata and individual occurrence offsets are available through `--json`.

### JSON output

`--json` emits one UTF-8, `ensure_ascii=False`, indented object followed by a newline:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "pattern": "foo",
  "source": "recent",
  "fixed_strings": false,
  "ignore_case": false,
  "complete": true,
  "sessions": [
    "default"
  ],
  "matches": [
    {
      "session": "default",
      "workspace_id": "w3",
      "tab_id": "w3:t4",
      "pane_id": "w3:p7",
      "agent_status": "idle",

          "start_byte": 0,
          "end_byte": 3
        },
        {
          "text": "foo",
          "start_byte": 4,
          "end_byte": 7
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "errors": []
}
```

Field semantics:

- `sessions`: sorted names of all targeted sessions, including one that later fails during enumeration.
- `line_number`: one-based, as reported by ripgrep.
- `line`: line text without its ending newline.
- `start_byte` and `end_byte`: zero-based, half-open UTF-8 byte offsets within `line`, not character indexes.
- `agent_status`, `foreground_cwd`, and `cwd`: string or `null`, copied from the pane-list object.
- `complete`: false if any selected session or enumerated pane could not be fully scanned.

Every error record has a fixed shape:

```json
{
  "scope": "pane",
  "session": "default",
  "pane_id": "w3:p7",
  "operation": "pane-read",
  "message": "herdr exited 1: pane not found"
}

Allowed scopes:

- `global`
- `session`
- `pane`

Use stable operation names:

- `dependency`
- `rg-validate`
- `session-list`
- `session-select`
- `pane-list`
- `pane-entry`
- `pane-read`

`session` and `pane_id` are nullable where the scope does not have them.

After successful argparse parsing, `--json` should still emit this valid schema for dependency, discovery, selected-session, and partial-scan failures. Argparse usage errors remain ordinary stderr usage output.

### Determinism

Sort final matches by:

```text
(session, workspace_id, tab_id, pane_id, line_number, first-submatch-start-byte)
```

Sort errors by:

```text
(session-or-empty, pane_id-or-empty, operation, message)
```

|---|---|
| 0 | At least one match and the scan completed |
| 1 | No matches and the scan completed |
| 2 | Usage, missing dependency, invalid regex, unavailable selected session, malformed JSON/schema, or any incomplete scan |

2. `--visible` and every accepted `--source` value reach `pane read` correctly.
3. Conflicting source flags are usage exit 2.
4. Default regex, `-F`, `-i`, and combined matcher argv.
5. Pattern beginning `-` is passed literally after ripgrep’s `--`.
6. No ambient socket leaves `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` unset for default pane calls.
7. Ambient socket is preserved and resolves its session name.
8. Named session sets only the selected socket for pane calls.
9. All-sessions scans running entries only and sorts session output.
10. Missing and stopped named sessions return 2 without enumerating panes.
11. No running sessions under `--all-sessions` returns 1.
12. Complete no-match returns 1 with empty human stdout.
13. Complete match returns 0 with the exact human prefix.
14. Multiple occurrences on one line produce one human line and multiple JSON submatches.
15. Pane metadata comes from explicit fields, using deliberately non-derivable IDs.
16. A disappearing pane/read failure preserves other matches and returns 2.
17. One failed session under `--all-sessions` preserves other sessions’ matches and returns 2.
18. Malformed session-list JSON returns 2.
19. Malformed pane-list JSON returns 2.
20. Malformed pane entries are reported while valid entries continue.
21. Invalid regex fails during preflight before pane enumeration.
22. Missing `herdr` and missing `rg` produce dependency exit 2.
23. JSON success, no-match, partial, and fatal outputs parse and have the exact top-level and record fields.
24. Shuffled session and pane fixtures produce identical sorted output.
25. `--list-sessions` prints only sorted running names.
26. `--help`, both completion files, and the accepted source values agree.

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

42	|---|---|---|

49	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
50
51	The `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism spans **6 surfaces that must move together** — devtools install, `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`, `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`, `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl` hooks, `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (+ its `modify_package.json`), and `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`'s producers API. Exact contents: [workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md) § Status icon mechanics; why it leaks: [workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
52
53	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (writes parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears). The workmux hook entries are **unconditional** — the `agentSounds` prompt gates only the notify.sh / peon-ping entries in the same file. `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux) stay distinct tools.
54
55	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
56
57	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply`; see [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template and disambiguation table.
58
59	**Fallback rules**, so this still binds when the skill can't be loaded:
60
61	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
62	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
63	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
64	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it recurs across machines, silently corrupts state, or has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.
