66	## Chezmoi templating conventions
67
68	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
69
70	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
71
72	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
73
74	## Hard repo invariants
75
76	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
77
78	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
79
80	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
81
82	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
83
84	**Hard rules**:
85
86	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
87	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
88	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
89
90	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
91
92	### Three-tier user-local override layer
93
94	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
95
96	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
97
98	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
99
100	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
101
102	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
103
104	**Hard rules**:
105
106	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
107	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
108	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
109	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
110	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
111
112	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
113
114	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
115
116	**Hard rules**:
117
118	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
119	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
120	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
121	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
122	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
123	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
124
125	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
126
127	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
128
129	**Hard rules**:
130
131	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
132	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
133	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
134	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
135	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
136
137	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
138
139	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
140
141	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
142
143	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
144
145	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
146	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
147	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
148	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
149	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
150	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
151	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
152	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
153
154	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
155
156	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
157	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
158
159	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
160
161	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
162
163	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
164
165	**Hard rules**:
166
167	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
168	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
169	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
170	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
171
172	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
173
174	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
175
176	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
177
178	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
179	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
180	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
181	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
182	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
183
184	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
185
186	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
187
188	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
189
```

250	```zsh
251	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
252	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)

256	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:

262	## FAQ
263
264	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
265	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
266
267	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
268	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
269
270	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
271	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.

143	class Runner:
144	    """Runs tailscale locally or on a remote host over ssh."""
145
146	    def __init__(
147	        self,
148	        host: str | None,
149	        ssh_opts: list[str],
150	        timeout: float,
151	        tailscale_bin: str | None,
152	    ):
153	        self.host = host
154	        self.ssh_opts = ssh_opts
155	        self.timeout = timeout
156	        self._probe: dict[str, str] | None = None
157	        self.bin: str | None = None
158	        if host is None:
159	            self.bin = find_tailscale(tailscale_bin)
160	            if self.bin is None:
161	                die(
162	                    "tailscale binary not found.\n"
163	                    "       macOS: install the `tailscale-app` cask (NOT the `tailscale` formula).\n"
164	                    "       Linux: enable installTailscale, or "
165	                    "curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh\n"
166	                    "       Override with --tailscale-bin / $TSNET_TAILSCALE_BIN.",
167	                    EX_NO_BINARY,
168	                )
169
170	    @property
171	    def where(self) -> str:
172	        return self.host or "local"
173
174	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- remote
175
176	    def _ssh_argv(self) -> list[str]:
177	        argv = ["ssh", "-o", "BatchMode=yes", "-o", f"ConnectTimeout={int(self.timeout)}"]
178	        for opt in self.ssh_opts:
179	            argv += ["-o", opt]
180	        argv.append(self.host or "")
181	        return argv
182
183	    def _run_probe(self) -> dict[str, str]:
184	        if self._probe is not None:
185	            return self._probe
186	        argv = self._ssh_argv() + ["--", "sh", "-c", shlex.quote(_REMOTE_PROBE)]
187	        try:
188	            p = subprocess.run(
189	                argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=max(self.timeout * 3, 30)
190	            )
191	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
192	            die(f"ssh to {self.host} timed out after {self.timeout * 3:.0f}s", EX_FAIL)
193	        if "TSNET_NO_TAILSCALE" in p.stdout:
194	            die(f"tailscale is not installed on {self.host} (or not on its PATH)", EX_NO_BINARY)
195	        if p.returncode != 0 and not p.stdout.strip():
196	            die(f"ssh to {self.host} failed: {p.stderr.strip() or p.returncode}", EX_FAIL)
197
198	        sections: dict[str, str] = {}
199	        current = None
200	        buf: list[str] = []
201	        for line in p.stdout.splitlines():
202	            if line.startswith("---TSNET-") and line.endswith("---"):
203	                if current:
204	                    sections[current] = "\n".join(buf)
205	                current = line.strip("-").removeprefix("TSNET-").lower()
206	                buf = []
207	            elif current:
208	                buf.append(line)
209	        if current:
210	            sections[current] = "\n".join(buf)
211	        # The END sentinel proves the stream was not truncated. Without this
212	        # guard a partial read degrades into "section missing" -> "{}" ->
213	        # "port free", which is confidently wrong.
214	        if "end" not in sections:
215	            die(
216	                f"probe output from {self.host} was truncated "
217	                f"(no END sentinel; got sections: {', '.join(sections) or 'none'})",
218	                EX_FAIL,
219	            )
220	        self._probe = sections
221	        return sections
222
223	    def _section(self, name: str) -> str | None:
224	        """Raw text of one probe section. None means the section is missing."""
225	        return self._run_probe().get(name)

119	class MiRouter:
120	    def __init__(self, host: str, username: str, password: str, timeout: float = 5.0):
121	        self.base = f"http://{host}"
122	        self.username = username
123	        self.password = password
124	        # LAN device — ignore ambient HTTP(S)/SOCKS proxy env (ALL_PROXY etc.);
125	        # otherwise httpx routes LAN traffic through the proxy and, with a
126	        # socks:// URL, crashes since httpx has no SOCKS support by default.
127	        self.client = httpx.Client(timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=False, trust_env=False)
128	        self.stok: str | None = None
129
130	    def login(self) -> None:
131	        r = self.client.get(f"{self.base}/cgi-bin/luci/web")
132	        r.raise_for_status()
133	        m_key = KEY_RE.search(r.text)
134	        m_mac = MAC_RE.search(r.text)
135	        if not m_key or not m_mac:
136	            raise RuntimeError("could not parse login key/mac from router page")
137	        key = m_key.group(1)
138	        mac = m_mac.group(1)
139	        nonce = f"0_{mac}_{int(time.time())}_{random.randint(1000, 10000)}"
140	        pwd_key = hashlib.sha1((self.password + key).encode()).hexdigest()
141	        pwd_hash = hashlib.sha1((nonce + pwd_key).encode()).hexdigest()
142	        r = self.client.post(
143	            f"{self.base}/cgi-bin/luci/api/xqsystem/login",
144	            data={
145	                "username": self.username,
146	                "password": pwd_hash,
147	                "logtype": "2",
148	                "nonce": nonce,
149	            },
150	        )
151	        r.raise_for_status()
152	        body = r.json()
153	        if body.get("code") != 0 or not body.get("token"):
154	            raise RuntimeError(f"login failed: {body}")
155	        self.stok = body["token"]
156
157	    def api(self, endpoint: str) -> Any:
158	        if self.stok is None:
159	            self.login()
160	        url = (
161	            f"{self.base}/cgi-bin/luci/;stok={self.stok}"
162	            f"/api/{endpoint.lstrip('/')}"
163	        )
164	        r = self.client.get(url)
165	        if r.status_code == 404:
166	            return {"_error": "endpoint not registered (404)", "endpoint": endpoint}
167	        r.raise_for_status()
168	        try:
169	            return r.json()
170	        except ValueError:
171	            return {"_unregistered_or_non_json": True, "preview": r.text[:200]}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
2	# Unit tests for `tsnet serve` / `tsnet doctor` — the preflight state machine.
3	#
4	# All offline. Two stubbing strategies, for a reason:
5	#
6	#   * LOCAL checks stub `tailscale` in $BATS_STUB_DIR.
7	#   * The Linux-vs-Darwin operator check is exercised through `--host`, with
8	#     `ssh` stubbed to emit a canned probe. tsnet reads the local platform via
9	#     os.uname() (a syscall, not the uname binary), so there is no honest way to
10	#     fake Darwin/Linux locally — and routing through --host has the bonus of
11	#     covering the remote code path, including the sentinel parser.
12	#
13	# The assertion that matters most in nearly every test is the NEGATIVE one:
14	# `tailscale serve` must never appear in the recorded argv when a check failed.
15
16	load "../test_helper.bash"
17
18	TSNET_SRC="$REPO_ROOT/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_tsnet"
19
20	setup() {
21	    setup_path_stub
22	    TS_TMP="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tsnet-serve.XXXXXX")"
23	    export TS_TMP
24	    _status_json '"CertDomains": ["my-mac.tailtest.ts.net"]'
25	    echo '{}' > "$TS_TMP/serve.json"
26	    echo '{}' > "$TS_TMP/prefs.json"
27	    _stub_tailscale
28	}
29
30	teardown() {
31	    [ -n "$TS_TMP" ] && rm -rf "$TS_TMP"
32	    cleanup_path_stubs
33	}
34
35	tsnet() { uv run --quiet --script "$TSNET_SRC" "$@"; }
36
37	_stub_tailscale() {
38	    cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/tailscale" <<'EOF'
39	#!/usr/bin/env bash
40	printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$TS_TMP/tailscale.argv"
41	case "$1 $2" in
42	  "status --json") cat "$TS_TMP/status.json" ;;
43	  "serve status")  cat "$TS_TMP/serve.json" ;;
44	  "debug prefs")   cat "$TS_TMP/prefs.json" ;;
45	  *) exit 0 ;;
46	esac
47	EOF
48	    chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/tailscale"
49	}
50
51	_status_json() {
52	    cat > "$TS_TMP/status.json" <<EOF
53	{
54	  "BackendState": "Running",
55	  "MagicDNSSuffix": "tailtest.ts.net",
56	  "Health": [],
57	  ${1},
58	  "CurrentTailnet": {"Name": "unit.test", "MagicDNSEnabled": true},
59	  "Self": {
60	    "HostName": "my-mac",
61	    "DNSName": "my-mac.tailtest.ts.net.",
62	    "TailscaleIPs": ["100.10.0.1"],
63	    "OS": "macOS",
64	    "Online": true
65	  },
66	  "Peer": {}
67	}
68	EOF
69	}
70
71	# A stub `ssh` that replays the batched probe tsnet expects. $1 selects the
72	# platform fixture; prefs content comes from $TS_TMP/prefs.json.
73	_stub_ssh() {
74	    local uname_s="$1" user="${2:-tester}" uid="${3:-1000}"

76	#!/usr/bin/env bash
77	printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "\$TS_TMP/ssh.argv"

79	echo "---TSNET-PLATFORM---"; echo "$uname_s"; echo "$user"; echo "$uid"
80	echo
81	echo "---TSNET-STATUS---";   cat "\$TS_TMP/status.json"
82	echo
83	echo "---TSNET-SERVE---";    cat "\$TS_TMP/serve.json"
84	echo
85	echo "---TSNET-PREFS---";    cat "\$TS_TMP/prefs.json"
86	echo
87	echo "---TSNET-LISTEN---";   echo "LISTEN 0 128 127.0.0.1:8787 0.0.0.0:*"

```text
1	# Zsh & Bash Completions
2
3	How tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project — for both upstream tools and in-house CLIs (`fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `mi-router`, `x`).
4
5	## How autocomplete works (mechanics)
6
7	Tab completion is the same idea on both shells but the plumbing differs.
8
9	### zsh — `compinit` + `fpath` + autoload `_<tool>` functions
10
11	1. **`compinit`** scans every directory in `$fpath` for files starting with `_` and registers them as completion candidates. Run by oh-my-zsh once at startup.
12	2. **`$fpath`** is zsh's function search path. Order in this repo (`dot_zshrc.tmpl:67-70`):
13	   ```
14	   ~/.zfunc                                             ← user-generated (this repo's lazy autoload target)
15	   ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/     ← community (184 tools)
16	   ~/.docker/completions/                               ← Docker-shipped
17	   $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/           ← Homebrew-managed
18	   ```
19	3. **The first line of each file** matters: `#compdef <name>` tells zsh which command to bind to. If you write `#compdef fleet`, then `fleet<TAB>` invokes the file's `_fleet` function.
20	4. **Autoload vs eager-load**: a file in `$fpath` is *parsed* the first time the user actually TABs the command (lazy). Files sourced explicitly at startup (e.g. via `load_modular_dir` in this repo) call `compdef _<func> <cmd>` directly — parsed eagerly, no need to be in `$fpath`.
21	5. **`_arguments` DSL** (zsh-only) lets you describe options + positional args declaratively: `'--hosts=[help text]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv'` defines the flag, hint, and a custom completer function. See `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh`.
22
23	### bash — `bash-completion v2` + `complete -F` + `COMPREPLY`
24
25	1. **bash-completion v2** is sourced at shell startup by `dot_config/bash/03_completion.bash`. It auto-loads completion files on first TAB.
26	2. **The user dir** is `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/` — drop a file named after the command (e.g. `mi-router`) here and v2 lazy-loads it on TAB.
27	3. **`complete -F _func cmd`** registers a bash function as the completer for `cmd`. The function reads `$COMP_WORDS` / `$COMP_CWORD` and writes candidates to `$COMPREPLY`.
28	4. **`_init_completion` + `compgen`** are bash-completion v2 helpers — `_init_completion` populates `cur`/`prev`/`words`/`cword`; `compgen -W "list" -- "$cur"` filters a wordlist by the current prefix.
29	5. **Eager vs lazy** mirrors zsh: a file in the user dir is lazy; a file sourced via `load_modular_dir` (this repo's `dot_config/bash/`) calls `complete -F` immediately.
30
31	### Three generation strategies in this repo
32
33	| Strategy | Where the file lives | Trigger | Best for |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **A. Lazy autoload** | zsh `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` / bash `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` | First TAB on the command | Tools that ship `--print-completion <shell>` or similar (tyro, click, clap-derive — including this repo's `mi-router`) |
36	| **B. Eager-load at startup** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<tool>_completion.bash` | Sourced via `load_modular_dir` after compinit / bash-completion v2 init | Hand-written completion (this repo's `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`) |
37	| **C. Cached eval at startup** | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>` | Sourced via shell `init` script (`dot_config/shell/<NN>_<tool>.sh`) | Slow generators whose output has side effects beyond `compdef` (e.g. `thefuck --alias` outputs an `alias` line — needs to land in the running shell's namespace, not just a deferred `_<tool>` function) |
38
39	Cache invalidation in classes A and C uses **binary-mtime check**:
40	```sh
41	[ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]  # → regenerate
42	```
43	This catches `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`, `mise install <NEW>` — anything that bumps the binary's mtime. Manual `<tool>-update-completion` helpers (in `dot_config/{shell,zsh}/10_aliases.zsh`) cover edge cases (gem-only upgrades, in-place replacements, cache corruption).
44
45	## Architecture
46
47	```
48	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
49	        │
50	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
51	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
52	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
53	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
54	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
55	        │     └── site-functions/
56	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
57	```
58
59	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.
60
61	## Completion Categories
62
63	Tools fall into four categories:
64
65	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
66
67	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. **Auto-generated for both shells** by the `chezmoi apply` hook (`run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` → `scripts/generate_completions.sh`); see [Generating Completions After Fresh Install](#generating-completions-after-fresh-install) for opt-out + manual rerun.
68
69	| Tool | Command |
70	|------|---------|
71	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
72	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
73	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
74	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
75	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
76	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
77	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
78	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
79	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |

81	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
82	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
83	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
84	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
85	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
86	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
87
88	**Usage pattern:**
89
90	```bash
91	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
92	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
93	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
94	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
95	```

97	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
98
99	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
100
101	| Tool | Source |
102	|------|--------|
103	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
104	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
105	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
106	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
107	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
108	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |

110	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
111
112	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Most live in the POSIX `dot_config/shell/` layer (sourced by both zsh and bash); zsh-only ones live in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
113
114	| Tool | Where | How | Cached? |
115	|------|-------|-----|---------|
116	| `fzf` | `dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh` | `eval "$(fzf --zsh)"` (zsh) / `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` (bash) | — |
117	| `zoxide` | `dot_config/shell/20_zoxide.sh` | `eval "$(zoxide init <shell>)"` | — |
118	| `direnv` | `dot_config/shell/30_direnv.sh` | `eval "$(direnv hook <shell>)"` | — |
119	| `marimo` | `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh` | `_MARIMO_COMPLETE=<shell>_source marimo` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/marimo_completion.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `marimo-update-completion` |
120	| `thefuck` | `dot_config/shell/27_thefuck.sh` | `thefuck --alias` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/thefuck_alias.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `thefuck-update-completion` |
121	| `try-cli` | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | `ruby try.rb init` (zsh-only) | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/zsh/try_init.zsh` — refresh via `try-update-completion` |
122
123	> **Cached entries** auto-invalidate when the tool's binary mtime is newer than the cache file (`[ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]`) — catches `mise install <NEW>`, `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`. Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. The pattern mirrors `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` (the canonical example).

125	### D. No completion support
126
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).

175	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
176	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
177	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
178	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
179	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
180
181	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
182
183	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
184
185	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
186	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
187	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
188	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
189
190	### What we DO track
191
192	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
193	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
194	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
195	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
196
197	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
198
199	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
200
201	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
202
203	Output paths:
204	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
205	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
206
207	### Manual rerun
208
209	```bash
210	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
```
</details></tool-use>

7
8	(( $+commands[wake] )) || return 0

10	_wake() {

```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6
7	- **Install**:
8	  - **Both platforms** — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-{linux,macos}-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr`, managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`. No tarball, so no unarchive step.
9	  - macOS is **deliberately not** Homebrew, and it is the only tool in this repo where that's true. Upstream disables `herdr update` on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs because the package manager owns the binary — which removes the *only* pane-preserving upgrade path and leaves a server restart, i.e. killing every pane process, as the sole option. The formula was dropped in favour of the release binary so macOS gets `--handoff` too. Boxes provisioned before the switch are migrated by a one-time `brew uninstall herdr` in the same role (leaving both installed would put two binaries on `PATH` and risk a client/server `protocol_mismatch` against yourself).
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: `just upgrade-herdr` (→ `herdr update --handoff`) on both platforms — **run it from outside herdr**, see below
12
13	> **`herdr update` refuses to run from inside a herdr pane.** The handoff replaces the server process that owns the pane you are typing in, so it fails closed:
14	>
15	> ```console
16	> $ herdr update --handoff          # from a pane inside herdr
17	> update failed: run `herdr update` outside herdr after detaching from the session
18	> ```
19	>
20	> The flow is **detach (`prefix+q`) → run it in a plain terminal → reattach with bare `herdr`**. Detaching does not kill anything (client close ≠ session loss), and `--handoff` then swaps the server without exiting pane processes — verified 2026-07 upgrading 0.7.1 → 0.7.5 with a Claude Code session running in a pane, which survived uninterrupted. `just upgrade-herdr` encodes this: it *skips with instructions* rather than failing when it detects `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`, so `just upgrade-all` from a herdr pane doesn't die here. Full trace: [`pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-update-handoff-refuses-inside-pane.md).
21
22	> **Install is version-blind; upgrades are yours to run.** The Linux ansible task gates on `herdr --version` returning non-zero — *"is it installed at all"*, not *"is it current"* — so a fresh box gets whatever is latest that day and `chezmoi apply` never touches it again. This is the repo's [install-vs-upgrade split](../this_repo/upgrades.md) working as designed, but herdr drifts faster than most because its config can outrun the binary (a `[[keys.command]]` using `type = "popup"`, added in 0.7.4, makes an older herdr reject **the entire keys block** — `reload-config` reports `status: "partial"` + `keeping current keys settings`, and only that one diagnostic line tells you).
23
24	> **Every herdr upgrade stales the agent integrations.** `herdr integration status` versions each one (`current (v9)` / `outdated (v7 < v9)`); reinstall with `herdr integration install <agent>`. These files (`~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh`, `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh`, `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh`, `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js`) are written by herdr and are **not** chezmoi-managed, so `chezmoi apply` will not restore or clobber them. `just upgrade-herdr` reports which went stale but deliberately does not auto-install them.
25	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` + managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`). The overlay enforces our managed tables on every `chezmoi apply` while preserving whatever herdr writes back at runtime (see [Config management](#config-management-why-modify_)).
26
27	> **Why a package-managed herdr strands its own server — the reason macOS left Homebrew.** herdr's socket API is protocol-versioned, and a package-manager upgrade cannot restart the server, so after `brew upgrade herdr` every CLI call (and therefore every `tv herdr-*` channel, `hvibe`/`hcode`, and `[[keys.command]]` helper) fails `protocol_mismatch` until the server restarts — which kills all pane processes. `herdr update --handoff`, the live pane-preserving path, is **disabled on Homebrew/mise/Nix installs**, so a brew-installed herdr has no way to avoid that restart. This repo now installs the self-managed release binary on macOS too, which is what closes the gap; the pitfall below is kept because it still describes what happens on any box that has not been migrated (and `just upgrade-herdr` skips with instructions when it detects a package-managed install). Check with `herdr status` (`compatible:` / `restart_needed:`), not `herdr --version`. Full recovery matrix: [`pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/herdr-brew-upgrade-strands-running-server.md).
28
29	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
30
31	---
32
33	## Model differences vs tmux
34
35	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
36
37	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
38
39	### Named sessions
40
41	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
42	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
43	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
44	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
45
46	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
47
48	## cwd & workspace-naming model
49
50	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
51
52	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
53	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
54	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
55	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
56	- **A relative `--cwd` is resolved by the SERVER, and a miss falls back to `$HOME` silently.** `herdr workspace create --cwd ../foo` joins `../foo` to the directory `herdr server` was launched from — *not* to your shell's `$PWD` — and when that path doesn't exist herdr returns `{"result":{"type":"ok"}}` with the pane opened at `$HOME`. No error, no warning. **tmux is the opposite**: `new-session -c ../foo` is resolved client-side, which is why the `shere`/`scode`/`svibe` originals never needed a guard and their herdr ports did. Any user-supplied path must be absolutized in the calling shell before it reaches the CLI — `24_herdr.sh` does this in `_herdr_abs_dir`. See [`pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/hhere-p-relative-path-opens-workspace-at-home.md).
57
58	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
59
60	| value | meaning |
61	|---|---|
62	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
63	| `home` | `$HOME` |
64	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
65	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
66
67	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
68
69	```toml
70	[[keys.command]]
71	key = "prefix+C"
72	type = "pane"
73	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
74	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
75	```

97
98	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.

100	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.

102	| Key | Action | Type |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
105	| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
106	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
107	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |

109	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator ([in-popup keys](#navigator-keys)) | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |

111	| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |

113	> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.

350	|---|---|
351	| **cwd** | `--cwd` → `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` → `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd` → `$PWD`. Preferring the env var means it still works when the CLI is protocol-mismatched with a stale server |
352	| **picker** | fzf over `$HISTFILE` (default `~/.zsh_history`), newest-first and de-duplicated. **Enter** runs the highlighted history entry; **`Alt+Enter` runs exactly what you typed**, even when history still matches it; typing something with no match at all and pressing Enter also runs it as a new command; `Esc` runs nothing. Falls back to a plain `read` prompt when fzf is absent |
353	| **shell** | `$SHELL -ic` by default, so this repo's aliases and functions resolve (`gst`, `cas`, `x`, …). `--sh` switches to `sh -c` — fast, but aliases do not exist |
354	| **on exit** | closes on success; on failure prints `[exit N]` and waits for Enter so the error stays readable. `HERDR_RUN_HOLD=always\|never` overrides |
355
356	> Two portability traps are handled inside the helper and are worth knowing if you edit it: `~/.zsh_history` is extended-history format (`: <ts>:<elapsed>;<cmd>`) **and contains non-UTF8 bytes**, so BSD `sed` aborts with `sed: RE error: illegal byte sequence` unless the parse runs under `LC_ALL=C`; and the newest-first reversal uses POSIX `awk` because `tail -r` is BSD-only while `tac` is GNU-only.
357
358	> **Why `Alt+Enter` had to exist.** Plain Enter cannot express *"run exactly what I typed"* while fzf still has a match — type `ls -la` with `ls -la /tmp` in history and Enter takes the history entry, which makes the picker feel like it can only replay old commands. `--expect=alt-enter` adds the escape hatch. Note that fzf's line layout is **not fixed**: with `--print-query --expect`, a no-match Enter prints only the query (one line), while an accepted match prints query / key / selection. The helper therefore reads the key from line 2 (empty or absent ⇒ plain Enter) and only trusts line 3 on exit code 0.

379	`dir` is the answer to *"what directory is this space about?"* — the thing you'd want from a right-click **Copy dir** on a sidebar workspace row. Three ways to reach it:

382	|---|---|---|

387	**herdr's context menus cannot be extended.** They are a fixed enum compiled into the binary — the whole inventory is one packed string blob (`Rename` · `Close` · `New worktree` · `Open worktree...` · `Close group` · `Expand` · `Delete worktree checkout...` for spaces; `New tab` · `Rename pane` · `Split right` · `Split down` · `Close pane` · `Swap with focused pane` · `Clear pane name` for panes). Verified on 0.7.5 from three directions: `config.toml` has no menu table (only `[[keys.command]]` and `ui.right_click_passthrough_modifier`, which governs whether right-click reaches the *inner app*); the plugin manifest's `[[actions]]` carries `contexts = ["workspace"]` that **looks** like menu placement but is inert; and `herdr api schema --json` contains no occurrence of "menu" at all, so nothing can inject one at runtime either.

419	**The noise problem, and how it's handled.** Unlike URLs (which self-identify with `scheme://`), file paths have no marker, so a regex alone matches dates (`2024/01/02`), rates (`10k/s`) and fractions (`1/2`). Two defenses:
420
421	| Defense | Behavior |
422	|---|---|
423	| Extraction | extrakto's path heuristics — slash-bearing tokens (`/…`, `~/…`, `./`, `a/b/c`) + bare `file.ext`; trailing `",):` stripped; rate/fraction tokens excluded outright |
424	| Existence check (the noise-killer) | Each candidate is resolved against the pane cwd (`$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`, else `herdr pane get` `foreground_cwd`, else process-info cwd) and `test -e`'d |
425	| **Two-tier list** | Paths that **exist** show first (copied as their resolved **absolute** path); everything else — remote / stale / hypothetical — appears below a `── unverified ──` separator (still selectable), so real-but-unresolvable paths aren't lost |

433	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
434
435	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
436	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
437	- **Decorative status-bar glyphs** (📌/🔖 as free-floating window labels): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation, so tmux-style status-bar bookmarks don't port. *(The specific "mark-unread / review-pending ⭐" use case IS solved — see the **Review-pending flag** section above — via a per-pane metadata token; only the purely decorative status-bar glyph remains a gap.)*
438	- **Per-key pane resize.** tmux binds `prefix+H/J/K/L` (and `M-hjkl` for fine steps) to resize directly; herdr has no per-key resize — it uses a modal `resize_mode` (`prefix+r`), then `h/j/k/l`. Not exact parity, but a close analog.
439
440	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
441

434	## AI 用量 / 額度狀態
435
436	herdr **沒有原生的用量/額度/token 顯示**（側欄只顯示 agent *狀態*）。它確實有一個逐 pane 的 hook——`herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --token usage="…" --ttl-ms N`——driver 可以把 `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` 之類的標籤推進去（與上方 **待 review 旗標** 用的是同一個 hook,但 herdr 0.7.4 起 token 是帶命名空間的 map,所以 `usage` token 與 `review` token 可以並存,不再互搶單一欄位）。有一個 Codex-only 的社群 plugin（[jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)）已從 [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) 讀的同一份 `~/.codex` 資料做到這件事；但沒有東西涵蓋 Claude/ChatGPT 額度。延後——CodexBar 的選單列仍是多供應商的檢視。設計與選項記在 [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md)。
437
438	## 缺口（沒有乾淨的 herdr 對應）
439
440	- **無縫 `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane 導覽。** `vim-tmux-navigator` 與 tmux 耦合（`is_vim` 的 `ps`/`pane_tty` 啟發式 + nvim plugin）。herdr 沒有 smart-splits 對應物——它的 pane focus 是 `prefix+h/j/k/l`，在邊界不會穿透進 nvim 的 splits。Workaround：在 nvim 裡用它自己的 `<C-w>hjkl`。這是相對 tmux 最大的 UX 退步。
441	- **OSC133 copy-mode**（`cpout` / `cpblock`、prompt 跳轉、最後輸出 yank）是 tmux 專屬。herdr 的 copy mode（`prefix+[`）是 vi 風格但沒有 OSC133 的 prompt 邊界感知。`cpcmd`（zsh history，與多工器無關）仍可用。
442	- **裝飾用的狀態列符號**（📌/🔖 當作自由浮動的視窗標籤）：herdr 沒有 `#{@option}` 的 format-string 插值,所以 tmux 風格的狀態列書籤不能移植。*（但「mark-unread / 待 review ⭐」這個具體用途已解決——見上方 **待 review 旗標** 一節——靠逐 pane 的 metadata token;只剩純裝飾的狀態列符號仍是缺口。）*
443	- **逐鍵 pane 縮放。** tmux 把 `prefix+H/J/K/L`（與 `M-hjkl` 微調）直接綁成縮放;herdr 沒有逐鍵縮放——它用模態的 `resize_mode`（`prefix+r`）再按 `h/j/k/l`。不是精確對等,但是相近的對應物。
444

Lighter counterpart to the `exec`-based `cas`/`cau`; inherits the same caveats as a manual `source ~/.zshrc`. On zsh it force-reinitializes `zsh-vi-mode` after re-sourcing so vim mode survives the reload — OMZ's unconditional `bindkey -e` + zsh-vi-mode's once-only init guard otherwise silently drop you back to emacs keys ([pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/zsh-vim-mode-lost-after-source-rc.md)) |

751:| `cref [-a\|-c] [-L] [-n] [--] FILE[:LINE[-LINE]]` | function | `dot_config/shell/59_cref.sh` | Copy a Cursor/Claude-Code-style file mention (`@path`, `@path:12`, `@path:12-40`) to the clipboard — the shell twin of Neovim's `<leader>y` [copy-reference](../neovim/copy-reference.md) maps. Path flavor: default = **git-root-relative** (falls back to cwd/`~`/absolute the way nvim's `:~:.` does); `-a`/`--absolute` = machine-absolute; `-c`/`--cwd` = relative to `$PWD`. Line info comes from `FILE:LINE[-LINE]`, trailing positionals (`cref FILE 12 40`), or — with no FILE arg — the first stdin line in grep/ripgrep `FILE:LINE:…` format (`rg -n foo \| cref`); a trailing `:col[:text]` is dropped and `:12-12` collapses to `:12`. Copies via the `x` CLI (OSC 52, SSH-safe); `-n`/`--no-copy` prints only, `-L`/`--no-line` forces a bare `@path`. stdout stays pipe-clean; `Copied @…` toast on stderr. Requires python3 |

6	"""agent-warmup — start the Claude Pro/Max 5-hour subscription window on a schedule.
7
8	Why interactive (and not ``claude -p``):
9	  Since the 2026-06-15 Anthropic billing split, only *interactive* Claude Code
10	  usage advances the rolling 5-hour subscription window. Headless ``claude -p``
11	  (and the Agent SDK) draw from a separate metered credit pool and do NOT move
12	  the window. So to "warm up" the window we must drive a real interactive
13	  ``claude`` TUI: this tool launches one in a detached tmux session (dedicated
14	  socket, isolated cwd, subscription auth), sends a tiny prompt + Enter, then
15	  tears the session down. See pitfalls/headless-claude-p-does-not-move-5h-window.md.
16
17	  Whether a *tmux-driven* interactive session still counts as interactive to
18	  Anthropic is unverified — run ``agent-warmup verify`` near a reset boundary and
19	  eyeball the captured /usage panel before trusting the recurring install.
20
21	Subcommands:
22	  run        Spawn interactive claude, send the warmup prompt, log the result.
23	  at         Queue a one-shot ``run`` via pueue (--at / --delay).
24	  install    Generate + load a recurring timer (macOS launchd / Linux systemd).
25	  uninstall  Unload + remove the recurring timer.
26	  status     Show pending one-shots, the installed timer, and recent run logs.
27	  cancel     Remove pending pueue one-shots.

31	  --model M     Claude model (default: $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or "haiku" — keeps
32	                window-token consumption tiny).

34	  --timeout S   Seconds to wait for a reply before giving up (default 120).
35	  --verify      After the reply, send /usage and capture the panel into the log.
36	  --keep        Do not kill the tmux session afterwards (for inspection).
37
38	Env:
39	  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL    default model (mirrors dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh)

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	#
3	# wake — Wake-on-LAN sender. Powers on a box by broadcasting a magic packet.
4	#
5	# The passive side (arming the target NIC + persisting it across reboots) is the
6	# `wake_on_lan` ansible role (chezmoi prompt `installWakeOnLan`). Wake-from-full-
7	# shutdown (S5) also needs a one-time BIOS change (Power On By PCI-E on, ErP off).
8	# Full setup + troubleshooting: docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   wake <host|MAC> [<host|MAC> ...]   # send magic packet(s)
12	#   wake --list                        # show configured hosts
13	#   wake <host> -b 192.168.1.255       # override the broadcast address
14	#
15	# Hosts live in ~/.config/wake/hosts.toml (seeded once by chezmoi):
16	#   [hosts.david-ubuntu]
17	#   mac       = "cc:28:aa:89:1b:9a"
18	#   broadcast = "192.168.31.255"   # optional; subnet-directed broadcast
19	#   # port    = 9                  # optional (default 9)
20	#
21	# Pure stdlib (socket + tomllib) — no external dependency, so it works on a
22	# fresh box before the `wakeonlan` apt/brew twin is installed.
23
24	from __future__ import annotations
25
26	import argparse
27	import os
28	import re
29	import socket
30	import sys
31
32	try:
33	    import tomllib  # stdlib, py3.11+
34	except ModuleNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover
35	    tomllib = None
36
37	CONFIG = os.path.join(
38	    os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", os.path.expanduser("~/.config")),
39	    "wake", "hosts.toml",
40	)
41	DEFAULT_PORT = 9
42	# aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff / aa-bb-.. / aabbccddeeff (separator must be consistent).

55	def load_config():
56	    if not os.path.exists(CONFIG):
57	        return {}
58	    if tomllib is None:
59	        die("python 3.11+ (tomllib) required to read the hosts file")
60	    try:

64	        die(f"bad config {CONFIG}: {e}", 2)

67	def normalize_mac(mac):
68	    """Return 12 lowercase hex chars, or None if the string is not a MAC."""
69	    mac = mac.strip()
70	    if not MAC_RE.match(mac):
71	        return None
72	    return re.sub(r"[:-]", "", mac).lower()

75	def magic_packet(mac_hex):
76	    return b"\xff" * 6 + bytes.fromhex(mac_hex) * 16
77
78
79	def send(mac_hex, broadcasts, port, count, quiet):
80	    pkt = magic_packet(mac_hex)
81	    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
82	    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_BROADCAST, 1)
83	    try:
84	        for _ in range(count):
85	            for dest in broadcasts:
86	                sock.sendto(pkt, (dest, port))
87	    finally:
88	        sock.close()
89	    if not quiet:
90	        pretty = ":".join(mac_hex[i:i + 2] for i in range(0, 12, 2))
91	        print(f"wake: sent {count}x magic packet to {pretty} "
92	              f"via {', '.join(broadcasts)}:{port}")
93
94
95	def resolve(target, hosts):
96	    """(mac_hex, host_broadcast, host_port) for a config name or a raw MAC."""
97	    if target in hosts:
98	        entry = hosts[target]
99	        mac = normalize_mac(str(entry.get("mac", "")))
100	        if not mac:
101	            die(f"host '{target}' has no valid mac= in {CONFIG}")
102	        return mac, entry.get("broadcast"), int(entry.get("port", DEFAULT_PORT))
103	    mac = normalize_mac(target)
104	    if mac:
105	        return mac, None, DEFAULT_PORT
106	    die(f"unknown host '{target}' (not in {CONFIG}) and not a MAC. "
107	        "Try `wake --list`.")
108

110	def main():
111	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
112	        prog="wake",
113	        description="Wake-on-LAN sender — power on a box by magic packet.",
114	    )
115	    ap.add_argument("targets", nargs="*",
116	                    help="host name(s) from the config, or raw MAC(s)")
117	    ap.add_argument("-l", "--list", action="store_true",
118	                    help="list configured hosts and exit")
119	    ap.add_argument("--list-names", action="store_true",
120	                    help="print bare host names (for shell completion)")
121	    ap.add_argument("-b", "--broadcast",
122	                    help="broadcast address (default: 255.255.255.255 + host's)")
123	    ap.add_argument("-p", "--port", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PORT,
124	                    help=f"UDP port (default {DEFAULT_PORT})")
125	    ap.add_argument("-c", "--count", type=int, default=3,
126	                    help="packets per target (default 3)")
127	    ap.add_argument("-q", "--quiet", action="store_true",
128	                    help="suppress per-packet output")
129	    args = ap.parse_args()
130
131	    cfg = load_config()
132	    hosts = cfg.get("hosts", {}) if isinstance(cfg, dict) else {}
133	    default_bcast = cfg.get("broadcast") if isinstance(cfg, dict) else None
134
135	    if args.list_names:
136	        print("\n".join(sorted(hosts)))
137	        return
138	    if args.list:
139	        if not hosts:
140	            print(f"(no hosts configured in {CONFIG})")
141	            return
142	        width = max(len(n) for n in hosts)
143	        for name in sorted(hosts):
144	            entry = hosts[name]
145	            bcast = entry.get("broadcast", default_bcast or "255.255.255.255")
146	            print(f"{name:<{width}}  {entry.get('mac', '?'):<17}  {bcast}")
147	        return
148
149	    if not args.targets:
150	        ap.error("no target given (a host name or MAC). "
151	                 "`wake --list` shows configured hosts.")
152
153	    for target in args.targets:
154	        mac, host_bcast, host_port = resolve(target, hosts)
155	        port = args.port if args.port != DEFAULT_PORT else host_port

# Recommended v1 Implementation Plan

## 1. CLI contract

Create `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_herdr-grep` as an executable, pure-stdlib Python CLI using `argparse`, `json`, `os`, `shutil`, and `subprocess`.

### Synopsis

```text
herdr-grep [OPTIONS] PATTERN
herdr-grep --list-sessions
```

Search options:

```text
-F, --fixed-strings
-i, --ignore-case
--source {visible,recent,recent-unwrapped}
--visible
--session NAME
--all-sessions
--json
-h, --help
```

Contract:

- `PATTERN` is one ripgrep regex by default.
- `-F` treats it literally.
- `-i` enables case-insensitive matching and combines with `-F`.
- Default source is `recent`, meaning full retained scrollback.
- `--visible` is a convenience alias for `--source visible`.
- Put `--source` and `--visible` in one mutually exclusive argparse group.
- Put `--session` and `--all-sessions` in another mutually exclusive group.
- A pattern beginning with `-` uses the standard terminator:

  ```text
  herdr-grep -- -leading-dash
  ```

- `--list-sessions` is public, standalone, and prints sorted running session names, one per line. It exists primarily for shell completion and does not require `rg`.
- Reject combining `--list-sessions` with `PATTERN` or search options as usage error 2.
- Do not add v1 context, count, color, multiline, pane-filter, TSV, `--host`, or Television options.
- Do not expose Herdr’s `detection` read source in v1.

### Session selection

Mirror `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh:80-121` exactly:

1. Always discover sessions with:

   ```text
   herdr session list --json
   ```

2. No session flag:
   - If `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is inherited, leave it untouched and scan that ambient socket.
   - Resolve its display name by matching `socket_path`; if no entry matches, use `default`, matching `_herdr_session_target`.
   - Without an ambient socket, leave the environment untouched so Herdr selects its default socket.

3. `--session NAME`:
   - Require an exact session entry.
   - Require `running == true`.
   - Require a non-empty `socket_path`.
   - Copy the parent environment and set `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` only in child Herdr calls.

4. `--all-sessions`:
   - Select only entries with `running == true`.
   - Sort them by session name.
   - Give each session’s Herdr children its own `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`.
   - Stopped entries are silently outside the scan, not failures.
   - An empty running-session set is a complete empty scan: exit 1.

Treat invalid JSON or an invalid top-level session schema as fatal exit 2. Validate each entry’s `name`, `running`, and `socket_path`; duplicate names or malformed entries also make discovery incomplete rather than guessing.

### Pane enumeration and reading

For each target session, sequentially run:

```text
herdr pane list
```

Parse only `.result.panes`. For every valid pane, retain these fields directly:

- `pane_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `tab_id`
- `agent_status`
- `foreground_cwd`
- `cwd`

Never derive workspace or tab identity by splitting `pane_id`.

Sort panes lexically by:

```text
(workspace_id, tab_id, pane_id)
```

Read each pane with:

```text
herdr pane read PANE_ID --source SOURCE --format text
```

This reuses the retained-scrollback behavior established at `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:135-143`.

Use argv arrays throughout, `shell=False`, captured stdout/stderr, UTF-8 decoding with replacement for invalid terminal bytes, and a copied child environment. An empty successful pane read is simply a no-match input.

## 2. Ripgrep adapter

Resolve `herdr` and `rg` once with `shutil.which`. Missing dependencies produce exit 2 with a clear `herdr-grep:` diagnostic.

Build one canonical matcher argv:

```text
rg --no-config --json --text [--fixed-strings] [--ignore-case] -- PATTERN
```

Reasons:

- `--json` provides an unambiguous internal protocol.
- `--no-config` prevents `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` from silently changing v1 semantics.
- `--text` ensures pane text is searched even if captured content contains NUL-like bytes.
- `--` safely protects patterns beginning with `-`.

Before any pane enumeration, run this matcher once with empty stdin:

- Exit 0 or 1 means the pattern is valid.
- Exit 2 or malformed output means fatal exit 2.
- This prevents repeating an invalid-regex error once per pane.

For each pane:

- Exit 0: parse the JSON-lines stream.
- Exit 1: no matches in that pane.
- Any other exit, malformed JSON line, or malformed match event: record a pane-level failure and continue.
- Parse all events for a pane before accepting its records, so malformed output does not produce a half-trusted pane result.

Ripgrep emits one `match` event per matching line. Preserve every occurrence from that event’s `submatches` array.

## 3. Output contract

### Human output

Emit one line per matching line:

```text
SESSION/PANE_ID:LINE_NUMBER:LINE
```

Example:

```text
default/w3:p7:42:connection refused while opening socket
```

Rules:

- Matching lines containing several occurrences are printed once, matching normal grep behavior.
- The session and pane prefix is repeated on every output line.
- Remove only the captured line terminator; preserve the rest of the line.
- No headings, summaries, colors, or “no matches” message.
- Rich pane metadata and individual occurrence offsets are available through `--json`.

### JSON output

`--json` emits one UTF-8, `ensure_ascii=False`, indented object followed by a newline:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "pattern": "foo",
  "source": "recent",
  "fixed_strings": false,
  "ignore_case": false,
  "complete": true,
  "sessions": [
    "default"
  ],
  "matches": [
    {
      "session": "default",
      "workspace_id": "w3",
      "tab_id": "w3:t4",
      "pane_id": "w3:p7",
      "agent_status": "idle",
      "foreground_cwd": "/Users/david/project",
      "cwd": "/Users/david",
      "line_number": 42,
      "line": "Foo foo",
      "submatches": [
        {
          "text": "Foo",
          "start_byte": 0,
          "end_byte": 3
        },
        {
          "text": "foo",
          "start_byte": 4,
          "end_byte": 7
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "errors": []
}
```

Field semantics:

- `sessions`: sorted names of all targeted sessions, including one that later fails during enumeration.
- `line_number`: one-based, as reported by ripgrep.
- `line`: line text without its ending newline.
- `start_byte` and `end_byte`: zero-based, half-open UTF-8 byte offsets within `line`, not character indexes.
- `agent_status`, `foreground_cwd`, and `cwd`: string or `null`, copied from the pane-list object.
- `complete`: false if any selected session or enumerated pane could not be fully scanned.

Every error record has a fixed shape:

```json
{
  "scope": "pane",
  "session": "default",
  "pane_id": "w3:p7",
  "operation": "pane-read",
  "message": "herdr exited 1: pane not found"
}
```

Allowed scopes:

- `global`
- `session`
- `pane`

Use stable operation names:

- `dependency`
- `rg-validate`
- `session-list`
- `session-select`
- `pane-list`
- `pane-entry`
- `pane-read`
- `rg-match`

`session` and `pane_id` are nullable where the scope does not have them.

After successful argparse parsing, `--json` should still emit this valid schema for dependency, discovery, selected-session, and partial-scan failures. Argparse usage errors remain ordinary stderr usage output.

### Determinism

Sort final matches by:

```text
(session, workspace_id, tab_id, pane_id, line_number, first-submatch-start-byte)
```

Sort errors by:

```text
(session-or-empty, pane_id-or-empty, operation, message)
```

Render collected stderr warnings in that same deterministic error order.

## 4. Exit behavior

Use grep-style statuses:

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | At least one match and the scan completed |
| 1 | No matches and the scan completed |
| 2 | Usage, missing dependency, invalid regex, unavailable selected session, malformed JSON/schema, or any incomplete scan |

A pane or session disappearing after enumeration must:

1. Preserve matches from successful panes.
2. Warn on stderr.
3. Set `complete: false` in JSON.
4. Return 2 regardless of whether good matches were found.

## 5. Internal structure

Keep the executable self-contained, but separate responsibilities into small functions and dataclasses:

- `build_parser()`
- `run_command(...)`
- `load_sessions(...)`
- `select_targets(...)`
- `list_panes(...)`

- `main()`

Suggested internal records:

- `SessionTarget(name, socket_override)`
- `PaneRecord(...)`
- `MatchRecord(...)`
- `ScanError(...)`
- `ScanResult(...)`

`socket_override=None` is meaningful: it means preserve ambient/default routing without assigning `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`.

113	            | jq -r '.result.workspace.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
114	        tb_label=$(herdr tab get "$tb" 2>/dev/null \
115	            | jq -r '.result.tab.label // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
116
117	        sock="${HERDR_SOCKET_PATH:-}"
118	        session=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null \
119	            | jq -r --arg s "$sock" \
120	                'first(.sessions[]? | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name) // empty' \
121	                2>/dev/null || true)
122	        [ -n "$session" ] || session="default"
123
124	        text=$(printf 'session=%s\nworkspace=%s%s\ntab=%s%s\npane=%s\n' \
125	            "$session" \
126	            "$ws" "${ws_label:+ ($ws_label)}" \
127	            "$tb" "${tb_label:+ ($tb_label)}" \
128	            "$pn")
129	        [ -n "$sock" ] && text=$(printf '%s\nsocket=%s' "$text" "$sock")
130	        text=$(printf '%s\n# herdr pane get %s' "$text" "$pn")

132	        copy "$text"
133	        echo "copied coordinate for $pane"
134	        ;;
135	    content)
136	        case "$source" in
137	            visible|recent|recent-unwrapped) ;;
138	            *) echo "pane-copy: --source must be visible|recent|recent-unwrapped" >&2; exit 64 ;;
139	        esac
140	        body=$(herdr pane read "$pane" --source "$source" --format text 2>/dev/null) \
141	            || { echo "pane-copy: failed to read content of $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
142	        copy "$body"
143	        echo "copied $source content for $pane"
144	        ;;
145	    dir)
146	        # WORKSPACE ("space") root dir — the sidebar row's directory, NOT the
147	        # pane's live cwd. Derivation is shared with prefix+C's new-tab helper
148	        # and the herdr-sesh tv channel; it lives in space-root.sh, which also
149	        # accepts a bare workspace id. Resolved beside this script rather than
150	        # via PATH (a command-pane may run us without the interactive PATH).
151	        here=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd -P)
152	        root=$("$here/space-root.sh" "$pane") || exit 1
153	        copy "$root"
154	        echo "copied space dir: $root"
155	        ;;
156	    cwd)
157	        # The pane's LIVE cwd — same answer `abspath` would give inside it.
158	        # foreground_cwd tracks the running process; cwd is the shell's start dir.
159	        dir=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
160	            | jq -r '.result.pane | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
161	        [ -n "$dir" ] || { echo "pane-copy: could not resolve cwd for $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
162	        copy "$dir"
163	        echo "copied pane cwd: $dir"
164	        ;;
165	    *) usage ;;
166	esac

2	# Unit tests for `ghget` in dot_config/shell/41_github.sh.
3	#
4	# ghget parses GitHub tree URLs and downloads a subdirectory. The parsing path
5	# is pure string manipulation in zsh — high silent-regression risk (wrong

13	# Stub curl + tar that just echo the args they were called with into a log
14	# file, so tests can assert on what URL curl was asked to fetch / what tar
15	# was asked to extract.
16	_install_curl_tar_stubs() {
17	  setup_path_stub
18	  : "${CAPTURE_LOG:=$BATS_STUB_DIR/capture.log}"
19	  export CAPTURE_LOG
20

22	#!/usr/bin/env bash
23	echo "curl $*" >> "$CAPTURE_LOG"
24	# Emit minimal bytes so the pipe to tar has something — tar stub ignores input.
25	printf 'fakearchive'
