# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

 - `~/.config/homebrew/` - Brewfiles for GUI apps (macOS casks + mas) plus selected CLI helper formulas (e.g., `mas` for App Store installs)

 SSH files are managed as create-only templates: if `~/.ssh/config` already exists, it is not overwritten. In that case, add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to your existing config manually to load the managed snippets.

diff --git a/docs/tools/herdr.md b/docs/tools/herdr.md
index 4fd573e..974eca6 100644
--- a/docs/tools/herdr.md
+++ b/docs/tools/herdr.md
@@ -45,6 +45,37 @@ The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessio

 **Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).

+## Search pane content with `herdr-grep`
+
+Herdr can read one pane but has no native cross-pane grep. This repo deploys **`herdr-grep`**, which packages `pane list → pane read → rg` and prints the exact Session / Workspace / Tab / Pane containing each match:
+
+```console
+$ herdr-grep -F 'connection refused'
+[session=default workspace=w1 tab=w1:t2 pane=w1:p4] 183:connection refused while opening socket
+```
+
+```bash
+herdr-grep 'error|failed'                   # regex; current/default session
+herdr-grep -F -i 'connection refused'       # literal, case-insensitive
+herdr-grep --visible 'ready'                # current visible screens only
+herdr-grep --source recent-unwrapped 'url'  # retained history without hard wraps
+herdr-grep --session work 'panic'           # one running named session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions 'rate limit'      # every running local session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions --json 'panic'    # structured matches + errors
+herdr-grep -F -- -leading-dash              # protect a pattern beginning with `-`
+```
+
+| Aspect | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Default scope | The ambient session when `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is set (inside Herdr); otherwise `default`. `--session NAME` resolves the authoritative socket from `herdr session list --json`; `--all-sessions` scans running sessions only. |
+| Content source | `recent` by default (full retained scrollback); `--visible` for the current screen; `--source recent-unwrapped` when terminal wrapping splits a phrase. |
+| Output | Human output repeats `session/workspace/tab/pane` on every matching line. `--json` adds socket, cwd, agent state, byte-offset submatches, `complete`, and structured errors. Line numbers are **relative to this capture**, not persistent pane coordinates. |
+| Exit status | `0` = match + complete scan; `1` = clean no-match; `2` = usage/error/**incomplete scan**. If a pane disappears mid-scan, good matches are preserved, the failure goes to stderr/JSON, and the command returns 2. |
+
+The search is bounded by what the live Herdr server still retains: closed panes, output older than the history limit, and alternate-screen content already discarded cannot be recovered. The command runs where the Unix socket is accessible. For a remote server, run the deployed CLI through SSH, for example `ssh server 'herdr-grep --all-sessions -F -- "connection refused"'`; **`herdr --remote` is an interactive thin-client attach, not an RPC prefix for pane subcommands**.
+
+`tv herdr-agent-panes` and `tv herdr-review` still fuzzy-search metadata only (pane/session identifiers, state, cwd). Their visible pane text is a preview and is not part of Television's searchable source; use `herdr-grep` when the query is terminal content.
+
 ## cwd & workspace-naming model

 herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):

@@ -50,6 +50,37 @@ herdr 的階層是 **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane**——比 tmux（Se

 **從 CLI 子指令鎖定某個 session**：`workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent` **沒有 `--session`/`--socket` flag**。唯一的槓桿是 **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** 這個環境變數 (env var)——把它設成某 session 的 `socket_path`，所有子指令就會導向該 session。在 herdr pane 內部它已經被 export 成當前 session 的 socket，所以*在 herdr 內*跑的腳本天生就鎖定當前 session。`hvibe --session NAME` 正是靠這個機制運作（見下文）。

+## 用 `herdr-grep` 搜尋 pane 內容
+
+Herdr 能讀取單一 pane，但沒有原生的跨 pane grep。本 repo 部署 **`herdr-grep`**，把 `pane list → pane read → rg` 包成一個指令，並印出每筆命中的完整 Session / Workspace / Tab / Pane 座標：
+
+```console
+$ herdr-grep -F 'connection refused'
+[session=default workspace=w1 tab=w1:t2 pane=w1:p4] 183:connection refused while opening socket
+```
+
+```bash
+herdr-grep 'error|failed'                   # regex；當前/default session
+herdr-grep -F -i 'connection refused'       # 固定字串、不分大小寫
+herdr-grep --visible 'ready'                # 只搜尋目前可見畫面
+herdr-grep --source recent-unwrapped 'url'  # 搜尋保留歷史，不受硬換行切斷
+herdr-grep --session work 'panic'           # 一個正在執行的具名 session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions 'rate limit'      # 所有正在執行的本機 session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions --json 'panic'    # 結構化 matches + errors
+herdr-grep -F -- -leading-dash              # 保護以 `-` 開頭的 pattern
+```
+
+| 面向 | 行為 |
+|---|---|
+| 預設範圍 | 有 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`（Herdr 內部）時搜尋 ambient session，否則搜尋 `default`。`--session NAME` 從 `herdr session list --json` 解析權威 socket；`--all-sessions` 只掃描正在執行的 session。 |
+| 內容來源 | 預設 `recent`（完整保留的 scrollback）；`--visible` 只看目前畫面；終端硬換行切斷片語時使用 `--source recent-unwrapped`。 |
+| 輸出 | 人類可讀輸出在每一筆命中重複 `session/workspace/tab/pane`。`--json` 另含 socket、cwd、agent 狀態、byte-offset submatches、`complete` 與結構化 errors。行號是**相對於這次 capture**，不是永久 pane 座標。 |
+| Exit status | `0` = 有命中且掃描完整；`1` = 完整掃描但無命中；`2` = 用法錯誤／執行錯誤／**掃描不完整**。pane 在掃描途中消失時，成功的 matches 仍會保留、錯誤送到 stderr/JSON，並回傳 2。 |
+
+搜尋範圍受限於 live Herdr server 仍保留的內容：已關閉的 pane、早於 history limit 的輸出，以及 alternate screen 已丟棄的內容都無法找回。命令必須在能存取 Unix socket 的環境執行；遠端 server 請透過 SSH 執行已部署的 CLI，例如 `ssh server 'herdr-grep --all-sessions -F -- "connection refused"'`。**`herdr --remote` 是互動式 thin-client attach，不是 pane 子指令的 RPC 前綴。**
+
+`tv herdr-agent-panes` 與 `tv herdr-review` 仍只 fuzzy-search metadata（pane/session identifiers、狀態、cwd）。可見 pane 文字只是 preview，不在 Television 的 searchable source 中；要查 terminal content 請用 `herdr-grep`。
+

 herdr 追蹤 cwd 的方式跟 tmux 不同,會顛覆兩個常見預期（皆用 `herdr pane list` 驗證）:

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

193	def load_sessions(herdr: str) -> list[SessionInfo]:
194	    result = run_command([herdr, "session", "list", "--json"])
195	    if result.returncode != 0:
196	        detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "herdr failed")
197	        raise ValueError(f"herdr session list failed: {detail}")
198
199	    payload = parse_json_bytes(result.stdout, "session-list")
200	    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get("sessions"), list):
201	        raise ValueError("session-list JSON must contain a sessions array")
202
203	    sessions: list[SessionInfo] = []
204	    names: set[str] = set()
205	    for index, item in enumerate(payload["sessions"]):
206	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
207	            raise ValueError(f"session entry {index} must be an object")
208	        name = item.get("name")
209	        running = item.get("running")
210	        socket_path = item.get("socket_path")
211	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
212	            raise ValueError(f"session entry {index} has an invalid name")
213	        if name in names:
214	            raise ValueError(f"session-list JSON contains duplicate session '{name}'")
215	        if not isinstance(running, bool):
216	            raise ValueError(f"session '{name}' has an invalid running value")
217	        if not isinstance(socket_path, str):
218	            raise ValueError(f"session '{name}' has an invalid socket_path")
219	        if running and not socket_path:
220	            raise ValueError(f"running session '{name}' has an empty socket_path")
221	        names.add(name)
222	        sessions.append(SessionInfo(name=name, running=running, socket_path=socket_path))
223	    return sessions

227	    by_name = {session.name: session for session in sessions}
228
229	    if args.all_sessions:

232	            for session in sorted(sessions, key=lambda item: item.name)
233	            if session.running

235
236	    if args.session is not None:

238	        if selected is None:
239	            raise ValueError(f"session '{args.session}' not found; start it with: herdr --session {args.session}")
240	        if not selected.running:

243	            )
244	        return [SessionTarget(selected.name, selected.socket_path, True)]
245
246	    ambient_socket = os.environ.get("HERDR_SOCKET_PATH")
247	    if ambient_socket:
248	        name = next(
249	            (session.name for session in sessions if session.socket_path == ambient_socket),
250	            "default",
251	        )
252	        return [SessionTarget(name, ambient_socket, False)]
253
254	    default = by_name.get("default")
255	    socket_path = default.socket_path if default is not None else None
256	    return [SessionTarget("default", socket_path or None, False)]

304	        if not isinstance(item, dict):

320	            )
321	            continue
322	        if pane_id in seen:
323	            errors.append(
324	                ScanError("pane", target.name, pane_id, "pane-entry", "duplicate pane_id in pane-list JSON")
325	            )
326	            continue
327	        seen.add(pane_id)
328	        panes.append(

379	def parse_submatches(value: Any) -> tuple[SubmatchRecord, ...]:
380	    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
381	        raise ValueError("ripgrep match event has no submatches")
382	    parsed: list[SubmatchRecord] = []
383	    for item in value:
384	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or not isinstance(item.get("match"), dict):
385	            raise ValueError("ripgrep submatch must be an object")
386	        text = item["match"].get("text")
387	        start = item.get("start")
388	        end = item.get("end")
389	        if not isinstance(text, str) or not isinstance(start, int) or not isinstance(end, int):
390	            raise ValueError("ripgrep submatch has invalid text or byte offsets")
391	        if start < 0 or end < start:
392	            raise ValueError("ripgrep submatch has invalid byte offset order")
393	        parsed.append(SubmatchRecord(text=text, start_byte=start, end_byte=end))
394	    return tuple(parsed)
395
396
397	def match_pane(
398	    rg_argv: Sequence[str],
399	    pane: PaneRecord,
400	    text: str,
401	) -> tuple[list[MatchRecord], ScanError | None]:
402	    result = run_command(rg_argv, input_bytes=text.encode("utf-8"))
403	    if result.returncode == 1:
404	        return [], None
405	    if result.returncode != 0:
406	        detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "ripgrep failed")
407	        return [], ScanError("pane", pane.session, pane.pane_id, "rg-match", detail)
408
409	    candidates: list[MatchRecord] = []
410	    try:
411	        output = result.stdout.decode("utf-8")
412	        for raw_line in output.splitlines():
413	            event = json.loads(raw_line)
414	            if not isinstance(event, dict) or not isinstance(event.get("type"), str):
415	                raise ValueError("ripgrep JSON event must be an object with a type")
416	            if event["type"] != "match":
417	                continue
418	            data = event.get("data")
419	            if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get("lines"), dict):
420	                raise ValueError("ripgrep match event has invalid data")
421	            line = data["lines"].get("text")
422	            line_number = data.get("line_number")
423	            if not isinstance(line, str) or not isinstance(line_number, int) or line_number < 1:
424	                raise ValueError("ripgrep match event has invalid line data")
425	            if line.endswith("\n"):
426	                line = line[:-1]
427	                if line.endswith("\r"):
428	                    line = line[:-1]
429	            submatches = parse_submatches(data.get("submatches"))
430	            candidates.append(
431	                MatchRecord(
432	                    session=pane.session,
433	                    socket_path=pane.socket_path,
434	                    workspace_id=pane.workspace_id,
435	                    tab_id=pane.tab_id,
436	                    pane_id=pane.pane_id,
437	                    agent_status=pane.agent_status,
438	                    foreground_cwd=pane.foreground_cwd,
439	                    cwd=pane.cwd,
440	                    line_number=line_number,
441	                    line=line,
442	                    submatches=submatches,
443	                )
444	            )
445	        if not candidates:
446	            raise ValueError("ripgrep exited with matches but emitted no match events")
447	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
448	        return [], ScanError("pane", pane.session, pane.pane_id, "rg-match", str(exc))
449	    return candidates, None
450
451
452	def match_sort_key(match: MatchRecord) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
453	    first_start = match.submatches[0].start_byte if match.submatches else -1
454	    return (
455	        match.session,
456	        match.workspace_id,
457	        match.tab_id,
458	        match.pane_id,
459	        match.line_number,
460	        first_start,
461	    )
462
463
464	def error_sort_key(error: ScanError) -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
465	    return (error.session or "", error.pane_id or "", error.operation, error.message)
466
467
468	def scan(
469	    herdr: str,
470	    rg_argv: Sequence[str],
471	    targets: list[SessionTarget],
472	    source: str,
473	) -> ScanResult:
474	    result = ScanResult(
475	        sessions=sorted(target.name for target in targets),
476	        matches=[],
477	        errors=[],
478	    )
479
480	    pattern_error = validate_pattern(rg_argv)
481	    if pattern_error is not None:
482	        result.errors.append(pattern_error)
483	        return result
484
485	    for target in targets:
486	        panes, pane_errors = list_panes(herdr, target)
487	        result.errors.extend(pane_errors)
488	        for pane in panes:
489	            text, read_error = read_pane(herdr, target, pane, source)
490	            if read_error is not None:
491	                result.errors.append(read_error)
492	                continue
493	            assert text is not None
494	            matches, match_error = match_pane(rg_argv, pane, text)
495	            if match_error is not None:
496	                result.errors.append(match_error)
497	                continue
498	            result.matches.extend(matches)
499
500	    result.matches.sort(key=match_sort_key)
501	    result.errors.sort(key=error_sort_key)
502	    return result
503
504
505	def render_human(result: ScanResult) -> None:
506	    for match in result.matches:
507	        coordinate = (
508	            f"session={match.session} workspace={match.workspace_id} "
509	            f"tab={match.tab_id} pane={match.pane_id}"
510	        )
511	        print(f"[{coordinate}] {match.line_number}:{match.line}")
512	    for error in result.errors:
513	        location = ""
514	        if error.session is not None:
515	            location += f" session={error.session}"
516	        if error.pane_id is not None:
517	            location += f" pane={error.pane_id}"
518	        print(
519	            f"herdr-grep:{location} {error.operation}: {error.message}",
520	            file=sys.stderr,
521	        )
522
523
524	def render_json(args: argparse.Namespace, result: ScanResult, source: str) -> None:
525	    payload = {
526	        "schema_version": 1,
527	        "pattern": args.pattern,
528	        "source": source,
529	        "fixed_strings": bool(args.fixed_strings),
530	        "ignore_case": bool(args.ignore_case),
531	        "complete": result.complete,
532	        "sessions": result.sessions,
533	        "matches": [
534	            {
535	                **{key: value for key, value in asdict(match).items() if key != "submatches"},
536	                "submatches": [asdict(submatch) for submatch in match.submatches],
537	            }
538	            for match in result.matches
539	        ],
540	        "errors": [asdict(error) for error in result.errors],
541	    }
542	    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
543
544
545	def fatal_result(operation: str, message: str) -> ScanResult:
546	    return ScanResult(
547	        sessions=[],
548	        matches=[],
549	        errors=[ScanError("global", None, None, operation, message)],
550	    )
551
552
553	def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
554	    args = parse_args(argv)
555
556	    herdr = shutil.which("herdr")
557	    if herdr is None:
558	        if args.list_sessions:
559	            print("herdr-grep: dependency: herdr not found on PATH", file=sys.stderr)
560	            return 2
561	        result = fatal_result("dependency", "herdr not found on PATH")
562	        if args.json:
563	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
564	        else:
565	            render_human(result)
566	        return 2
567
568	    try:
569	        sessions = load_sessions(herdr)
570	    except ValueError as exc:
571	        if args.list_sessions:
572	            print(f"herdr-grep: session-list: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
573	            return 2
574	        result = fatal_result("session-list", str(exc))
575	        if args.json:
576	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
577	        else:
578	            render_human(result)
579	        return 2
580
581	    if args.list_sessions:
582	        for session in sorted(item.name for item in sessions if item.running):
583	            print(session)
584	        return 0
585
586	    rg = shutil.which("rg")
587	    if rg is None:
588	        result = fatal_result("dependency", "rg not found on PATH")
589	        if args.json:
590	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
591	        else:
592	            render_human(result)
593	        return 2
594
595	    try:
596	        targets = select_targets(args, sessions)
597	    except ValueError as exc:
598	        result = fatal_result("session-select", str(exc))
599	        if args.json:
600	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
601	        else:
602	            render_human(result)
603	        return 2
604
605	    result = scan(herdr, build_rg_argv(rg, args), targets, args.source)
606	    if args.json:
607	        render_json(args, result, args.source)
608	    else:
609	        render_human(result)
610	    return result.exit_status()
611
612
613	if __name__ == "__main__":
614	    try:
615	        raise SystemExit(main())
616	    except BrokenPipeError:
617	        try:
618	            sys.stdout.close()
619	        finally:
620	            raise SystemExit(0)
621

 **Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).

+## Search pane content with `herdr-grep`
+
+Herdr can read one pane but has no native cross-pane grep. This repo deploys **`herdr-grep`**, which packages `pane list → pane read → rg` and prints the exact Session / Workspace / Tab / Pane containing each match:
+
+```console
+$ herdr-grep -F 'connection refused'
+[session=default workspace=w1 tab=w1:t2 pane=w1:p4] 183:connection refused while opening socket
+```
+
+```bash
+herdr-grep 'error|failed'                   # regex; current/default session
+herdr-grep -F -i 'connection refused'       # literal, case-insensitive
+herdr-grep --visible 'ready'                # current visible screens only
+herdr-grep --source recent-unwrapped 'url'  # retained history without hard wraps
+herdr-grep --session work 'panic'           # one running named session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions 'rate limit'      # every running local session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions --json 'panic'    # structured matches + errors
+herdr-grep -F -- -leading-dash              # protect a pattern beginning with `-`
+```
+
+| Aspect | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Default scope | The ambient session when `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is set (inside Herdr); otherwise `default`. `--session NAME` resolves the authoritative socket from `herdr session list --json`; `--all-sessions` scans running sessions only. |
+| Content source | `recent` by default (full retained scrollback); `--visible` for the current screen; `--source recent-unwrapped` when terminal wrapping splits a phrase. |
+| Output | Human output repeats `session/workspace/tab/pane` on every matching line. `--json` adds socket, cwd, agent state, byte-offset submatches, `complete`, and structured errors. Line numbers are **relative to this capture**, not persistent pane coordinates. |
+| Exit status | `0` = match + complete scan; `1` = clean no-match; `2` = usage/error/**incomplete scan**. If a pane disappears mid-scan, good matches are preserved, the failure goes to stderr/JSON, and the command returns 2. |
+
+The search is bounded by what the live Herdr server still retains: closed panes, output older than the history limit, and alternate-screen content already discarded cannot be recovered. The command runs where the Unix socket is accessible. For a remote server, run the deployed CLI through SSH, for example `ssh server 'herdr-grep --all-sessions -F -- "connection refused"'`; **`herdr --remote` is an interactive thin-client attach, not an RPC prefix for pane subcommands**.
+
+`tv herdr-agent-panes` and `tv herdr-review` still fuzzy-search metadata only (pane/session identifiers, state, cwd). Their visible pane text is a preview and is not part of Television's searchable source; use `herdr-grep` when the query is terminal content.
+
 ## cwd & workspace-naming model

 herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
diff --git a/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md b/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md
index 038e655..fc5d272 100644
--- a/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md
+++ b/docs/tools/herdr.zh-TW.md
@@ -50,6 +50,37 @@ herdr 的階層是 **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane**——比 tmux（Se

 **從 CLI 子指令鎖定某個 session**：`workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent` **沒有 `--session`/`--socket` flag**。唯一的槓桿是 **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** 這個環境變數 (env var)——把它設成某 session 的 `socket_path`，所有子指令就會導向該 session。在 herdr pane 內部它已經被 export 成當前 session 的 socket，所以*在 herdr 內*跑的腳本天生就鎖定當前 session。`hvibe --session NAME` 正是靠這個機制運作（見下文）。

+## 用 `herdr-grep` 搜尋 pane 內容
+
+Herdr 能讀取單一 pane，但沒有原生的跨 pane grep。本 repo 部署 **`herdr-grep`**，把 `pane list → pane read → rg` 包成一個指令，並印出每筆命中的完整 Session / Workspace / Tab / Pane 座標：
+
+```console
+$ herdr-grep -F 'connection refused'
+[session=default workspace=w1 tab=w1:t2 pane=w1:p4] 183:connection refused while opening socket
+```
+
+```bash
+herdr-grep 'error|failed'                   # regex；當前/default session
+herdr-grep -F -i 'connection refused'       # 固定字串、不分大小寫
+herdr-grep --visible 'ready'                # 只搜尋目前可見畫面
+herdr-grep --source recent-unwrapped 'url'  # 搜尋保留歷史，不受硬換行切斷
+herdr-grep --session work 'panic'           # 一個正在執行的具名 session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions 'rate limit'      # 所有正在執行的本機 session
+herdr-grep --all-sessions --json 'panic'    # 結構化 matches + errors
+herdr-grep -F -- -leading-dash              # 保護以 `-` 開頭的 pattern
+```
+
+| 面向 | 行為 |
+|---|---|
+| 預設範圍 | 有 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`（Herdr 內部）時搜尋 ambient session，否則搜尋 `default`。`--session NAME` 從 `herdr session list --json` 解析權威 socket；`--all-sessions` 只掃描正在執行的 session。 |
+| 內容來源 | 預設 `recent`（完整保留的 scrollback）；`--visible` 只看目前畫面；終端硬換行切斷片語時使用 `--source recent-unwrapped`。 |
+| 輸出 | 人類可讀輸出在每一筆命中重複 `session/workspace/tab/pane`。`--json` 另含 socket、cwd、agent 狀態、byte-offset submatches、`complete` 與結構化 errors。行號是**相對於這次 capture**，不是永久 pane 座標。 |
+| Exit status | `0` = 有命中且掃描完整；`1` = 完整掃描但無命中；`2` = 用法錯誤／執行錯誤／**掃描不完整**。pane 在掃描途中消失時，成功的 matches 仍會保留、錯誤送到 stderr/JSON，並回傳 2。 |
+
+搜尋範圍受限於 live Herdr server 仍保留的內容：已關閉的 pane、早於 history limit 的輸出，以及 alternate screen 已丟棄的內容都無法找回。命令必須在能存取 Unix socket 的環境執行；遠端 server 請透過 SSH 執行已部署的 CLI，例如 `ssh server 'herdr-grep --all-sessions -F -- "connection refused"'`。**`herdr --remote` 是互動式 thin-client attach，不是 pane 子指令的 RPC 前綴。**
+
+`tv herdr-agent-panes` 與 `tv herdr-review` 仍只 fuzzy-search metadata（pane/session identifiers、狀態、cwd）。可見 pane 文字只是 preview，不在 Television 的 searchable source 中；要查 terminal content 請用 `herdr-grep`。
+
 ## cwd 與 workspace 命名模型

 herdr 追蹤 cwd 的方式跟 tmux 不同,會顛覆兩個常見預期（皆用 `herdr pane list` 驗證）:

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — drive a real interactive agent TUI at a scheduled time to move the quota window (launchd/systemd/pueue). See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with three pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`). See `docs/tools/herdr.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the

in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

193	def load_sessions(herdr: str) -> list[SessionInfo]:
194	    result = run_command([herdr, "session", "list", "--json"])
195	    if result.returncode != 0:
196	        detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "herdr failed")
197	        raise ValueError(f"herdr session list failed: {detail}")

199	    payload = parse_json_bytes(result.stdout, "session-list")
200	    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not isinstance(payload.get("sessions"), list):
201	        raise ValueError("session-list JSON must contain a sessions array")
202
203	    sessions: list[SessionInfo] = []
204	    names: set[str] = set()
205	    for index, item in enumerate(payload["sessions"]):
206	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
207	            raise ValueError(f"session entry {index} must be an object")
208	        name = item.get("name")
209	        running = item.get("running")
210	        socket_path = item.get("socket_path")
211	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
212	            raise ValueError(f"session entry {index} has an invalid name")
213	        if name in names:
214	            raise ValueError(f"session-list JSON contains duplicate session '{name}'")
215	        if not isinstance(running, bool):
216	            raise ValueError(f"session '{name}' has an invalid running value")
217	        if not isinstance(socket_path, str):
218	            raise ValueError(f"session '{name}' has an invalid socket_path")
219	        if running and not socket_path:
220	            raise ValueError(f"running session '{name}' has an empty socket_path")
221	        names.add(name)
222	        sessions.append(SessionInfo(name=name, running=running, socket_path=socket_path))

243	            )

252	        return [SessionTarget(name, ambient_socket, False)]

254	    default = by_name.get("default")
255	    socket_path = default.socket_path if default is not None else None
256	    return [SessionTarget("default", socket_path or None, False)]
257
258
259	def child_env(target: SessionTarget) -> dict[str, str]:
260	    env = os.environ.copy()
261	    if target.override_socket and target.socket_path is not None:
262	        env["HERDR_SOCKET_PATH"] = target.socket_path
263	    return env
264
265
266	def optional_string(item: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> str | None:
267	    value = item.get(key)
268	    return value if isinstance(value, str) else None
269
270
271	def list_panes(
272	    herdr: str,
273	    target: SessionTarget,
274	) -> tuple[list[PaneRecord], list[ScanError]]:
275	    result = run_command([herdr, "pane", "list"], env=child_env(target))
276	    if result.returncode != 0:
277	        detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "herdr failed")
278	        return [], [
279	            ScanError("session", target.name, None, "pane-list", detail),
280	        ]
281
282	    try:
283	        payload = parse_json_bytes(result.stdout, "pane-list")
284	    except ValueError as exc:
285	        return [], [ScanError("session", target.name, None, "pane-list", str(exc))]
286
287	    panes_value = payload.get("result", {}).get("panes") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
288	    if not isinstance(panes_value, list):
289	        return [], [
290	            ScanError(
291	                "session",
292	                target.name,
293	                None,
294	                "pane-list",
295	                "pane-list JSON must contain result.panes array",
296	            )
297	        ]
298
299	    panes: list[PaneRecord] = []
300	    errors: list[ScanError] = []
301	    seen: set[str] = set()
302	    for index, item in enumerate(panes_value):
303	        pane_id = item.get("pane_id") if isinstance(item, dict) else None
304	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
305	            errors.append(
306	                ScanError("pane", target.name, None, "pane-entry", f"pane entry {index} must be an object")
307	            )
308	            continue
309	        workspace_id = item.get("workspace_id")
310	        tab_id = item.get("tab_id")
311	        if not all(isinstance(value, str) and value for value in (workspace_id, tab_id, pane_id)):
312	            errors.append(
313	                ScanError(
314	                    "pane",
315	                    target.name,
316	                    pane_id if isinstance(pane_id, str) else None,
317	                    "pane-entry",
318	                    f"pane entry {index} is missing workspace_id, tab_id, or pane_id",
319	                )
320	            )
321	            continue
322	        if pane_id in seen:
323	            errors.append(
324	                ScanError("pane", target.name, pane_id, "pane-entry", "duplicate pane_id in pane-list JSON")
325	            )
326	            continue
327	        seen.add(pane_id)
328	        panes.append(
329	            PaneRecord(
330	                session=target.name,
331	                socket_path=target.socket_path,
332	                workspace_id=workspace_id,
333	                tab_id=tab_id,
334	                pane_id=pane_id,
335	                agent_status=optional_string(item, "agent_status"),
336	                foreground_cwd=optional_string(item, "foreground_cwd"),
337	                cwd=optional_string(item, "cwd"),
338	            )
339	        )
340
341	    panes.sort(key=lambda pane: (pane.workspace_id, pane.tab_id, pane.pane_id))
342	    return panes, errors
343
344
345	def read_pane(
346	    herdr: str,
347	    target: SessionTarget,
348	    pane: PaneRecord,
349	    source: str,
350	) -> tuple[str | None, ScanError | None]:
351	    result = run_command(
352	        [herdr, "pane", "read", pane.pane_id, "--source", source, "--format", "text"],
353	        env=child_env(target),
354	    )
355	    if result.returncode != 0:
356	        detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "herdr failed")
357	        return None, ScanError("pane", target.name, pane.pane_id, "pane-read", detail)
358	    return result.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), None
359
360
361	def build_rg_argv(rg: str, args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[str]:
362	    argv = [rg, "--no-config", "--json", "--text"]
363	    if args.fixed_strings:
364	        argv.append("--fixed-strings")
365	    if args.ignore_case:
366	        argv.append("--ignore-case")
367	    argv.extend(["--", args.pattern])
368	    return argv
369
370
371	def validate_pattern(rg_argv: Sequence[str]) -> ScanError | None:
372	    result = run_command(rg_argv, input_bytes=b"")
373	    if result.returncode in (0, 1):
374	        return None
375	    detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "ripgrep failed")
376	    return ScanError("global", None, None, "rg-validate", detail)
377
378
379	def parse_submatches(value: Any) -> tuple[SubmatchRecord, ...]:
380	    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
381	        raise ValueError("ripgrep match event has no submatches")
382	    parsed: list[SubmatchRecord] = []
383	    for item in value:
384	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or not isinstance(item.get("match"), dict):
385	            raise ValueError("ripgrep submatch must be an object")
386	        text = item["match"].get("text")
387	        start = item.get("start")
388	        end = item.get("end")
389	        if not isinstance(text, str) or not isinstance(start, int) or not isinstance(end, int):
390	            raise ValueError("ripgrep submatch has invalid text or byte offsets")
391	        if start < 0 or end < start:
392	            raise ValueError("ripgrep submatch has invalid byte offset order")
393	        parsed.append(SubmatchRecord(text=text, start_byte=start, end_byte=end))
394	    return tuple(parsed)
395
396
397	def match_pane(
398	    rg_argv: Sequence[str],
399	    pane: PaneRecord,
400	    text: str,
401	) -> tuple[list[MatchRecord], ScanError | None]:
402	    result = run_command(rg_argv, input_bytes=text.encode("utf-8"))
403	    if result.returncode == 1:
404	        return [], None
405	    if result.returncode != 0:
406	        detail = clean_message(result.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"), "ripgrep failed")
407	        return [], ScanError("pane", pane.session, pane.pane_id, "rg-match", detail)
408
409	    candidates: list[MatchRecord] = []
410	    try:
411	        output = result.stdout.decode("utf-8")
412	        for raw_line in output.splitlines():
413	            event = json.loads(raw_line)
414	            if not isinstance(event, dict) or not isinstance(event.get("type"), str):
415	                raise ValueError("ripgrep JSON event must be an object with a type")
416	            if event["type"] != "match":
417	                continue
418	            data = event.get("data")
419	            if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get("lines"), dict):
420	                raise ValueError("ripgrep match event has invalid data")
421	            line = data["lines"].get("text")
422	            line_number = data.get("line_number")
423	            if not isinstance(line, str) or not isinstance(line_number, int) or line_number < 1:
424	                raise ValueError("ripgrep match event has invalid line data")
425	            if line.endswith("\n"):
426	                line = line[:-1]
427	                if line.endswith("\r"):
428	                    line = line[:-1]
429	            submatches = parse_submatches(data.get("submatches"))
430	            candidates.append(
431	                MatchRecord(
432	                    session=pane.session,
433	                    socket_path=pane.socket_path,
434	                    workspace_id=pane.workspace_id,
435	                    tab_id=pane.tab_id,
436	                    pane_id=pane.pane_id,
437	                    agent_status=pane.agent_status,
438	                    foreground_cwd=pane.foreground_cwd,
439	                    cwd=pane.cwd,
440	                    line_number=line_number,
441	                    line=line,
442	                    submatches=submatches,
443	                )
444	            )
445	        if not candidates:
446	            raise ValueError("ripgrep exited with matches but emitted no match events")
447	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
448	        return [], ScanError("pane", pane.session, pane.pane_id, "rg-match", str(exc))
449	    return candidates, None
450
451
452	def match_sort_key(match: MatchRecord) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
453	    first_start = match.submatches[0].start_byte if match.submatches else -1
454	    return (
455	        match.session,
456	        match.workspace_id,
457	        match.tab_id,
458	        match.pane_id,
459	        match.line_number,
460	        first_start,
461	    )
462
463
464	def error_sort_key(error: ScanError) -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
465	    return (error.session or "", error.pane_id or "", error.operation, error.message)
466
467
468	def scan(
469	    herdr: str,
470	    rg_argv: Sequence[str],
471	    targets: list[SessionTarget],
472	    source: str,
473	) -> ScanResult:
474	    result = ScanResult(
475	        sessions=sorted(target.name for target in targets),
476	        matches=[],
477	        errors=[],
478	    )
479
480	    pattern_error = validate_pattern(rg_argv)
481	    if pattern_error is not None:
482	        result.errors.append(pattern_error)
483	        return result
484
485	    for target in targets:
486	        panes, pane_errors = list_panes(herdr, target)
487	        result.errors.extend(pane_errors)
488	        for pane in panes:
489	            text, read_error = read_pane(herdr, target, pane, source)
490	            if read_error is not None:
491	                result.errors.append(read_error)
492	                continue
493	            assert text is not None
494	            matches, match_error = match_pane(rg_argv, pane, text)
495	            if match_error is not None:
496	                result.errors.append(match_error)
497	                continue
498	            result.matches.extend(matches)
499
500	    result.matches.sort(key=match_sort_key)
501	    result.errors.sort(key=error_sort_key)
502	    return result
503
504
505	def render_human(result: ScanResult) -> None:
506	    for match in result.matches:
507	        coordinate = (
508	            f"session={match.session} workspace={match.workspace_id} "
509	            f"tab={match.tab_id} pane={match.pane_id}"
510	        )
511	        print(f"[{coordinate}] {match.line_number}:{match.line}")
512	    for error in result.errors:
513	        location = ""
514	        if error.session is not None:
515	            location += f" session={error.session}"
516	        if error.pane_id is not None:
517	            location += f" pane={error.pane_id}"
518	        print(
519	            f"herdr-grep:{location} {error.operation}: {error.message}",
520	            file=sys.stderr,
521	        )
522
523
524	def render_json(args: argparse.Namespace, result: ScanResult, source: str) -> None:
525	    payload = {
526	        "schema_version": 1,
527	        "pattern": args.pattern,
528	        "source": source,
529	        "fixed_strings": bool(args.fixed_strings),
530	        "ignore_case": bool(args.ignore_case),
531	        "complete": result.complete,
532	        "sessions": result.sessions,
533	        "matches": [
534	            {
535	                **{key: value for key, value in asdict(match).items() if key != "submatches"},
536	                "submatches": [asdict(submatch) for submatch in match.submatches],
537	            }
538	            for match in result.matches
539	        ],
540	        "errors": [asdict(error) for error in result.errors],
541	    }
542	    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
543
544
545	def fatal_result(operation: str, message: str) -> ScanResult:
546	    return ScanResult(
547	        sessions=[],
548	        matches=[],
549	        errors=[ScanError("global", None, None, operation, message)],
550	    )
551
552
553	def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
554	    args = parse_args(argv)
555
556	    herdr = shutil.which("herdr")
557	    if herdr is None:
558	        if args.list_sessions:
559	            print("herdr-grep: dependency: herdr not found on PATH", file=sys.stderr)
560	            return 2
561	        result = fatal_result("dependency", "herdr not found on PATH")
562	        if args.json:
563	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
564	        else:
565	            render_human(result)
566	        return 2
567
568	    try:
569	        sessions = load_sessions(herdr)
570	    except ValueError as exc:
571	        if args.list_sessions:
572	            print(f"herdr-grep: session-list: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
573	            return 2
574	        result = fatal_result("session-list", str(exc))
575	        if args.json:
576	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
577	        else:
578	            render_human(result)
579	        return 2
580
581	    if args.list_sessions:
582	        for session in sorted(item.name for item in sessions if item.running):
583	            print(session)
584	        return 0
585
586	    rg = shutil.which("rg")
587	    if rg is None:
588	        result = fatal_result("dependency", "rg not found on PATH")
589	        if args.json:
590	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
591	        else:
592	            render_human(result)
593	        return 2
594
595	    try:
596	        targets = select_targets(args, sessions)
597	    except ValueError as exc:
598	        result = fatal_result("session-select", str(exc))
599	        if args.json:
600	            render_json(args, result, args.source)
601	        else:
602	            render_human(result)
603	        return 2
604
605	    result = scan(herdr, build_rg_argv(rg, args), targets, args.source)
606	    if args.json:
607	        render_json(args, result, args.source)
608	    else:
609	        render_human(result)
610	    return result.exit_status()
611
612
613	if __name__ == "__main__":
614	    try:
615	        raise SystemExit(main())
616	    except BrokenPipeError:
617	        try:
618	            sys.stdout.close()
619	        finally:
620	            raise SystemExit(0)

7	_herdr_grep() {
8	    local context state state_descr line
9	    typeset -A opt_args
10
11	    _arguments -C -s \
12	        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
13	        '(-F --fixed-strings)'{-F,--fixed-strings}'[treat PATTERN as a literal string]' \
14	        '(-i --ignore-case)'{-i,--ignore-case}'[search case-insensitively]' \
15	        '(--source --visible)--source=[pane content source]:source:(visible recent recent-unwrapped)' \
16	        '(--source)--visible[search only the visible pane screen]' \
17	        '(--session --all-sessions)--session=[search one running named session]:session:->session' \
18	        '(--session)--all-sessions[search every running local session]' \
19	        '--json[emit one structured JSON document]' \

30	}
